pe-00001:
1) Warm up in pairs by tossing a ball straight up, clapping, and catching.
2) Draw an outer circle (6m diameter) and inner circle (3-4m) with stacked cardboard boxes in the center.
3) Play 3v2 (3 attackers outside the outer circle, 2 defenders between the circles); knock down the top box for 1 point.
4) Progress to using 1 ball per team, passing to open teammates away from defenders before shooting.
pe-00002:
1) Practice dribbling and stopping the ball with soles or hips, then kick at targets 5-8m away.
2) On a 20-30m by 12-15m court, start 4v4 without defenders, shooting from a 5m shoot line and rounding a cone.
3) Advance to 6v6 with 2 defenders blocking shots between the shoot line and goal line and placing stopped balls into side baskets.
4) Award 2 points for kicking under the central rope gate and 1 point for the side gates.
pe-00003:
1) Play 4v4 on a triangle-base court; batters hit a stationary ball off a tee using a hand or tennis racket.
2) Batters run 1st, 2nd, and home (or round 1-, 2-, or 3-point cones along the 1st-base line).
3) Fielders catch the ball, choose the nearest hula-hoop out-zone, and all sit together inside/around it to call 'Out!'
4) Rotate offense and defense after all 4 batters hit; optionally start every turn with bases loaded.
pe-00004:
1) Warm up with Dribble Tag, 45-degree Continuous Shooting, and Pass & Pass support drills.
2) Play 3v2 half-court basketball where offense always has 3 players and defense has 2, with defender-free 'Free Shoot Zones' at 45° angles near the hoop.
3) Advance to 4v3 Grid-Court Basketball by dividing the court diagonally (2 players right, 1 left, 1 free roamer).
4) Reset at the start line whenever the ball goes out or defense gains possession, rotating offense/defense on a timer.
pe-00005:
1) Use a badminton-sized court (13m×6m) for 3v3 play (rotating if 4+ players per team).
2) Game 1 (Prellball-style, 50-60cm net): let the ball bounce once on your side, slap it down with both hands to pass from player 1 to 2 to 3, then catch and throw over.
3) Game 2 (Soft Volleyball-style, 150-170cm net): serve with a gentle underhand arc; Player 1 catches and passes to Player 2, Player 2 catches and tosses up, and Player 3 hits it over.
4) Allow one-bounce catches if direct catching is too difficult so rallies continue.
pe-00006:
1) Warm up with all-vs-all tail tag and Rock-Paper-Scissors breakthrough tag.
2) Treasure Tag (4v4, 18-21m×12-15m): 2 defenders stand in each of 2 tag zones; attackers wear 2 waist tags and must grab 1 beanbag from Treasure Island and return around the outside without losing both tags (2-min halves).
3) Ball-Carry Tag (3v2 then 3v3, 20m×12m): 3 attackers carry balls from start to end zone without losing their waist tag (1 pt per runner).
4) Variation: use 1 ball per team (ball carrier scores 3 pts, decoys score 1 pt).
pe-00007:
1) Warm up with sole ball taps, dribble-and-stop, knockout dribble tag, and 2v1 grid passing.
2) Play 4v4 (two 3-minute halves) on a 30m×18m court with a 4m×4m central 'Free Zone' holding 1 unguarded Freeman per team.
3) Pass into the Freeman and spread wide left or right so no defender blocks the passing lane before receiving and shooting.
4) Score 2 points through the center cone gate and 1 point through the outer gates (below cone height).
pe-00008:
1) Warm up with 'Say the Same, Do the Opposite' directional jumping.
2) River Jumping: lay two ropes to form straight, wide, or winding rivers designed by each group, leaping across with one or two feet.
3) Elastic Jumping: jump over elastic cords set at progressive heights (Frog, Rabbit, Kangaroo levels) using a rhythmic run-up.
4) Hoop Hop Relay: carry a ring baton through custom hoop patterns; adjust hoop counts by team rank so every team can win.
pe-00009:
1) Lay long ropes in zigzag or winding shapes on the ground; run along the rope and tag the next runner's right palm.
2) Progress to passing a ring baton after rounding the back of the team line.
3) Set up low cardboard boxes as hurdles for an obstacle relay.
4) Let teams experiment with box height and spacing to discover the layout that lets them run without losing speed.
pe-00010:
1) Touch Dash (1v1): front runner holds hands behind back; back runner fakes with one hand and taps with BOTH hands to trigger a sprint race.
2) Feint Tag (1v1): whenever the leader steps on a side marker, the tagger must also step on it before blocking the gate.
3) Marker Tag (3v1): 3 defenders guard 4 floor markers by standing on them so the walking tagger cannot step on an empty marker.
4) Math Relay & RPS Sprint: relay to collect numbered bibs totaling 20+ (or exactly 20), and play Rock-Paper-Scissors where winners/losers race to opposite color markers.
pe-00011:
1) Try Race (1v1): coach tosses a rugby ball for an irregular bounce; first to grab it tries to score while the other pulls their waist tag.
2) Cat & Mouse (1v1): called player grabs the ball and sprints to their back line while the partner chases their tag (start standing, sitting, or prone).
3) RPS Try & Gate Pass (1v1): RPS loser touches a coach/cone before defending; in Gate Pass, defender must touch whichever side cone the leader touches.
4) Triangle Tag (3 players): 1 tagger chases 2 ball-carriers around a cone triangle.
pe-00012:
1) Luck Tag: pass balls left (1 clap) or right (2 claps) in a circle; on the whistle, ball holders evade taggers for 5 seconds.
2) 6v1 Cone-Safe Tag: only the ball carrier can be tagged; players without the ball stand safely touching a cone and use hand-to-hand crossovers.
3) All-Out Tag & Roulette Tag: 10-second free-for-all tag, or spin a bottle (1 tagger) / rugby ball (2 taggers) in the center to pick taggers instantly.
4) Train Tag (1v3): 3 connected players maneuver together to protect the back player's tag from 1 chaser.
pe-00013:
1) Bingo Relay: 3 cones per team on a 3×3 grid; shift your own cones after placing all 3 to make 3-in-a-row.
2) Color-Sort Relay: 16 mixed cones (4 colors × 4); each runner swaps just 2 cones per turn until all 4 columns match by color.
3) Hand-Hold Chain Relay: runner 1 completes a lap, grabs runner 2's hand, then runner 3, running together as a growing chain.
4) Obstacle & Bib-Layering Relay: zigzag/two-foot jump relay, and a relay where runners put on one extra bib each lap and pass the entire stack to the next teammate.
pe-00014:
1) Jump RPS Warmup: jump while spinning arms overhead, play Rock-Paper-Scissors with partners, and perform 5 high jumps if you lose.
2) Linked-Circle Blindfold Tag: 6-8 runners hold hands in a circle around 1 blindfolded tagger in the center.
3) Runners must evade the blindfolded tagger's touch by shifting and rotating the entire circle without ever letting go of hands.
4) If tagged, become the new tagger; if two runners accidentally break hands, those two play RPS and the loser becomes the tagger.
pe-00015:
1) Apple-Hang Dash (pairs): while Partner A holds a flexed-arm hang on the low bar, Partner B sprints to touch distance-scored lines and returns before A drops.
2) 1v1 Hand Pull & 3-Way Rope Tug: pull a looped rope among 3 players to be the first to touch your outer floor marker.
3) Plastic-Bag Sled Pull (pairs): one partner puts both feet inside a plastic bag, squats, and holds a rope while the other pulls them through a cone slalom course.
4) Finish with a team sled-pull slalom relay.
pe-00016:
1) Stationary Shoulder Tap (pairs): stand facing a partner without moving your feet; twist, lean, and arch your torso to tap their shoulders as many times as possible in 30 seconds.
2) Stationary Tag Pull (pairs): without moving your feet, pull your partner's waist tag/towel while twisting to protect your own.
3) Ninja Training Game (pairs): one partner swings a rolled-up newspaper sword while the other dodges left, right, ducks, or jumps for 30 seconds.
4) Apply these body-dodging skills to outdoor directional tag.
pe-00017:
1) Rush Hour Tag (pairs or quads): inside a compact cone zone, players may ONLY fast-walk (no running), including linked-arm walking; if tagged, do 5 jumps and switch taggers.
2) Shwatch Freeze Tag: tagged players freeze in place and call 'Help!'
3) To unfreeze a classmate, TWO (and later THREE) teammates must arrive together, duck under the frozen player's arms, and pop up shouting 'Shwatch!'
4) Variation: 3 rescuers join hands to form a complete circle around the frozen player to unfreeze them.
pe-00018:
1) 3 Icicle taggers hold blue foam noodles and 3 Fireball rescuers hold red foam balls.
2) Players get frozen in 3 ways: tagged by an icicle, stepping out of bounds, or falling down; frozen players pump one fist high in the air while stepping side-to-side in place.
3) To unfreeze, a Fireball holder tosses the ball and the frozen player must catch it cleanly in the air, becoming the new Fireball holder.
4) Level 1: dropped fireballs can be re-tossed and fire holders are invincible. Level 2: dropped fireballs die on the floor. Level 3: icicles can freeze Fireball holders too!
pe-00019:
1) Set up a 15-foot square (or 4 cones) for groups of 6-7 players: 4 on the corners, 1 in the middle, and 1 caller waiting 2 steps outside in line.
2) When the caller shouts 'Switch!', all 5 active players must sprint to claim a different corner.
3) The odd player out (or anyone who falls off their feet) goes to the back of the waiting line, and the caller steps into the middle.
4) Resolve ties by whose foot touched the corner first, or quick Rock-Paper-Scissors.
pe-00020:
1) Place a large exercise ball or Kin-Ball ('Monster Ball') in the center of a large floor square, with 2 or 4 teams behind the outer lines.
2) On the whistle, throw small foam balls overhand to hit the Monster Ball and roll it across the opposing team's boundary line for 1 point.
3) Players may enter the square anywhere to retrieve small balls, but MUST step completely outside the square before throwing.
4) Stepping inside the square while throwing results in sitting in the penalty box for the round; touching or blocking the Monster Ball with your body awards 1 automatic point to the other team.
pe-00021:
1) Everyone starts as a Scorer throwing balls into targets (ball cart/box = 2 hoops, side basketball hoop = 4 hoops, far hoop = 6 hoops; no guarding targets).
2) Builders collect earned hoops and construct a Hula Hut on their side whenever they have 6 hoops (1 base, 2 inner leaning, 2 outer leaning, 1 roof).
3) Protectors guard their team's Hula Huts using their bodies while Destroyers throw balls to knock down opposing Hula Huts.
4) Gatherers ride scooters onto the other side to retrieve balls; the team with the most standing Hula Huts at the end wins.
pe-00022:
1) Divide the class into small teams of 3–4 players scattered freely across the gym with 4 foam balls.
2) Players CANNOT run while holding a ball—they must pass to teammates to set up throws.
3) When hit, players go to the sideline; each player gets ONE chance per round to re-enter the game.
4) If a surviving teammate makes a direct air catch (no floor or wall bounce), the teammate waiting longest returns; a second hit eliminates the player for the round until one team remains.
pe-00023:
1) Place 4 colored hoops (nests) in the corners and 10+ mixed balls/beanbags (eggs) in the center.
2) One runner per team collects 1 egg at a time from the middle; once the middle is empty, the teacher calls 'Rob the Nest!' and runners steal 1 egg at a time from other nests (no guarding nests).
3) Progression: each egg type requires a specific movement (soccer ball = foot dribble, basketball = hand dribble, beanbag = balance on head, bouncy ball = jump with ball between knees).
4) Add 1–2 'Angry Bird' taggers who force tagged runners to return the stolen egg.
pe-00024:
1) Start with 1 tagger holding a tennis ball, softball, or pinnie in hand while extra balls/pinnies are placed along the sideline.
2) The tagger runs and touches fleeing players directly with the ball/pinnie in hand (no throwing).
3) Anyone tagged grabs a tennis ball or puts on a pinnie and joins the taggers, growing like an avalanche until only 1 runner remains.
4) If holding a small ball is hard to spot, have taggers wear pinnies and tag by hand.
pe-00025:
1) Place a large pile of tennis balls or beanbags inside the center circle, and set up 4+ teams at corner cones with a bucket per team.
2) Basic Relay: one player per team sprints to the center, grabs 1 ball, places it in their team bucket, and tags the next runner.
3) Scooter Variation: players propel themselves on a scooter board to collect each ball.
4) Skill Variations: older grades use a hockey stick to dribble a ball back or wear a baseball glove to pick it up; count balls when the center is empty.
pe-00026:
1) Stand in personal space with arm's-length clearance facing the screen in the gym or classroom.
2) Follow the on-screen rhythm cues set to the 'APT' beat, including alternating hand-stacking motions, step-touches, jumps, and heart poses.
3) Increase intensity during the chorus with continuous knee bounces and overhead arm reaches.
4) Complete the full 3-minute song nonstop as an energizing warm-up or brain break.
pe-00027:
1) Divide the gym in half; each team has a back base holding 3 gold pieces (pins/beanbags) and a corner mat jail.
2) Cross into enemy territory to reach their safe base; from there, choose EITHER to carry 1 gold piece back OR high-five a jailed teammate for a free walk back (hands raised).
3) If tagged while carrying gold, return the gold and go to jail; settle any borderline line-tags instantly with Rock-Paper-Scissors.
4) Limit each team to 1 jail guard inside a coned buffer zone; first team to collect all 6 gold pieces wins.
pe-00028:
1) Place 2 dodgeballs on the free-throw lines and 1 on the center line of a basketball court; players inside CANNOT walk with a ball (pivoting only).
2) Players are out if hit by a ball, caught throwing, stepping on/over the boundary line, or walking with a ball, and must exit the court.
3) Out players can re-enter and swap places by (a) grabbing a loose ball outside (5-sec limit, walking allowed outside) and hitting/catching an active player, or (b) tagging an active player standing too close to the boundary line.
4) Jailbreak Bonus: if an out player shoots a basket from outside the court, ALL out players return to the game!
pe-00029:
1) Half the class joins hands in a circle with arms raised high to form the 'mousetrap', while the other half are 'mice'.
2) While music plays, the mice run in and out of the circle underneath the raised arms.
3) When the music stops, the circle players immediately drop down into a squat position to close the trap.
4) Any mice trapped inside the circle join the circle hands, making the trap larger each round until all mice are caught; then switch roles.
pe-00030:
1) Set up 4 gym mats as bases; divide into a batting team lined up safely along the wall and a scattered fielding team.
2) The batter hits a pitched or tee-placed indoor ball and must run around ALL 4 bases nonstop without stopping at any base.
3) Meanwhile, the fielding team retrieves the ball and must complete 5 clean passes to different teammates while counting aloud (dropped passes don't count, just continue).
4) If the batter reaches home before 5 passes are completed, they score 1 point; otherwise they are out. Bat through the entire lineup before switching.
pe-00031:
1) Set up bowling pins or cones ('planets') across one side of the gym and divide K–2 students into Aliens (throwers) and Astronauts (defenders).
2) On the whistle/music, Aliens grab foam dodgeballs ('missiles') and use overhand throws to knock down the planets.
3) Astronauts defend the planets by blocking incoming missiles, throwing/rolling balls back to the Aliens' side, and standing knocked-down planets back up.
4) Play continuously for 2–3 minutes, then switch roles so everyone plays both sides.
pe-00032:
1) Place 4 benches (flipped on their sides as goals) across the 4 corners of the gym; divide into 4 teams crouching behind their bench and number players 1–5.
2) Place a soccer ball in the center and call out a number (e.g., 'Number 4!'); all four #4 players jump into the court for a 1v1v1v1 battle.
3) Score 1 point by kicking the ball against any of the other 3 teams' benches; the other 3 teams perform quick jumping jacks before resetting.
4) Call two numbers at once for 2v2v2v2 cooperative play.
pe-00033:
1) Set up 4 teams with 1 Rescuer holding a hula hoop at the far cone facing the rest of their team at the start cone.
2) On the whistle, the Rescuer runs across, places the hoop over the first teammate, and both run back together inside the hoop.
3) The rescued player becomes the new Rescuer and runs back to save the next teammate until the entire team is across.
4) Finale: once all teammates are rescued, they immediately hold hands in a line and pass the hula hoop down the entire human chain without letting go of hands!
pe-00034:
1) Assign 1–2 taggers wearing pinnies, each controlling a giant Kin-Ball.
2) Taggers move with the Kin-Ball by rolling it with their hands only (lifting or kicking the Kin-Ball is prohibited).
3) Runners evade the rolling Kin-Balls; anyone touched by a Kin-Ball exits to the sideline.
4) Sideline players perform fitness tasks (squats or jumping jacks) to immediately re-enter the game.
pe-00035:
1) All students except the runner ('Jerry', wearing a pinnie) form two concentric circles—an inner circle and an outer circle.
2) Inner-circle players face outward and outer-circle players face inward, creating a circular track between them.
3) Jerry and the Kin-Ball start inside the track; circle players cooperatively push and roll the Kin-Ball along the track to tag Jerry within the time limit.
4) Role-reversal ('Tom' mode): the chaser is 'Tom' trying to touch the Kin-Ball while circle players rapidly roll the Kin-Ball away in either direction.
pe-00036:
1) Push desks to the walls, arrange chairs in a circle, and start with the teacher and 1 first tagger sitting on opposite chairs while everyone else stands inside.
2) Seated players roll a large gym ball across the floor; anyone hit by a smooth roll is out (bouncing hits do not count) and sits on a chair to join the rollers.
3) Inside players are automatically out if they touch or kick a stopped ball in the middle—only seated players may retrieve it.
4) When only 2 dodgers remain, the very first tagger re-enters the circle for a second chance; the last player standing wins.
pe-00037:
1) Set a mini soccer goal or target at the far end of the gym or field as the disc-golf hole.
2) Individual Race: players throw their soft foam disc from the start line, run to where it lands, and throw again until it enters the goal.
3) Team Relay Golf: Teammate 1 throws from start, Teammate 2 throws from where Teammate 1's disc landed, and Teammate 3 putts into the goal.
4) Count total throws per team—the team that scores in the fewest throws wins.
pe-00038:
1) Play two-team Ultimate Frisbee in the gym, passing a soft foam disc to score in the opponent's goal/endzone.
2) Enforce a quick 3-second stall count so players pass rapidly without holding the disc.
3) To prevent rough crowding, any defender who makes physical contact with the thrower must step off the court and complete 5 jumping jacks before rejoining.
4) Dropped discs or interceptions result in an immediate turnover on the spot.
pe-00039:
1) Game 1 (Zombie Stick Tag): start with 1 'Mother Zombie' holding a foam play-stick; tagged runners do a quick exercise, pick up a stick, and become zombies too—naturally distributing sticks to the whole class.
2) Game 2 (Nutmeg Ring Circle): form circles of 6–8 players standing with feet wide apart.
3) Place the stick tip inside the ring center and sweep it across the floor to slide the ring through a classmate's legs while others block their own legs with their sticks.
4) If scored on, do jumping jacks or frog jumps; ban passing to immediate neighbors to increase difficulty.
pe-00040:
1) Grip the short Padminton paddle ('Handler') securely with thumb and four fingers after a full-body joint warm-up.
2) Step 1 (Solo Control): hit the shuttlecock straight up with a forehand stroke and catch it, then practice backhand hits, and combine alternating forehand-backhand juggling.
3) Step 2 (Partner Cooperative Rally): stand a short distance apart and rally continuously using both forehand and backhand strokes.
4) Step 3 (2-Try Juggling Challenge): each player gets 2 attempts to set a high score for alternating forehand/backhand solo hits.
pe-00041:
1) Two teams line up on opposite sides of a turning long rope; one jumper from each team enters the spinning rope together.
2) While jumping the rope, the two players play Rock-Paper-Scissors.
3) The winner stays jumping inside the rope while the loser exits cleanly and the next challenger from the losing team immediately jumps in.
4) Anyone who trips on the rope during a duel is automatically eliminated; the team with survivors remaining wins.
pe-00042:
1) Two turners spin the long rope while the group sings the traditional Korean jump-rope rhyme ('Kkoma-ya Kkoma-ya').
2) Action 1 ('Turn around'): jump inside and spin 180 degrees.
3) Actions 2 & 3 ('Touch the ground' / 'Shout Hurray'): bend knees to touch the floor between jumps, then raise both arms high overhead.
4) Action 4 ('Goodbye'): exit the turning rope cleanly without tripping; progress from 1 jumper to 2, 3, and 4 jumpers in sync!
pe-00043:
1) Line up 8–10 students behind an agility ladder on the gym floor.
2) Perform 4 progressive footwork patterns: (1) Two-foot forward hops in each rung, (2) Lateral side-to-side hops, and (3) Straddle-in-and-out hops.
3) Pattern 4 ('Out-Out-In-In'): step one foot at a time outside-outside-inside-inside along the ladder.
4) Instead of racing against classmates, time how long it takes the ENTIRE group to complete all 4 patterns and work together to beat your team record!
pe-00044:
1) Canopy Lift: hold the parachute handles around the perimeter and lift together on '1, 2, 3!' to feel the air resistance.
2) Canopy Swap: while the parachute floats high overhead, the teacher calls a trait (e.g., 'Anyone wearing a black shirt!') and those students run underneath to swap spots before it settles.
3) Alligator & Lifeguards: 'Alligators' crawl under the shaking parachute to gently pull 'swimmers' while 'Lifeguards' on the outside rescue them.
4) Igloo Dome: lift the parachute high, step two feet inside together, and pull the edges down behind your backs to sit inside an inflated dome!
pe-00045:
1) Draw a start line and target line 6 paces apart for 3v3 teams; defenders stand their targets (wooden blocks, 500ml bottles, or milk cartons) on the target line.
2) Attackers advance through progressive stages to knock down the targets; missing a target or dropping your striker mid-walk ends your turn.
3) Four Core Stages: Stage 1 (Throw from start line), Stage 2 (Foot-Instep Carry & Drop), Stage 3 (Knee-Squeeze Waddle & Drop), Stage 4 (Head-Balance Walk & Drop).
4) Add custom stages such as ankle-squeeze, underarm-tuck, or eyes-closed drops.
pe-00046:
1) Draw a large spiral ('snail shell') track on the ground; one team lines up at the inner home and the other at the outer home.
2) On the start signal, the first runner from each team runs along the spiral path toward the opposing home.
3) Where they meet, both runners must stop 1 step apart, exchange a greeting and quick prompt (e.g., favorite animal or food), and play Rock-Paper-Scissors.
4) The winner continues running toward the opponent's home while the loser exits the spiral to the back of their line and their next teammate immediately sprints out; first team to step into the opponent's home wins.
pe-00047:
1) Mark a large outer boundary circle with a single spot marker ('button') in the exact center; throw 1 ball per team to determine 1st-set hammer.
2) Standing outside the circle, teams alternate throwing/rolling their colored balls toward the center spot marker until all players have thrown (End of Set 1).
3) Curling Scoring: only the team with the ball closest to the center spot marker scores in that set, earning 1 point for each of their balls that is closer to the marker than the opponent's closest ball.
4) Play 3 sets (scoring team throws first in the next set); optionally vary into 'Spot-Marker Pool' with multiple colored markers.
pe-00048:
1) Everyone starts at Stage 1 (Neck rotations) and walks around performing their current joint exercise to find a classmate at the SAME stage.
2) Face your partner, perform 4 counts one way + 4 counts the other way together, clap twice, double high-five, and play Rock-Paper-Scissors.
3) Winners advance through the 5 stages: (1) Neck → (2) Shoulders → (3) Wrists & Ankles → (4) Waist/Hips → (5) Knees; losers stay at their current stage.
4) After winning Stage 5 (Knees), do 3 jumping jacks in front of the teacher and beat the teacher at RPS to graduate (if you lose to the teacher, win Stage 5 again first).
pe-00049:
1) Taggers hold or wear pinnies and chase runners inside a coned boundary square.
2) When about to be tagged, runners can shout 'Banana!' instead of 'Freeze!' and press both hands together high overhead like a banana.
3) A single player CANNOT unfreeze a banana—TWO free players must arrive at the exact same time and gently pull down the left and right arms ('peeling the banana') to free their classmate.
4) If tagged before calling 'Banana!', the runner takes the pinnie and becomes the new tagger.
pe-00050:
1) Draw a single 10m circle; 4 attackers from Team A and 4 from Team B (8 total) stand mixed around the outside, while all remaining players from both teams enter the circle together as defenders.
2) Outside attackers CANNOT pass side-to-side—they must throw into the circle; inside defenders catch balls thrown by boys to pass back out to their own outside attackers.
3) Co-Ed / Skill Handicap Rule: balls thrown by boys count only on a direct hit (1 penalty point) and can be caught, whereas balls thrown by girls CANNOT be caught, count even off a bounce/graze, and inflict 2 penalty points!
4) Hit players are never eliminated—they step outside, do jumping jacks, add 1 or 2 penalty points to their team's flip-scoreboard, and immediately re-enter; lowest penalty score wins.
pe-00051:
1) Introduce two golden cues: (1) 'Run forward whenever you have the ball' and (2) 'After passing or off-the-ball, loop behind the ball carrier.'
2) Warm up with team Tag-Snatch Tag (no ball) followed by a 30-Pass Circle Race using two-handed underhand lateral/backward passes before gathering in the center to shout 'Try!'
3) Run 3 simultaneous courts (6 teams) using student self-officiating; encourage carriers to run forward until their tag is pulled before passing.
4) Simplify offside by making the first pass immediately after a tag un-interceptable.
pe-00052:
1) Place a gym mat against a sturdy wall; face the wall, swing your torso down, plant both hands, and kick one leg up so both feet rest against the wall.
2) Practice the 3 key checkpoints: (1) plant hands shoulder-width apart and parallel with fingers spread wide, (2) lock elbows, back, and hips like one straight pole, and (3) keep eyes focused on the mat between your hands.
3) To overcome fear of inversion, pad the wall and floor with extra mats so any fall is painless.
4) Beginners may rest their back, hips, or thighs against the wall first before straightening into a full handstand.
pe-00053:
1) Balance: perform 2-, 4-, and 8-person lean-back counter-balances holding hands, then test balance walks on folded newspaper and a mat-lined balance beam.
2) Locomotion & Strength: jump a turning long rope in pairs for 10 consecutive reps, and play Piggyback Rock-Paper-Scissors moving around the gym to crown a grand champion.
3) Combined Movement 1 & 2: toss balls straight up and swap places to catch each other's ball; carry 4 balls of different sizes/weights on a large drawing board in a team relay.
4) Combined Movement 3: have a partner toss a soft ball high while you perform a quick forward roll on a mat and catch the ball as you stand up.
pe-00054:
1) Roly-Poly & Balance: press soles together, rock back onto the mat, and roll up to stand solo, in pairs, and in linked groups of 4.
2) Animal-Cone Relay: run to a cone, peek at the animal picture hidden underneath, and travel back using that animal's locomotion.
3) Manipulative Play: spin hula hoops upright on the floor, run through rolling hoops, and practice backward jump-rope.
4) Movement-Shop Lands & Bingo: students take turns as 'shopkeepers' and 'customers' at stations (Jump Land, Ball-Pinch Land) to teach tricks and color in a 3-person Movement Bingo card.
pe-00055:
1) Warm up with rhythmic skipping and partner stretching to notice how your body and your partner's body feel.
2) All Aboard! ('Minna de Norou'): fit the entire group onto a small floor mat/island and chant your team name 3 times to pass; shrink the island each round by reaching across to hold distant teammates' hands in a tight 'onion huddle.'
3) Balance-Beam / Newspaper Line-Up Switch: stand single-file on a narrow folded newspaper strip or low balance beam and rearrange the group by height, roster number, or birth month (Jan–Dec) without anyone stepping off.
4) If anyone steps off, restart together while supporting teammates as they pass.
pe-00056:
1) Cone-Ball Color Match Relay: 16 colored balls sit on mismatched colored cones (4×4); each runner swaps 2 balls until every ball matches its cone color.
2) Ball Bingo Relay: gently place balls inside a 3×3 hoop grid without letting them roll out to complete 3-in-a-row.
3) First-to-3 Ball Raid: 4 teams collect 1 ball at a time from the center (then from the fullest opponent hoop, no guarding) to be first to hold 3 balls.
4) 3v1 4-Cone Guard & Endless Leg-Tunnel Roll: 3 defenders guard 4 cones for 10 seconds, then the whole group forms a line of wide legs to roll a ball cleanly through 11+ leg tunnels in a row by sprinting to the end of the line.
pe-00057:
1) Seated Foot-Pick to Cones (1v1): sit facing your partner, grip 4 colored balls between your feet one by one, and balance each ball on its matching colored disc cone.
2) 9-Hoop Color Sort Race: sprint to sort mixed colored balls into their matching colored hoops in a 3×3 grid.
3) Backward-Roll Foot-to-Basket: sit with a ball pinched between your feet, roll onto your back, and reach your feet overhead to drop the ball into a basket behind your head.
4) Hoop-Drag Slalom & Leash-Hoop Ball Walk: drag a hula hoop trapping a ball around a cone, then attach a jump-rope leash to a hoop and pull it smoothly around the gym without losing the ball inside.
pe-00058:
1) Spinning-Hoop Timer & Hip Sumo: race to move balls one by one before a spinning hula hoop falls flat; then stand back-to-back with hips touching inside a hoop and push with hips only to grab the ball.
2) Rolling-Hoop Pass & Reverse-Cue Catch/Dodge: pass through a rolling hoop and over the top; then face a wall and react as your partner rolls a ball and calls 'Through!' (dodge) or 'Catch!' (then reverse the cues!).
3) Drop-Ball Split Dodge & Follow-the-Leader Dribble: split feet to dodge a dropped ball/towel, and dribble a soccer ball through the exact floor rings your leader visited.
4) Hoop-Window Bounce Pass & Seated Cone Hockey: hold a hoop with your non-dominant hand to bounce-pass through the hoop, and sit to trap or score rolling balls using an upside-down cone.
pe-00059:
1) Warm up by forming instant group shapes (circles/triangles), embodying the texture of flying/crumpling newspaper from head to toe, and acting out slow-motion 'Air Sports.'
2) Explore the theme 'Intense / Explosive Energy' (soda fizz, bursting water balloons, jack-in-the-box, volcano eruption) by taking turns improvising one after another in small groups.
3) Select your group's favorite motif and structure it into a 3-part sequence ('Beginning tension – Middle explosion – Ending aftermath') with clear contrast and dynamics.
4) Share group performances and finish with the entire class performing the volcano eruption together.
pe-00060:
1) Warm up with a variation of Red Light, Green Light and teacher-led Ninja stealth walks ('tip-toe, crouch low, scan the ceiling and floor').
2) In trios, flip over one 'Ninja Technique Image Card' at a time, immediately act out the technique together, and turn the card back face-down.
3) Each trio picks their 3 favorite cards and links them into a continuous Ninja story (including dramatic 1v1 or 2v1 battle moments).
4) Pair up with a neighboring trio for a quick 'Show & Feedback' check before performing for the class.
pe-00061:
1) Begin with bar familiarization drills: front-support side travel, swing-and-push backward dismount, continuous jump-to-front-support, thigh-hug swings, skin-the-cat, and bat-hang swings with a walk-out hand dismount.
2) Set the lesson goal: master at least one mount and one support-circle skill so you can link 'Mount + Circle + Dismount' in the next lesson's showcase.
3) Use kick-off ramps/pads and peer spotting to practice pullover mounts and controlled dismounts.
4) Practice forward and backward hip circles, sharing your target skill with a partner for specific form feedback.
pe-00062:
1) Warm up with 1-step takeoffs swinging both arms and kicking the lead leg to shoulder height, plus vertical jumps toward high overhead targets.
2) Practice a rhythmic 5-step approach ('1-2-1-2-3!') with a start marker and takeoff board while teammates chant the cadence aloud.
3) Choose task-specific stations: (a) a cloth ribbon tied at bar center for takeoff accuracy, (b) an X-shaped elastic cord to cue high leg clearance, (c) double parallel bars for wide mid-air 'figure-4' scissors action, or (d) 7-step speed approaches.
4) Hold a final team meet where points are awarded based on each student's improvement over their personal target height.
pe-00063:
1) Start every lesson with the 'Familiarization Challenge' combining lower- and middle-grade rolls and balances.
2) Basic Time (three 4-minute rotations): practice individual skills—such as handstand forward roll, straddle forward/backward roll, and cartwheel—using stacked mats to cushion impact and aid rotation.
3) Challenge Time (Routine Combination): link 3–4 mastered skills smoothly without extra steps, focusing on a clean final standing finish.
4) If one skill breaks down during the routine, rotate back to the single-skill station for a quick fix before re-attempting the full sequence.
pe-00064:
1) Warm up with 3-step rhythm jumps over elastic cords and mini-hurdles, practicing soft knee-bent landings on a safety mat.
2) Progress from a 3-step approach to a 5-step takeoff-board jump while teammates chant '1, 2, 1, 2, Bang!' in rhythm.
3) Focus on stamping the takeoff foot strongly while driving the opposite lead knee high and landing on the lead foot first.
4) Final Team Contest: compare each student's 5-step height against their baseline 3-step height from Lesson 1, summing everyone's improvement points for the team score.
pe-00065:
1) In groups of 4 around a single center cone, place 4 different colored beanbags (e.g., red, blue, yellow, green) just outside the cone.
2) On the first whistle, all 4 players circle slowly around the cone in one direction.
3) Every time the whistle blows again, players must immediately reverse their circling direction.
4) When the teacher calls out TWO colors (e.g., 'Green and Yellow!'), the first two players to grab those two beanbags win the round!
pe-00066:
1) Scatter 10–20 hula hoops across the gym floor and briefly discuss personal space and how many classmates might fit inside a single hoop.
2) While music plays, students run or skip freely around the gym without stepping inside any hoops.
3) When the music stops, everyone jumps into the nearest hula hoop—multiple students can share the same hoop with zero elimination.
4) Remove several hoops after each round so students must cooperate and squeeze more classmates into the remaining hoops!
pe-00067:
1) Place half the class around a large circle with soft foam volleyballs as 'Rollers', and put the other half inside the circle as dodgers.
2) Rollers roll their balls across the floor trying to hit the feet of players inside the circle.
3) Whenever an inside player's foot is hit, they leave the middle and join the outer circle as an additional Roller.
4) Continue until only 1 survivor remains in the middle, then swap the starting halves for Round 2.
pe-00068:
1) Spread out 2 hula hoops of each color across the gym floor and give taggers short foam noodles matching those exact colors.
2) Exercise Mode: when tagged by a colored noodle, run to a matching colored hula hoop and complete a jump/exercise inside it to re-enter.
3) 10-Point Countdown Mode: everyone starts with 10 points; each time you are tagged, tap your foot inside the matching colored hoop to deduct 1 point and keep running.
4) Course-Change Rule: if you are heading toward a red hoop after a red tag and get tagged by a blue noodle along the way, immediately change course and head to a blue hoop instead!
pe-00069:
1) Cut a slit near one end of a pool noodle and tape both ends of the slit so it fits snugly on top of a tagger's head like a mosquito proboscis.
2) Mosquito taggers chase players around the gym; anyone tagged gets 'itchy' and must freeze in place scratching both shoulders.
3) Rescuers carrying a hula hoop ('medicine') cure itchy classmates by placing the hoop over their head and dropping it to the floor.
4) Anyone currently holding a medicine hula hoop cannot be tagged by mosquitoes!
pe-00070:
1) Set 1 hula hoop at the throwing line and 5 bowling pins at the far end for each team.
2) The first thrower steps into the hoop, grips the football laces (side to target, step with opposite foot), and throws once to knock down their team's pins (knocking down a neighbor's pin helps that neighbor!).
3) The thrower runs to retrieve the football and MUST hand it directly to the next teammate in line (throwing the ball back is forbidden).
4) Any pin accidentally bumped by a runner's body must be stood back up; first team to knock down all 5 pins wins.
pe-00071:
1) Place 4 gym mats in the corners as 'animal cages' with students on the mats and 2–3 Zookeepers in the center.
2) Tell a quick story: 'The zookeepers were just finishing work for the day when suddenly all the MONKEYS escaped!'
3) All students leave the cages moving and acting like that animal while the Zookeepers try to tag them.
4) Tagged animals return to their corner mat cages until everyone is caught; start the next round by calling a new animal (kangaroos, crabs, frogs, horses) to practice varied locomotor skills.
pe-00072:
1) Divide the gym in half for two teams (Red vs. Green); every student places 1 bowling pin of their team color on a floor spot and guards it.
2) Grab foam balls, return to your pin, and throw to knock down pins of the OPPOSITE color while blocking balls aimed at your pin.
3) Whenever your pin is knocked down, pick up your pin, go to the back exercise zone, and complete 10 reps (push-ups, shoulder taps, or jumping jacks).
4) Cross-Court Respawn Twist: after finishing your 10 reps, re-enter on the OPPOSITE side of the gym, set your pin on an open spot, and keep throwing at the opposing team's pin color!
pe-00073:
1) Form 6–8 small teams of 2–3 players each stationed at perimeter hula hoops with a large supply of balls in the center.
2) Players alternate retrieving 1 ball at a time from the center, and once the center is empty, stealing 1 ball at a time from other teams' hoops (no defending allowed).
3) Apply sport-specific skill rules to every trip: (a) Soccer: foot-dribble back and trap inside the hoop; (b) Basketball: hand-dribble back.
4) (c) Volleyball: continuously self-set overhead all the way back to your hoop; (d) Football/Baseball: run to grab a ball and throw it from there to your partner standing inside your home hoop for a clean catch!
pe-00074:
1) Line up each team behind a start cone with 3 hula hoops placed in a straight line ahead at short (yellow), medium (red), and long (blue) distances, and a pile of flags/beanbags at the far end.
2) One teammate stands inside the 1st hoop; the first thrower in line throws the ball to the hoop player. On a clean catch, the catcher sprints to the far end, grabs 1 flag, and brings it to the team cone.
3) Rotation: the thrower moves into the hoop, and the catcher joins the back of the line (if the pass is dropped, the thrower retrieves the ball for the next person in line while the hoop player stays until they make a catch).
4) Collect 5 flags from Hoop 1, then advance to Hoop 2 for 5 flags, and Hoop 3 for 5 flags—first team to capture 15 flags wins!
pe-00075:
1) Divide the class into even teams behind starting cones, with 1 scooter board per team and a turnaround pylon at the far end.
2) Seated on the scooter, the first player propels themselves down, rounds the far pylon, and returns to hand off the scooter to the next teammate.
3) Competitive Mode: players sit down at the back of their line after finishing their lap; first team all seated wins.
4) Non-Competitive Skill Mode: run continuous laps while changing the movement challenge every few minutes (forwards, backwards, sideways, or balancing a beanbag on your head).
pe-00076:
1) Two teams of 3–5 players line up behind starting cones facing their own laundry basket/crate target, with 1 beanbag per team.
2) Between the two teams, lay a line of 7 hula hoops with a large cone standing in the center (4th) hoop as a tug-of-war score marker.
3) On 'Go!', the first player in each line tosses their beanbag toward their basket, sprints to retrieve it, hands it to the next player, and rotates to the back.
4) Every time a player makes a basket, they move the center cone 1 hoop closer to the opponent's end; first team to push the cone all the way off the opponent's end wins!
pe-00077:
1) Split the class into two lines on opposite sidelines; place 1 cone about one-third of the way ahead of each line in a counterclockwise loop.
2) One runner from each line steps out to start at their ahead cone (the 'rabbit'), while the next player in each line readies to chase.
3) On the whistle, all 4 runners (2 chasers and 2 rabbits) sprint at maximum speed counterclockwise toward the opposite line.
4) Runners join the back of the opposite line while the next player steps up to the cone; even if caught, nobody is eliminated!
pe-00078:
1) Number the four corners of the gym or classroom 1, 2, 3, and 4, and choose 1 'It' player to stand in the center.
2) The center player closes their eyes and counts to 10 while performing 10 jumping jacks; meanwhile, everyone else skips or gallops to choose one of the 4 corners.
3) At 10, keeping their eyes closed, the center player calls out a corner number (1–4).
4) Everyone in that called corner comes to the middle to join the center player in doing jumping jacks for the next countdown until 1 winner remains!
pe-00079:
1) Spread out across the playing area and choose 2 'Monkeys' as taggers.
2) Round 1 (Peel the Banana): if tipped by a monkey, freeze with both hands overhead like a banana until a classmate peels one arm down and then the other; players not frozen at the whistle earn 1 point.
3) Round 2 (15-Second Flamingo Balance): when tipped by a monkey, balance on one leg for 15 seconds without letting your raised foot touch the ground.
4) Once you complete the 15-second balance, you are free to run again!
pe-00080:
1) Pac-Man Line Tag: everyone moves strictly along gym floor lines; if tagged by a Pac-Man, sit down on the line as a roadblock that runners cannot pass (add a Doctor who heals roadblocks!).
2) Shadow Tag & Leg Tag (pairs): chase your partner until the freeze whistle—if within arm's reach, the runner does 5 star jumps, otherwise the shadow does; in Leg Tag, tap behind your partner's knees to trigger a quick push-up.
3) Knock & Run and Conditional Bull Rush: creep up behind a partner, tap their shoulder, and race back to start; or run across the field when the Bull Rush tagger calls a trait matching you.
4) Revenge Survivor Tag & Number Wall Relay: everyone is 'It'—sit when tagged and re-enter as soon as your tagger gets tagged; finish with multi-number wall sprint relays.
pe-00081:
1) Dig Challenges (1–5): (1) Bounce-Dig-Bounce with straight forearms and leg push, (2) Throw-Clap Behind Back-Dig-Catch, (3) Throw-360° Spin-Dig-Catch, (4) Alternating Right/Left Single-Arm Touches, and (5) Continuous Wall Digging (allow 1 bounce if needed).
2) Set Challenges (6–11): (6) Bounce High-Set High-Catch, (7) Throw-Multi Clap-Set-Catch, (8) Throw-360° Spin-Set-Catch, (9) Continuous Overhead Setting while slowly turning 360°, (10) Two-Foot Jump Catch at peak reach & Jump-Set, and (11) Wall Setting & Seated Floor Setting.
3) Spike Challenge (12): stand 3–4m from a wall, toss the ball high, hit a downward 'big high-five' spike so it bounces off the floor onto the wall, and catch the rebound.
pe-00082:
1) Pass & Go: 3 feeders stand at the net; each passer moves laterally across 3 cones digging (then setting) a tossed ball back to each feeder, progressing to a 3-team race to complete 30 over-the-net digs into a net catcher's hands.
2) Spike Jailbreak: players toss and spike balls over the net from the attack line; if you hit the net/out or your spike is caught on the fly by a player in 'Jail' on the other side, you go to Jail while the catcher breaks out!
3) Battleships Serving: two teams serve continuously from behind the service line to bounce balls inside 5 target hula hoops on the opponent's court (retrieve each hit hoop), or knock down a corner pin for an instant win!
pe-00083:
1) Set up a 3×3 grid of 9 hula hoops at one end of the gym and give each team 4 colored pinnies (markers) at the start line.
2) Players relay one at a time (running or crab-walking) to place a marker inside an empty hoop and tag the next runner behind the start line.
3) First team to line up 3 markers horizontally, vertically, or diagonally wins (settle simultaneous arrivals with Rock-Paper-Scissors).
4) Tactical Variation: on your turn at the grid, you may choose EITHER to place your own marker OR to pick up an opponent's marker and return it!
pe-00084:
1) Set up a large hexagon court with 3 cones placed side-by-side at each of the 6 vertices (18 cones total = 6 goals).
2) Divide into 2 teams; each team starts owning 3 goals and receives 2 soccer balls (4 balls in play simultaneously).
3) Attackers dribble and kick to knock down a cone at any opposing goal; as soon as a cone falls, that entire 3-cone goal converts to the attacking team's ownership!
4) Only 1 defender may guard a goal at a time (no hands allowed); after 5 minutes, the team owning more goals wins.
pe-00085:
1) Divide into two 8-player teams; 2 players from each team stand along the opponent's endline holding a hula hoop together as a 'moving basketball hoop.'
2) Players advance the ball using PASSES ONLY (no dribbling allowed) so every teammate touches the ball.
3) Defenders must stay 1 meter away from the ball holder with zero physical contact (2 contact warnings = 2-minute penalty).
4) The 2 hoop-holders move the hula hoop up, down, left, or right to help their teammates' shots pass through the hoop for 1 point; play four 5-minute periods, rotating the hoop-holders each period.
pe-00086:
1) Set up a 4-base baseball diamond (Home, 1st, 2nd, 3rd) and place a basket of wristbands/rings at Home plate.
2) Students pair up at Home plate and play Rock-Paper-Scissors.
3) The winner hits a 'Home Run'—sprinting counterclockwise around 1st, 2nd, and 3rd base back to Home to put on 1 wristband before challenging a new partner.
4) The loser stays at Home plate to play RPS against another waiting player (or does jumping jacks if no partner is available); celebrate the first players to collect 2–5 wristbands!
pe-00087:
1) Draw a center line and two outer safety lines; pairs face each other across the center line holding opposite ends of the same foam noodle with their left hands.
2) Play Rock-Paper-Scissors with your right hand.
3) On a tie, both players slide their grip closer toward the middle of the foam stick.
4) As soon as someone wins, the loser lets go of the stick, turns, and sprints for their safety line while the winner chases to tap their back once before they cross the safety line!
pe-00088:
1) Lay a curling house target sheet (or taped concentric circles) on a smooth classroom or gym floor, and seat teams behind the start line with colored jumbo stacking cups.
2) From a seated or kneeling position, slide your upside-down stacking cup smoothly along the floor toward the target rings.
3) Knock opposing cups out of the rings or curl your team's cups onto the center red button.
4) Score points at the end of each round based on the cups closest to the center of the house.
pe-00089:
1) Set up 4 corner cones in the classroom for a 3-part warm-up: (1) jog 3 laps around the cones, (2) high-knee skips (tapping knees up to a horizontal foam stick), and (3) touch-the-floor-and-jump reaches.
2) The tagger puts on a cap with a blindfold over their eyes and holds a soft foam stick.
3) Runners move around the classroom clapping their hands and calling out so the blindfolded tagger can locate them by sound.
4) When the tagger gently touches a runner with the foam stick, rotate taggers until every student has had a turn.
pe-00090:
1) Lay 1 foam noodle flat on the classroom or gym floor as a mini net between two players (1v1, or 2v2 in a larger space).
2) Rally a slow-moving balloon ball across the foam noodle using open hands.
3) Allow either zero bounces or 1 bounce on your side, and allow each player up to 3 consecutive self-touches to control and hit the ball over.
4) Play to 11 points, rotating opponents after each mini-match.
pe-00091:
1) Everyone scatters across the gym in an all-vs-all game as the teacher tosses 3 soft dodgeballs into play.
2) Any player who grabs a ball may take up to 3 steps and throw at anyone (except another player currently holding a ball—ball holders have a truce!).
3) If hit, perform 5 jumping jacks and immediately continue playing; if you catch an incoming throw in the air, skip the jumping jacks and immediately take 3 steps to counter-attack!
4) Designate a '1-Minute Rest Zone' on the sideline where tired students can catch their breath for up to 1 minute before jumping back in.
pe-00092:
1) Every player—including the tagger—chooses and carries 1 ball (mix of large and small soft balls).
2) The tagger chases classmates and must touch them directly with the ball held in their hand (no throwing).
3) Tagged players become 'Statues' by holding their ball high overhead and standing with legs wide apart.
4) Free players rescue a Statue by rolling their own ball cleanly through the Statue's legs; rotate taggers every 1–2 minutes.
pe-00093:
1) The first tagger holds a dodgeball high overhead to signal they are 'It' while everyone else scatters.
2) The tagger throws the ball to hit any runner; once the ball hits the floor, anyone can grab it, raise it overhead, and immediately become the new tagger!
3) Anyone hit by a throw steps outside the boundary, performs 5 star jumps (jumping jacks), and immediately re-enters the game.
4) Progression: add a 2nd ball so two taggers are active at the same time.
pe-00094:
1) Partners face each other a few steps apart; each player places 2 sport-stacking cups shoulder-width apart in front of their feet as their goalposts.
2) Staying in a low athletic stance, players slap/roll a small ball across the floor with their open hands to score.
3) Rolling the ball cleanly between the opponent's 2 cups scores 1 point; knocking down one of the opponent's cups directly scores 2 points!
4) Level 2: put 2 balls in play at the same time for non-stop 1v1 hand-eye action.
pe-00095:
1) Each student sits at their desk or floor spot with a set of colored sport-stacking cups facing the projector screen.
2) The teacher flashes a photo of a specific multi-colored cup tower (including balance tricks where cups hook onto inner rims) for 3–10 seconds, then hides the image.
3) Students reconstruct the exact color positions, cup orientations, and balance tricks from memory.
4) As soon as a student finishes, they sit down quietly and raise their hand for the teacher to verify; keep the image visible for younger grades.
pe-00096:
1) Place 4 cones in the corners of the gym; the Defense team splits across 3 corners while the Offense team forms two lines at the 4th corner.
2) Offense runners sprint out in both directions to meet a Defender at the midpoint line.
3) Before throwing Rock-Paper-Scissors, the Defender MUST call out either 'Winner!' or 'Loser!'
4) If 'Winner!' was called, the RPS winner chases the loser back to their cone; if 'Loser!' was called, the RPS loser chases the winner! If the Offense player wins Stage 1, they advance to the next corner Defender—winning 2 stages in a row scores 1 point for Offense (7-min halves).
pe-00097:
1) Groups of 4–5 players stand in a spaced line on floor spot markers, with the last player holding a soccer ball at their feet.
2) The back player dribbles the soccer ball with their feet in a zigzag slalom around their teammates to reach the front marker.
3) From the front marker, the player turns and passes the ball along the floor back through the line of teammates' wide-stanced legs.
4) Moving-Tunnel Rule: waiting teammates may shuffle left or right so the rolling ball passes cleanly through EVERYONE'S legs to the new back player, who immediately starts the next zigzag dribble!
pe-00098:
1) Line up 5 sport-stacking cups overhanging the edge of your desk ('Ground' = cup upside-down; 'Sky' = cup right-side-up).
2) Stages 1 & 2 (Right Hand): flip Cup 1 with your right hand from Ground to Sky, then flip Cup 2 with your right hand from Sky to Ground.
3) Stages 3 & 4 (Left Hand): flip Cup 3 with your left hand from Ground to Sky, then flip Cup 4 with your left hand from Sky to Ground.
4) Stage 5 (Double Simultaneous Flip): flip 2 cups at the exact same time with both hands so BOTH land standing upright on the same try, then sit down and call finish!
pe-00099:
1) In pairs, the Tagger walks slowly in front while the Runner follows about 2 paces (2 meters) behind, moving away from the safe home line (marked with hoops/cones).
2) The Tagger may fake by glancing over their shoulder; if the Runner panics and runs before the Tagger fully turns around, the Runner loses the round.
3) At any moment of their choosing, the Tagger spins 180 degrees around to chase the Runner!
4) The Runner pivots and sprints back to the safe home line—scoring 1 point if they reach safety untagged, then partners switch roles.
pe-00100:
1) Stage 1 (All-vs-All Beanbag Slide Tag): players slide beanbags flat across the gym floor to hit classmates' feet (throwing in the air never counts); after being hit 3 times, return your beanbag to the bucket.
2) Stage 2 (Team Beanbag Slide Dodgeball): two teams face off across a center line, crouching low to slide beanbags across the floor at opponents' feet.
3) Sole-Trap 'Catch' Rule: if a sliding beanbag hits your foot, you are out—EXCEPT if you lift your toes and trap/stop the sliding beanbag cleanly underneath the sole of your shoe, which counts as a 'catch' (safe + your ball)!
4) If you try to sole-trap a beanbag and it deflects off your foot, you are out; add 2–4 beanbags as players get better.
pe-00101: Warm up with leapfrog and arm-support jumps. Students practice straddle vaults or forward rolls on the vaulting box while a partner stands inside a designated observation hula hoop next to the landing mat to give one specific tip before swapping via high-five. When switching from rotational skills to support vaults, students first perform bunny hops across a transition mat.
pe-00102: Groups rotate every 4 minutes through 4 Mat Adventure Worlds: (1) Wall-Climb World (inverted lateral wall-walks), (2) Winding Slope World (log and tucked rolls down a springboard ramp), (3) River-Jump World (two-hand support lateral jumps over mats/elastic cords), and (4) Rocker & Animal Walk World. When every group member clears a world, the team earns a gold coin sticker.
pe-00103: Students practice cartwheels along a blue tape line on the mat while partners check 7 key form points (straight lunge, torso twist, locked elbows, high leg swing). Students then choose tiered stations: cartwheeling over stacked mini-mats/vault boxes or clearing a bell-rigged elastic cord ('Chiriri Machine') without ringing the bell.
pe-00104: After a rhythm-based 'Red Light, Green Light' warm-up, students learn the cultural story behind the Russian folk dance 'Korobushka.' Forming concentric inner and outer circles facing partners with joined hands, students perform the '3 walks + hop forward and back' step, 3-step turns, and smooth partner rotations around the circle.
pe-00105: After a circle warm-up, the teacher plays a continuous 4-song medley featuring contrasting tempos and moods. Students improvise full-body movements—shifting their core forward/back, changing high/low levels, robot moves, and back-to-back partner grooves—finishing with an interactive 'dance-along exchange' rather than a seated recital.
pe-00106: Students rotate on musical cues through 4 stations: (1) Frog-Jump Course (bunny-hop approach over low boxes), (2) 'Ton-Ton' Takeoff Course (two-foot board punch and two-hand box mount), (3) Rainbow Jump Course (step up tiered boxes and stick a two-foot landing in target color zones), and (4) Balance-Beam Side-Hops.
pe-00107: Six progressive indoor ball games: (1) Circle Pass (bounce/toss your ball straight up on cue and step laterally to catch your neighbor's ball), (2) Kick Dodge (inner players dribble their own ball while dodging kicked balls from outside), (3) Dango Train (walk in a line holding balls between backs and bellies with no hands), (4) Dribble Red-Light Green-Light, (5) Line Ball Tag, and (6) Pass & Duck (neighbors on both sides of the receiver must immediately duck).
pe-00108: A 1v1 invasion lead-up drill in 3 stages: (1) Line Break—defender moves only along the line between 2 cones while the attacker uses left/right feints to cross untouched; (2) Area Break—4 cones form a box where the defender moves freely in any direction; (3) Tail-Tag Break—attacker wears a waist tail and must cross the box without losing the tail.
pe-00109: Every player dribbles a ball with their feet inside a coned square, shielding their own ball while trying to kick others' balls out of bounds. Kicking an opponent's ball out earns +1 point; having your own ball go out (including self-dribble errors) costs -1 point and you immediately re-enter. Progress to a 2-team cumulative score battle.
pe-00110: Two complementary games that cure 'bee-hive' ball crowding: In Game 1, the tagger can only tag the player holding the ball (who cannot walk), forcing quick, flat passes to open teammates before the tagger arrives. In Game 2, the passing team cannot walk with the ball and must string quick passes to corner and tag a fleeing runner with the ball.
pe-00111: Five indoor games: (1) 3x3 Cone Bingo Relay, (2) 9-Square Simultaneous Jump Tag, (3) 4x4 Color-Sorting Relay (each runner swaps 1 pair of cones until all 4 columns match by color), (4) Hand-in-Hand Chain Relay (1st runner picks up 2nd, then 3rd, running together around the cone), and (5) Color Word Fake-Out Cone Grab.
pe-00112: Set up a 3x3 (9 rings) or 4x4 (16 rings) floor grid. Teams relay one by one to place 3 (or 4) colored cones, then reposition existing cones until they complete a straight line. Runners must process the board state while sprinting to decide whether to block an opponent's threat or build their own line.
pe-00113: Divide the class into small teams of 3-4 players and assign a moderately challenging jump-rope skill (such as criss-cross 'Ayatobi' or double-unders). On the start signal, all #1 jumpers begin jumping simultaneously. The instant #1 catches their rope, #2 starts jumping immediately, continuing through #3 and the #4 anchor. The last team still jumping wins.
pe-00114: A 5-stage shuttle relay where students travel to the turnaround line using a specific bodyweight support movement and sprint back upright: (1) High-arm skipping, (2) High-hip bear crawl (weight on hands), (3) High-hip crab/spider walk, (4) Bunny hops (feet landing beside hands), and (5) Frog jumps (pushing off the floor with hands and lifting the head).
pe-00115: Five fast indoor warm-ups: (1) Touch Dash (rear partner taps front partner's hands to trigger an instant sprint chase), (2) Feint Marker Tag (shadow the leader's marker touches without getting tagged), (3) 3-on-1 Four-Marker Guard (3 defenders shift across 4 floor spots to block 1 tagger from stepping on an open spot), (4) Number-Bib Mental Math Relay, and (5) Win-White / Lose-Red RPS Marker Sprint.
pe-00116: Divide the gym into 4 mini fields so 8 small teams play simultaneously with zero long batting lines. Each field has a large cone tee and a single mat base at the opposite end. Batters hit the foam ball off the cone and sprint to the mat base to score 1 run before being tagged, forced out at the mat, or caught on the fly. Hitting a ball into another quadrant's field is an automatic out.
pe-00117: Ten foundational K-2 games: (1) Musical Hoop Twister ('Left foot in green hoop!'), (2) Plants vs. Animals Noodle Tag, (3) Lily-Pad Color-Pattern Memory Run, (4) Center Bucket Ball Relay, (5) Escaped Zoo-Animal Tag, (6) Secret 3-Treasure Relay, (7) Snowflakes (white ball freeze) & Suns (yellow ball melt) Tag, (8) Hidden Beanbag Cone Scavenger Hunt, (9) Target-Roll Toy Collector, and (10) Cooperative Shrinking Hoop Islands.
pe-00118: Four color teams start in 4 corner jails on a basketball court with two live balls: a Throwing Ball (throw only, no walking with ball) and a Kicking Ball (kick only, touching with hands in play sends you to jail). Hit players enter any corner jail and may switch jails freely. Players escape jail in 3 ways: (1) tag a live player who backs too close to jail, (2) throw a loose Throwing Ball from jail to hit a live player, or (3) pick up the Kicking Ball ('Jailbreak Ball') when it rolls into a jail and make a basketball shot to free everyone in that jail.
pe-00119: Two teams (Red flags vs. Yellow flags) start in the 4 corners of the gym, with a 4-exercise fitness circuit posted on the whiteboard (10 jumping jacks, 10 squat jumps, 10 burpees, 10 plank up-downs). On the whistle, teams battle to pull the opposing team's waist flags. Any player who loses their flag returns to their home corner to cycle through the fitness routine until one team loses all its flags.
pe-00120: Students line up on the baseline while one center tagger yells 'Blob Tag!' to trigger a cross-gym run. Tagged players link hands with the tagger to form a 2-player, then 3-player Blob. As soon as a Blob reaches 4 players, it splits into two 2-player Blobs, continuing end-to-end waves until everyone is caught.
pe-00121: Two small groups of 3-4 players stand opposite each other and take turns throwing a flying disc to the other group. Catching the disc directly scores 0 points; instead, the first receiver must tip the disc up into the air for a teammate to catch before it hits the ground. A finger/hand tip scores 1 point, a knee/foot tip scores 2 points, and a head tip scores 3 points (consecutive tips add together).
pe-00122: Relay teams of 3-5 line up behind a baseline with a row of hula hoops placed in front of each team and a far-end cone opposite each row. Players roll a foam ball so it stops inside one of their hoops to capture that hoop. Once a team captures all of its own hoops, it moves to the far-end cones to roll from the opposite side and steal remaining hoops from other teams.
pe-00123: Four bowling variations: (1) Obstacle Bowling (curve or bank shots around a standing mat barrier), (2) Blindfold Partner-Coached Bowling (teammates guide the blindfolded bowler's alignment while the bowler focuses on kinesthetic arm swing), (3) Scooter Bowling, and (4) Team Bowl (two teams on opposite halves with 1 pin and 1 goalie each, rolling multiple balls to knock down the opponent's pin).
pe-00124: Set up 6 trick-shot stations around the gym: (1) Mini-Parachute Team Launch into a basketball hoop, (2) Hockey Sniper through a narrow barrier gap, (3) Rainbow/Backward Basketball Bank Shot, (4) Ping-Pong Bounce into Wall Cups, (5) Long Football Bin Toss, and (6) Flying-Disc Pin Knockdown on a table. Groups then invent and film their own custom trick-shot challenge.
pe-00125: Students imagine a giant protective 'bubble' around their body and practice steering into open space inside the boundary line without popping anyone's bubble. In a call-and-response ('I see!' / 'What do you see?'), the teacher prompts imaginative locomotor scenarios—walking a pet, galloping on a horse, swimming, ice skating, imaginary basketball, and tiptoeing past a sleeping monster—while music plays, freezing on the stop cue.
pe-00126: Four teams are each assigned one card suit (Diamonds, Clubs, Hearts, Spades) while a full deck of cards (plus 2 '+1' Jokers) is spread face-down across the gym floor. Runners sprint out one at a time and may flip over only ONE card: if it matches their team's suit (or is a Joker), they bring it back; if not, they secretly turn it face-down again and tag the next runner.
pe-00127: Set up 4 corner cones and a 5-minute timer with upbeat music. The entire class runs or power-walks laps around the perimeter for 5 minutes while the teacher clicks a tally counter every time any student completes a lap. Divide total laps by the number of students present to post the 'Average Laps per Student' on a grade-level leaderboard.
pe-00128: Part 1 (Mixer): Pairs take turns flipping a cone (up to 10 tries total). Whoever lands it upright first wins; both players exchange a fist-bump/high-five saying 'Good game!', the loser jogs 1 perimeter lap, and both find new partners. Part 2 (Relay): Teams sprint out one by one to flip a line of 4 small cones and 1 final jumbo cone upright—strictly 1 flip attempt per turn before sprinting back to tag the next runner.
pe-00129: Taggers fold a round poly spot in half like a taco shell with a rubber chicken (or beanbag/fish) tucked inside and chase classmates. When a runner is tagged, the tagger drops the poly spot and chicken on the floor; the newly tagged player must pick up both pieces, fold them back into a 'Chicken Taco,' and continue tagging for a 2-minute round.
pe-00130: Every student dribbles a basketball continuously inside the court, including the taggers, who dribble with one hand while holding a half-noodle in the other. When tagged, a player freezes with feet wide apart and their basketball held overhead. A teammate rescues them by dribbling over and rolling their basketball through the frozen player's legs (rescuers have safe immunity while rolling).
pe-00131: One 'Farmer' tagger pretends to sleep in the center while all 'Turkeys' gather close and flap their wings. Turkeys chant 'Wobble, wobble, gobble, gobble!' three times: first in a whisper, second in a normal voice, and third at a loud shout. On the third shout, the Farmer wakes up and has 10 seconds to tag as many Turkeys as possible. All tagged players become sleeping Farmers for the next 10-second round until one Turkey remains.
pe-00132: Every student is simultaneously a tagger and a dodger in open space. When you tap someone and call 'Tip!', they sit down on the spot. Seated players watch the person who tagged them—as soon as their tagger gets tagged by someone else, the seated player stands right back up into the game. Simultaneous tags are settled by rock-paper-scissors.
pe-00133: Five versatile warm-ups: (1) 4-Zone Tag (4 taggers restricted to their own quadrant while runners cross freely), (2) Kangaroos & Crocodiles (centerline reaction chase with fitness cues), (3) Court-Line Call Sprint, (4) Grab the Apple (pairs react to posture cues before grabbing or foot-trapping a ball on a cone when 'Ball!' is called), and (5) Speed Chasers (10-second blitz where 1-2 chasers enter a square to tag dodgers).
pe-00134: Players control their own hockey ball, basketball, or soccer ball inside a coned ring while trying to knock opponents' balls out as the boundary gradually shrinks. Variation 1 (Tackler Time Trial): 2-3 ball-less tacklers try to clear all balls as fast as possible. Variation 2 (Partner Pass Mode): pairs share 1 ball with 5 lives, passing between each other to evade knockouts.
pe-00135: Runners hold a beanbag ('egg') on the start line while taggers with short foam noodles guard the middle. When their color or group is called, runners sprint to the finish line to score 1 point. Any runner tagged along the way stops on the spot and performs 3 self-toss-and-catches (or toss-clap-catches) with their beanbag to revive and finish the run.
pe-00136: When tagged by a foam-noodle tagger, players squat and hug their knees on the spot as an 'Egg.' Two Eggs can play rock-paper-scissors: the winner evolves into a 'Duck' (moving via duck-walk) while the loser stays an Egg. Two Ducks then duck-walk to each other and play RPS—the winner evolves back into a human runner and the loser returns to an Egg.
pe-00137: Students stand at their spot cones in a circle in complete silence while passing 1, then 2 foam balls across the circle. Anyone who speaks, drops a catchable pass, or throws a second ball to someone already holding a ball jogs one lap around the outside of the circle and re-enters immediately. Progress to right-hand-only (left hand behind back) and left-hand-only rounds.
pe-00138: Each group places 2 hula hoops touching end-to-end like a snowman in front of their serving line. Servers aim to land the shuttlecock inside the FAR hoop. Each time a serve lands inside the far hoop, the retriever moves the front hoop over the far hoop to advance the target one hoop-length farther away, then brings the shuttlecock back to the line for continuous rotation.
pe-00139: On a 3x3 floor grid, runners start in separate squares while 1 tagger starts on the edge. On every '1, 2, 3!' chant, everyone jumps one square in any direction (the tagger may feint and stay in the same square). If a runner lands in the same square as the tagger—or if two runners land in the same square ('1 Household, 1 Home' rule)—they are out. Time how many seconds each squad survives.
pe-00140: Players from two teams kangaroo-jump (two feet together) through a line of hula hoops to meet in the middle for rock-paper-scissors. The RPS winner grabs a point cone and kangaroo-jumps back across their safe line, while the RPS loser grabs a foam ball and throws from the center to hit the fleeing winner below the waist. If hit, the runner performs a quick fitness task; if missed, the thrower performs it.
pe-00141: The teacher holds 1 dodgeball in front of the class while students bounce on the balls of their feet. Students react instantly to the teacher's ball cues: (1) side throw motion = dodge the opposite way, (2) overhead lift = duck low, (3) floor bounce = jump wide, (4) switching the ball from one hand to the other = freeze still, and (5) a real two-hand toss to a student = catch and throw back.
pe-00142: Starts with 1 'Zombie' tagger who must walk with both arms stretched straight out in front. Runners also move by speed-walking or hopping inside the boundary lines. Anyone tagged—or anyone who steps out of bounds—immediately stretches both arms forward and joins the growing Zombie horde until only 3-5 survivors remain.
pe-00143: Players from both teams duck-walk ('Lilliput walk') to the centerline and play rock-paper-scissors. The winner grabs a scoring cone and duck-walks back toward their safe line while the loser grabs a foam ball and rolls/throws low from a crouched position to tag the fleeing player before they cross the line.
pe-00144: A zero-running classroom tag game: whenever the tagger calls 'One Step!' (or 'Two Steps!'), both the tagger and all dodgers take strictly 1 (or 2) giant steps simultaneously and freeze in balance. If the tagger can reach and tap a player with a foam noodle from their landing spot, roles switch (after nearby players take 1 buffer step back).
pe-00145: Form an octagonal Gaga pit in the classroom or gym using folding boards, milk crates, or tipped chairs. Players start touching the wall; the teacher drops the ball in for 3 bounces ('Ga-Ga-Ball!') with a 5-second no-out grace period. Players may only strike or roll the ball with an open palm (no catching/throwing and no double-touches) to hit opponents below the knee.
pe-00146: Three or four 'Hunters' wear pinnies and carry soft foam balls, while the rest of the class are 'Animals' with 4 hula-hoop shelters spread on the floor. Hunters run and throw foam balls to hit Animals below the waist. Hit Animals freeze with both arms out as a 'Tree' until 2 different teammates each tap one arm down to revive them. One Animal may rest safe inside a hoop shelter until another Animal runs up and yells 'Out!', forcing the resting player to flee to a different hoop.
pe-00147: Two teams roam the entire court with 6 foam balls in play and a coned Base/Jail zone at each end. Players holding a ball cannot walk and must pass to moving teammates to hit opponents. Hit players sit inside the opponent's Base/Jail and revive by catching a no-bounce air pass from a live teammate, raising one hand ('twinkle hand') while jogging outside the court back to their home base.
pe-00148: Simplifies kickball by replacing 4 bases with a Home line and a Safe Zone line 7m (10 paces) away. The pitcher rolls the ball; the kicker kicks it and runs to the Safe Zone, where multiple runners may wait before sprinting back across Home for 1 point each. Fielders get runners out by catching fly balls, tagging runners, or throwing the soft ball to hit runners below the waist between lines. All players kick each inning.
pe-00149: In a 3v3 or 4v4 coned square with 1 ball and man-to-man defense, the attacking team passes the ball with no dribbling allowed. Every completed pass adds 1 point, and the entire team must shout the cumulative count aloud ('1, 2, 3...'). Turnovers switch possession, and when a team regains the ball, they resume counting from their previous score until one team reaches 20 total passes.
pe-00150: Safe zones are marked at both ends of the gym with 1 mobile tagger in the center. On each whistle turn, runners sprint from one safe zone to the other. Any runner tagged freezes permanently on that exact floor spot as a 'Sea Anemone.' On subsequent turns, Sea Anemones must keep both feet planted on their spot while waving their arms like tentacles to tag passing runners alongside the mobile tagger.
pe-00151: Played 3v3 (4-5 players per team rotating on each point) using a soft 50-100g volleyball. Teams progress across Stage 1 (Catch Volleyball where the 2nd player catches and tosses a set), Stage 2 (One-Bounce allowed), and Stage 3 (No-Bounce 3-touch Soft Volleyball), starting rallies with an underhand rainbow toss serve and self-officiating.
pe-00152: Students run a 15-20m (or 7-step) rhythmic approach, quickening the final 3 steps ('ta-ta-tan!') to take off from a wide 30-50cm zone. Leading with their belly button over an elastic cord or mini-hurdle, they tuck knees in flight and land on both feet in a forward-leaning 'U' posture.
pe-00153: Students march to a tambourine beat, form groups on whistle counts, link into a Rock-Paper-Scissors Cargo Train, and wind into a giant spiral. Seated in a circle, they perform back-tap and shampoo massages, a circle domino lean, giraffe partner stretches, and finish with a cooperative group balloon keep-up rally.
pe-00154: Starts with facial/full-body rhythm warm-ups and partner mirror dancing, followed by 3-step rock/seaweed rolls, 'Pumpkin Seed to Watermelon' growth RPS, 'Knock-Knock Character Transform', and an 'Animal Land Adventure' where students fly like airplanes and embody heavy elephants, tiny mice, crabs, octopuses, and sprinting cheetahs.
pe-00155: Students rotate through 6 'Tetsubo Land' stations with a skill passport: (1) Jump-support & swing-back dismount, (2) Swallow front-support hold, (3) Pillbug, Roast-Pork & Bat hang (with Bat RPS), (4) Leg-through circle & forward roll dismount, (5) Futon-fold hang & swing, and (6) Monkey 4-limb swing plus 2-move combinations.
pe-00156: Includes feint-step evasion tag, a cooperative group balloon keep-up rally using hands, feet, and heads, partner post-exercise relaxation massage and breathing, synchronized circle hand-linked stand-ups, and cooperative long-rope jumping while passing a ball.
pe-00157: Students rotate through 4 fitness pillars: (1) Agility/Coordination (jumping a short rope while entering a turning long rope + quick-feet drills), (2) Muscular Strength (partner wheelbarrow walk aiming to cross Line 1 in <=3 hand-steps, Line 2 in <=5 steps, Line 3 in <=7 steps), (3) Flexibility (heel-down calf/Achilles stretch), and (4) Endurance (5-minute continuous jump rope).
pe-00158: After synchronized partner warm-ups on the bar, students design and perform a smooth 3-skill routine combining a Mount (pullover or single-leg swing-up), a Circle skill (forward/backward hip circle or knee circle), and a Dismount (single-foot swing-off landing) without pausing between moves.
pe-00159: A 10-part indoor movement circuit: (1) Cue-inhibition hand game, (2) Animal walks tag (inchworm, bear, alligator, spider, otter), (3) Radish pull, (4) Partner jump-over & crawl-under race, (5) 16-beat shoulder rhythm song, (6) Color association touch, (7) Tissue Belly Dash (sprint fast enough that a tissue stays flat on your stomach without hands), (8) Tissue drop catch, (9) Knotted-towel cone knockdown, and (10) Towel-ball circle dodgeball.
pe-00160: Seven quick coordination warm-ups: (1) Partner back-to-back synchronized stand-up, (2) Jump-over & crawl-under switch, (3) Marionette cross-limb jump punch, (4) Rolling ball dodge jumps, (5) 'Fish Flip' prone core hold resistance, (6) Color-call ball drop catch, and (7) Pat-head/rub-belly hand switch ('Tonton-Surisuri').
pe-00161: Five indoor games: (1) 4-Line Ball Color-Swap Relay, (2) Ring-Ball 3x3 Bingo Relay, (3) 4-Team Center Ball Raid (first team to collect 3 balls into their hoop wins), (4) 3v1 Walk-Only 4-Cone Guard, and (5) Kick-Tunnel Relay (roll/kick the ball through teammates' wide legs and sprint to the front to receive it).
pe-00162: Four relay variations where strategy beats raw speed: (1) 1-Swap Marker Color-Sort Relay (each runner swaps two markers in a vertical line until all colors are grouped), (2) 3-Marker Bingo Relay, (3) Student-Designed Zigzag & Jump Course Relay, and (4) Multi-Layer Bib Relay (putting on and passing layered pinnies at the exchange zone).
pe-00163: Five sprint menus: (1) Multi-Direction Dash (forward, lateral, backward, 360-spin start, mid-run 180-turn), (2) Visual/Opposite Cue Reaction Dash, (3) Body-Part Hold Dash (running with hands on head, belly, or hips before swinging arms freely to feel how arm drive powers sprinting), (4) 1-Foot Handicap Pair Dash (winner moves 1 shoe-length back each race), and (5) Whistle Cutback Dash.
pe-00164: Features innovative Japanese PE tag games including: (1) Lion & Rabbit prone/seated reaction chase, (2) Pair-Link Slice Tag, (3) Cone-Touch Moving Safe-Zone Tag, (4) 'Mamoru-kun' (3 linked teammates rotate as a human shield to protect 1 designated teammate from a solo tagger), and (5) Color Hoop & Cone-Flip Tag.
