pe-00165: Ten fast 30-60 second tag games: (1) Increase Tag, (2) RPS Increase Tag, (3) 4-Player Split Linked Tag, (4) Clap Freeze Tag, (5) Leg-Tunnel Freeze Tag, (6) Leapfrog Freeze Tag, (7) 'Outlet!' Arm-Plug Freeze Tag, (8) 'Microwave Ding!' 2-Player Hug-Circle Rescue Tag, (9) Banana Peel Tag, and (10) Eyes-Closed Secret Tagger ('Dokidoki Tag').
pe-00166: Uses an inner fielding cone diamond inside an outer base-hoop diamond across 3 builds: Build 1 (counter-clockwise base runner vs clockwise fielding pass relay), Build 2 (throw-in fielding where all fielders must claim a Stop Spot poly spot and return the ball to the center hoop to freeze runners), and Build 3 (teammate-pitched batting with 4 attempts; 4 misses = automatic walk to 1st base).
pe-00167: Players stand in a large circle, each guarding a personal goal gate between two cones. Using open-palm floor strikes only (no catching or kicking), players hit the ball across the circle to score through opponents' cone gates. Conceding a goal means jogging one lap around the outside of the circle and rejoining immediately.
pe-00168: The entire class starts in the kicking line while the teacher starts as the lone pitcher/fielder. Any kicker who fouls, misses a fair pitch, or gets caught/tagged/forced out immediately joins the fielding team, making defense tougher each turn until one final survivor remains.
pe-00169: Cones divide the gym into 4 quadrants for 4 teams. When hit below the waist by a foam ball, you immediately join the quadrant team that hit you. Once a quadrant loses its last player, the dividing cones are removed so the winning team claims half the gym until one quadrant absorbs everyone.
pe-00170: Two teams line up 5-6 bowling pins or tall cones along their backline behind a marked no-guard zone. Staying on their half of the gym, players roll, underhand toss, or overhand throw foam balls to knock down all opposing pins first.
pe-00171: Every student rides a scooter board (seated or kneeling) while 2-3 penny-wearing taggers chase. When tagged, a player spins 5 times in place on their scooter (or performs 5 jumping jacks) and immediately re-enters the game.
pe-00172: Students learn the Frisbee grip ('Thumb on top, fingers in the scoop'), 4-step backhand cue ('Point shoulder, Cross body, Step, Flick wrist'), and 'Crab Claws / Alligator Catch', then rotate through 4 skill stations (partner catch, hula-hoop target rings, cone knockdown, and leading passes).
pe-00173: Students rotate through 6 numbered perimeter skill stations (jump rope, hula hoops, target toss, balance, agility). When music plays, students practice; when music stops, they clean up equipment within 5 seconds, sit, and point their finger toward the next numbered cone before rotating on the whistle.
pe-00174: Lower-grade students rotate through 4 striking implement stations (foam paddle, bowling pin, frisbee, foam noodle) aiming for 50 consecutive upward hits. Next, they keep one foot 'glued' to a poly spot for 25 controlled hits before partnering up for an over-the-line balloon rally.
pe-00175: Runners evade foam-noodle taggers by standing inside floor hula hoops for up to 3 seconds (1 player per hoop; 3 jumping jacks if tagged). Meanwhile, a 'Hula Hoop Master' carries a cone and collects any unoccupied hoops, shrinking the available safe islands over a 2-minute round.
pe-00176: Runners hold an inverted cone like an ice cream cone with a ball balanced on top, weaving through cones and passing it to the next teammate. If the ball drops, the runner must sit down and use only their feet (no hands!) to place the ball back onto the cone before continuing.
pe-00177: Outer-circle attackers pass and throw 2-3 foam balls to knock down 7+ center castle cones guarded by 2-3 Knights. Whenever a Knight catches an incoming throw on the fly without a bounce, they earn the right to stand one fallen castle cone back up.
pe-00178: Two teams line up on opposite endlines with numbered players (1, 2, 3...) and a ball in the center. When the teacher calls one or more numbers, those players sprint to touch the opposite goal and their own goal (or run around the perimeter) before entering the court to battle 1v1, 2v2, or 3v3 in soccer, basketball, or hockey.
pe-00179: Runners line up in one endzone while 2 tippers wait in the middle. When the tippers yell 'Bull Rush!', everyone sprints across to the opposite safe zone. Tagged runners join the middle tippers; in Variation 2, everyone tucks a bib tail into their waistband for non-contact tail-snatching.
pe-00180: The teacher calls 'Cross the river if...' (e.g., wearing red shorts), prompting matching students—and then the rest of the class—to cross to the far endzone while sideline rollers roll small foam balls along the floor to tag feet. Tagged runners join the sideline rollers.
pe-00181: Every player's two hands act as two 'Band-Aids'. On the 1st tag by a Wasp, cover the tagged spot with one hand and keep running; on the 2nd tag, cover with the second hand; on the 3rd tag, visit the 'Waspital' cone zone to complete 10 star jumps or a 20-second single-leg balance to restore both hands.
pe-00182: Designed for classrooms or compact gym zones: inner dodgers stay in a low seated/squat posture and evade exclusively by jumping upwards or ducking in place, while outer throwers pass rapidly and roll or throw soft foam balls low at the feet.
pe-00183: Defenders stand in pyramid rows (e.g., 4 guards in Row 1, 3 in Row 2, 2 in Row 3, and 1 King at the apex). Attackers sprint through each tier by winning Rock-Paper-Scissors; a loss sends the runner jogging back along the outside sideline to start at Row 1 again, while beating the apex King scores 1 team point.
pe-00184: A modern PE adaptation of Korean traditional Tuho: teammates relay to a throwing line and toss foam noodles (safe javelins) or beanbags through upright or floor-arranged hula-hoop targets at tiered distances.
pe-00185: A runner balances a stick vertically on a forward poly spot and releases it on cue while calling the next teammate, who must sprint from the start line and catch the stick before it hits the floor.
pe-00186: A cooperative shuttle-run progression: in Activity 1 (pairs 10m apart) and Activity 2 (4 teammates at the corners of a square), players run inward to high-five (or stack hands for 4 players) and loop around their corner cone 5 times. Faster runners run deeper toward slower teammates' corners so everyone finishes together faster.
pe-00187: Pairs stand 2-3m apart passing a ball back and forth (chest pass, bounce pass, overhead pass) on a single whistle. When the teacher blows a double whistle, whoever holds the ball becomes the chaser and must tag their fleeing partner with the ball before the stop whistle (loser does 5 squat jumps).
pe-00188: Attackers advance toward a single cone placed 2-3m in front of the defensive line. Once an attacker touches the cone, all defenders may chase freely (bringing the cone home scores 1 point). However, if a defender rushes out BEFORE the cone is touched and fails to tag any attacker, that defender is eliminated! Teams get 3 cone-grab attempts per inning.
pe-00189: Two challengers meet at center court for Rock-Paper-Scissors. The winner grabs a scoring cone and sprints for their home line, while the loser sprints to grab a foam dodgeball resting on a tee-cone and throws it to tag the runner before they cross home safe.
pe-00190: Four cones are placed in a line (Team A Far Cone - Team A Start - Team B Start - Team B Far Cone). Runners sprint to the opposing team's start cone and play full-body RPS: winners turn around immediately for a short return, while losers must run all the way around the far back cone before tagging their next teammate.
pe-00191: Starts by tossing 3 soft dodgeballs into the air for an all-vs-all game. Ball holders may take up to 3 steps before throwing. Hit players sit in order on the sideline bench; whenever any player on the court catches a thrown ball in the air, the first player in the bench queue re-enters the game.
pe-00192: With heads down, the teacher secretly taps 3 Angels, then announces 2 Zombies and starts a 2-minute timer. Walking only is allowed between desks. Citizens tagged by Zombies sit in place, while Secret Angels discreetly tap seated Citizens to revive them without revealing their identity to the Zombies. If 10+ Citizens survive 2 minutes, Citizens win.
pe-00193: A hunter holding a foam stick starts in a center hoop while squirrels stand on perimeter poly spots holding 1 beanbag ('acorn') each. On 'Hunter!', squirrels dash to new spots. If tagged, a squirrel leaves their acorn on a spot and steps out; whenever an active squirrel collects 3 acorns and yells 'Three!', all eliminated classmates revive at once.
pe-00194: In trios with 3 hula hoops, jumper #1 performs two-foot standing broad jumps from hoop to hoop while teammates #2 and #3 continuously pick up the rear hoop and place it ahead to build a stepping-stone bridge to the turnaround cone and back.
pe-00195: Players slide rubber rings or poly spots along the floor toward a target floor line. In Round 1, closest to the line wins; in Round 2 ('Don't Cross the Line!'), any ring that slides completely past the target line is eliminated (0 points), rewarding precise force control.
pe-00196: When tagged, players freeze in a designated yoga balance pose (Tree pose, Airplane scale, or seated V-sit Boat pose). To rescue a frozen classmate, a teammate must stand or sit face-to-face and hold the exact same yoga pose together for 3 counts.
pe-00197: Students play Rock-Paper-Scissors against the teacher or a partner with three active outcomes every round: Winners perform a celebration dance (e.g., Floss or rhythm swing), Ties perform 5 squats, and Losers perform 5-10 jumping jacks or burpees before immediately finding a new partner.
pe-00198: In trios at a desk (1 caller, 2 players with hands behind backs): Game 1 (caller places a colored tall cone; first player to cap it with the matching disc cone scores), Game 2 (caller drops 1 or 2 disc cones; players grab the matching tall cones), and Game 3 (arrange 3 tall cones to match the caller's 3-color sequence).
pe-00199: Students form a large circle and roll a giant stability ball across to tag center dodgers across 3 modes: (1) Survive for 60 seconds, (2) Class Cooperative Goal (add everyone's survival seconds together to beat a class target), and (3) Team Total Survival Time comparison.
pe-00200: Players gather around a spinning finger pointer on the floor while a bouncy foam ball sits on a cone a few meters away. Whoever the pointer lands on sprints to grab the ball from the cone while everyone else scatters. Vary rounds between hand-throwing, foot-kicking, and moving the ball's cone into the escape path.
pe-00201:
1) Mark a rectangular court with 2m endzones at both ends using 8 cones; two teams line up on their start lines.
2) The team losing Rock-Paper-Scissors throws the soft ball deep to the opposing team to start.
3) Players cannot run or dribble with the ball and must pass within 5 seconds; catching a pass inside the opponent's endzone scores 1 point.
4) Any incomplete pass, deflection, interception, or out-of-bounds turnovers possession immediately, and teams swap endzones after each score.
pe-00202:
1) Divide a rectangular court in half; place 6 cones on spot markers along each endline and 2 hula-hoop prisons in the middle of each half.
2) Players invade the opponent's half to grab 1 endline cone and carry it back outside the sideline to place between cones on their own endline.
3) Players tagged in enemy territory go to either of the 2 hula-hoop prisons; a teammate's tag frees everyone in that hoop.
4) Freed players and cone-carriers wave both hands ('twinkle hands') for safe passage home; the team with more cones when time expires wins.
pe-00203:
1) Place 4 corner cones around the court and scatter spot markers (2/3 of class size) inside as 1-person safe zones; each student draws a secret name slip.
2) Chase and tag the target on your slip, reveal the slip, and play full-body Rock-Paper-Scissors; players on a spot marker are safe until someone calls 'Vacate!' to take the spot.
3) If the chaser wins RPS, the target is out, hands over their name slip, and removes 1 spot marker to sit on outside while the chaser hunts the new target.
4) If the runner wins RPS, the chaser must touch one of the 4 outer cones before resuming; the game ends when all spot markers are removed.
pe-00204:
1) Arrange 10 cones in a W/M zigzag pattern with 2 waiting spot markers set safely behind opposite starting cones.
2) Stage 1 (Solo Time Trial): start seated with left fingers touching the start cone, weave left and right around all cones, and return to touch the start cone to beat your personal time.
3) Stage 2 (Team Pursuit Relay): two 4-player teams start at opposite ends and run full zigzag laps, tagging the next teammate.
4) Waiting runners stay on the back spot marker until the opposing runner passes; the first team to finish 12 laps (3 per runner) or overtake the opponent wins.
pe-00205:
1) Arrange 25 disc cones in a 5×5 grid in the field and set separate offensive and defensive home bases on the right and left.
2) Play 9v9 all-batter innings; the batter throws a flying disc into fair territory, grabs 1 or more disc cones from the grid, and runs to offensive home base.
3) Fielders score an out by catching the disc in the air or relaying/running a grounded disc to defensive home base before the runner returns.
4) Safe runners score 1 point per cone retrieved (cones are returned if out); play 2 innings and total the points.
pe-00206:
1) Sit in a large circle on the classroom floor; attackers sit around the outside with 1–2 plastic rings while dodgers stand inside.
2) Attackers slide the rings flat across the floor without lifting them; dodgers jump or sidestep so the ring does not touch their feet.
3) Mode 1 (Group Time Trial): each small group enters the circle and times how long they survive up to 1 minute.
4) Mode 2 (Two-Team Point Battle): play 2-minute halves with 2 rings; hit dodgers step out, do 5 squats, add 1 point to the opponent's scoreboard, and re-enter.
pe-00207:
1) Form teams of 4–6 in a single file with backs to the direction of travel; Player 1 holds a ball.
2) On the signal, pass the ball backward overhead (or between legs/sideways) to the next teammate.
3) As soon as a player passes the ball, they sprint to the end of the line toward the turning cone to receive the ball again.
4) Teams continuously pass and sprint around the turning cone and back to the start line; first team across wins.
pe-00208:
1) Mark a square court; 4 attackers stand around the outside perimeter while 1–2 attackers and all defenders start inside the square.
2) Attackers cannot walk with the ball and must pass quickly between perimeter and inside teammates to corner defenders.
3) An attacker holding the ball scores an out by reaching out and touching ('tagging') a defender with the ball—throwing the ball at a defender does not count.
4) Compare total time to eliminate all defenders or count surviving defenders after a 3-minute round.
pe-00209:
1) Set 2 home bases (trees outdoors or hula hoops indoors) and divide into two 10-player teams, each split into 4 attackers (pinnie tied on arm) and 6 defenders (wearing pinnie).
2) Each team's 4 attackers chase the opponent's 6 defenders and escort tagged defenders to their own base prison.
3) Captured defenders cannot be rescued by their own attackers—only a surviving teammate defender can run in, slap the base, and shout 'Dabanggu!' to free everyone.
4) Play for 5 minutes; the team with more uncaptured defenders at the buzzer wins.
pe-00210:
1) Place spot markers one arm's length apart along the center line with 2 end cones 1m beyond the ends; chasers stand on the spots facing alternating directions.
2) Three runners enter the court at a time and may cross the center line freely, whereas the active chaser cannot cross the center line.
3) To pursue a runner on the other side, the chaser must either run around an end cone or tap the back of a teammate facing that side while shouting 'Kho!' to transfer the chaser role.
4) Tagged runners exit, add 1 point to the chasers' scoreboard, and tag in the next runner; play two 3-minute halves.
pe-00211:
1) Divide a rectangular court in half and mark a treasure vault at each endline with 4 cones filled with equal beanbags.
2) Players sprint into enemy territory to grab 1 beanbag from the vault and return along the outside sideline to deposit it in their own vault.
3) If a defender tags an attacker before they touch a beanbag, both play Rock-Paper-Scissors; the winner immediately continues their action (taking treasure or defending).
4) An attacker who loses RPS steps off the court for 5 jumping jacks before returning to start, while a losing defender does 5 jumping jacks in place; most beanbags after 3 minutes wins.
pe-00212:
1) Mark a square court with cones and a start spot marker; half the class starts inside as runners while the other half lines up at the start spot as taggers.
2) The first tagger sprints into the court and has 20 seconds to tag any runner.
3) If the tagger tags a runner within 20 seconds, the tagger becomes a runner on the court, the tagged runner joins the back of the tagger line, and the next tagger enters immediately.
4) If 20 seconds expire without a tag, the whistle blows, that tagger returns to the back of the line, and the next tagger enters; runners inside at the 5-minute mark win.
pe-00213:
1) Divide into teams of 6 with start and turnaround cones; each team sends 1 defender to stand at the turnaround cone of the team to their right.
2) Practice basic turnaround relays first, then practice looping all the way around the back of your team's line before tagging the next runner.
3) In the main game, each runner sprints to the turnaround cone and plays Rock-Paper-Scissors against the opposing defender stationed there.
4) Winners run straight back while losers do 3 jumping jacks before returning, looping behind their team line to tag the next runner.
pe-00214:
1) Divide the court into a 2×2 grid of 4 squares using cones and spot markers; all runners start in 1 square while taggers divide equally into the 4 squares.
2) Taggers must stay inside their assigned square, while runners move between adjacent squares (diagonal movement is forbidden for both teams).
3) Only taggers holding one of the 2 'tag pinnies' may tag a runner; as runners flee to adjacent squares, taggers pass or toss the tag pinnies to teammates in those squares.
4) Tagged runners step out, add 1 point to the scoreboard, and re-enter any square; play two 3-minute halves.
pe-00215:
1) Form teams of 4 at the start line; at the far end, another team shuffles and lays 9 number cards (1–9) face down in a 3×3 grid.
2) Runners take turns sprinting to flip 1 card; if it is not the next required number (starting from 1), they hold it overhead to show teammates before placing it back face down.
3) If the flipped card matches the next number in sequence, the runner brings it back to the team.
4) Teammates share memory clues to collect cards 1 through 9 in exact order; award 3, 2, and 1 points for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place across rounds.
pe-00216:
1) Place 2 large cones in the center; two teams form human chains holding hands outward from their center cone (the innermost player touches the cone).
2) On the whistle, the outermost player on each team sprints counterclockwise around both human chains for one full lap.
3) When the opponent's runner rounds your team's chain, stretch your hand-chain out wide to make their path longer; when your own runner rounds your chain, shrink shoulder-to-shoulder.
4) The first runner to complete the lap and grab their outermost teammate's hand scores 1 point; if a team's hand-chain breaks at any time, the opponent automatically gets the point.
pe-00217:
1) Select an age-appropriate long rope (4m for grades 1–2, 5m for grades 3–4, 6m for grades 5–6); two turners swing the rope while jumpers line up.
2) Learn entry timing: enter as the rope hits the floor on an 'away' swing, or as the rope rises upward on a 'toward' swing, jumping in the center.
3) Jumpers enter one after another on every turn, jump once, and exit diagonally to trace a continuous figure-8 path around the turners.
4) Compete for the most jumps during a set time (or one song) or race to reach a target jump count first.
pe-00218:
1) Designate a prison area (goalpost outdoors or mat/circle indoors) and boundary lines; divide into Cops and Robbers wearing pinnies.
2) Robbers scatter before the start signal; Cops chase and tag Robbers to put them in prison (stepping out of bounds also counts as captured).
3) Any free Robber who breaks through and tags a jailed teammate frees all Robbers currently in prison.
4) In the advanced variation, a tagged Robber being escorted to prison may bolt and escape if the Cop's grip or attention loosens before reaching prison.
pe-00219:
1) Select taggers holding foam noodles while the rest of the class flees across the gym or field.
2) Before being tagged, a runner can shout 'Banana!' and clasp both hands high overhead to freeze safely in place.
3) To unfreeze a 'Banana', two free runners must come to opposite sides, gently lower the frozen player's left and right arms like peeling a banana, and shout 'One, two, three, unfreeze!'
4) Anyone tagged before calling Banana becomes the new tagger after a 5-second count; taggers win if all runners are frozen.
pe-00220:
1) With 8 or more players, pick 1 Cat (tagger) and 1 Mouse (runner); all other players pair up holding hands scattered around the space.
2) On the signal, the Cat chases the Mouse around the standing pairs.
3) Whenever the Mouse grabs the free hand of a standing pair, the player on the other end of that pair immediately becomes the new Mouse and must flee.
4) The Cat switches targets to chase the new Mouse; if the Cat tags the Mouse, they swap roles and restart after a 5-second count.
pe-00221:
1) Stand several cones in the center of the court surrounded by a 5-step-radius circle that no player may enter.
2) Two teams in pinnies dribble and pass using feet only (no hands) to shoot at the cones inside the center circle.
3) Knocking down a center cone scores 1 point; reset the fallen cone immediately and continue play.
4) Variation: place 1 or 2 cone-goals at each end of a rectangular court (up to 4 total goals) and try to knock down the opponent's cones.
pe-00222:
1) Mark safe zones at both ends of a rectangular court; 1 tagger stands in the center while all runners line up in one safe zone.
2) When the tagger calls 'Start!', runners dash across to the opposite safe zone.
3) Anyone tagged along the way freezes on that exact spot as a 'Sea Anemone'—feet planted, waving both arms left and right to help tag remaining runners.
4) Surviving runners shuttle back and forth on each signal as more Sea Anemones fill the court until everyone is caught.
pe-00223:
1) Set a square or circular court; the attacking team stands around the outside with 1 attacker inside, while the defending team moves inside.
2) Attackers cannot walk while holding the ball and must pass among outside and inside teammates to close in on defenders.
3) Instead of throwing the ball, an attacker holding the ball stretches their arm to touch ('tag') a nearby defender with the ball for an out.
4) Variations: add a second ball or let tagged defenders flip the opponent's scoreboard by 1 point and immediately re-enter for a timed game.
pe-00224:
1) Mark a starting line; in Round 1, runners take 1 big jump forward and turn around while the tagger reaches from the line to tag anyone within reach, then runners must jump back across the line in 1 jump.
2) In Rounds 2 through 10, runners take N jumps out and must return in N jumps, while the tagger chases using (N−1) jumps (one jump fewer than the runners).
3) After Round 10, runners return to the start line following the tagger's creative command (one-foot hopping, duck walk, traffic-light signals, bouncing a shoe like a hot sweet potato, or blindfolded step-estimation).
4) Anyone tagged, failing the command, or falling short of the start line becomes the next tagger.
pe-00225:
1) Mark a rectangular court with 4 narrow 'River' defense zones (2 steps wide) alternating with 3 'Land' safe zones (4 steps wide), placing a basket of blocks/beanbags at the far turn line.
2) Defenders station themselves inside the River zones while attackers start at the home line.
3) Attackers dodge through all 4 Rivers to grab 1 block from the far line and cross back to drop it into the start basket for 1 point.
4) Tagged attackers raise both hands, walk out along the sideline to restart from the start or turn line; swap roles after 5 minutes.
pe-00226:
1) Chasers sit two steps apart along the center line facing alternating sides while 1 active chaser starts at the end of the line.
2) Three runners enter the court at a time (as soon as 1 runner is tagged out, 1 waiting teammate enters to keep 3 active runners).
3) Runners may cross through the center line freely, whereas the active chaser cannot cross the center line and must tap a seated teammate's shoulder to switch chasers.
4) Time how long it takes to tag all runners out or play timed halves, then swap team roles.
pe-00227:
1) Place separate offensive and defensive home-base spot markers near the kicking plate, and set cones 5m (1 point) and 10m (2 points) away along the running line.
2) After kicking the ball, the kicker chooses whether to round the 5m cone or 10m cone and return to offensive home base.
3) Fielders retrieve the ball and pass or run it to step on defensive home base; if the runner returns first, they score 1 or 2 points accordingly.
4) Swap roles after all batters kick; play 3 innings and compare total scores.
pe-00228:
1) Hold 1 badminton racket per student and perform 5 progressive stroke-and-footwork missions to 110–120 BPM music using 4×8-count phrases.
2) Mission 1 (Stationary): practice wrist-snap forehand/backhand and underhand strokes in place on the beat.
3) Missions 2–4 (Stepping): perform One-Step lunge overhead/underhand strokes, Two-Step side-sliding strokes, and Back-Step overhead strokes.
4) Mission 5 (Hairpin Combo & Choreography): combine one-step and two-step net hairpin strokes, then let groups rearrange the 5 missions into a custom routine.
pe-00229:
1) Draw a large circle; the attacking team sits around the outside line while the defending team stands inside.
2) Seated attackers roll a soft ball across the floor (no throwing allowed); hits above the knee do not count.
3) Any defender touched below the knee by a rolling ball is out, steps outside to do jumping jacks, and re-enters while adding 1 point to the attackers' tally.
4) Compare total outs scored in 2–5 minutes, or add a 2nd ball / slide rings or flying discs indoors.
pe-00230:
1) Form groups of 6 numbered 1–6; each player wears 3 same-colored wristbands on their right wrist and stands in a circle.
2) Roll a large foam dice-ball into the center; the player whose number lands on top grabs the ball and shouts 'Freeze!' while the other 5 freeze in place.
3) The attacker takes at most 1 step and throws at a defender, who must dodge or catch without moving their feet.
4) A hit lets the attacker take 1 wristband from the defender, while a clean catch lets the defender take 1 wristband from the attacker; win by collecting the most bands or all 6 colors ('Rainbow Dodgeball').
pe-00231:
1) Set 2 base hoops and divide each team in a 1:2 ratio of Attackers (pinnie tied on arm) to Defenders (wearing pinnie).
2) Attackers chase and tag the opposing team's Defenders, sending tagged Defenders to stand inside the Attacker's base hoop.
3) Only free teammate Defenders (not Attackers) can sprint to the opponent's base, tag the prisoners, and shout 'Dabanggu!' to release them all.
4) After 5 minutes, the team with more free Defenders wins; for small groups, use 1 center base with 1 base-guard tagger and 1 chaser tagger.
pe-00232:
1) On a small square or circle court, 2 players start outside as throwers and 1 player starts inside as the dodger.
2) The 2 outside throwers may pass the ball overhead (above shoulder height) up to 3 times maximum before attacking.
3) Any throw below shoulder height aimed at the inside player counts as an attack; the inside player faces the ball at all times to dodge or catch it.
4) Whenever the inside player is hit or catches an attack cleanly, they swap places with the thrower.
pe-00233:
1) Set up 1.5L plastic bottle targets at 10m and a large basket at 30m in the gym or field.
2) Stage 1 (10m Target Knockdown): teams take turns throwing flying discs to knock down the most bottles (add obstacles in between to increase difficulty).
3) Stage 2 (30m Long-Range Basket): alternate throws at a large basket 30m away; first team to land a disc inside wins.
4) Stage 3 (10-Pin Disc Bowling): arrange 10 plastic bottles in a bowling triangle and compete to knock down the most pins.
pe-00234:
1) Each student holds a flying disc in an open space and attempts 5 consecutive skill challenges.
2) Stages 1–3: (1) balance the disc on your head while turning 360° → (2) spin the disc on one finger for 5 seconds → (3) toss the disc behind your back and catch it in front.
3) Stages 4–5: (4) toss the disc high, spin 360°, and catch it → (5) throw the disc into a basketball hoop.
4) Team Relay Variation: teams of 5 complete Stages 1 to 5 in relay order, restarting from Stage 1 if a teammate misses.
pe-00235:
1) Set up a compact court (3 steps long by 6 steps wide on each side of a badminton or volleyball net) using disc cones.
2) 1v1 Singles: serve underhand from behind the endline; return the ball over the net in 1 touch (either on the fly or after 1 bounce) to play to 5 points.
3) 2v2 Doubles: blocking at the net is allowed, and both teammates must touch the ball (exactly 2 touches per side) before sending it over.
4) Cooperative Rally Mode: pairs work together across the net to achieve the highest consecutive rally count.
pe-00236:
1) Use any straight floor line and upbeat music to learn 8 rhythm jump steps in 8-count sets.
2) Steps 1–4: (1) alternating running jumps → (2) 4× right/left one-foot hops → (3) straddle jumps over the line → (4) side-to-side zigzag line jumps.
3) Steps 5–8: (5) squat-and-jump straddles → (6) two hops + cross-line squat jump → (7) 180° turn straddle jumps → (8) mid-air heel-clap jumps.
4) Compete in 3-player endurance survival (continuous 8-step combos) or 4-player shuttle relays advancing along a floor line while performing all 8 steps.
pe-00237:
1) Place 1 target hula hoop in the center, surrounded by individual spot markers and an outer running track marked with cones.
2) On 'Go!', players holding a ball sprint one full lap around the outer cone track.
3) Upon returning to step on their spot marker, players roll their ball toward the center hula hoop.
4) Award 40, 30, 20, and 10 points in the order balls stop inside the hoop; players who miss retrieve their ball and keep rolling from their spot until everyone scores.
pe-00238:
1) Set 4 home spot markers in a square with 1 cone on each home base and 2 extra cones in the center (6 cones total).
2) Four players start at their home bases; on 'Go!', everyone sprints to grab 1 cone at a time from the center or from any opponent's home base.
3) Players may carry only 1 cone at a time and cannot block or guard their own home cones.
4) The first player to gather 3 cones simultaneously at their own home base wins the round.
pe-00239:
1) Groups of 5–6 stand in a small circle with 1 ball and 1 inflated balloon per group.
2) Player 1 taps the balloon straight up using the ball they are holding ('Keep it up!'), then immediately hands the ball to the neighbor on their side ('Pass!').
3) The next player takes the ball, taps the falling balloon straight up with the center of the ball, and hands the ball to the next teammate.
4) Continue around the circle without letting the balloon touch the floor until reaching the target count (e.g., 10 or 20 hits).
pe-00240:
1) Pair up to practice 7 active Rock-Paper-Scissors (RPS) variations for warm-ups and fair game officiating.
2) Variations 1–3 (Hand): (1) Palm-top RPS → (2) High-five clap RPS → (3) Double-hand RPS.
3) Variations 4–6 (Foot & Full-Body): (4) Foot RPS (feet together=rock, front-back stride=scissors, wide straddle=paper) → (5) Full-body pose RPS → (6) Jumping-Jack RPS (arms crossed overhead=scissors, together=rock, wide=paper).
4) Variation 7 (1-2-3-4 Turnaround RPS): stand back-to-back, jump 3 times on '1, 2, 3', and spin 180° in the air on '4' to land in your RPS pose.
pe-00241:
1) Set up two concentric base diamonds—an inner blue diamond and an outer pink diamond—plus separate offensive and defensive home bases.
2) Before throwing the ball into the field, the batter calls out either '1 Point!' or '2 Points!'
3) On a '1 Point' call, the batter runs the shorter inner blue bases while fielders must relay the ball around the wider outer pink bases to defensive home.
4) On a '2 Points' call, the batter must run the longer outer pink bases while fielders step onto the shorter inner blue bases to relay the ball home.
pe-00242:
1) Every student—including 1–2 taggers holding foam sticks—stands inside a large hula hoop.
2) All players must move by holding the back of their hoop while dragging the front edge along the floor (lifting the whole hoop off the floor is a foul).
3) Taggers also drag their hoops while chasing runners to tap them below the shoulder with a foam stick.
4) Tagged runners stay on the court, spin their hula hoop 10 times around their waist, arm, or neck, and immediately rejoin the chase.
pe-00243:
1) Two teams play on a gym court with goals at each end using a large lightweight ball (big volleyball, mini Kin-Ball, or light gym ball).
2) Players cannot walk while holding the ball and must advance it via air passes without letting the ball touch the floor.
3) Goals cannot be scored by throwing—a teammate near the goal must toss/set the ball into the air and another teammate must spike/hit it into the goal.
4) If the ball touches the floor, possession changes; defenders may intercept passes but are penalized for pressing down on a held ball.
pe-00244:
1) Lay 8 flat hoops at various distances in front of each team's start line; players hold beanbags in a relay line.
2) Player 1 tosses a beanbag toward a target hoop and runs out; if the beanbag lands completely inside the hoop, they pick up both the beanbag and the hoop.
3) If the beanbag misses or touches the hoop rim (for upper grades), the runner retrieves only the beanbag.
4) Returning runners must hand the beanbag and captured hoop directly hand-to-hand to the next teammate (no throwing) to stack behind the line until all hoops are captured.
pe-00245:
1) Form groups of 2 or 3 with 1 hula hoop and 1 cone per player.
2) One player rolls the hula hoop forward across the floor while the other 1–2 players sprint alongside holding their cones.
3) Right before the wobbling hoop falls flat onto the floor, players must drop their cone cleanly inside the center of the hoop.
4) Dropping the cone after the hoop is already flat on the floor does not count; the first player to land their cone inside before it falls scores 1 point, and roles rotate.
pe-00246:
1) Use this warm-up right before a main ball game; teams race to collect cones or jumbo stacking cups from the far side to build their goalposts.
2) Players sprint to meet opponents and play Rock-Paper-Scissors; the winner takes 1 cone or jumbo cup back to assemble their team's goal tower.
3) The loser performs 2 quick squats on the spot and immediately jumps back into the next RPS duel.
4) The first team to finish building their goal structure wins the warm-up, and the completed towers serve directly as the goals for the main game.
pe-00247:
1) Two players face each other in a push-up (plank) position on a smooth gym or classroom floor, with 2 cups/cones flanking each player to mark goal width.
2) Maintaining a plank, players use one flat palm to slide a beanbag across the floor toward the opponent's goal.
3) Sliding the beanbag past the opponent between their outer cups scores 1 point; sliding it right between the opponent's hands and feet (under their body) scores 3 points!
4) Players block and shoot one-handed while holding the plank with the other arm(allow knee-plank modification as needed).
pe-00248:
1) Divide into an Odd Team (1, 3, 5) and an Even Team (2, 4, 6), with safe home lines at opposite ends of the room.
2) Roll a foam dice-ball in the center; if an odd number lands up, the Odd Team attacks while the Even Team flees to their home line (and vice versa).
3) Running is strictly forbidden—all players must move by fast walking only as attackers pass the dice-ball and try to hit defenders before they cross their safe line.
4) Score 1 point per hit (or have hit players perform the fitness task on the die), then return to the center for the next roll.
pe-00249:
1) Pair up with 2 soft balls; Partner A sits on the floor leaning back in an engaged V-sit core posture holding 1 ball, while Partner B stands at their feet holding the 2nd ball.
2) Partner B places their ball on top of Partner A's ankles/shins.
3) Partner A chest-passes the ball in their hands to Partner B, then immediately reaches forward to grab the ball resting on their ankles and passes it next.
4) Partner B catches each pass and quickly places it back on Partner A's ankles in a continuous juggling rhythm for 10–15 reps before switching roles.
pe-00250:
1) Pairs or small groups gather around a foam fitness dice-ball (printed with numbers 1–6 and exercises) and a scoreboard.
2) Before each roll, every player/team predicts both 'Odd or Even' AND one specific number from 1 to 6.
3) Guessing Odd/Even correctly earns 1 point, while nailing the exact number earns 3 points; anyone whose prediction misses performs the fitness exercise shown on the top face.
4) First player or team to reach 15 points wins.
pe-00251:
1) Spread out with enough space between classmates and travel around the area using basic locomotor movements such as walking, jumping, and hopping.
2) Learn skipping (alternating a walk and a hop with rhythm) and galloping (one foot leads while the other follows, like a horse).
3) Learn leaping (spring from one foot and land on the other as if crossing stepping stones) and sliding (glide along the floor sweeping the soles of the feet).
4) Link the movements you have learned and travel freely around the space, expressing them.
pe-00252:
1) Players hold hands, circle around, and chant together.
2) The player whose turn it is throws the dice ball to the center; the player whose number is on top grabs it quickly and shouts 'Scatter!', and everyone running away freezes on the spot.
3) The catcher throws at another player; a hit wins that player's bracelet, but if the target catches the ball, the thrower must hand over a bracelet.
4) The first player to collect bracelets of every color wins.
pe-00253:
1) A game combining table tennis and badminton; split into two teams facing each other across a net.
2) Serve diagonally into the opponent's court, serving from the right side when your score is even and from the left when it is odd.
3) Hit the shuttlecock without letting it bounce and send it into an open space on the opponent's court to score.
4) Play three sets of 25 points each; the first team to win two sets wins the match.
pe-00254:
1) A golf-style activity in which players throw flying discs from the tee toward a target called a discatcher.
2) After the first tee throw, the player farthest from the hole (discatcher) throws next, and so on in turn.
3) Place a spot marker where each disc lands; stepping on or over the marker while throwing costs a 1-stroke penalty.
4) After all holes are finished, the player or team with the fewest total throws wins.
pe-00255:
1) Form teams including a goalkeeper and start the match at the center face-off spot on the referee's signal.
2) Pass or dribble the ball with your stick and shoot into the opponent's goal to score.
3) Lifting the stick above waist height when attacking or shooting is called a foul.
4) Play two 10-minute halves; the team that scores more goals wins.
pe-00256:
1) A handball-style game in which a team passes up to 3 times and then shoots at a rebound net.
2) Defenders may not block passes or movement with their bodies or intercept the ball; they defend only by catching the rebounded ball.
3) If the ball bounces off the net and lands outside the forbidden zone without a defender catching it, the attackers score; if it lands inside the forbidden zone or goes out of bounds, the opponents score.
4) Play three 10-minute sets; the team with the higher total score wins.
pe-00257:
1) Begin the expressive activity by learning the basic moves of the Hawaiian folk dance, hula, step by step.
2) The first move pushes the hips side to side with rhythm; the second draws rolling waves with the hands while gliding smoothly left and right.
3) The third move stretches the heel forward to show surprise at discovering a sea turtle; the last move links picking a star and holding it to the chest with a greeting.
4) Connect the moves you have learned and complete the whole routine to the music.
pe-00258:
1) A home workout for growing students to build cardiovascular endurance and physical development; begin by jogging lightly in place to the beat of the music as a warm-up.
2) Perform full-body aerobic moves such as jumping jacks, arm walking, and high knees in order.
3) Follow the teacher's demonstration and count, and keep moving without rest for the set number of sets.
4) Finish with stretching to settle your breathing and relax the whole body.
pe-00259:
1) Learn the five main moves of the traditional Russian folk dance, the polka, one by one, starting with a step that alternately taps the heel and the toe to the rhythm.
2) Add a turning move: jump on the left foot and spin once in place.
3) Practice drawing a mountain with the hands while squatting and then rising with arms wide, and the 'Tetris' pose with arms crossed and legs kicked out forward.
4) Link all the moves together and perform the whole routine to lively music.
pe-00260:
1) Push the desks against the walls, set up a net with box tape across the middle of the classroom, and split into two teams; everyone sits on the floor and may not lift their bottom or move from their chosen spot.
2) Start with a serve and, as in volleyball, hit the balloon within 3 touches to send it to the opponents' side.
3) If the balloon touches the floor, ceiling, desks, or walls, or hits the net, the other team scores; one player touching it twice in a row or the balloon passing under the net also loses the point.
4) The first team to reach 5 points wins.
pe-00261:
1) The zombie (tagger) is blindfolded with a scarf or eye mask and searches for classmates using only touch and hearing.
2) Runners hide silently under desks or around chairs during the time limit, while the teacher gives verbal hints about the room layout and positions so the zombie can search safely.
3) A runner who is touched by the zombie or gives themselves away by making noise becomes the next zombie.
4) As a variation, runners can move silently to avoid the zombie instead of staying frozen in their hiding spot.
pe-00262:
1) Learn to throw the disc with backhand, forehand, and hammer grips, and to catch it safely with pancake, overhead, and underhand catches.
2) Set up cones and practice space passes timed to the direction and speed of a teammate running into open space away from defenders, and learn the cut-in move of faking and then changing direction quickly.
3) Progress step by step by combining return passes with forward-space passes, or by advancing with continuous passes between points.
4) In the real game, keep passing and score by catching the disc in the opponent's end zone.
pe-00263:
1) Balance a pool noodle (fun stick) on the palm, run with it, and pass it to the next runner like a baton in a stick-balance relay.
2) Stand in a circle with each noodle upright on the floor; on the signal, step one place to the right and catch your neighbor's noodle before it falls. In pairs, one partner holds a noodle and raises or lowers it while the other jumps over or limbos under it.
3) In noodle tag, the tagger touches a specific body part (back, top of the foot, etc.) and the person touched becomes the tagger; in noodle 'Cham-chamcham', face each other over a noodle in the center, play rock-paper-scissors, and the winner grabs the noodle to touch the loser, who runs to their own line.
4) Rotate turns and repeat each activity several times.
pe-00264:
1) Split into two teams with a warm-up game: stand back to back, follow the body-part commands, and grab the scarf first; then both teams sit in a zigzag W and M formation facing each other on floor spot markers.
2) The attacking team passes a beanbag in order from player 1 to the last player, while the defenders reach out to block passes without lifting their bottoms off the floor.
3) When the beanbag reaches the last player safely, that player may try to shoot it into the basket.
4) After a successful shot, the whole scoring team stands and rotates: the front player goes to the back and everyone moves up one seat.
pe-00265:
1) Check the step-by-step training moves shown on screen and get ready on your spot marker.
2) Follow the count to do moves that build whole-body strength and balance, such as knee-kick walking, Superman holds, and ice-sled riding.
3) Build rhythm and coordination with the 'corner-point dance', then build muscular endurance with high-intensity plank up-downs.
4) After all the stages are done, finish by settling your breathing with whole-body breaths and gently shaking out your arms and legs.
pe-00266:
1) Follow Tabata home-workout moves based on the Avengers heroes, staying in place.
2) Repeat moves that use both upper and lower body for the set time, such as Hulk punches, Captain America jumps, and Iron Man laser blasts.
3) Stimulate flexibility and whole-body strength with dynamic moves that use many joints, such as Spider-Man web shooting.
4) After all the hero training is done, take deep breaths to settle your breathing and finish.
pe-00267:
1) Learn about the features and origins of the traditional Chinese lion dance, then get ready on your spot marker to express a lion's day through body movements.
2) The lion wakes up and walks carefully left, right, forward, and back looking for prey; when it meets the prey, it swings its arms high overhead and threatens with a fierce motion and face.
3) After pouncing and catching the prey, the lion leaps for joy, runs happily back to its den, and falls into a deep sleep again.
4) Follow this story line and complete the whole routine to music.
pe-00268:
1) Learn about the features of hip-hop culture, which originated in the United States, and practice the bounce: bow the head and upper body, bend the knees lightly, and march in place.
2) Learn the 'one-two' move, stepping with feet apart while punching the fists forward strongly, and the 'rock-it-down' move, swinging the arms freely while crossing the legs.
3) Learn the 'poke-poke' move, punching toward the sky and both sides and then folding the arms, and the 'doggie dance', crossing both arms beside the chin while riding the groove.
4) Link the five moves together and dance to upbeat hip-hop music.
pe-00269:
1) Start a whole-body stretch in place, following the teacher's count.
2) Interlace your fingers, push forward, then stretch up over your head; with fingers still interlaced, lean the upper body side to side in turn to loosen the flanks.
3) With feet shoulder-width apart, continue the whole-body flexibility exercises by crossing or stretching the arms and legs.
4) Keep your breathing relaxed and follow every move through to the end within a comfortable range.
pe-00270:
1) Learn the basic moves of the haka, the traditional folk dance of the Maori people of New Zealand, starting with the basic horse-riding stance.
2) Slap the knees and chest with the hands while stamping the feet strongly, and show the fierce expression with a threatening glare and the tongue stuck far out.
3) Repeat the moves in the set choreography order, powerfully and crisply, to the commands and shouts.
4) Line up as a whole group and finish by matching the moves together with one unified shout.
pe-00271:
1) Start a whole-body strength workout in place indoors, following the teacher's demonstration and count; get into the ready position by interlacing the fingers or extending the arms, and settle your breathing.
2) Build abdominal and lower-body strength with moves that cross or lift the legs and arms.
3) Bend forward, place the hands on the floor, and stretch the body into a mountain shape to stimulate the whole body.
4) Complete every move to the end with steady breathing, in time with the count.
pe-00272:
1) Put the ankle jump rope loop on your dominant ankle and place the rope and ball behind the opposite foot.
2) Lightly kick the ball forward with the heel of the opposite foot.
3) Time a light jump with the opposite foot to clear the rope and ball as they swing around to the front.
4) Once comfortable, swing the ankle back and forth or in a half circle to keep the rope turning continuously while you jump.
pe-00273:
1) Adjust the rope to your height and get ready with your heels lightly raised.
2) Practice the two-foot jump in both the 1-turn-2-jump and 1-turn-1-jump styles, then learn alternate-foot jumping (running step) and the alternate-foot double-beat step with two hops on each foot.
3) Challenge the cross-shaped step, jumping while moving left-right and forward-backward.
4) After learning all the basic steps, jump continuously to the beat of music.
pe-00274:
1) Stack 3 paper plates and fix them together with tape on four sides.
2) Cut long strips of box tape or electrical tape and wrap them around the whole rim so no air gets into the gaps, then rub firmly to finish a solid disc shape.
3) Decorate the disc surface with your own design and pictures using markers or colored pencils.
4) Throw and catch the finished disc with a wrist snap in a safe space.
pe-00275:
1) Turn a plastic or paper cup upside down and place a ping-pong ball on its flat bottom.
2) Hold the cup with one hand and keep it steady so the ball does not fall.
3) Flick the cup upward slightly to launch the ball into the air, then quickly flip the cup right side up while the ball is airborne to catch it inside.
4) The first player to succeed a set number of times without dropping the ball wins.
pe-00276:
1) Learn the basic Running Man shuffle step in place, alternately extending and sliding the feet.
2) Once comfortable with the basic step, advance to a traveling shuffle step that feels like going up and down stairs, and combine crossing-foot kicks and arm moves with the step's beat.
3) Perform the steps continuously in place or while moving, to the beat of upbeat music.
4) Line up in formation with friends and complete the stair shuffle dance as a group routine.
pe-00277:
1) Mark a path on the floor with spot markers, and have two teams start facing each other.
2) When you meet a player from the other team along the way, play rock-paper-scissors.
3) The winner keeps advancing, while the loser's team sends the next runner out immediately.
4) Besides the basic rule of winning by reaching the far end of the opposing side, the game can be run in 3 variations, such as joining runners together.
pe-00278:
1) Set up a net across the middle of the classroom with an elastic band or similar, and sit in two teams.
2) After the serve, the balloon must be passed twice within your own team and sent to the opponent's court only on the third touch.
3) Sending it over on the first or second touch gives the point to the other team.
4) A balloon that falls to the floor or gets caught in the net costs your team a point.
pe-00279:
1) While the long rope is turning, students enter one after another along a figure-8 path.
2) Jump once in the center of the rope and quickly exit to the opposite side.
3) When jumping and exiting, circle out diagonally rather than staying in place or going sideways.
4) Once skilled, continue the challenge with two-sided entry, jumping in alternately from both sides.
pe-00280:
1) Set up a net rope across the middle of the classroom and sit in two teams with bottoms on the floor.
2) Throw the ball with one or two hands so it lands on the floor of the opponent's area to score 1 point.
3) As in volleyball, teammates may pass up to 2 times, and the ball must be sent to the other side on the third touch.
4) Do not hold the ball for more than 1 second after catching it.
pe-00281:
1) Stand properly beside your desk or in an open space in the classroom and start the aerobic workout while watching the video.
2) Keep up jumping jacks and high-knee jumps in place for a set time, then repeat cross steps and butt kicks to the rhythm.
3) Do squat jumps and lunges that alternate the feet forward and back.
4) Finish the aerobic exercise with 10 slow burpees.
pe-00282:
1) In classroom groups, take on cooperative missions in turn using speed stacking cups and balloons.
2) The first is Cup Elevator: pull cups out from the top one by one and slot them in at the bottom of a stack of 12; the second is Cup Flip Relay: flick the bottom of a cup with a finger at the desk edge so it lands upright.
3) The third mission has two people inflate a balloon and then release the air to knock down all 12 cups on the desk.
4) The fourth is a relay in which a paper cup on the floor is pushed only by the air from a balloon around the turning point and back.
pe-00283:
1) Sit properly on a classroom chair and start the stretching routine to the music and the beat on the screen.
2) Loosen the shoulders by shrugging both shoulders up and down, then do shoulder rolls.
3) Extend both arms forward and pull one hand back like drawing a bow, throw diagonal punches, slowly turn the neck left and right, and shake out the shoulders from side to side.
4) Repeat moves such as reaching the arms back to twist the upper body and crossing the arms to loosen tight upper-body muscles.
pe-00284:
1) Inside a court marked with cones, choose one mother zombie to hold a pinny in hand while everyone else scatters around the court.
2) When the game starts, the mother zombie runs freely and tags the fleeing classmates.
3) A tagged player goes to the teacher, takes a pinny to hold in hand, and becomes a regular zombie; regular zombies can never run and may only tag others while walking.
4) The game ends when everyone has become a zombie or when a last survivor lasts through the set time.
pe-00285:
1) Split into two teams, choose one goalkeeper per team, and make a goal 10 steps wide with 2 cones.
2) Start at the center circle by passing the ring backward; the ring must be passed by sliding it with a play-stick placed through the middle of the ring.
3) Dribbling and kicking are forbidden, the player who first gets the ring with the stick has possession, a player holding the ring must pass within 5 seconds, and you may not take the ring directly from an opponent.
4) There are no sidelines or end lines, so the whole gym is in play; putting the ring into the opponent's goal scores 1 point.
pe-00286:
1) Students pair up, face each other, and play rock-paper-scissors.
2) The winner becomes the runner and flees at once into the designated area; the loser becomes the tagger, does 3 jumping jacks, and then chases the runner.
3) When the runner is tagged, both freeze on the spot and play rock-paper-scissors again to reset their roles.
4) Repeat with the same partner for the set time to build cardiovascular endurance and quickness.
pe-00287:
1) Make several narrow horizontal 'rivers' (defense zones) in a rectangular court and place about 2 defenders in each river.
2) Attackers wait at the start line, and on the signal dodge the defenders to cross the rivers to the return line, take a soft dice ball (beanbag) from the basket there, and dodge the defenders again on the way back to the start line.
3) Putting the ball into the start-line basket without being tagged scores 1 point; an attacker who is tagged is out, goes around the outside of the court to the start or return line, and may re-enter without limit.
4) After a set time (3 minutes), swap attack and defense; the team with more points wins.
pe-00288:
1) Split into two teams and put on pinnies; each team chooses one tagger, and everyone else balances a soft dice ball on their head to be 'charged'.
2) The tagger uses a fun-stick pole to push the ball off an opposing runner's head, putting them in a 'discharged' (frozen) state.
3) A discharged runner is revived when a teammate picks up the ball from the floor and places it back on their head; if the tagger's own ball falls, they must also stop until a teammate puts it back.
4) After the set time, the team with more survivors, or the team that has put every opponent out, wins.
pe-00289:
1) Group members gather in a circle and hold hands with their neighbors in an X, right palm facing down and left palm facing up.
2) Without letting go, turn and move your bodies to untangle the knotted arms and form one circle.
3) Start in pairs and gradually increase the number of people to 4, a small group, and the whole class.
4) Without letting go, make a gate to pass through or turn around, communicating with friends to find a solution.
pe-00290:
1) Place one box in the center of the court and group boxes around it; each student holds 2 soft dice balls and throws in turn.
2) On your turn, avoid your own group's box and throw a ball into another group's box.
3) If a ball lands in another team's box, the whole of that team does a frog-jump penalty task.
4) If a ball lands in the center box, the 'time bomb' goes off: everyone runs one fast lap around the track holding a ball, then comes back and throws it into their own group's box, and the last group to get the ball in takes the penalty.
pe-00291:
1) The tagger stands by the wall and the other players line up at the start line on the opposite side.
2) The tagger shouts 'Mugunghwa kkochi gawi-bawi-bo' and holds out a hand overhead, and the players show rock-paper-scissors at the same time.
3) Players who beat the tagger take two big steps forward, those who tie take one big step, and those who lose stand beside the tagger and link pinky fingers to form a chain.
4) When a player breaks the pinky link of a caught player, the tagger chases and touches the others, and whoever is touched becomes the new tagger.
pe-00292:
1) Choose 2 Gargamels, 1 Cat and 1 Papa Smurf; everyone else is a Smurf and runs away.
2) Smurfs can only be caught by Gargamel when alone; a Smurf holding hands with friends cannot be caught.
3) The Cat breaks up a group by touching the person at either end of a chain of linked Smurfs.
4) A Smurf tagged by Gargamel is out, does 10 jumping jacks, then must ask Papa Smurf for a rescue to come back in.
pe-00293:
1) Arrange chairs in a circle and everyone starts seated.
2) Starting from one student, children stand up in the order 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1 people and call out the chant matching the number.
3) After the single-person round, everyone stands up and sits down together while shouting "We all came!"
4) Standing out of turn, with the wrong number of people, or missing the chant puts you out and earns a penalty.
pe-00294:
1) Form groups of 2, 3 or 4 and place spot markers at the corners and the center.
2) Pass with a chest or bounce pass to the player on your right or across from you, then move to the right and join the back of the line.
3) In the rolling pass, pass the ball, move to the center marker, give a return pass, then rotate to the next position.
4) After a set number of successes (e.g., 20), move to the next stage or add a second ball to raise the difficulty.
pe-00295:
1) Pick one Raccoon by rock-paper-scissors; the other children are Squirrels who stand in squirrel houses (spot markers) around the edge, with at most 2 per house.
2) When the Raccoon in the middle house shouts "Raccoon!", every Squirrel must leave its house and move to a different one.
3) A Squirrel tagged by the Raccoon while moving becomes the new Raccoon, and the old Raccoon becomes a Squirrel.
4) If the Raccoon tags no one, it returns to the Raccoon house and starts again from the call.
pe-00296:
1) Place 3 cones in the center of a circular field; fielders stand on dish cones around the edge and kickers line up behind the base.
2) Fielders pass up to 3 times, then on the 4th roll the ball at the center cones; the kicker kicks the rolling ball far, runs to touch the base for 1 point, and high-fives the next kicker.
3) If the rolled ball knocks down a cone the kicker is out; if it misses and goes past, play continues.
4) When all 3 cones are down, teams switch roles, and after the set number of innings the team with more points wins.
pe-00297:
1) Everyone pairs up and holds hands, and the tagger pair also chases while holding hands.
2) A pair about to be caught shouts "Freeze!" and raises their joined hands overhead to form a gate; frozen pairs cannot be tagged, so the taggers chase other pairs.
3) When two other runners safely pass under a frozen pair's gate, they shout "Ddaeng!" and the pair is free to run again.
4) A pair tagged by the taggers becomes the new tagger pair and the roles swap.
pe-00298:
1) Use dish cones to mark a figure-8 (S-shaped) course on the floor with gaps in the path.
2) Choose one tagger by rock-paper-scissors; the others are runners inside the course, and the tagger shouts "Start!" from the opposite side and chases only along the connected 8-shaped line.
3) Runners may move along the lines and also jump across the gaps, but the tagger cannot cross a gap.
4) A runner tagged by the tagger becomes the next tagger.
pe-00299:
1) Set up the indoor roller stones and a target mat, and mark a delivery line and a hog line at fixed distances.
2) Teams decide who goes first by rock-paper-scissors and take turns sliding a set number of stones toward the target (house); stones that do not pass the hog line are removed immediately.
3) After each end, only the team with the stone closest to the button can score, earning one point for each of its stones closer to the center than the opponent's nearest stone.
4) Add up the points from all the agreed ends to decide the winner.
pe-00300:
1) For the chest pass, hold the ball with both hands at the chest and push it firmly toward the partner's chest while stepping forward with one foot.
2) For the bounce pass, aim under the defender's arms and bounce the ball about two-thirds of the way to the receiver.
3) For the overhead pass, throw from above the head with two hands or one hand to a teammate far beyond the defender.
4) When receiving, reach out with both hands, catch the ball in the air by jumping, and land with a one-two step to avoid a traveling violation.
pe-00301:
1) The kicker kicks the ball from the cone at home base, then runs around the 1-point or 2-point cone ahead and back home.
2) The fielding group picks up the kicked ball and carries it, or passes it among teammates, to the fielding home base.
3) If a fielder holding the ball steps on the fielding home before the kicker gets back, the kicker is out; a safe return earns 1 or 2 points depending on the cone, and if the fielders are slow the kicker can circle the cones several times for extra points.
4) After every member has kicked once, teams swap roles; play 4 rounds each and the team with the higher total wins.
pe-00302:
1) Arrange one chair per player in a circle or freely, and choose one tagger (the Ant) to stand in the middle.
2) Every other student sits on a chair, and the Ant walks around trying to sit in an empty chair.
3) Students work together to move quickly into the empty chair so the Ant cannot sit down.
4) If the Ant cannot sit within the set time (e.g., 1 minute), the students win; if the Ant sits in an empty seat, the Ant wins.
pe-00303:
1) Choose 1 tagger (or several); the tagger holds a balloon and starts at a set distance from the other players.
2) On the referee's signal or when the tagger shouts "One step!", all players move at the same time, taking exactly one step in any direction.
3) The tagger keeps calling "One step!" and chases the others, who each take one step to escape.
4) A player touched by the tagger's hand or balloon after a step is out or becomes the next tagger.
pe-00304:
1) Lay out 9 spot markers in a 3x3 grid to make a bingo board, and split the class into two teams.
2) Each team's first runner takes a pinnie, runs from the start line to place it on any spot marker, returns, circles around the team, and tags the next runner; runners 1 to 3 each place a new pinnie to build toward bingo.
3) From the 4th runner on there are no new pinnies, so each runner moves one of their team's placed pinnies to a different empty marker.
4) The first team to line up 3 pinnies in a row, column or diagonal wins.
pe-00305:
1) Split into two teams and sit side by side on the floor in a line or zigzag; hands stay on the floor for support and only feet may be used.
2) Pinch the indoor shoe from the start point between both feet and pass it from foot to foot to the person next to you.
3) The last player uses only their feet to place the shoe safely on the target chair.
4) A dropped shoe goes back to the start; the team that moves more shoes within the time limit (1 minute) wins.
pe-00306:
1) Stack 12 paper cups and mark the rim of the top cup with a marker.
2) In the first activity, "Cup Elevator", start the timer and move cups one at a time from top to bottom until the marked cup goes to the bottom and comes back to the top, timing the whole process.
3) In the second activity, "Spread and Gather", hold 6 cups in each hand, lay them out on the desk one by one with both hands, then quickly stack them back in reverse order and stop the timer.
4) Repeat each activity 5 times and try to beat your own best time.
pe-00307:
1) Poke 4 holes in the bottom of each of 12 paper cups with a pencil to make speed-stacking cups.
2) On a flat desk or floor, stack the cups one at a time in alternating up-and-down orientation into a tall column.
3) Balance carefully and try to reach the highest level you can, taking photos along the way to record your best height before it falls.
4) Do not give up when it falls; try again and share your records on the class or group board.
pe-00308:
1) A series of 5 games to learn classmates' names naturally at the first meeting: begin with "Name Bingo", where students fold a name tent to introduce themselves and talk with friends to fill a 5x5 bingo board.
2) In "Star and Fans", pairs play rock-paper-scissors and the loser follows the winner (the star) chanting the star's name.
3) In "Peek-a-Boo", players hide on both sides of a blanket and shout the opponent's name first the moment the blanket drops.
4) In "Before I Call Three Times", a tagger approaches and the other player must say the tagger's name before it is called three times.
pe-00309:
1) As the first step toward 3-ball juggling, use one sock ball for a 7-step challenge, standing with feet shoulder-width apart.
2) Step 1 uses the right hand and step 2 the left, throwing straight up and catching with the same hand; steps 3 and 4 toss in an arc from right to left hand and left to right hand.
3) In steps 5 and 6, hold one hand out and slip the other hand underneath to throw the ball up and catch it with the outstretched hand.
4) Step 7 passes the ball back and forth continuously with both hands in a gentle "U" shape from outside to inside; complete each step 20 times.
pe-00310:
1) Practice 7 continuous steps toward 3-ball juggling using 2 sock balls; in step 1, hold a ball in each hand and throw straight up alternately with the right and left hand.
2) In step 2, throw both balls up at the same time and catch with the same hands; in steps 3 and 4, hold both balls in one hand and throw them one after another to the other hand with a slight delay.
3) In step 5, throw with the right hand first and when it peaks throw the left-hand ball so they cross (throw, throw, catch, catch); step 6 does the same crossing throw starting with the left hand.
4) In step 7, alternate right-hand starts and left-hand starts and succeed 20 times.
pe-00311:
1) Learn and practice, in order, the 11 locomotor movements that form the basis of the expression area.
2) First practice 8 basic movements: walking, running, jumping (two-foot landing), hopping (one foot), leaping (like crossing stepping stones), skipping, galloping (running while facing forward) and side-stepping; then add sliding, rolling and crawling on all fours.
3) Watch the teacher's explanation and demonstration, then move in place or through the space, bringing out the features of each movement.
4) Apply the movements you have learned as ways of traveling in later tag games or expressive performance pieces.
pe-00312:
1) Stretch the legs in place to fully lengthen the thigh and leg muscles.
2) Hold the ankles and squat down and stand up, then swing the arms in big circles to loosen the joints, and tap the toes on the floor while reaching the arms up and out to move the whole body.
3) Place your hands on the floor and walk them out (inchworm), then sit down and continue with leg stretches.
4) Reach up with interlaced fingers to stretch, and finish the routine with deep breaths.
pe-00313:
1) Put a basket at one end of an open space and place a cup three steps away to mark the throwing line.
2) Stand at the cup and throw 3 sock balls one after another into the basket; pick up any misses and throw them again.
3) When all 3 balls go in, move to the next level, stepping one pace farther back each level (four steps, five steps and so on).
4) During the lesson time, try to get all the sock balls in from the farthest level you can reach.
pe-00314:
1) Students follow the guided full-body bodyweight exercises in place, one after another, including squats, lunges with a kick, planks and mountain climbers.
2) The moves are mostly non-jumping so they do not make noise for the floor below, and each is done with focus for about 30 seconds.
3) The moves are chosen to work the lower-body muscles and the core evenly, and are performed in sequence.
4) Complete all 8 or more Tabata-style home workout moves through to the end.
pe-00315:
1) Stack paper cups into a pyramid (rows of 4-3-2-1, 10 cups in total) on a chair or desk as the target, and mark a throwing line five steps away using spare cups.
2) Throw the 3 prepared sock balls one after another and count the cups knocked down (each cup on a higher row scores 1 point).
3) After throwing all the balls, collect them and restack the fallen cups.
4) Measure the total score earned within the time limit (3 minutes).
pe-00316:
1) Assign the roles of star, bodyguard and fan in groups of 3 or 4.
2) Bodyguards hold the star's hand or block the way to stop the fan, while the fan moves quickly to dodge the bodyguards and touch the star.
3) The round ends when the fan touches the star.
4) After each round, rotate roles one place; numbering the roles and rotating in order keeps things running smoothly.
pe-00317:
1) Place spot markers at even intervals along the center line, with taggers standing on them facing alternating directions.
2) The runner groups move freely over the whole court, dodging between the taggers on the center line; each tagger can chase only in the zone they are facing and cannot cross the center line.
3) To hand the tagger role to the opposite zone, a tagger goes up to a tagger facing away, pushes their back and shouts "Avatar!".
4) Time how long it takes to tag out all runners; the group that lasts the longest wins.
pe-00318:
1) Two teams sit on the floor facing each other across the center line; all players stay seated and move only with their bottoms on the floor.
2) The serve goes over in one hit; an all-touch rule applies so every teammate touches the ball at least once, and the ball must cross to the opponents' court within 3 touches.
3) The opponents score if the ball is sent over in one go, or if a failed toss or receive lets the ball hit the floor.
4) A balloon floats for a long time, so teammates should call out and hit the ball in turn.
pe-00319:
1) Sitting at the desk, gently move the head down, right, left and up, twice each, then hold the head with both hands and press gently down and to each side to stretch the neck muscles.
2) Turn the waist to the right and then to the left, holding the chair back to twist the torso.
3) With fingers interlaced, stretch up over the head and forward, then lean to each side to stretch the ribs and upper body.
4) Do shoulder rolls and chest-out fist punches, then finish by slowly rolling the neck.
pe-00320:
1) Stand and loosen up to the music by circling the arms side to side and then both arms together.
2) Tap the foot to the hand on the same side, then continue with the opposite hand and foot crossing to touch, and step side to side in place like skating, shifting body weight with rhythm.
3) Place hands on the head and bend the waist left and right to stretch the sides, then reach out and touch the fingertips and toes in a long stretch.
4) Raise the knee and open it out to the side, then pull the front of the thigh with a hand and balance to finish.
pe-00321:
1) Lie on a mat and do leg raises, lifting and lowering the legs without letting the feet touch the floor, then touch opposite hand and foot diagonally and sit up to clap between the legs.
2) Sit with hands behind you for V-ups pulling the knees to the chest, then continue with crunches touching the knee to the opposite elbow.
3) Do push-ups face down, and as skill allows, switch to a variation alternately touching the floor with each palm.
4) Build the core by holding a basic elbow plank in a straight line and then side planks on each side.
pe-00322:
1) Sport stacking is racing against the clock to stack and take down 12 cups by the rules, following 3 basic principles: go from left to right, alternate hands, and stack everything up (upstack) before taking it all down (downstack).
2) In the 3-3-3 event, stack three sets of 3 cups in turn, then nest them back down in order from the start.
3) In the 3-6-3 event, stack 3 cups on each side and 6 in the middle, then take them down in order.
4) The Cycle event starts from 3-6-3, goes through 6-6 and the 1-10-1 pyramid, and finishes by returning to the 3-6-3 shape.
pe-00323:
1) Push the chair back to make room between the desk and chair and sit comfortably to get ready.
2) Seated with both feet flat on the floor, hold the camel pose (opening the chest) and the cat pose (rounding the back) for 10 seconds each, then hold the chair pose for 5 seconds with arms stretched forward and hips lifted slightly off the seat.
3) Continue with the crescent-moon pose, reaching both arms up and leaning side to side, and a forward-fold stretch with the legs extended.
4) Finish by hugging one knee at a time to the chest, then fold the upper body onto the thighs in child's pose while settling the breath.
pe-00324:
1) Pairs stand in the play area facing each other and play rock-paper-scissors.
2) The winner becomes the runner and escapes at once; the loser becomes the tagger, does 3 jumping jacks as the physical task, then chases the runner.
3) When the runner is caught, the pair plays rock-paper-scissors again on the spot to decide roles and repeats the process.
4) Partners stay the same throughout, and the game repeats until students are tired, working well as a warm-up.
pe-00325:
1) Take on throw-and-catch missions with a sock ball from level 1 to level 9 in order; to pass each level you must succeed 20 times in a row without a single drop, and after a failure you restart from 0.
2) Levels 1 to 4: throw with one hand (right or left) and catch the sock ball with the same hand or the opposite hand.
3) Levels 5 and 6: raise the difficulty by snatching the ball from the air with a top-down grab.
4) Levels 7 to 9: throw the sock ball against a wall and snatch the rebound with two hands or one hand, reaching 20 in a row.
pe-00326:
1) When the bell rings at the set signal interval, run from the start line toward the target line on the opposite side.
2) You must reach the opposite line before the next bell rings.
3) The signal interval gets shorter as the levels go up, so you must keep up the pace.
4) The test ends when the number of times you fail to arrive before the bell adds up, and the final number of successful laps is recorded.
pe-00327:
1) When the bell rings at the set signal interval, set off toward the opposite target line.
2) You pass a lap only by reaching the opposite line before the next bell rings.
3) The gap between bells gets shorter as the levels rise, so you must increase your speed.
4) Count the total number of laps until you are eliminated for missing the signal, and use it to assess cardiorespiratory endurance.
pe-00328:
1) Before PE class, raise body temperature and heart rate with joint loosening and stretching.
2) Gently rotate the main joints in order: wrists and ankles, knees, waist, shoulders and neck.
3) Then do dynamic and static stretches for the legs, thighs (lunges), shoulders, arms and sides.
4) After the main activity, cool down with only calming muscle stretches, leaving out the joint loosening.
pe-00329:
1) Form teams of 4 and start on a volleyball or badminton court with a net; throw the ball over from the serve line into the opposing court.
2) The receiving team catches the ball and passes it to every teammate once, and the last player to catch it throws the ball over the net into an empty space on the opponent's side.
3) A point is scored if the opponent fails to catch the ball or it goes out of the lines, and the first team to 15 points wins.
4) Walking while holding the ball, and spiking down hard just in front of the net, are not allowed.
pe-00330:
1) Split into two teams and assign each team 1 Killer, 1 Healer and the rest as runners.
2) The Killer carries a soft hammer (or foam stick) and chases the other team's runners, tagging them out; a tagged runner leaves the field at once, does a physical task (e.g., 10 jumping jacks) and waits.
3) The Healer wears a pinnie tied on the wrist and touches teammates who have finished their task to bring them back.
4) When time is up (2 minutes), the team with more surviving runners wins.
pe-00331:
1) Participants stand on the start line, ready for a shuttle run in which a bell rings at set signal intervals, and set off with the signal sound.
2) You must reach the target line on the opposite side before the next bell rings.
3) The signal interval and running pace get faster as the levels go up.
4) The test ends when you cannot keep up with the signal, and the number of completed laps is recorded.
pe-00332:
1) Students get ready on the start line and run to the opposite side on the start signal of the bell, which rings at set intervals.
2) A lap counts only if you reach the target line exactly before the next bell rings.
3) Starting at level 1, the time allowed gets shorter as the levels rise.
4) When you fail to arrive within the time limit, the test ends and your record is checked.
pe-00333:
1) Draw start lines for the two groups 15m apart and place balls (one per group member) on dish cones behind each line.
