1) Each player tucks a towel or scarf into the waist like a tail and, in a small area, faces a partner one-on-one, trying to grab the other's tail first.
2) Next, two players form a train by holding hands or waists in a line, and a tagger tries to grab the tail of the last person in the train tail tag.
3) Vary the number of players and formation, such as having several players make a circle and take the tail of a specific target.
4) Twist your body to dodge opponents to build agility and body control.
pe-00485:
1) Two players stand or sit back to back, twist at the waist, and pass the ball by hand without dropping it.
2) Two players hold the ball between their hands, backs, or foreheads and move together in step without dropping it.
3) Do partner juggling with two balls, passing and catching at the same time on a signal; also, one player bounces a ball up and the other runs once around the thrower and catches it.
4) Place a ball on your palm and play ball fencing, protecting your own ball while knocking the ball off the opponent's hand.
pe-00486:
1) Work through difficulty levels 1 to 10 in order, cooperating from solo moves to 2-person and 3-person moves.
2) Hold basic individual poses steadily for 5 seconds, such as the V-balance at level 1 and the one-hand balance at level 2.
3) Progress through 2-person moves such as the double balance and slide to 3-person moves such as the flower, fan, Skytree, and bridge.
4) At each level, the group succeeds when all members time their signal together and hold the pose for 5 seconds or more.
pe-00487:
1) Close your eyes, stand on one foot, and hold your balance for 5 seconds.
2) Lying down, lift your legs or rotate them forward and backward as if pedaling a bike; then, lying face down, lift one hand and the opposite foot and keep your center steady.
3) Lying on your back with legs straight, write big numbers or letters in the air with the soles of your feet.
4) Facing a wall, do a handstand with eyes on the space between your hands and keep your core tight.
pe-00488:
1) Lie on a mat with your feet on the wall and get a feel for pushing off with the soles of your feet.
2) Place your palms precisely on the mat behind your ears and roll backward with your neck and back rounded.
3) If rolling is difficult, build a slope on one side of the mat to get help with the rotation going backward.
4) Push the floor away with your palms so your head is not pressed, rotate, and land safely on your feet.
pe-00489:
1) With hands and feet on the floor and hips held high, walk forward; from the same position, twist the body and move left and right sideways like a crab.
2) Walk backward with your chin tucked, looking between your legs toward the direction you are moving.
3) Do a rotating bear walk, circling in place to get a feel for rotation.
4) Lift one leg in the air and move forward supported on three limbs to build the support strength needed for handstands.
pe-00490:
1) Lay the rope straight on the floor and, eyes forward, jump lightly back and forth over it with both feet.
2) Clap in place in time with each jump over the rope to learn a combined body-coordination rhythm.
3) Fold the rope in half, hold it in one hand, and slowly practice turning it in circles beside your body; also hold both ends with a teacher or parent to learn the feel and timing of the turn.
4) The moment the rope touches the floor in front of your feet, jump over it lightly and quietly.
pe-00491:
1) On the teacher's signal or command, do standing balance moves such as the flamingo and the horizontal balance.
2) Then move on to core balance moves where you support yourself on the floor, such as the V-balance and the one-hand balance (side plank).
3) From a face-down position, do the seal pose, arching the upper body, and the bow-shaped airplane pose.
4) Lying on your back, do the bridge and the Skytree with legs raised straight, holding each pose for a few seconds in order.
pe-00492:
1) Practice the basic two-foot forward jump and the grouper jump, which opens and closes the feet.
2) Learn rhythm with the rock-paper-scissors step, which crosses the feet front and back and side to side, and one-foot hopping; then challenge the turning forward jump, slowly turning the body in place while jumping, and the hopping turn jump.
3) Step by step, do traveling jump rope while running, sideways running jump rope, and backward running jump rope.
4) To finish, run toward a mat, jump the rope, and smoothly link it into a forward roll.
pe-00493:
1) Kick off the wall and slide backward on your hips to get the feel of moving backward.
2) Lying on a mat, practice the shrimp pose, lifting the hips and bringing the toes over behind the head, and the shoulder stand; also learn how to place the palms beside the ears with the fingers pointing toward the shoulders.
3) From a rounded cradle position, roll backward and practice the rebound of quickly placing the hands and rocking back.
4) Try the full backward roll step by step, starting from a crouching position and then from a standing position.
pe-00494:
1) Run forward through mini hurdles set at regular intervals, stepping quickly one foot at a time between them.
2) Perform high-knees, driving the knee up to chest height with each hurdle you cross.
3) Turn your body sideways and pass quickly between the hurdles using side steps and cross steps.
4) Face the hurdles and jump over them continuously with both feet together; then stand sideways and do agility drills, jumping the hurdles in a two-foot zigzag or continuous side jumps.
pe-00495:
1) Seated at your desk, move both hands in turn to train brain-body coordination; at Level 1, one hand makes a fist and taps while the other rubs with an open palm at the same time, switching hands on the signal.
2) At Level 2, make different Rock-Paper-Scissors shapes with the right and left hands and practice always having the right hand win.
3) At Level 3, follow the leader's commands to touch a body part, or apply the contrary 'frog' rule and touch the opposite one.
4) At Level 4, watch the leader's hand signal and play Rock-Paper-Scissors one beat late, winning or losing on purpose.
pe-00496:
1) Set out cones in a triangle shape on the floor and have one group member wear a team pinnie to be the tagger.
2) Runners move along the sides and corners of the cone triangle to escape the tagger, and the tagger also chases only along the outline of the cones, never cutting across the inside of the triangle.
3) When the tagger touches a runner's body, they swap roles and the game continues.
4) During the time limit, use fake moves and changes of direction actively to shake off or catch the other player.
pe-00497:
1) Prepare this basic support activity of jumping sideways over the vaulting box to reduce fear before straddle-vaulting it from the front.
2) Place your hands on the box from either side, spring off the springboard, lift your hips high, and push your body over.
3) Land safely on the landing mat and return to the starting position.
4) To balance left and right sides, repeat the same jump with the hands placed in the opposite direction.
pe-00498:
1) Before the main activity, do 6 step-by-step warm-ups that move the whole body and build coordination; first, in pairs to groups of 4 holding hands, play an attack-and-defense game of touching the opponent's back or knees first.
2) Do copycat running, where the person behind immediately copies the leader's various steps or animal-imitation moves.
3) Do the cooperative carry, where two players stand back to back and move with a ball held between their belly and back without using hands.
4) Do the centipede race, where the back player holds the front player's one leg and they hop forward in step on one foot.
pe-00499:
1) Repeat a jump in place, opening and closing your feet, with a steady rhythm.
2) Along with the foot movement, add punches: 2 to the front and 2 to the side.
3) At higher levels, add 2 punches upward after the 2 front and 2 side punches for 6 in total; at the final level, change your hand shape, punching with a fist to the front and opening the palm to the side as if touching a wall.
4) Gradually speed up the tempo to build agility and body coordination.
pe-00500:
1) Place the ball on the floor and kick it lightly forward.
2) While the ball rolls, sprint ahead quickly and get in front of it.
3) Stand with your legs apart in front of the rolling ball and let it pass between your legs.
4) Run back again before the ball hits a wall or obstacle, and count how many times you let it through.
pe-00501:
1) Two students stand back to back with a spot marker between them in the center; one is the 'Cat' and the other is the 'Mouse'.
2) The caller fakes with other words and then shouts 'Cat' or 'Mouse'; the named player sprints toward their safety-zone cone.
3) The player who was not named immediately turns around and chases the fleeing opponent to tag them.
4) Besides standing starts, vary the start position, such as crouching or lying down, to sharpen reaction time.
pe-00502:
1) One person sits on the floor with legs together and raises both arms overhead in a cheering pose.
2) The partner stands behind, crosses both arms in an X, and takes hold of the seated partner's hands.
3) The standing partner pulls the arms alternately to spin the seated person around in place like a spinning top.
4) Once comfortable, gradually speed up the rotation and try spinning in the opposite direction too.
pe-00503:
1) Stand on the floor, ready to combine punches and footwork with both arms and feet to a set rhythm.
2) Start by bouncing lightly and practice punching forward twice and sideways twice, matching hands and feet.
3) Punch as if hitting a wall to make the arm movements clear, and keep the off-beat rhythm between lower-body steps and upper-body moves.
4) Once comfortable, raise the level by alternating two punches each forward, sideways, and upward.
pe-00504:
1) Sit or stand and get ready to stretch both hands out in front.
2) Extend one hand forward with an open palm (paper) and place the other on the chest in a fist.
3) On a signal or command, switch the shape and position of both hands to the opposite at the same time.
4) Once comfortable, change the combinations of fist, scissors, and paper, or add variations such as tapping the chest before switching.
pe-00505:
1) Gather in a circle, assign numbers, and complete the mission of passing or calling numbers (or passing a towel ball) quickly for 3 rounds, then sit down.
2) With eyes closed and hands joined, play an impulse game that passes a signal by squeezing hands.
3) In a trust circle, one student stands stiff like a tree trunk and falls while group members safely catch and support them.
4) Run through a tunnel of hands with trust, or have everyone stand on a picnic mat and flip it over without stepping off.
pe-00506:
1) Two students face each other and decide who attacks and who defends.
2) The attacker swings one or both hands down from above in an attacking motion.
3) The defender claps both hands together to catch the descending hand in an instant.
4) Vary the clap timing and mix in fake moves to battle with quick reflexes, then swap roles.
pe-00507:
1) Hold hands with a partner and play rock-paper-scissors with the free hand; the winner tags and the loser runs away, changing the rules to practice quick reactions.
2) Loosen up and relax with mirror stretching, copying a partner's movements exactly.
3) One student falls like a pillar while group members catch and support them, building mutual trust.
4) Sit facing each other with toes touching and hands joined, then stand up together on command; also guide a partner who has their eyes closed to a destination using hand, voice, or shoulder-tap signals.
pe-00508:
1) Fold a towel lengthwise twice and tie it twice to make a safe towel ball.
2) One student lies flat on the floor while the partner stands over them with legs apart.
3) The standing student slowly drops the towel ball between the legs, over the face, or onto the belly; the lying student watches it fall and quickly spreads the legs or turns the head to dodge it.
4) Swap roles, gradually lowering the drop height or speeding up the drop.
pe-00509:
1) Face a partner holding hands; without letting go, score a point by touching the partner's back first.
2) Play Knee Touch by placing both hands on your own knees and trying to touch the opponent's uncovered knee first, and Foot Stomp by keeping hands joined while dodging and lightly stepping on the partner's foot.
3) Balance a ball on one hand and play rock-paper-scissors; the winner knocks the opponent's ball off while the loser protects it with both hands.
4) Tuck a jump rope behind the waist like a tail; the front player changes direction to shake off the tail while the back player follows without letting go in a tail-recovery game.
pe-00510:
1) Sit with knees together and arms out while a helper crosses and holds both hands to turn you left and right (spinning cup); also gently hold the helper's index finger and spin around while changing direction (washing machine spin).
2) Stand back-to-back or with a cone or ball against the back and twist the upper body left, right, and down between the legs to pass the object back and forth.
3) Hold hands side by side with a helper and do forward rolls together on the mat in the same rhythm.
4) While held by a helper, hang tightly with the legs, lean the upper body backward upside down, and practice the leg-release spin.
pe-00511:
1) Two students stand together on an unfolded towel and hold their balance for 5 seconds.
2) Each time they succeed, fold the towel in half to make it smaller and keep balancing while pressing close together.
3) Hold both ends of a towel and pull; whoever moves a foot or loses balance first loses in a towel tug game.
4) Progress to jumping over a folded towel on the floor, or tying the towel into a ball and softly throwing it at a partner standing on one foot to knock them off balance.
pe-00512:
1) To improve running times, learn proper arm swing step by step, starting from standing and moving to long-sitting, kneeling, and lunge positions.
2) Combine the arm swing with hopping on one foot in place or skipping to build arm-leg coordination.
3) Press a towel against the wall, lean the forehead or side of the head on it, and swing the arms while keeping the upper body still.
4) Finally, sprint between cones while keeping the correct arm swing.
pe-00513:
1) In this 3-stage activity for a safe front roll on the vaulting box, Stage 1 builds the basic feel on a folded mat or thick blanket by lifting the hips and rolling while looking at the belly button.
2) In Stage 2, step on the springboard, climb onto the top of the box for a moment, then roll down slowly while looking at the belly button.
3) In Stage 3, take a run-up, push off the springboard hard, and connect a bold front roll on the box without stopping.
4) After the roll, land safely on the mat.
pe-00514:
1) A step-by-step indoor activity for lower-grade beginners: hold the rope in one hand and twirl it small and fast overhead like a helicopter to feel the wrist rotation.
2) Jump over a rope lying on the floor without stepping on it while clapping in the air, and try running jumps by moving forward or sideways over the rope.
3) Swing the rope slowly in place, watch it land in front of the feet, then jump; learn the slow jump and the feet-together/apart and feet-together/cross steps.
4) Tuck a team pinnie under the armpit and jump without dropping it to learn a compact arm motion.
pe-00515:
1) A drill and game for running fast around curves by overcoming centrifugal force: bend the arms at 90 degrees and swing them in place, learning to swing the outer arm bigger on a curve.
2) Do reaction steps: stamp the feet quickly to the leader's clap or finger direction, then twist sharply and dash.
3) In groups of three, the middle student keeps the body straight and leans left and right while the two side partners support them to learn the leaning posture.
4) Set up a figure-8 course with cones and practice running while leaning outward, then start from opposite sides and chase the opponent for 2 laps in a figure-8 chase race.
pe-00516:
1) Learn six solo bodyweight gymnastics and balance moves on a mat step by step; for the horizontal balance, face forward, slowly lower the body tilt, and hold for 5 seconds.
2) Strengthen the core and abs with the V-balance and a one-hand balance in a side-plank form.
3) Practice the seal pose, lying face down and arching the upper body up, and the bridge, lying on the back and lifting the body with hands and feet on the floor.
4) Finally, complete the skytree pose, a pre-step to the handstand, supporting the body on the shoulders with the lower body extended straight up.
pe-00517:
1) With a parent or partner standing, the child clings firmly to the front of their legs and waist.
2) The adult gently supports the child's back and slowly rotates them downward until hanging upside down.
3) While hanging upside down, sway lightly left and right to build spatial awareness, then try variations such as swinging the spread legs back and forth or walking slowly while rotating.
4) When finished, the child places both hands safely on the floor and comes down gently.
pe-00518:
1) Two students wear tail bands at the back of the waist, start from cones on opposite sides, and run to the center.
2) They meet in the middle, play rock-paper-scissors, and react quickly according to the rule decided in advance.
3) In Stage 1, the winner runs back to their own start line while the loser chases and grabs the tail.
4) In Stage 2, the winner dashes past into the opponent's side; in Stage 3, the loser flees and the winner chases; runner and chaser switch in real time depending on who wins.
pe-00519:
1) Two students pair up, face each other, and play rock-paper-scissors.
2) The winner stands at attention in place, while the loser circles once around the partner using the assigned step (rock: two-foot jump, scissors: gallop/front-back jump, paper: straddle jump).
3) After one lap, they face each other again and continue playing rock-paper-scissors.
4) Vary the game by switching between clockwise and counterclockwise circling or increasing the number of laps to 2.
pe-00520:
1) An adult or older student sits with legs extended, and the child, as the taxi driver, sits facing them on their thighs.
2) On the driving signal, lean and sway the upper body left and right to play a balance game.
3) Once comfortable, move forward, back, and sideways by pushing the floor with the bottom while carrying the child; the child can also play the passenger, leaning back on the floor and crab-walking forward with hips lifted.
4) Raise the difficulty with moves such as a 360-degree bottom-walk spin to strengthen the lower body and core.
pe-00521:
1) Stage 1: React quickly to a disc dropped from above by a partner and dodge it by spreading or closing the legs.
2) Stage 2: Watch where the disc falls and, with hands on the belly, shoulders, or head, reach out fast to touch it; Stage 3: throw the disc up yourself, clap or touch body parts, and catch it with both hands.
3) Stage 4: Face your partner or sit with your back turned, then turn on a signal and softly catch the disc between both hands from above and below like a hamburger.
4) Stage 5: Try catching the disc one-handed in the air or while passing back and forth with a partner.
pe-00522:
1) Two students pair up; one sits cross-legged and seats the other on their lap.
2) The student behind firmly wraps their arms around the front student's feet or body.
3) Keeping the body curled round, roll straight back, then use the momentum to come back up to the original seat.
4) Once rolling backward is comfortable, try a side roll that goes one full turn and returns to the starting spot.
pe-00523:
1) The spotter stands beside the chair while the performer sits on it with their back turned, and the spotter firmly supports the performer's back and waist with both hands.
2) The performer slowly leans back and places both hands on the floor to form a handstand-like position.
3) After confirming the hands are fully on the floor, the spotter lifts the legs and guides them over.
4) After landing, the performer balances and strikes a finishing pose.
pe-00524:
1) One student takes a holding posture such as a push-up or all-fours position.
2) The partner tries to break the balance by pushing, pulling, or tickling, while the holder tenses the core and limbs to stay balanced.
3) When the holder loses balance and falls or the set time runs out, the roles switch.
4) Raise the difficulty by switching to variations such as lifting one hand.
pe-00525:
1) Two students pair up; one holds a towel and the other gets ready to catch the towel's end.
2) The towel holder suddenly pulls the towel downward or away without warning.
3) The partner quickly moves a hand or foot to press down and stop the slipping towel.
4) Once comfortable, play from different starting positions such as facing away, standing, or lying face down, and the puller mixes in fakes to challenge the partner's quickness and judgment.
pe-00526:
1) The child stands on top of a parent's or partner's feet, facing each other, and they hold both hands.
2) Keeping balance so the feet do not slip off, walk like penguins in various directions such as forward, backward, sideways, and spinning in place.
3) Once comfortable, try walking with eyes closed, or stepping onto one foot and being lifted high with a bounce.
4) Switch roles and challenge the handstand penguin, in which the child puts both hands on the floor and the feet on the partner's insteps and moves along upside down.
pe-00527:
1) Fold a towel small and lay it flat on the floor.
2) The student stands in front of the towel and practices a light two-foot jump over it.
3) Each time they succeed, unfold the towel a little to widen it and take on the next level.
4) Finally, unfold it to the size of a large bath towel and try to clear it in one jump.
pe-00528:
1) Tie both ends of a towel to make a round towel ball.
2) Lying on the floor, hold the elbow still with the opposite hand and practice alone by tossing the towel ball up and catching it.
3) Sit facing a partner with legs extended and pass the towel ball back and forth using upper-body rotation and wrist snap.
4) Stand with feet spread wide side to side or front to back, and play catch while widening the distance using trunk rotation and weight shift.
pe-00529:
1) Two students face each other, and one holds a folded glove or small item in each hand at head height.
2) The dropper lets go of the item in one hand without warning.
3) The partner quickly snatches the item before it touches the floor.
4) Once comfortable, raise the difficulty by changing the starting hand position (overhead, belly, behind the back) and switching from two-hand catches to one-hand catches.
pe-00530:
1) Two students stand back to back or one behind the other with feet shoulder-width apart.
2) One student twists sideways to hand the ball to the one behind, who then turns the other way and passes it back, continuing in a cycle.
3) Once side-to-side passing is easy, pass overhead and receive between the legs in an over-under pass.
4) Go further with a figure-8 pass that crosses left and right to build whole-body coordination.
pe-00531:
1) Two students face each other and each holds one end of a towel with one hand.
2) On the start signal, pull or ease the towel to break the opponent's balance.
3) If a foot moves even one step from the floor spot or the student loses balance and falls, they lose.
4) Once comfortable, adjust the difficulty, for example by standing on one foot or playing with eyes closed.
pe-00532:
1) Two students each stand on a spread-out sheet of newspaper on the floor, facing each other.
2) On the signal, play rock-paper-scissors.
3) The loser folds their newspaper in half and steps back onto it.
4) As the paper keeps shrinking, anyone whose foot goes off the paper or who loses balance loses.
pe-00533:
1) Set up goals at both ends and place cone obstacles around the floor.
2) Shoot at one goal, then dribble the ball toward the opposite goal, taking care not to bump into the cones or other students on the way.
3) When you reach the far goal, shoot again, repeating in both directions to increase the number of touches on the ball.
4) Once comfortable, add rules such as weaving through the cones in a zigzag or spinning once before shooting.
pe-00534:
1) Two students face each other, and one spreads the legs wider than shoulder width to make a tunnel.
2) The partner rolls the ball along the floor, and the tunnel player lets it pass between the legs without moving the feet.
3) Once comfortable, raise the difficulty by turning around and letting the ball pass through while looking between the legs.
4) The roller calls out "catch," "kick," or "pass (no reaction)" as the ball rolls, and the receiver immediately performs that action.
pe-00535:
1) Twist a towel lengthwise and tie two or three firm knots to make a ball shape; two students stand facing each other about 1–2 m apart.
2) The dodger keeps both feet fixed on the floor and avoids the incoming towel by bending or leaning the upper body.
3) The thrower aims the towel at the dodger's body; the dodger must not be hit, and catching it by hand also counts as disqualification.
4) Throw alternately with the dominant and non-dominant hand to test reflexes.
pe-00536:
1) Hold a rolled newspaper stick low to the floor and move it back and forth or in a circle toward the child.
2) The child times a two-foot jump to clear the approaching stick.
3) When the stick is swung alternately up and down, jump when it comes low and duck down when it comes high.
4) Switch roles so the child swings the stick while another person jumps.
pe-00537:
1) The defender (tagger) moves only along a set line and tags the attacker who holds the ball.
2) The attacker carries the ball and breaks through the defensive line by dodging tags with left-right fake moves.
3) Expanding the defending zone from a line to a rectangular area widens the defender's range and raises the difficulty.
4) Progress to team breakthroughs, passing the ball among teammates so the ball carrier is not tagged.
pe-00538:
1) Two students stand together on a towel spread on the floor and hold for 5 seconds.
2) Each time they succeed, fold the towel in half to shrink the area.
3) As the towel gets smaller, they hug tightly or stand on one foot to keep their feet from leaving the towel.
4) If it becomes too small for both to stand on, one steps onto the other's foot and balances on one leg.
pe-00539:
1) Two students face each other and hold the towel's two ends together.
2) Place a balloon or light ball in the middle of the towel and, on the command, launch it high into the air.
3) Quickly judge where the balloon or ball will land, move, and catch it again with the towel before it touches the floor.
4) Once comfortable, raise the challenge by closing and opening the eyes or sitting and standing up.
pe-00540:
1) Stand facing a partner at a set distance and pass a soft disc (Dodgebee), watching the disc's path all the way and catching it securely with both hands wrapping from above and below.
2) First practice solo skills in place, such as tossing up and catching with both hands, clapping before the catch, and throwing under the leg to catch.
3) Practice posture variations such as throwing while sitting on the floor and standing up to catch, and catching a rolling disc.
4) Once comfortable, widen the distance from the partner and try low trajectories and fast passes to raise the catch success rate.
pe-00541:
1) Pair up with a helper and learn basic spinning moves such as spinning while holding hands and passing through the legs.
2) On the mat, do forward rolls, log rolls, and side rolls step by step with the helper's support.
3) Use a chair or mat for assisted flipping exercises to build spatial awareness and balance, and continuously practice spinning and balance control while moving plate cones on the floor over with the feet or hands.
4) While doing the moves, also learn how to fix the gaze on one spot so students do not get dizzy.
pe-00542:
1) Practice the basic Double Dutch motion of turning two long ropes alternately with both hands.
2) Watch the moment the rope passes at torso height as it turns and enter quickly into the middle.
3) Jump lightly to the rhythm in the center of the ropes, on both feet or alternating one foot.
4) After the set number of jumps, exit quickly to the other side without hesitating.
pe-00543:
1) A reaction drill: respond quickly to the start signal and run straight ahead.
2) Run with the body centered, eyes forward so the head does not wobble.
3) Swing the arms big and fast back and forth while keeping the shoulder and elbow angles.
4) React to the signal from different starting positions, such as lying face down or facing backward, then stand up and sprint.
pe-00544:
1) Grip a low horizontal bar with both hands and get ready on top of a mat.
2) Hook the legs over the outside of the bar and learn the feel of rotating the body sideways.
3) Keep the hips lifted so they do not sag, and rotate around the bar while holding on.
4) After one full turn, bend the knees and land safely on the mat.
pe-00545:
1) Games for building body coordination by moving the hands and feet to different rhythms while sitting or standing face to face.
2) Tap one hand to 2 beats and the other to 3 beats or alternate foot moves to coordinate hands and feet together, then alternate on command between pounding the thigh with a fist and rubbing it with the other palm.
3) Use a towel or tissue for one-foot balance contests, or toss it up, clap, and catch it.
4) Face a partner and, on a signal, both drop a tissue and move toward each other to snatch it, extending into a quick-reflex activity.
pe-00546:
1) Do the pencil roll, rolling along the floor with the body straight like a pencil, and the daruma move, rolling and popping back up like a tumbler doll.
2) Build core strength with the ninja wall walk, going into a handstand with feet on the wall and moving sideways, and the spider crawl.
3) In a plank position, play catch with a partner by rolling a ball back and forth along the floor.
4) Take on the challenge in a fun way by gradually adding more balls or holding for longer.
pe-00547:
1) Stand beside a long rope laid out in a straight line on the floor.
2) Jump back and forth over the rope with both feet together, keeping the rhythm of claps or music.
3) Adjust the jump tempo to a steady beat or to varied rhythms such as "boom, boom-boom."
4) Combine arm movements, spreading both arms above, below, and out to the sides of the shoulders, with the jumps to build complex body control.
pe-00548:
1) Practice the correct start position, with the front foot and opposite hand forward, a hand lightly on the knee, and the weight leaning forward.
2) Learn the in-place arm swing, bending the elbows at right angles and swinging big back and forth so the thumb reaches nose height.
3) Pick a target ahead (a tree or cone) so the head does not wobble sideways, and run a 5 m sprint.
4) Build quickness and focus by starting from facing backward or spinning once in place and then running at the target.
pe-00549:
1) Lay a mat on the floor, sit with the soles of the feet together, and hold the feet firmly with both hands.
2) Keeping the body curled round, roll sideways and backward, then use the momentum to come back up to the starting position.
3) Once comfortable, roll in the opposite direction too and balance and rise like a tumbler doll.
4) Keep the body tucked until the end without letting go of arms and legs to build the core and balance.
pe-00550:
1) Lay a step ladder out long on the floor and stand sideways beside it.
2) Step alternately in the "in-in-out-out" pattern and move quickly sideways along the ladder squares.
3) Step nimbly inside and outside the ladder and connect a Hip Change move that twists the pelvis.
4) Turn and repeat the same steps in the opposite direction to build agility and quickness both ways.
pe-00551:
1) Groups of 3–4 sit in a circle on the floor, hold hands, and prepare to raise their feet together in the middle for the 'flower' formation.
2) In the 3-person fan formation, the middle student steps back one pace, holds hands with the two side students, and they bring their feet together to balance.
3) Several students lie in a row on their stomachs and link up in the 'wave (bridge)' move by resting each person's ankles on the shoulders of the person in front.
4) Everyone holds the pose in time with each other until the move is finished.
pe-00552:
1) Crouch at the front of the mat with both hands placed on it.
2) Lift the hips, tuck the chin, and round the body so the back of the head touches the mat first.
3) A spotter lightly supports the learner's waist or hips to help them roll forward.
4) After rolling, place both feet safely on the floor and stand up.
pe-00553:
1) Practice one-leg standing and horizontal balance while keeping the head fixed and steady.
2) From a seated position, hold a V-sit balance with legs and arms stretched out, then a side bridge with one hand on the floor and hips lifted into a straight line.
3) Build spinal flexibility with the bow pose (lying on the stomach, holding the ankles and lifting the chest) and the bridge (arch) pushing up with hands and feet.
4) Finish with the 'sky tree' (a basic shoulder stand): lie on the back and push the hips high, supporting the body on the shoulders.
pe-00554:
1) Two students stand face to face, each holding one end of a towel.
2) Without ever letting go of the towel, they pass their bodies and legs over it to get tangled up like a knot.
3) Still holding on, they turn their bodies or pull their legs back out until they return to the original face-to-face position.
4) Once comfortable, raise the difficulty by having one partner close their eyes and untangle the towel loop by following the other's guidance.
pe-00555:
1) Prepare for a coordination exercise in which students jump in place while moving hands and feet by set rules.
2) Level 1: Jump while closing (gu) and opening (pa) both hands and feet at exactly the same time.
3) Level 2: Try crossed jumps, with hands together and feet apart, or hands apart and feet together.
4) Level 3: Vary the hand and foot combinations further, such as one hand closed and the other open, to build body control.
pe-00556:
1) Stand face to face with a partner (or teacher/parent), hold both hands, and lay out mats to get ready to rotate safely.
2) Step 1: While holding hands, the child looks at their belly button and rolls forward in a forward roll.
3) Step 2: Climb up the partner's legs and flip backward through the air to land, learning the back-flip rotation.
4) Step 3: Reach through the partner's legs to clasp hands, then lift and rotate for a straddle spin that builds different rotation senses.
pe-00557:
1) Place both hands on the floor shoulder-width apart and crouch like a frog.
2) Press firmly into the floor with both hands and kick the hips and legs up into the air.
3) While airborne, clap the soles of the feet together to make a 'clap' sound, then land lightly.
4) After succeeding once, progress to 2 or 3 foot claps in a row, or play rock-paper-scissors with the feet in mid-air.
pe-00558:
1) Line up at the start line and move to the opposite goal imitating different animals.
2) Do the bear walk (hands and feet on the ground, going forward, backward, and turning) and the crocodile crawl on the stomach, one after the other.
3) Move like a rabbit or frog by placing the hands down first and jumping the feet up to them.
4) Build body control with 10 full-body moves in all, including sea otter (lying on the back, pushing with feet), seal (pulling with arm strength), crab (side steps), and kangaroo (two-foot jumps).
pe-00559:
1) Stand on a long rope without stepping off it and swap places to line up in height or birthday order.
2) Stand in a circle, cross hands to grasp others, and untangle the human knot without letting go.
3) Work through cooperation steps in stages: back-to-back stand-ups, a finger-grabbing game, and a hopping 'ken-ken train' where partners hold each other's feet.
4) Throughout, communication among teammates and keeping balance are the key rules for success.
pe-00560:
1) Two students stand face to face and play rock-paper-scissors.
2) The loser runs one full lap around the winner.
3) In the next stage, the loser changes how they circle: feet-together jump (rock jump), legs-apart jump (paper jump), then front-back split jump (scissors jump).
4) In the final stage, the loser circles with a skip, alternating the front and back foot rhythmically, learning the basic skip step naturally through the game.
pe-00561:
1) Build body coordination with marionette jumps, moving the hands and feet to different jump rhythms.
2) Stand on a sheet of newspaper and play rock-paper-scissors; each time you lose, fold the newspaper in half and keep your balance on it.
3) With a partner, practice whole-body balance through palm-slapping and letter-writing movements.
4) Finish with reaction play, dodging a ball made of a bunched-up towel or holding steady on one leg, to complete the sensorimotor work.
pe-00562:
1) Lay a step ladder on the floor and start with the basic rule of passing through each square without stepping on the rungs.
2) Walk or run through with one step per square, then raise the difficulty with two foot-touches per square.
3) Practice the side-moving two-step by standing sideways to the ladder, and the 4-beat in-in-out-out step.
4) Finish with the 3-beat in-in-out step, done facing forward and sideways, to learn footwork and weight shift.
pe-00563:
1) Go through the step ladder quickly with the 4-beat in-in-out-out step and the 3-beat in-in-out step, then sprint out.
2) Jump with both feet together (gu jump), leaping rhythmically from square to square to exit.
3) Do the feet-together-then-apart jump (gu-ba jump) and the ken-ba jump (alternating one-foot and two-foot hops) in and out of the ladder.
4) Finish by standing sideways and passing through the squares with side jumps, feet together, to train lower-body quickness and balance.
pe-00564:
1) Using a mat or the floor, work through 7 balance and flexibility moves that can be done alone, one after another.
2) For the flamingo pose and the horizontal balance, fix the gaze straight ahead and hold steady for 10 seconds.
3) The V-sit balance, with legs straight and raised, builds abdominal and back strength; for the one-hand balance, keep the body in a straight line, reach one arm up, and look forward.
4) With the bridge and the sky tree (shoulder stand / back-supported lift), steadily support the lower back and straighten the body.
pe-00565:
1) Set cones at regular intervals and prepare to practice the three key elements of running in turn: keeping the head still, big arm swings, and running through the finish line.
2) Run a straight lane with the eyes forward and the head steady.
3) In place, train arm swings to a steady rhythm with a big form: one hand up to nose height and the opposite elbow up to shoulder height.
4) Finally, practice running through the line at full speed, without stopping at the finish, to a target beyond it.
pe-00566:
1) Learn the basic throwing motions step by step indoors with a safe towel ball made by knotting the ends of a towel.
2) First hold both ends of the towel and swing it in big circles between the legs and around the body to widen the range of motion of the shoulders and shoulder blades.
3) Toss the towel, tied into a round loop, into the air, clap or strike a pose, and catch it safely with both hands.
4) Facing or back to back with a partner, twist the upper body in a figure-eight to pass the towel ball, then gradually widen the distance and play catch face to face.
pe-00567:
1) Start with one-leg balance in a scarecrow pose for 10 seconds, then extend the leg to the side and the back.
2) From a plank position, lift one arm or one leg and hold it level in a two-point support move.
3) Sit on the floor, lift the legs, and pedal forward and backward like a bicycle to build abdominal strength; then do partner work, holding steady without wobbling as a partner gently pushes or pulls.
4) Move forward, back, and side to side with the hips raised like a spider to build whole-body strength.
pe-00568:
1) Split the feet front and back (scissor stance), shift weight forward and back, and check the timing of the rope passing.
2) Run boldly into the middle of the rope without stopping.
3) Right after jumping the rope once, do not stay in place; exit at once toward the rope turner, and repeat practicing touching the turner's hand or passing between their legs to leave close to the pivot.
4) Once skilled, run in and jump one after another without a break as the rope turns in a continuous figure-8.
pe-00569:
1) Start with the 3-point support: form an equilateral triangle on the floor with both hands and the head, and lift the hips to get the feeling of being upside down.
2) Stand with your back to the wall, place your hands down, and gradually walk your feet up the wall to straighten the body in one line.
3) Once used to the wall, fix the gaze on the floor between the hands and pull the hips up over the shoulders.
4) Try the handstand by kicking up with one leg and touching the wall with the feet, step by step, with a spotter supporting the learner's waist and hips with both hands.
pe-00570:
1) Two students face each other, hold hands, and each lifts one foot to find a V-shaped balance.
2) One lies on the floor while the other stands, holds the lying partner's ankles, and lifts them so the shoulders and hands are vertical.
3) Rest the ankles on the shoulders of a partner in plank position to complete a slide-shaped two-person pyramid; the top student hooks the ankles firmly over the shoulders and tenses the body to hold.
4) After every move, lower the legs slowly together on a signal and dismantle the pose safely.
pe-00571:
1) Start with quick-reaction games that follow the leader's cues, such as Daruma, touching body parts, and 'Lightning'.
2) Lay jump ropes long on the floor and balance-walk along them while avoiding a 'shark'.
3) Toss a towel up, clap or touch a body part, and catch it; then play Bomb Pass, throwing a towel tied into a ball over to the other side.
4) Build balance with the 'hat-wearing Jizo' game: walk slowly with a towel on the head without dropping it.
pe-00572:
1) First get the feel of balancing in place and jumping with the heels slightly raised.
2) While jumping, quickly clap twice or tap the hips or knees twice to learn the rhythm of the double-under.
3) Practice fast arm turning so the rope can go around 30 or more times in 15 seconds, and mix one single jump with one double-under, balancing after each landing.
4) Finally, link double-unders continuously without stopping the rope and raise the target count.
pe-00573:
1) 'Lightning' is a quick-reaction activity: when the signal sounds, drop to the floor fast and hide your belly button.
2) In 'Moving House', cross to the other side in different poses, such as sitting and moving with only the feet, bear walking, or crocodile crawling.
3) In 'Ninja', quietly follow behind the 'it' player and freeze when they turn around, then jump or duck to the signal of a flying shuriken.
4) 'Flip the Fish' is a core activity where a partner flips over a student holding a prone plank so the belly faces up, and in 'Pulling the Radish' group members lie on the floor holding hands while others slowly pull their legs to uproot them.
pe-00574:
1) First practice the basic timing of watching the turning long rope and entering and leaving it smoothly.
2) Practice jumping 3 times inside the rope and leaving, learning the gap so the next person enters as the one ahead jumps; when comfortable, cut it to 2 jumps to shorten the time in the rope.
3) Do reaction training in which the rope turner calls out numbers at random to tell jumpers how many times to jump.
4) Finally, complete the continuous figure-8: moving in a figure-8 pattern, each person jumps just once and the next person follows immediately with no gap.
pe-00575:
1) Work with a partner to make and pass through various poses using only the body to build body control; in the first game, one partner lies down with legs stretched out or forms a tunnel and the other jumps over or crawls under.
2) In the second, play rock-paper-scissors and the loser crawls between the winner's legs or under their body.
3) The third is the 'vacuum cleaner', where one grabs the ankles of a partner holding their legs up and pulls them along like a sled; the fourth is a balance game in which a partner in a push-up hold is gently pushed and pulled to try to knock them off balance.
4) Finally, play a cognitive-reaction step game in which students jump as the leader calls out, or do the opposite of the call.
pe-00576:
1) Throw safe balls made of crumpled newspaper wrapped in tape to reach different goals; in the Bomb Game, scatter newspaper balls on both teams' sides of the center line and, at the start signal, throw them all to the opponent's side.
2) In the Bomb Game, the team with fewer balls on its side at the end wins; in the second game, one student runs away carrying a basket on the head or back while the others throw newspaper balls into it.
3) The third is target knockdown: throw newspaper balls from a set distance to knock down all the upright targets, such as wrap tubes or mini cones.
4) The fourth is umbrella ball toss: open an umbrella upside down on the floor, throw balls into it from a set distance, then flip it over to spill them out at the end.
pe-00577:
1) Use hoops and balls to communicate with group members and build quick reactions; in the first game, the group holds hands in a circle and passes a hula hoop all the way around by stepping through it without letting go.
2) In the second game, jump stop, a partner rolls a hoop along the floor and you time a jump, in place or to the side, to land and stop inside it.
3) In the third, while a hoop is rolling, another student quickly moves in and out of it exchanging hand touches with a partner; in the fourth, hand or pass a ball between the rolling hoops without letting body or ball touch them.
4) The last is a reaction catch: a hoop is held against the wall, then dropped without warning, and you catch it by pinning it to the wall with a ball before it hits the floor.
pe-00578:
1) Take a run-up toward the springboard and push off strongly with both feet.
2) Place both hands on the vaulting box, touch the back of the neck and shoulders to it, and lift the body.
3) Kick the legs up forcefully and use the rebound of arching the body back.
4) Land steadily on both feet on the mat with good balance.
pe-00579:
1) First, jump with both feet together to find a light rhythm and build spring.
2) Turn the rope twice in quick succession during a single jump.
3) On the first turn, spread the arms to the sides and do the basic jump.
4) On the second turn, cross the arms in front of the chest to complete the crossed jump.
pe-00580:
1) On the mat, plant both hands and the crown of the head firmly in a tripod shape and lift the hips.
2) As the hips move past the head, shift the weight so the body forms an L-shape.
3) Kick both legs up and back forcefully while arching the upper body and lower back like a bow.
4) The moment the feet touch the floor, push hard against the floor with both arms, lift the head, and hold the bridge position.
pe-00581:
1) Climb onto the bar and take a support position with one leg swung over and hooked on the front side of the bar.
2) Begin the rotation by leaning the unhooked rear leg and upper body far backward.
3) Once the leg is hooked, kick the rear leg up forcefully and throw the head back to create centrifugal force; as you come back up, do not tuck the chin but pull the hips close to the bar and round the body.
4) At the end of the rotation, turn the wrists over to grip the bar, raise the upper body, and return to the original support position.
pe-00582:
1) Stand properly in front of the mat, bend the knees, and place both hands on the mat shoulder-width apart.
2) Lower the head to look at the belly button and lift the hips high.
3) Round the body and roll forward so the back of the head, not the crown, touches the mat, with the back of the head, back, and lower back touching in that order.
4) Reach the pushing hands forward, land on both feet, and stand up.
pe-00583:
1) Place both hands flat on the mat shoulder-width apart.
2) Gently rest the inner sides of the bent knees on the bent elbows.
3) Keeping the gaze on the mat ahead, slowly shift the weight of the upper body forward.
4) Lift the feet off the floor and balance with the arms and elbows, holding for 10 seconds or more.
pe-00584:
1) In the water, lie on your back looking up at the sky.
2) Spread the hands and feet lightly and relax the whole body as much as possible.
3) Keep the lungs full of air and control the breath so you do not let out too much at once; move the hands and feet slightly to avoid sinking and try to hold the float for 20 seconds.
4) Once comfortable, progress to back-float travel by hugging a kickboard or kicking.
pe-00585:
1) Without jumping, tap the rope on the floor at both sides of the body to find the rhythm.
2) After hitting the floor with one hand, swing that hand behind the back and pass the rope to the opposite side.
3) Raise the other hand overhead and bring it down to strike the floor on the other side.
4) Step lightly left and right while continuing to swing the rope in alternating cross patterns.
pe-00586:
1) Grip a bar at a height that suits your own height firmly with both hands and bend the knees to get ready.
2) Straighten the knees forcefully and jump up so the belly button rises above the bar.
3) Straighten the arms to support your weight, then swing the legs forward and back to build momentum.
4) On a 'one, two, three' rhythm, push back hard and jump down to the landing spot, bending the knees slightly to absorb the shock on landing.
pe-00587:
1) Lie on your back on the mat and bend the knees lightly to get ready.
2) Swing the legs forcefully up and over toward the back of the head to roll the body backward.
3) Firmly support the lower back with both hands to carry the body weight.
4) Stretch both toes straight toward the ceiling, line the body up straight, and hold for 10 seconds or more.
pe-00588:
1) Grip the bar shoulder-width apart, climb up properly, and take the support position.
2) Lean the upper body deeply forward and rotate, keeping the hips bent all the way through.
3) Swing the head widely outward as if drawing a big circle with the upper body, rotating forward.
4) When the rotation ends, bring both feet together and land steadily on the footing where you started.
pe-00589:
1) Stand properly in front of the mat, place both hands on the floor, and kick up into a handstand.
2) When the handstand begins to tip forward, curl up in order: head, back, belly, legs.
3) Support the body weight firmly with both arms and roll so the back of the head and back touch the mat softly.
4) Carry on the rolling momentum, place both feet on the floor, and stand up.
pe-00590:
1) Stand properly on the mat and start rolling backward by sitting down hard onto the hips.
2) Curl the body so the hips, lower back, back, and shoulders touch the mat in that order.
3) Place both hands on the mat beside the ears to support the body and push hard against the floor.
4) Keep the rotation going to the end, land on both feet, and stand up straight.
pe-00591:
1) Start with a short run-up of about 3 steps and step firmly on the takeoff board.
2) On a 'one, two, three' beat, swing both arms deep behind the body.
3) At the moment of jumping, swing both arms forward and down forcefully.
4) In the air, arch back and then fold forward to form the 'ん' (N) shape, and land safely in the sand pit.
pe-00592:
1) Lie face down on a mat with your back to the wall, hands on the floor, and put your feet up on the wall.
2) Walk your feet up the wall one step at a time while bringing your hands steadily closer to the wall.
3) Keeping your gaze on the mat between your hands, straighten the body until your belly is close to the wall.
4) Try to reach a position where your body is parallel with the wall, then walk the hands and feet back to come down safely.
pe-00593:
1) Get ready for bar play, learning different moves by hanging from or supporting the body on the bar.
2) Hang with both hands and feet hooked on like a whole roasted pig and move left and right.
3) Hang in a monkey pose and swing the body front-to-back or side-to-side, or try a chin-up hold.
4) Try hanging upside down with the knees hooked like a bat, or lie belly-down over the bar in the 'airing the futon' pose and rock back and forth.
pe-00594:
1) Prepare an activity that compares and observes two rotating vaults: going over with the neck (shoulders/back) on the box and going over with the head on the box.
2) After a run-up and takeoff, observe the form of placing the hands and neck on the box, arching the body, and landing.
3) For the head spring, observe how the crown of the head is the support point and the arms push off as the body rotates.
4) Analyze the differences between the two moves and learn the timing of arching the body and a safe landing posture.
pe-00595:
1) Jump up onto the bar and get ready for the basic hold, supporting the body with straight arms.
2) With the arms straight, extend the body so the back and legs form a straight line.
3) Look straight ahead rather than at the ground and balance on the pelvis (near the thighs).
4) Once balanced, gradually tilt the body forward to form the swallow shape and even try briefly lifting the hands off the bar.
pe-00596:
1) Prepare an activity that teaches the frog kick, the basic leg movement of breaststroke, step by step.
2) Gently pull the heels toward the buttocks, then flex the ankles outward.
3) Kick diagonally backward as if pushing the water firmly with the soles, then bring both feet together and stretch them out long.
4) Repeat kicking practice holding a kickboard face down, or lying on the back where you can watch your own foot movement.
pe-00597:
1) Lie on your back on the mat, bend the knees, and pull the heels close to the buttocks.
2) Place the palms on the mat beside the ears, turning the fingers toward the shoulders so the thumbs point beside the ears.
3) Push hard against the mat with hands and feet and lift the hips and back, arching the body like a bow.
4) Hold the bridge pose; if flexibility is limited, practice with the head resting on the mat.
pe-00598:
1) Form groups of 5 with 2 on the bottom tier, 2 on the middle tier, and 1 on top; the two bottom students lie on all fours back to back, hips together, in a table (horse) position.
2) The two middle-tier students climb up, placing hands and feet on the bottom tier's waist and shoulder-blade area, and hold firm back to back.
3) The top-tier student signals the middle tier that they are coming up, climbs onto their thighs, finds balance, and spreads both arms.
4) Hold the pose on the completion signal, then come down safely in reverse order.
pe-00599:
1) Pair up in twos: the front person is the base and the back person is the climber.
2) The base student spreads the feet, bends the knees into a horse stance, and keeps the center of gravity low.
3) The climber holds the base's shoulders and steps up one foot at a time onto the upper thighs (near the hip crease) of the base.
4) After both find balance, spread both arms out to the sides on the signal to complete the cactus shape.
pe-00600:
1) Two students stand back to back, one as the Cat and one as the Mouse, and a safe zone is marked with cones.
2) The teacher calls out the name of the Cat or Mouse, or tells a story and suddenly shouts a key word.
3) The student whose name is called runs to the safe zone at once, while the other turns around quickly and chases to tag; the chaser succeeds by tagging before the runner reaches the safe zone.
4) Swap roles and repeat, mixing silly words into the story to sharpen concentration.
pe-00601:
1) Make just enough space for each student to stand, then loosen up with light deep breaths and joint circles.
2) Step in place to the music beat and follow the jumping and stretching moves.
3) Link rhythm moves one after another, such as touching elbow to knee, clapping under the thigh, and tapping the soles of the feet.
4) Connect jumping jacks and full-body cross jumps to build cardiovascular endurance and coordination.
pe-00602:
1) Prepare a bucket, basin, bathtub, or pool and goggles to practice basic underwater breathing.
2) In the bubbling stage, blow out air bubbles through the nose and mouth underwater.
3) In the bobbing stage, exhale underwater, push up to the surface blowing out the last of the air, and immediately take a big breath in.
4) Once comfortable, speed up the up-and-down repetitions to build a continuous breathing rhythm.
pe-00603:
1) Spread students out and have them stand upright, waiting for the signal.
2) On the signal, squat down, place both hands on the floor, and kick both legs back into a push-up position.
3) Pull both legs back toward the chest into a squat, then jump up powerfully and clap overhead.
4) Repeat these four moves 5 to 10 times in a row, and vary it by counting together with a partner or racing for speed.
pe-00604:
1) Set up a run-up lane with a springboard in front of the vault box and plenty of landing mats.
2) Run up, push off the springboard with both feet, and place both hands and the front of the head on top of the box to lift the body.
3) As the body turns upside down, push off the box with hands and head and kick the legs forward over it.
4) Use the rebound to land on both feet on the mat, stand up straight, and raise both arms to finish.
pe-00605:
1) Prepare aids under the horizontal bar, such as a step board, a vault box, and a towel.
2) Step up on the step board and gradually lower the kicking position to learn the feel of the backward pull-over.
3) Use a small step such as a vault box, or have a partner support the back and body as a spotter.
4) Tie the waist to the bar with a towel or support band so the body cannot fall away, and practice rotations safely on your own.
pe-00606:
1) Check that sand or safety mats are under the schoolyard climbing poles, and let each group decide its turn order.
2) Try the Two-Pole Climb, gripping two poles with hands and feet spread apart, and the Ranger Climb, going up using only arm and upper-body strength.
3) Hold an Upside-Down Hang on the pole and compete to see who lasts longest.
4) Try the advanced Koinobori (carp streamer) move, holding the pole with the body floating horizontally.
pe-00607:
1) Crouch down sideways next to the mat in the ready position.
2) While crouched, twist the upper body and place the leading hand on the near edge of the mat first.
3) Place the other hand on the far side of the mat and press firmly into the floor with both hands.
4) Support the weight on both hands, lift the hips and waist over the mat, and land on the other side.
pe-00608:
1) Lay a safety mat right beside a wall and stand with your back to the wall.
2) Following the cartwheel hand-placement steps, place both hands one after the other on the mat and near the wall corner.
3) Kick the legs up so the feet or hips tap the wall for a brief handstand, then lower the legs one at a time while holding, and push off the last hand to stand up.
4) If starting beside the wall feels scary, begin by doing a handstand facing the wall and lowering one foot at a time to the side.
pe-00609:
1) Lie face down on the mat in the seal position, hips lowered toward the floor.
2) Support the weight firmly on the arms and use the spring of the lower body to lift the hips high in one motion.
3) Tuck the head deeply toward the chest and roll so the back of the head, back, and waist touch the mat in that order.
4) Land on the hips and then the soles of the feet and stand up on both feet; this is a mat drill that prepares students for rotating vaults.
pe-00610:
1) Tie a cord across the middle of the court as a low net, place cones behind each side, and form teams of 2 (doubles).
2) Serve with a light toss that is easy to receive, alternate the serve every rally, and have the two teammates take turns hitting like table-tennis doubles.
3) Every hit must be an underhand pass; no-bounce, two-bounce, or one-handed hits are faults, and after hitting the ball the player must run around the back cone to return.
4) Send the ball into the opponent's court with one bounce to keep the rally going; the first team to 10 points wins.
pe-00611:
1) Mark the field with cones; players wear tags on both sides of the waist and start with a free pass from the center.
2) The ball carrier may run forward, but passes may only go sideways or backward.
3) When a defender pulls the carrier's tag and shouts 'Tag!', the carrier's advance stops.
4) After the defense makes 4 tags, possession changes; grounding the ball inside the opponent's goal line scores a try.
pe-00612:
1) Stand in shallow water at the pool and get ready.
2) Hold your breath without fully blowing it out through the nose or mouth, and sink under the water.
3) Push off the bottom and jump up to the surface; just as you come up, blow out with a 'pah' and then take a big breath.
4) Go back under with your lungs full and repeat continuously; once comfortable, move forward little by little as you jump.
pe-00613:
1) In front of the mat, jump off both feet, place both hands on the mat, tuck the head, and start a big forward roll.
2) At the moment the back of the neck touches the mat, swing the feet down hard.
3) When the eyes face the ceiling, arch the waist up in one motion without letting the back touch the mat.
4) Plant both soles on the floor and push the mat hard with the hands to finish in an arched bridge position.
pe-00614:
1) Place a safety mat under the bar and stand supporting yourself on the bar with both hands.
2) Swing the legs forward strongly, using enough momentum to lift the belly fully off the bar, and find the timing of the rotation.
3) As you swing back and the belly touches the bar, bend the waist and knees and wrap the belly around the bar.
4) At the same time, lean the upper body back powerfully to rotate, then turn the wrists to return to the starting support position.
pe-00615:
1) Place a springboard in front of the vault box and lay landing mats to set up the course.
2) Push off the springboard with both feet, place both hands on the front of the box, support the body weight, lift the hips, and straddle-sit on top of the box (mount).
3) While seated, place the hands on the edge of the box and shift weight to slide the hips forward.
4) At the end of the box, push strongly against it with the hands, swing the legs forward, and land safely on the mat with bent knees (dismount).
pe-00616:
1) Give each student a jump rope and spread out so no one collides.
2) Cross the arms, tap the rope on the floor at the sides of the body once, then practice continuous crossed jumps.
3) With hands crossed, switch the tapping side and crossing position with each jump to keep the rhythm.
4) Once single jumps feel easy, try the double-under side swing, combining the floor tap and cross in one jump, and keep repeating without stopping even after mistakes.
pe-00617:
1) Stand in front of the mat, place both hands down, and take a handstand position, at first with a spotter holding you up.
2) At the top of the handstand, keep the gaze steady, arch the back and waist like a bow, and lower the feet to the back of the mat.
3) Absorb the impact of the feet touching down with arm and shoulder strength and finish in an arched bridge position.
4) Once skilled, link the moves continuously to learn the basic feel of the forward handspring.
pe-00618:
1) In pairs, one student becomes the horse on the mat and the other runs up from behind, ready to leap over.
2) Place hands on the horse's back or sides and jump by pushing off strongly with both feet.
3) Spread the legs to the sides to clear the horse safely, push off the hands, and land steadily on both feet.
4) Raise the difficulty step by step, from kneeling (level 1) and lying (level 2) to standing and bending (levels 3-5), and try jumping in a row.
pe-00619:
1) Get ready to jump lightly from foot to foot in place to the song or clapping rhythm.
2) Jump right, left, right and so on, and every time a certain syllable ('sa') comes up in the lyrics, jump forward, then return to the spot on the next beat.
3) When the very last syllable ('se') of the song comes, freeze and strike your own unique pose.
4) When comfortable, extend it to a group version where four or more line up and move together in one direction on the key syllable.
pe-00620:
1) Build a six-station circuit on the field: two-foot cone jumps, hoop hopping (kenpa), long-rope river jumps, standing long jump, elastic-band high jump, and mini hurdles.
2) Students move through the stations in the given order, doing zigzag two-foot jumps, hoop rhythm jumps, wide rope jumps, and more in a row.
3) At the elastic-band high jump and mini hurdles, use the running rhythm (0, 1, 2, 3) to leap over powerfully.
4) Go around the course with friends, measuring records or trying different jumping styles to build whole-body power and jumping ability.
pe-00621:
1) Lay mats in a long line and make room for a run-up.
2) After the run-up, take a hop step and kick up one leg at a time, placing both hands on the mat in turn while twisting the body a half turn.
3) At the highest point in the air, bring both legs together, push the floor away with both hands, and bring the legs down strongly.
4) Turn in the air so you face backward and land on both feet.
pe-00622:
1) Place cones at even intervals to mark the running zone.
2) Do track conditioning drills one after another, such as high knees, butt kicks, and side steps.
3) Stamp the feet with a good rhythm and gradually increase the running speed.
4) Finish by activating the whole body evenly and widening the joints' range of motion for the main exercise that follows.
pe-00623:
1) Stand upright at the end of the mat, ready for a backward roll.
2) Just before the hips touch the floor, place both hands on the mat and start rotating with the knees held straight.
3) As soon as the hips touch down, bring the hands beside the ears, ready to push the mat strongly.
4) Keep the knees fully straight, push the mat hard with the hands, and stand up.
pe-00624:
1) Two rope turners swing the long rope at a steady speed.
2) The jumper runs into the long rope in time with the song and starts jumping.
3) Jump the rope while touching the floor or doing the actions that match the lyrics or chant of 'Mr. Mailman'.
4) After finishing all the actions without being caught, exit the rope safely.
pe-00625:
1) Lay several gym mats and stand in front of them.
2) Place both hands on the mat, touch the back of the head down, and start rotating in a big forward roll.
3) When the feet pass over the face, spread the legs wide to the sides, place both hands on the mat close to the body between the legs, and push hard against the floor.
4) Lean the upper body forward, carry the momentum, and stand up with the legs still apart.
pe-00626:
1) Lay a mat on the gym stage step and set up a thick safety mat below it.
2) Push off strongly with both feet, place both hands on the mat at the edge of the stage, and lift the hips high.
3) Touch the crown of the head to the mat and, as the hips pass over the head, extend the legs and kick up powerfully.
4) Push hard against the floor with the hands, arch the body back, and land lightly on the safety mat.
pe-00627:
1) Run up to the springboard, take the last step on one foot, and spring off the board with both feet.
2) Place both hands firmly on the far edge of the vault box and lift the body.
3) Bring both feet together onto the top of the box in a safe crouch, then find balance and stand up.
4) Jump lightly toward the mat in front, bending the knees slightly to absorb the shock on landing.
pe-00628:
1) Clear the ground under a low bar, then grip the bar with one hand over and one hand under (mixed grip) and lift the body.
2) Hook one leg naturally over the bar on the side of the under-grip hand.
3) Step on the bar with the hooked foot and release the under-grip hand from the bar.
4) Keeping hold with the over-grip hand, turn the body sideways and come down safely to the ground.
pe-00629:
1) Hang from a low bar, gripping firmly with both hands in an overhand grip with the thumbs wrapped around.
2) Lift both legs through the gap between the body and the bar to the front, rotating until hanging upside down, then land.
3) To rotate the other way from behind, bend the knees and jump, lift the hips high, and bring the legs out through the gap as if rolling forward.
4) When the feet safely touch the ground after the rotation, release the hands and stand up.
pe-00630:
1) Two turners swing a long rope, and students first practice the enter, jump, and exit moves on the floor without a rope to the chant 'One, two, hup!'.
2) Follow the magic spell 'One, two, hup!': enter the rope in two steps on 'One, two' and jump over the rope on 'hup'.
3) On the next 'One, two, hup!' beat, quickly exit to the outside of the rope, tracing a figure-8 path.
4) Take turns in order and keep jumping so the figure-8 rope jumping continues without stopping.
pe-00631:
1) Lay a mat under the bar, climb on top of the bar, swing one leg over the front, and set a support position with the legs split front and back and the bar between them.
2) Grip the bar with both hands, swing the upper body far forward with the body weight, and rotate forward.
3) During the rotation, stretch the back and body straight to draw a big circle and keep the wrists soft.
4) As you come up in the second half, hook the back of the knee on the bar, curl the body round, and wrap the wrists back to return to the original support on top of the bar using the swing and rotation.
pe-00632:
1) Set up a safety mat and a platform against the wall and stand facing the wall.
2) Place both hands and the head on the platform in a triangle support and take a run-up and spring toward the wall.
3) Catch the moment the hips pass over the head and touch the wall to learn the timing, then stretch both legs strongly toward the ceiling into a handstand position.
4) Repeat the bow-like arching rebound timing again and again with the wall support.
pe-00633:
1) Line up a run-up springboard, a low one-tier vault box, and a landing mat.
2) Run up, spring off the board powerfully, and step onto the top of the box with one or both feet, loading the body weight.
3) Use the spring on the box to jump forward and dismount safely, landing steadily on both feet with slightly bent knees on the mat.
4) Change the difficulty with different takeoffs (one-foot or two-foot) or striking cool poses in the air to give more success experiences.
pe-00634:
1) Stand in place with space around you, swing both arms back, and bend the knees deeply to load a powerful two-foot takeoff.
2) Jump straight up in place and spread both legs wide apart to the sides in mid-air.
3) At the peak of the jump, reach both hands out to touch your toes simultaneously with your fingertips.
4) Quickly bring both legs back together before touching down and land softly with bent knees, progressing toward a full horizontal 'Superman' straddle.
pe-00635:
1) The two teams face each other on start lines marked with spot markers.
2) On the signal, play rock-paper-scissors with the whole body: the winner advances 3 steps, a tie moves both sides forward 1 step, and the loser stops in place and waits for the next round.
3) Keep playing, and the first person to reach the opposing team's area or the goal line wins.
4) Vary it by changing the way of moving, such as hopping on one foot or jumping with two feet.
pe-00636:
1) Standing on spot markers, jump lightly in place to keep a rhythm and wait for the leader's signal.
2) Jump in the direction the leader points an arm (left, right, up, or down) with the call, turning the body or crouching.
3) At the basic level move in the same direction as the leader; raise the difficulty by changing the rule to jump in the opposite direction.
4) Gradually speed up the tempo of the calls, or combine up-and-down jumps and crouches beyond left and right, and compete in quick reactions.
pe-00637:
1) Space students widely apart and have them take the basic ninja stance, focusing and getting ready.
2) React immediately with a move to the position call of the imaginary shuriken thrown by the leader (teacher).
3) When the leader calls 'Head shuriken!', crouch quickly to dodge, and when 'Foot shuriken!' is called, jump high to dodge.
4) For 'Ninja chop' defend by slapping it away with the hands, and for energy-blast or spinning-attack calls, turn around once or block with the whole body.
pe-00638:
1) Learn basic body skills by rolling a hoop straight ahead and running through it, or giving it backspin and jumping over the returning hoop.
2) Arrange hoops in a circle on the floor, have each student sit inside one, and start a gym version of Fruit Basket.
3) When the leader names a condition (for example, people who ate bread this morning or a certain hoop color), everyone it applies to stands up and moves to an empty hoop.
4) Vary the way of moving, not only running but also hopping on one foot or jumping with two feet.
pe-00639:
1) Mark one end of a roughly 2 m cord or tape with red and wear it behind the waist as a tail.
2) Warm up in stage 1 by sprinting at full speed so the long tail streams in the air and does not drag on the floor.
3) In the main game of stage 2, run freely inside the set area and snatch the end of another student's tail by hand.
4) A student who takes a tail can add it to their own waist and keep running, and a student whose tail was taken can keep trying by grabbing someone else's tail.
pe-00640:
1) Loosen up by jumping lightly in place to the music and shaking both hands.
2) Walk forward striking a V-pose, come back, and then take a horse stance.
3) Repeat the full-body rock-paper-scissors moves (crouch, feet apart front and back, feet apart sideways), do side steps and quick foot steps, then continue with full-body rock-paper-scissors again.
4) Finish by freely shaking body parts and doing kicking moves.
pe-00641:
1) The defending team stands at set positions and keeps jumping rope, while the attacking team's runner jumps rope toward the first defender.
2) With both people still jumping rope, play rock-paper-scissors with the feet or hands.
3) If the attacker wins, advance to the next defender and play again while jumping rope; if the attacker loses, return to the start line.
4) Compete for points by the number of runners or times passed within the time limit.
pe-00642:
1) Standing in place, practice opening both arms out to the sides and bringing them together in front of the chest.
2) Link a jump in which both feet also open to the sides and close together with the arm movement.
3) Take on the opposite-rhythm challenge: spread the legs while the arms close, and bring the legs together while the arms open.
4) Once the moves feel familiar, sing a children's song and keep up the opposite hand-and-foot movement to a steady rhythm.
pe-00643:
1) Each student holds a jump rope and stands at a distance so no one collides.
2) Jump lightly on the toes in place, turning the wrists to practice various basic rope skills, then jump rope while moving through the space.
3) Lay the rope on the floor in a long straight line and jump rope while stepping only on the line.
4) When meeting a classmate coming the other way, play foot rock-paper-scissors while jumping rope, and the loser gives way.
pe-00644:
1) Press the head, shoulders, hips, and heels against a wall to learn a correct standing posture, then step one pace forward.
2) Practice the standing start by bending the knees lightly, shifting weight onto the front foot, and setting off.
3) Repeat quick springy hops on the toes to minimize ground contact time, and learn the arm swing, driving both arms straight forward and back so the upper body does not sway.
4) Finish with a pelvis and hip-joint stretch by lying on the floor and rocking like a roly-poly doll to widen the range of motion.
pe-00646:
1) Step in place to the beat of the traditional children's song 'Antagata Dokosa'.
2) Apply the rule of jumping, changing direction, or striking a pose every time a certain word ('sa') comes up in the song.
3) Change the formation in various ways, such as a single line, two facing lines, or a circle, and keep up the cooperative steps.
4) In the last phrase, each group strikes an agreed group pose to finish the routine.
pe-00648:
1) Place a ball at center court; on the start signal, players from both teams sprint out to claim it.
2) The player who gets the ball dribbles quickly into the opposing half to shoot or passes to a teammate entering behind.
3) Following the signals, later players are sent onto the court one after another, creating numbers-up fast-break situations.
4) After a score or a rebound, possession switches immediately so players practice quick transition play.
pe-00650:
1) Two teams face each other across a low net in this net-game.
2) For a serve or return, bounce the ball on the floor once, then hit it over with the hand or arm.
3) Passes between teammates also use a floor bounce before sending the ball to the other court; if the ball hits the net or goes out, the other team scores.
4) The first team to reach the set score wins.
pe-00651:
1) Lay a step ladder in a long line on the floor; the first runner of each team starts from opposite ends.
2) Runners move forward stepping through the ladder squares with the assigned step (jumps or quick feet).
3) When the two runners meet in the middle, they stop and play Rock-Paper-Scissors; the winner keeps advancing while the losing team's next runner starts immediately to block.
4) The team whose runner first reaches the cone at the opponent's end scores a point.
pe-00652:
1) Every player tucks a tail band (headband) at the back of the waist and stands inside the marked area.
2) On the start signal, players grab opposing players' tails while protecting their own.
3) A player whose tail is pulled moves to the designated waiting area outside the court.
4) When time is up, the team with players still surviving or with more tails taken wins.
pe-00653:
1) A turner in the center keeps turning the rope (a jump rope or long rope) while jumping.
2) Teammates standing around the edge take turns running in, timed to the turning rope.
3) After jumping together in rhythm, each player exits on the other side without catching the rope and swaps with the next person.
4) As levels go up, increase the difficulty with simultaneous jumps or changes in turning direction.
pe-00655:
1) Place several balls on both sides of the hoop at a set distance; two teams (or pairs) each take one side of the hoop.
2) On the start signal, players pick up the basketballs one by one and shoot close to the basket.
3) After a rebound, or whether the shot goes in or not, they quickly grab the next ball and keep shooting continuously.
4) The team that makes more baskets in the set time wins.
pe-00656:
1) Each group lays a step ladder in front of the start line and places a cone at the turning point.
