2) On the signal, each group's first runner passes through the ladder section with fast, short steps.
3) After the ladder, the runner goes around the turning cone and sprints back to the start line.
4) Runners tag the next teammate with a hand clap to swap, and the team whose members all finish first wins.
pe-00658:
1) Inner players sit on the floor with their legs gathered toward the center.
2) Outer players stand and connect with the inner players by holding rolled newspaper sticks from both sides.
3) Controlling their strength so the newspaper does not tear or slip, the outer players slowly walk around in a circle.
4) Inner players feel the centrifugal force and support their bodies; the team succeeds if everyone makes one full turn without a break.
pe-00659:
1) Each team lines up at the start line, and a long rope turning area is set up midway along the course.
2) On the start signal, the runner dashes to the turning long rope and jumps through it without getting caught.
3) After passing the rope, the runner picks up 1 beanbag from the basket at the turning point and returns to the start line.
4) Runners tag the next teammate to swap, and the team that first collects all of its beanbags wins.
pe-00661:
1) Every player wears a tail band (scarf) at the back of the waist and has their own soccer ball.
2) On the start signal, players dribble skillfully with their feet inside the play area.
3) While controlling their own ball, players also pull the tail bands from opponents' waists by hand.
4) While guarding their own tail, the team or individual who collects the most tails within the time limit wins.
pe-00663:
1) Each group lines up in a single file, with each player holding their own jump rope and keeping a steady gap.
2) Players jump rope while running forward.
3) They keep the line formation by matching the rhythm and moving speed of the person ahead, circling the whole gym.
4) The goal is for the whole team to keep the rhythm and finish the course without getting caught on the rope.
pe-00664:
1) On the signal at the start line, the runner sets off holding a small ball.
2) The runner steps through hula hoops laid out at regular intervals and places the ball inside the hoop at the target spot.
3) After setting the ball down safely, the runner quickly returns to the start line and tags the next runner.
4) The whole group runs the relay, and the team that first carries all of its balls wins.
pe-00665:
1) Scatter cones around a wide activity area and pair up in twos.
2) Pairs dribble freely around the area, find an empty cone, and pass back and forth with the cone between them.
3) Pairs search for open space so they do not overlap with other pairs.
4) Within the time limit, each pair completes the set number of successful passes.
pe-00666:
1) Set up two step ladders side by side while group members line up and wait.
2) The whole group moves forward in time with the call, doing jump steps (in-out, in-in-out, etc.) or crossing foot steps at the same beat.
3) When the lead runner moves through the ladder, the next runner follows right away in rhythm; the group succeeds if everyone finishes without catching a foot.
4) For a harder version, run a crossing-step relay with teams facing each other from both ends.
pe-00667:
1) Two players stand back to back and slowly bend their knees to sit in an invisible chair.
2) Once the balance is steady, they stretch both arms overhead or hold the position.
3) If they succeed, add one player on each side, then 3, 4, and so on, gradually lengthening the line of players standing back to back.
4) Everyone pushes against each other's backs and holds with lower-body strength; the group succeeds if all hold the pose without collapsing for the target time.
pe-00669:
1) The tagger (zombie) team moves around the court with a ball to catch the runners, while the runners dodge inside the limited area, watching the zombies' passing lanes and positions.
2) A zombie holding the ball cannot run and tag directly; the ball must travel near a runner only by passing.
3) When a zombie who has received a pass touches a runner with the ball in hand, that runner also becomes a zombie.
4) The runners win if anyone survives to the end of the time limit; the zombies win if they catch every runner in time.
pe-00670:
1) Split into teams marked by pinnie colors, and put 2 handball-sized balls into play at the same time.
2) The attacking team passes without dribbling and advances toward the opponents' goal, while defenders intercept passes or touch the ball carrier to take over possession.
3) With 2 balls in play, players on both teams watch the flow of both balls and move into open space.
4) The team that puts more balls in the handball goal within the time limit wins.
pe-00671:
1) Two turners swing a long rope in a large, steady arc.
2) Teammates waiting outside the rope run in one at a time on the signal and join the jumping.
3) Players inside breathe together and keep jumping in place so the rope does not catch them.
4) The mission is complete when all teammates are inside and succeed in the set number of continuous jumps.
pe-00672:
1) Each player gets a hula hoop, places it around the waist, and waits.
2) On the signal, players swing their hips to keep the hoop spinning without dropping it.
3) Once waist spinning feels easy, they try spinning the hoop lower on the body, such as at the knees or ankles.
4) Keep the hoop spinning continuously without dropping it to the floor for the set time.
pe-00673:
1) Divide roles into a thrower, a target holder, and a ball retriever.
2) The thrower stands on a floor spot and throws the ball accurately through a hula hoop held high.
3) The retriever behind quickly catches the ball that passes through or falls and gives it to the next runner.
4) Extend the game as a relay: hang the hoop on a wall and have throwers move by stepping on step-training spots before throwing.
pe-00675:
1) Split into an offense team and a defense team and practice shooting in the mid-range area around the basket.
2) Stage 1: with no defense, pass the ball around and shoot mid-range shots from assigned spots to learn shooting form and release.
3) Stage 2: defenders gradually guard more actively while the offense creates open chances through passing and takes shots.
4) Stage 3: in a game-like situation with quick ball movement and rebounding battles, players work to make their shots.
pe-00677:
1) Each student holds a ball, stands in place, throws it high, and catches it accurately with both hands.
2) At the next level, throw the ball and jump to catch it in the air, or clap before catching it.
3) Throw the ball, bend down to touch the floor with one or both hands, then stand up and catch it; or step with one or both feet, or turn 360 degrees in place, and then catch it steadily.
4) Complete various body-coordination missions, such as throwing while moving and walking forward to catch.
pe-00678:
1) Place a box of beanbags (or balls) in front of each team's start line, with rope turners waiting at the center with a long rope.
2) On the signal, the first runner takes 1 beanbag from the box, sprints, and jumps through the turning rope at the center without getting caught.
3) After passing the rope safely, the runner leaves the beanbag in the designated zone on the other side and returns, or, in the reverse version, brings one back and puts it in the team box.
4) All teammates run in relay, and the team that moves the most treasure within the time limit wins.
pe-00679:
1) Group members hold hands in a circle to prepare a cooperative activity in which a hula hoop is passed through every body without letting go of hands.
2) Stage 1: while holding hands, move the head, torso, and legs to pass the hoop to the next person.
3) Stage 2: pass the hoop continuously between the legs or under the bodies of group members crouching in a line.
4) Stage 3: extend into a relay in which the runner spins the hoop like a jump rope, jumps through it, and goes around the turning cone and back.
pe-00681:
1) Two people pair up, face each other, and do various body-control exercises with a ball.
2) Stage 1: at close range, one person throws the ball up and the other runs forward to catch it without a bounce, or jumps to catch it.
3) Stage 2: face each other, bend the knees to quickly catch a ball rolled along the floor, and roll it back.
4) Stages 3 and 4: widen the distance and exchange the ball with chest-high passes and high shot-put-style passes to build quickness and coordination.
pe-00682:
1) Line up along a straight line on the floor and step to the rhythm of the traditional children's song "Anta Gata Dokosa."
2) Step in place to the lyrics, and jump back and forth over the line each time the "sa" beat comes.
3) Change formations, such as standing in a row side by side or holding hands in a circle and jumping in and out.
4) Perform unified steps and jumps as a group in time with the beat to build rhythm and cooperation.
pe-00685:
1) In pairs, sit facing each other on the floor with the soles of the feet touching and both hands clasped.
2) On the signal, pull each other at the same time and stand up, balancing with leg strength.
3) After 2 people succeed, gradually increase the number to 3, 4, 6, and 8, sitting together in a circle.
4) As the group grows, cross arms or grip hands firmly and breathe together; the mission succeeds when every member lifts off the floor, stands up completely, and keeps balance.
pe-00686:
1) On a half court, split into offense and defense teams and play a 3-on-3 or 4-on-4 mini basketball game.
2) On the start signal, the offense quickly inbounds the ball from the end line side to create a shooting chance.
3) The defense hustles back from the outside or assigned spots on the signal and plays man-to-man defense.
4) The offense scores by exploiting gaps in the defense with quick passes and dribbles before shooting; if the defense grabs a rebound or steals the ball, they take over possession.
pe-00687:
1) One or two taggers hold a hula hoop near the floor or roll it to act as an obstacle.
2) As the hoop spins or rolls, the other players run in with the right timing and pass through it or jump over it.
3) Players jump continuously over the hoop rolling along the floor without getting caught; when the tagger stands and swings the hoop low and level with the ground, players can also jump in place in time with it like a jump rope.
4) When every member gets through without touching the hoop, raise the difficulty to the next level.
pe-00688:
1) Practice the ninja stand-up: from a kneeling seated position, stand silently using only a swing and a jump, without using the hands.
2) Extend it into a partner activity, holding hands with a friend or family member and standing up at the same time in rhythm.
3) Jump high in place and clap the soles of the feet together in the air, then take on the challenge of clapping the hands as well.
4) In a crawl position with both hands on the floor, keep the hips off the floor and pass the legs between the arms to move forward and back, or draw circles on the floor with the legs, as a full-body coordination movement.
pe-00689:
1) Sit on the floor with legs stretched out and move forward by wiggling the bottom side to side without using the hands (bottom walking).
2) Sit side by side with a friend and race to a target spot, or line up front to back as a train and move together.
3) With the legs as the pivot and both hands on the floor, lift the hips and rotate 360 degrees like the hand of a clock.
4) Apply it as a quiz game: with the hips slightly off the floor, move the body to write a word or number on the floor and have the partner guess it.
pe-00690:
1) To a familiar melody like the children's song "Make a Fist and Open Your Hand," do rhythm exercises that cross or spread and close the hands and feet.
2) Following the teacher's signals or the movement cues in the lyrics, jump with feet apart to the sides or step sideways like a crab.
3) Gradually speed up the tempo and combine clapping with steps to build body control.
4) With the whole class in formation, sing together and match movements to the rhythm as a body-expression game.
pe-00691:
1) Start with the rule "same words, same action": listen to the direction the teacher calls, say it, and jump that way.
2) At the next level, apply "same words, opposite action": shout the same direction the teacher called but jump in the opposite direction.
3) To raise the difficulty, switch to "opposite words, same action": shout the opposite direction while jumping in the direction called.
4) Gradually speed up the clapping tempo or mix up the direction cues randomly to compete in quickness and instant focus.
pe-00692:
1) This is a basic cognitive-reaction game in which players say and do exactly what the tagger or leader says and does.
2) When the leader says "right" while pointing or stepping to the right, the players also say "right" and move the same way.
3) Test reaction speed by gradually speeding up the beat of the signals or mixing front, back, left, and right irregularly.
4) Develop it into a full-body coordination activity by connecting it with hand motions, steps in place, or jumps in place.
pe-00693:
1) Draw a scarecrow-shaped footpad grid on the floor with tape or chalk by connecting 6 squares and 2 triangles.
2) Starting from the start line, move to the scarecrow's head square in rhythm, alternating two-foot jumps and one-foot hops (kenpa).
3) Once comfortable, raise the difficulty by placing a marker such as a bottle cap in a square, passing through without stepping on that square, then standing on one foot to pick it up on the way back.
4) When two or more play, take turns by order and compete to see who succeeds to the end.
pe-00694:
1) Players jump lightly in place, chanting a call in rhythm.
2) At the signal at the end of the chant, everyone strikes one of the agreed animal poses (horse pose, crocodile pose, spider pose, etc.) at the same time.
3) A player who strikes the same animal pose as the tagger or opponent earns a point.
4) As a penalty, players who struck different animal poses hold their pose and turn around once in place.
pe-00695:
1) Stand with both arms stretched out to the sides and touch the opposite hand and foot across the body.
2) First, in front of the body, alternately touch the inside of the left foot with the right hand and the inside of the right foot with the left hand.
3) Next, fold the leg up behind the body and touch the heel or sole with the opposite hand.
4) Alternate front and back moves, gradually speeding up with the beat, and move rhythmically while calling the counts to music or a song.
pe-00696:
1) Tie a knot in the end of a towel and compete to pass through the spinning towel as many times as possible in 30 seconds.
2) Jump to avoid a towel swung along the floor while completing a mission of touching the floor.
3) Crumple the towel into a ball and toss it high and catch it, alone or with a partner.
4) Finally, roll the towel like a bat and hit a towel dangled by a partner or a light ball.
pe-00697:
1) Use hands or feet to keep a balloon from touching the floor for as many hits as possible.
2) Increase to two balloons and use the whole body to raise the keep-up count.
3) Tap the balloon up, quickly touch a wall or a partner's hand, then hit the balloon up again.
4) Finish with a circle of linked hands keeping the balloon alive with feet and body, and a Balloon Bomb game of passing it over a floor line.
pe-00698:
1) Lay a towel, rolled newspaper stick, or jump rope in a long straight line on the floor to make an obstacle line.
2) Practice two-foot side-to-side hops, one-foot flamingo jumps, and kenkenpa (alternating one-foot and two-foot hops).
3) Master various step patterns such as jogging steps and continuous two-foot jumps.
4) Perform all the learned jumps in a row to the rhythm of the children's songs 'Tulip' and 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star.'
pe-00699:
1) Cross two towels or ropes into a plus (+) shape on the floor to make four zones.
2) Jump side to side and front to back across the cross to the rhythm of a traditional children's song.
3) Only when a specific lyric ('sa') comes up, make a quick reaction jump to the front zone and return to the starting spot.
4) Jump one full turn around the cross clockwise or counterclockwise, or jump facing a partner in sync.
pe-00700:
1) Stand on the floor and jump lightly in place to the rhythm of a traditional children's song.
2) While singing and jumping, land with both feet spread wide to the sides the moment a specific lyric ('sa') comes up.
3) In the next stage, perform a freeze mission such as sitting down or stopping on the lyric 'sa.'
4) Progress to an advanced version: hop on one foot (kenken) and land big on two feet at the timing of 'sa.'
pe-00701:
1) Learn the rotation of the neck-spring vault (kubi-hane tobi) and head-spring vault (atama-hane tobi) on the vaulting box.
2) After a run-up, place the hands on the box, extend the toes upward, and rotate the body.
3) For the neck spring, tuck the chin, round the back, and rise using a pendulum-like swing.
4) For the head spring, keep the chin up and the eyes forward, use the neck reflex to extend the body straight, and land.
pe-00702:
1) Hold a whistling javelin rocket ball and stand straddling the throwing line with both feet.
2) With arms spread and eyes on the throwing direction, shift weight back and forth to create a pendulum motion.
3) Load the weight backward, then as it moves forward, turn the front foot toward the target and link hip rotation with the arm swing to throw in an arc.
4) After releasing, finish with a full follow-through of the throwing arm.
pe-00703:
1) Step lightly in place to the music while waving both hands.
2) Extend the arms to the upbeat rhythm and perform the choreography mixing various hand motions and jumps.
3) Face a partner and dance together, matching movements and breathing.
4) To finish, the whole class dances together in sync with plenty of fun.
pe-00704:
1) Divide the class into an attacking team and a defending team, decide who goes first, and have the attackers line up in one file at the start line.
2) The defenders take bowling-pin (pyramid) positions: first row, second row, third row, and one final King.
3) On the signal, attackers play Rock-Paper-Scissors against the first-row defenders in turn; a win advances to the next row, and a loss sends them straight back to the start line to try again from the first row.
4) Beating the final King earns 1 point, and teams switch roles after the time limit (about 3 minutes).
pe-00705:
1) Scatter cones all around the track or play area and give each student one ball.
2) On the signal, each student dribbles toward any cone they like and tries a shot.
3) After hitting a cone or getting close to it, find another cone and keep shooting; confident students aim at far cones and less confident ones at near cones, so everyone plays at their own level.
4) Once students are comfortable, expand to teams of 2-3 playing a mixed attack-and-defense game of stealing the ball and shooting.
pe-00706:
1) Put beanbags (or balls) in front of the start line, and set up upside-down flying discs and a box in order along a straight line ahead.
2) On the start signal, the first runner takes one ball, runs to the nearest disc, places the ball on it, and runs back.
3) Next, carry another ball to the second disc, and put the last ball in the farthest box, then return to finish.
4) Vary it by reversing the order, placing targets randomly, or bringing the balls back in turn, and play as an individual time challenge or a team relay.
pe-00707:
1) Split into batting and fielding teams; the pitcher rolls the ball and the batter kicks it.
2) After kicking, the batter sprints to first base, third base, and then home.
3) After the fielding team catches the ball, every fielder lines up in a row behind the person holding it, raises their arms, and shouts 'Out!'
4) If the batter touches first base before the whole fielding team has lined up, they score 1 point, 2 points for third, and 3 points for home; a ball over the fence or caught on the fly is an immediate out.
pe-00708:
1) Jump in place with 90- or 180-degree turns on the signal of a rhythm drum (such as a paranku) beaten by the teacher.
2) Make different sounds by hitting the drum skin and the rim, and progress to a variation where the sound decides the turning direction (right or left).
3) For jump rope, set cones 2 m apart and pair students up to count one-bounce-per-turn jumps (two-foot jumps) in 30 seconds; the partner counts successes by clapping or pointing in front of the jumper, then they switch roles.
4) Try rhythm variations such as 2, 3, or 4 jumps per turn and the spread-foot (rock-paper-scissors) step.
pe-00709:
1) Set turnaround lines (or cones) every 5 m from the start line up to 50 m and form pairs.
2) Each runner chooses the first turnaround distance that suits their fitness and starts on the teacher's signal.
3) Completing the round trip before the signal that sounds every 30 seconds earns 1 point, and failing to return in time earns 0; run 10 round trips in 5 minutes while the partner records the points on a score card.
4) After 10 trips, lengthen or shorten the turnaround distance for the next set based on the points earned to find your own steady pace.
pe-00710:
1) Divide the court into three vertical lanes (side grids) or diagonal zones (triangle) for a cesto-ball/basketball-style game; as a warm-up, step over a rubber band shifting weight from the back foot to the front foot and practice catching at different distances.
2) A player holding the ball cannot move, so teammates without the ball must find open space and move to support the pass.
3) Use a free-roaming 'freeman' (lucky man) so the offense creates a 3-on-2 advantage.
4) After passing to the basket area, form a triangle around the basket with teammates to shoot or go for the rebound.
pe-00711:
1) In 'Unify the Realm,' about 10 soft volleyballs are placed in the center of the gym, and on the signal everyone grabs balls and tries to hit each other in a survival dodgeball game.
2) A student who is hit goes to the stage (waiting area) and sits; if the person who hit them is later put out, they revive and return to the court, and the last one standing alone on the court unifies the realm.
3) In 'Bring the Balls to Your Base,' divide into 4 teams and compete to carry as many balls as possible from the hoop in the court center to their own base hoop.
4) When the center balls run out, teams may steal balls from opponents' bases, and the team with the most balls when time ends wins.
pe-00712:
1) Move around on the teacher's signal and play Rock-Paper-Scissors with whomever you meet using the whole body.
2) A student who wins three times within one minute goes up on the stage (platform) and waits.
3) Then pair up with the students on the stage to explore and demonstrate new body-based Rock-Paper-Scissors expressions.
4) With your partner, create creative moves such as stretching the whole body wide or curling up small, and share them with the whole class.
pe-00713:
1) In the first game, 'Free Throw Game,' players take turns shooting free throws one-on-one, and the student who makes more of 5 shots wins.
2) Raise the tension by making the fifth shot worth 2 points or giving experienced players a handicap.
3) In the second game, 'Hula Hoop Basketball,' place 2 hula hoops in each team's zone on a regular court; when an attacker catches the ball inside a hoop, defenders cannot interfere, so even less skilled students can shoot calmly.
4) Add a dribble-only lane on each side of the court that only one attacker may enter, so students who struggle to dribble can still receive a pass and create shooting chances.
pe-00714:
1) Push off the springboard in front of the box with both feet and leap.
2) Place both hands on the marked spot at the front of the box top, and lift the hips high during the jump.
3) Tuck the chin to the chest and roll smoothly so the back of the neck touches the box first.
4) After rotating, land on the mat with good balance.
pe-00715:
1) With hands on the hips, lift one knee above hip height into the 'base position.'
2) Pull the toes of the raised foot up so they point forward (upward), and keep the supporting leg's knee straight without bending.
3) Hold the posture for 10-20 seconds, or repeat raising and lowering the leg, to strengthen the iliopsoas.
4) Learn to have the other leg already lifted at the moment the foot touches the ground, cutting ground contact time to about 0.1 seconds.
pe-00716:
1) Reduce fear of water through familiar games such as splashing and imitating animals to help students adapt to the water.
2) Hold hands with friends and dive under together, or play a game of passing through leg tunnels.
3) Repeat breath-holding practice, such as opening the eyes underwater to play Rock-Paper-Scissors.
4) Run a team-vs-team treasure hunt to find various objects and rings sunk on the bottom.
pe-00717:
1) Form buddy pairs (2 per group) who observe and assist each other's stroke form while learning.
2) Check and practice key points of the crawl (freestyle), such as arm motion and head position with the ears, during breathing.
3) For breaststroke, practice gaining propulsion with a kick that pushes water with the soles and with proper hand-foot timing.
4) Take on individual challenges such as swimming 25 m with the fewest strokes possible.
pe-00718:
1) Set the running distance and baton-touch rules, and run a relay in which teams compete to reach a target time.
2) In the face-to-face race, runners start from both sides on the signal and compete to touch the center cone first, building quickness.
3) For baton passes, the outgoing runner sends a start signal when the incoming runner reaches a preset stride mark, and the baton is handed over on that signal.
4) Compare each team's reduced target time and improvement over previous records to calculate points and decide rankings.
pe-00719:
1) A basic swimming challenge to learn various relaxed floating and prone positions in the water.
2) Using aids such as kickboards, repeatedly practice the kenobi (streamline) position by pushing off the wall and stretching the body into a straight line.
3) Learn the kicks, arm motions, and breathing of freestyle and breaststroke step by step in level-based zones (A, B, C).
4) With a partner, observe and assess each other's flow of movement and whether body balance stays intact.
pe-00720:
1) Run over mini hurdles, clearing the obstacles lightly at a steady rhythm.
2) Practice the basics of crossing a 40 m section in a three-step rhythm using a springboard or ground marks.
3) Run all-out along the center line of the course, counting 1-2-3 starting from the landing foot while keeping rhythm and speed.
4) In a group competition, run the set distance and add up the points for time cut from previous records to compare rankings.
pe-00721:
1) Simplify the rules and play area in a modified soccer game so students do not all bunch up around the ball.
2) Side attackers may handle the ball with their hands, quickly linking short passes along the sidelines to create scoring chances.
3) Divide the court into lengthwise grids and create a 3-attackers-vs-1-defender advantage to go for a shot.
4) Adjust numbers to team level, such as 3-vs-2, and play repeatedly against the same team while applying tailored tactics.
pe-00722:
1) The batter hits a stationary ball on a batting tee or a slowly pitched ball and runs the bases to try to score.
2) Even after a runner reaches home, if the defense has not called an out, the runner may continue on a second lap.
3) Fielders can put the batter-runner out only if two of them gather in the out zone near the base before the runner arrives, shout 'Out!', and sit down.
4) To speed up handling hits, start play with a runner always on first base, or apply a rule where 4 fielders gather and sit in the middle of the infield to make an out.
pe-00723:
1) Lead-up Drills: practice 3-step and 5-step rhythmic jumps over mini-hurdles onto a crash mat with soft two-foot landings, plus a 5-step 'Elastic Long Jump' aiming the belly button toward an overhead elastic cord.
2) Find a personalized 5-10m start mark and run a 5- or 7-step rhythmic approach while teammates chant '1-2-1-2-Ton-Gyu-Pan!' to cue a powerful single-foot takeoff.
3) Compare each jumper's 7-step distance against their initial 5-step baseline and sum the growth points across each group to crown a team champion.
pe-00724:
1) Warm-up & Sprints: practice skips, high-knee steps, crossed-arm dashes, and backward runs, followed by 40-60m sprints using fixed-time distance challenges and staggered start lines.
2) Cornering & Baton Drills: practice leaning slightly inward around curves and extending the arm to pass a ring or standard baton inside the takeover zone.
3) Dual-Circle Relay: two teams of 4 run simultaneous half-laps on adjacent left and right circular tracks and sprint into a single shared finish cone placed squarely between the two circles.
pe-00725:
1) Set goal lines at both ends of the field, and each team splits into field players and linemen (keepers) who guard the goal line.
2) Field players pass and dribble the ball with their feet and advance toward the opposing goal line.
3) The ball completely crossing the opposing goal line scores 1 point, and linemen and goalkeepers on the goal line may block incoming balls with their hands.
4) Adjust the difficulty by narrowing the distance between goal lines or changing the goal width with cones.
pe-00726:
1) Place several cardboard box targets near the center line, and both teams line up on their own start lines.
2) On the signal, kick the balls in your own zone to hit the center boxes and push them into the opponent's zone.
3) When a ball goes to the other side, fetch it again or stop a rolled-back ball and keep kicking at the boxes.
4) When the game time ends, the team with more boxes pushed onto the opposing team's side wins.
pe-00727:
1) The attacking team kicks the ball from the start line through a goal line between cones or at a target on top of a cone.
2) The kicker immediately runs to the turnaround cone or hoop zone to score points in a running mission.
3) The defending team quickly catches the rolled ball and returns it to a designated basket or hoop.
4) Points accumulate according to the number of runs or goal-line conditions achieved before the fielders fully retrieve the ball.
pe-00728:
1) Stack several large cardboard boxes as targets near the center dividing line.
2) Each team stands in its own throwing zone and throws foam balls with one or both hands to hit the boxes.
3) Hit the boxes to push them toward the other side, and quickly pick up balls rolling on the floor to keep throwing.
4) When time runs out, the team with more boxes pushed into the opponent's zone scores and wins.
pe-00729:
1) Set up PET bottles as targets inside circular zones at both ends of the court.
2) Teammates pass the ball back and forth, advance into the opponent's half, and score by throwing the ball to knock down a bottle.
3) The scorer who knocks down a bottle must go and stand it back up, record their own point on the scoreboard, and then return.
4) While the scorer resets the target, a temporary numerical advantage arises, so quick counterattacks and passing play are important.
pe-00730:
1) Before the vaulting lesson, learn the safety rules and how to carry and set up the equipment.
2) Lay a non-slip sheet on the floor first, and two students carry the box together, holding both sides in time with a call.
3) Set up the landing mats with two or four students, handles facing down and mats fitted tightly together, and place the springboard.
4) When vaulting, start after a friend gives the 'Go' signal and call out your target move; an observer checks form from the side and shares feedback.
pe-00731:
1) Learn various rotation and dismount skills on the horizontal bar step by step, such as the leg-hook dismount, forward-rotation dismount, and inverted climb.
2) Create a swing while hanging and use a wrist turn-over motion to lift the body naturally and come down.
3) The spotter supports the waist or thighs at the right moment to help acceleration so the rotation does not stall.
4) Start from a low bar suited to your level and gradually raise the difficulty.
pe-00732:
1) Form groups of 4 and divide roles such as filming with a tablet, physically spotting, and observing.
2) The performer first tells group members their practice goal (for example, tucking the chin or rolling on a vaulting box tier) and then performs the move.
3) Group members film the attempt with a tablet and look together at whether it succeeded and which parts were lacking.
4) Review the footage in slow motion, share feedback, and practice repeatedly aiming to succeed on a flat mat by yourself.
pe-00733:
1) Grip the bar shoulder-width with both hands, jump up, and take a front support position with straight arms.
2) Lean the upper body forward while strongly pulling both knees toward the chest to curl into a tight round shape.
3) Rotate smoothly one full turn forward around the bar.
4) When the turn is finished, bring both feet together and land safely on the ground.
pe-00734:
1) Hang from the bar supported by both hands, then swing one leg over the bar and hook it on.
2) Using the leg hooked over the bar as the axis, rotate the body's direction 180 degrees.
3) As you turn, bring the leg off the bar and steady your balance.
4) Jump down toward the ground behind the bar in a stable posture and land.
pe-00735:
1) Hang from the bar with both hands, lean back, and hook one knee over the bar.
2) Keep the other leg straight and swing it back and forth to build a big body swing.
3) At the moment the swing comes forward and up, press on the bar and pull the upper body up strongly.
4) Get on top of the bar, straighten the arms into a support position, then take the leg out to the opposite side and come down.
pe-00736:
1) Run up with a steady approach and push hard off the springboard with both feet.
2) Place both hands on the front of the box, bend the arms naturally, and let the back of the head touch the box.
3) Round the back and waist and roll smoothly over the box as if doing a forward roll.
4) Keep the rotational momentum through the box and land steadily on the mat with both feet.
pe-00737:
1) In a straight-arm support on top of the bar, swing one leg over the bar so the bar sits between the legs.
2) Hook the back of one knee firmly over the bar and set the upper body upright.
3) Lean the upper body forward and rotate one full turn forward around the bar with the hooked leg as the axis.
4) Use the rotation momentum to come back up to the support position on top of the bar, then take the leg back off and land on the ground.
pe-00738:
1) Practice bouncing the ball a set number of times (for example, 3) in place and then catching it with both hands.
2) Once comfortable, bounce hard above head height on the third bounce, then clap or spin one full turn (360 degrees) in place before catching the ball.
3) Make zones with colored cones and dribble freely inside them.
4) On the teacher's signal (for example, boys to red cones, girls to white cones), dribble to the matching cone.
pe-00739:
1) Several students line up side by side and jump together over the long rope coming toward them with kangaroo jumps.
2) When the returning rope passes overhead, crouch down to dodge it so it does not touch the head.
3) In the 'railroad gate' motion, where the rope is swung up and down, jump over it when it goes down and pass through when it goes up.
4) Once students are used to the gate motion, move naturally on to continuous long-rope jumping.
pe-00740:
1) Move along a line in a bear walk with palms spread wide and knees off the floor.
2) Do a bear walk with one leg raised high, or practice cartwheel basics over a rubber-band 'spider web.'
3) Build supporting strength with frog jumps, placing both hands down, spreading the legs, and landing ahead of the hands.
4) Progress to vaulting basics on mats and a sponge box: with no run-up, place hands on the box and spread the legs to jump over.
pe-00741:
1) Hold hands in a circle and play a body game of hopping with spread feet to a children's song.
2) Play full-body Rock-Paper-Scissors and perform a set action (jump, run, etc.) depending on the result.
3) Two students sit back to back with linked arms and stand up together by pushing at the same time, or walk while balancing a rolled newspaper stick on the palm.
4) Draw a circle on the floor with the feet, then run along the line or play push-out and hat-grabbing games inside the circle.
pe-00742:
1) To build arm support strength and a sense of rotation that lead into mat exercises, crawl on a two-line track with knees off the floor in a 'bear train.'
2) Continue with moves that support body weight on the arms, such as one-leg bear walking.
3) Take on the side handstand pose, holding still with the feet lifted while the arms support the body weight.
4) In pairs, play a relay of rolling over the mat while passing a baton, or a bowling game.
pe-00743:
1) Get a feel for throwing and catching with homemade balls made by stuffing newspaper into plastic bags.
2) Practice the basic throwing motion to the rhythm of rock (lean back), scissors (twist), paper (throw).
3) Split into two teams and throw or kick balls over the zone line into each other's court.
4) When time ends, the team with fewer balls left in its own court wins.
pe-00744:
1) One student jumps a short rope while teammates time their jumps to run in and out of it.
2) Two students turn a rope side by side, and the group moves through it in step.
3) Run continuously into a turning long rope and pass through it, or exit by turning back in a V shape.
4) Take on the harder challenge of running through two long ropes crossed in an X, and the whole-class figure-8 marathon jump rope.
pe-00745:
1) Set up a variety of tag games where caught players become taggers or the tagging net grows, and have everyone wear caps or tail bands to tell taggers from runners.
2) Mark four zone bases and, on the signal, move to a neighboring base while avoiding the taggers.
3) Form groups of five in which three hold hands in a circle to protect a runner from the tagger in a circle-defense tag game.
4) Finish with a tag variation where players split into Head, Belly, and Bottom aliens and tag the other teams to convert them to their own side.
pe-00746:
1) Group members stand in a circle and join hands.
2) Without letting go, they move their bodies flexibly to pass through the hula hoop.
3) Pass the hoop to the neighbor so it travels all the way around the circle once.
4) Once comfortable, add rules such as going around twice or passing in reverse, and race the other groups for speed.
pe-00747:
1) Baby Kangaroo Jump: jump forward with feet and knees pressed tightly together, holding a small object between the knees without dropping it.
2) Rhythm Kangaroo: jump to irregular tambourine beats and freeze cleanly whenever the sound stops.
3) Stepping Stones 1-4: hop across floor rings (1) freely, (2) starting strictly with the right foot, (3) starting strictly with the left foot, and (4) in pairs holding hands while syncing jumps.
4) Treasure Carry Relay: teams race across the stepping-stone course carrying a ball as a treasure baton around a turning cone.
pe-00748:
1) Kangaroo Jump & Tricky Tambourine: jump on tiptoes with knees together, jumping only when the tambourine actually rings and holding still on fake outs.
2) Long-Rope Small & Big Waves: jump rhythmically over a swaying rope, pausing the rope briefly at the bottom for beginners.
3) Short-Rope Progression: practice overhead 'Cowboy' swings before advancing from single jumps to continuous forward, backward, and one-foot hops.
4) Mogul Zigzag Turn & Jump-Rope Circuit: hop side-to-side along a stretched elastic cord and rotate through a multi-station circuit combining vault boxes, balance beam, hoops, elastic cords, mats, and jump ropes.
pe-00749:
1) Inchworm Walk & Relay: from standing, bend forward without bending knees to place hands near feet, walk/extend feet backward to plank, then pull hands back to feet; race individually or in team relays once form is solid.
2) Pair Hand-Holding Twist: face a partner holding both hands and rotate, step under legs, cross arms, and twist bodies without ever letting go.
3) Partner Tree Climb: one partner stands braced like a tree trunk while the other climbs onto their back and circles 360 degrees around their torso without touching the floor.
pe-00750:
1) Rope Walk 1-3: walk arms-out with eyes forward along (1) a straight floor rope, (2) an irregularly curved rope, and (3) two parallel curved ropes while holding hands with a partner.
2) Balance Beam 1-4: walk across the beam (1) slowly, (2) at a brisk pace, (3) looking into the distance relying on foot proprioception rather than vision, and (4) executing a 360-degree one-foot turn at the center.
3) Balance Beam Dual-Task 5-6: (5) duck under an approaching rope held by two classmates without falling, and (6) crab-walk sideways along the beam while catching and throwing back a ball.
pe-00751:
1) Two-Stage Frog Hops: build arm support and leg drive with bouncy 'Tree-Frog Hops' and 'Bullfrog Jumps' where both heels land ahead of the hands (focusing on form over speed).
2) Box Support Progression: progress from straddle-mount (narrow hand placement, head up) and squat-on jump to a full straddle vault by placing both hands together near the far front edge of the box.
3) Stuntman Jump & Multi-Box Vaults: leap off the box adding a mid-air clap or body twist to stick a motionless target landing, then link multiple boxes in a continuous vaulting line.
pe-00752:
1) Chase Tag (Oikake-Oni): play 1v1 hand RPS, full-body jump RPS, or 3v3 huddle RPS where winners (or losers in reverse mode) chase opponents, plus audio-cue 'Cat & Mouse' / 'Octopus & Raccoon' group chases.
2) Hand-Holding Tag (Tetsunagi-Oni): tagged runners join hands with the tagger and split into pairs of 2 whenever a chain reaches 4 players.
3) Tokoroten (Jelly-Push) Tag: 1 tagger chases 1 runner while all other students sit in scattered lines of 3-4; when the runner sits at one end of any line, the student at the opposite end is pushed out to become the new runner (if tagger and runner face off across a line, they settle who is 'It' via RPS).
pe-00753:
1) Pre-Bar Floor Games: build arm support and inversion awareness with 'Alligator Walk', 'Injured-Leg Alligator' (dragging the body using arms only), and 'Rescue Squad' (partner wheelbarrow hold).
2) Core Bar Skills: progress from 'Swallow Support' (using a floor wood block for beginners) and 'Roast-Pork Hang' (turning the head and swinging) to 'Forward Roll Dismount' (tucking chin to look at the belly button) and 'Pullover'.
3) Five Bar Play Games: play the 'Swallow Jump Distance Game' (swinging backward from support to land past floor score lines), 'One-Leg Swing', 'Foot-Clapping Hang', 'Upside-Down RPS', and 'Around-the-World (Chikyu-mawari)'.
pe-00754:
1) Circle & Line Simultaneous Catch: in a circle with 1 ball per player, pass or bounce simultaneously to a neighbor, then toss/bounce straight up and rotate bodies to catch the neighbor's ball (in a straight line, the end player sprints to the opposite end to catch).
2) 5m Triangle Hoop Ball Raid: place 3 hoops at the vertices of a 5m triangle with 4 balls in the center; race (1 ball at a time, stealing allowed) to collect 2 balls in your hoop (advance to 2v2v2 pairs collecting 3 of 6 balls).
3) Roll-and-Overtake Relay: roll a ball forward, outrun and catch it past a target line, sprint back, and pass it to the back of the line to relay overhead; vary by having a teammate roll the ball to match the runner's speed.
pe-00755:
1) Divide players into 5v5 teams inside a marked court area.
2) The attacking team must complete 3 consecutive passes among teammates while evading defenders.
3) The player who catches the 3rd pass immediately throws the ball to tag a nearby opponent on the feet or lower legs to score.
4) If the ball is intercepted or recovered by the defense at any point, possession switches immediately and the new attacking team starts their 3-pass count.
pe-00756:
1) Get ready to follow the dance moves in place with the lively music and the on-screen character's guidance.
2) Move to the rhythm using the whole body, such as stretching the legs out to the sides, swinging the arms, and doing frog jumps.
3) Repeat aerobic fitness moves such as jumping jacks and side steps to the beat of the music.
4) Keep going without stopping until the end to build cardiovascular endurance and a sense of rhythm.
pe-00757:
1) Start the fitness dance by stepping lightly in place to the music.
2) Raise the arms, throw punches to the rhythm, and link them with jump moves.
3) Follow the beat and flow of the moves in the video, using the whole body for an aerobic workout.
4) Keep moving until the song ends to build fitness and release stress.
pe-00758:
1) Stand in place and take the basic ready position along with the intro and lyrics of the music.
2) Repeat coordination moves such as jumping jacks, arm crosses, and squat taps to the chorus rhythm.
3) Follow the kicks, running in place, and breakdance steps that come up in the middle of the song to the rhythm.
4) Move the whole body evenly to raise body temperature and loosen up before the main activity.
pe-00759:
1) Crumple a sheet of paper into a small ball and mark a circular zone on the floor with a stuffed toy or objects as your own play area.
2) Use your hand like a tennis racket to bat the ball upward with your palm without catching it, keeping it from dropping to the floor.
3) Stepping outside the circle counts as a fail; you get 3 tries to beat your personal best for the most hits.
4) To make it easier, use a paper plate as a racket; to make it harder, hide one hand behind your back.
pe-00760:
1) Begin an aerobic dance warm-up, following the on-screen moves in place to the music.
2) Step in place to the beat, lifting one leg at a time and swinging the arms.
3) During the "Hey Hey Goodbye" part, wave one hand over your head as if saying goodbye.
4) Combine punches and jumps to raise body temperature and loosen up the whole body.
pe-00761:
1) Start a dance fitness activity, copying various moves in place to "The Gummy Bear Song."
2) Raise the heart rate with light jogging in place and jumping jacks.
3) Stretch by reaching the arms forward, back, and out to the sides while swaying the torso left and right.
4) Keep going with in-place kicks and hip shakes to activate the whole body.
pe-00762:
1) Behind the start line, do one jumping jack, then toss a sock ball underhand at the towel spread on the floor.
2) Step forward with the opposite foot and swing the arm like a pendulum to land the sock ball accurately on the target.
3) When the ball lands on the towel, pick it up and fold the towel in half to shrink the target.
4) After folding it three times, unfold it one step for each hit to bring it back to full size; complete the whole sequence within the time limit to finish the challenge.
pe-00763:
1) Begin a warm-up that combines boxing and fitness moves to the theme song of the movie Rocky.
2) Bounce lightly on the feet to the rhythm in place and take a guard stance.
3) Throw jabs and straight punches to the beat, and add weaving and squat moves.
4) Strengthen the heart and lungs and loosen the whole body with jumping jacks and high knees in place.
pe-00764:
1) Start a dance warm-up, stepping in place and following along to a cheerful pop song.
2) Jog lightly in place to get a feel for the rhythm of the music.
3) Lift the knees high while reaching out the arms, then side-step and sway the hips.
4) Repeat jumping jacks and arm-spreading jumps to loosen the joints and muscles of the whole body.
pe-00765:
1) Begin an aerobic warm-up, copying basic movements in place or around the room to the lyrics of the song "Walking Walking."
2) Walk, hop, and run in place as the song directs, and freeze immediately and hold the stop pose when you hear "stop."
3) Follow the next directions in order: tip toe, jump, swimming, and sleep.
4) In the second half the tempo speeds up, so repeat walking, hopping, running, and stopping at a faster pace.
pe-00766:
1) Start a dance fitness warm-up to the song "Raining Tacos," which students from kindergarten through 5th grade can enjoy.
2) Do aerobic moves in a row to the rhythm, such as stepping in place, lifting the knees, and reaching out the arms.
3) Follow the lyrics and beat with whole-body stretching moves such as jumping jacks and side leg extensions.
4) Repeat a variety of steps and jumps to the upbeat music to raise the heart rate happily and loosen up.
pe-00767:
1) Begin a rhythm warm-up of touching body parts to the children's song "Head, Shoulders, Knees, & Toes."
2) Touch the head, shoulders, knees, and toes accurately with both hands as the lyrics say, then point to the eyes, ears, mouth, and nose on the following lines.
3) After learning the moves at the basic speed, repeat the touches as the music gradually gets faster.
4) Finish the moves through each speed-up stage without losing rhythm or balance.
pe-00768:
1) Follow the Tabata format: 20 seconds of exercise and 10 seconds of rest, repeated for 8 sets.
2) Choose to copy either the Fortnite character dance on the left of the screen or the basic fitness move on the right.
3) Perform a variety of aerobic and strength moves such as jumping lunges, jump rope jumps, side steps, and high knees.
4) On the timer signal, catch your breath during rest and get ready for the next move.
pe-00769:
1) Keep running in place to match the first-person running view on the screen.
2) Jump when a Goomba appears and kick when a Koopa Troopa shows up.
3) Lean left or right to dodge Piranha Plants and fireballs, and punch when a question-mark block appears.
4) Clear the levels, collect coins and power-up stars, defeat the boss Bowser, and rescue Princess Peach.
pe-00770:
1) While the lively party music plays, copy the dances of the on-screen characters or dance freely.
2) When the screen changes to "FREEZE & COPY THE POSE," stop moving immediately.
3) Copy the yoga or stretching silhouette pose shown on screen exactly and hold your balance during the 15-second countdown.
4) When the timer ends and the music returns, continue dancing to build body control.
pe-00771:
1) Follow the Tabata format: 20 seconds of exercise and 10 seconds of rest according to the on-screen countdown.
2) Copy the Marshmello character dance on the left of the screen, or pick the fitness style you prefer from the moves on the right.
3) Over 8 interval cycles, do a variety of whole-body aerobic and rhythm moves such as lunges, jumping jacks, and knee lifts.
4) Keep going to the end without tiring, following the timer and music beat.
pe-00772:
1) When two winter/Christmas-themed choices appear on screen (e.g., sledding vs. snowball fight), silently pick the one you like during the 10 seconds.
2) When choosing time ends, the dance and exercise moves for each choice appear on screen for 30 seconds.
3) Follow the moves of your chosen side energetically while watching the screen.
4) During the 5-second rest and reset after the 30-second activity, catch your breath and get ready for the next question.
pe-00773:
1) While the characters on screen dance to the music, dance freely to the rhythm in party-style moves.
2) When the screen stops and shows the "FREEZE" signal with a yoga/balance silhouette pose, stop moving immediately.
3) Copy the silhouette pose exactly and hold your balance without wobbling during the 10-second countdown.
4) When the countdown ends and the music returns, continue with the next dance party moves.
pe-00774:
1) Start the lesson by loosening up the body with a full-body stretch.
2) Do 8 rounds of bodyweight Tabata fitness (30 seconds of exercise, 10 seconds of rest), then recover with deep breathing and mindfulness breathing.
3) Practice hand-eye coordination with a ball or socks, such as one-handed toss and catch and clap-and-catch.
4) Finish with a cool-down while reviewing the moves in a row.
pe-00775:
1) Find and choose, from two options, the word that rhymes (has the same ending sound) with the given base word.
2) During the countdown, look at the exercise shown for each option while thinking about the answer.
3) When the answer word is revealed, do the exercise matched to that word card (plank, side lunge, burpee, etc.).
4) Each round brings a new word and exercise, training the body and brain together.
pe-00776:
1) Count from 1 to 100 in groups of ten to the music, switching the exercise at each group.
2) Do high knees for 1-10, jumping jacks for 11-20, and lunge hops for 21-30.
3) Do squats for 31-40, mountain climbers for 41-50, jogging in place for 51-60, and twist jumps in place for 61-70.
4) Do push-ups for 71-80, sit-ups for 81-90, and crunches/bicycle moves for 91-100 to reach 100 and finish the full-body workout.
pe-00777:
1) The screen shows a target number (e.g., 5, 7, 4) along with two equations and the exercise matched to each.
2) During the 30-second countdown, read the problem and work out in your head which equation gives the answer.
3) Do the exercise of the character shown with the correct equation (jumping jacks, push-ups, squats, etc.).
4) After the countdown, the answer screen and a highlight video appear; take a 10-second rest and move on to the next round.
pe-00778:
1) Two autumn-themed choices appear (e.g., Thanksgiving vs. Halloween, hayride vs. hot air balloon ride).
2) Check the exercise assigned to each choice (squats, jumping jacks, burpees, planks, etc.) and pick the side you want.
3) Follow the screen to do the exercise for your chosen activity for the set time.
4) During the rest after the exercise, catch your breath and get ready for the next choosing round.
pe-00779:
1) Loosen up first with the light neck, arm, and leg stretches shown on screen.

pe-00856:

2) Dodge approaching obstacles such as hay bales, pumpkins, hats, and flying bananas by jumping, ducking, sidestepping, punching, or kicking.
3) Between stages, figure out which basket hides the food and a Minion, and hold the right yoga/stretch pose to answer.
4) Clear all 3 levels in order and win back the turkey and all the food to finish the run.
pe-00857:
1) Copy the yoga and stretching moves of the Paw Patrol characters on the screen.
2) Relax your body and focus on breathing in and out deeply.
3) Following the on-screen cue, switch to the opposite side as well.
4) Keep your balance for the time limit to build flexibility.
pe-00858:
1) First choose the racer character you want to cheer for on the screen.
2) Do the warm-up move assigned to your racer along with the screen.
3) When the race starts, run in place or cheer hard for your team.
4) Join the mini-game (spot the difference) that appears during the race.
pe-00859:
1) While the music plays, dance and move around freely and with energy.
2) Copy the dance shown, or make up your own creative dance moves.
3) When the music stops, freeze right away in the Minion's yoga pose shown on the screen.
4) Keep going through the mini-games that pop up and meet different Minion characters.
pe-00860:
1) Pick the side you like from the two Disney choices on the screen.
2) Move to the right if you like the right choice, or to the left if you like the left one.
3) When the screen changes, do the exercise that matches the character you chose.
4) Join the running race and spot-the-difference mini-games that appear during the activity.
pe-00861:
1) Help Luigi in the Mushroom Kingdom, now full of ghosts, by running in place and dodging obstacles.
2) Follow the obstacle cues in each level with moves such as jumping, ducking, and punching.
3) Solve quiz challenges such as finding the hidden ghost box or counting the ghosts flying by.
4) In the final lava-floor section, strike the pose shown to escape without falling into the lava.
pe-00862:
1) Copy the yoga poses of the Moana characters shown on the screen exactly.
2) Breathe in and out deeply and focus on releasing tension in body and mind.
3) After a set time, when the screen signal appears, switch to the opposite side.
4) Build your sense of balance and hold each pose with good posture.
pe-00863:
1) Run down a Halloween street collecting candy and dodging the obstacles that come at you.
2) Punch the pumpkins, chop the spider webs, jump over the brooms, and duck under the bats.
3) When a ghost appears, stop moving at once and hold a freeze pose.
4) Dodge the flying skulls and flames with side kicks and sidesteps, and finish all 3 stages.
pe-00864:
1) Run in place and dodge obstacles to find the Christmas presents Olaf lost.
2) Follow the obstacle cues in each level with jumping or dodging moves.
3) Solve the quiz of guessing which bag hides the present, and choose how to escape the snowy path.
4) Finish the mission of catching falling presents in a sack and clear all 3 levels.
pe-00865:
1) Following Mario's adventure on the screen, run and jump in place to dodge obstacles.
2) When a bonus quiz appears, work out which box hides the character and answer.
3) In the kart race stage, dodge obstacles and copy the motion of throwing Koopa shells.
4) Clear the final castle stage and rescue all your friends to succeed.
pe-00866:
1) Dance to the music, creatively acting out the movements of the animals shown, such as a kangaroo, bear, and monkey.
2) When the music stops, freeze completely in place like ice.
3) In the lily-pad stepping-stone mission, jump in place and balance so you do not fall into the water.
4) Through the last round, express each animal's features with your whole body to build body control.
pe-00867:
1) Watching the screen, run in place, jump, and duck to avoid the obstacles in the haunted mansion.
2) Collect coins and use the guessing quiz to find and rescue Toad and Mario hidden behind boxes.
3) Beat the ghosts by pointing the flashlight you picked up toward them.
4) Finally, rescue Princess Peach and escape at full speed from King Boo.
pe-00868:
1) While the upbeat music plays, dance freely or step in place.
2) When the music stops, check the yoga pose shown on the screen (tree pose, warrior pose, downward dog, etc.).
3) Following the on-screen countdown, hold that yoga pose steadily for 10 seconds.
4) Play several rounds to build flexibility and a sense of body balance.
pe-00869:
1) Play a running game in place with Olaf, dodging obstacles to find the missing gift box.
2) In the dance battle stage, stomp or jump in place to match the direction of the arrows at the bottom of the screen.
3) In the mini-game stage, quickly spot the differences between two pictures.
4) Move your whole body doing the exercise that matches the quiz answer in the Elsa and Anna themes.
pe-00870:
1) Watching the screen, run in place, jump, and duck to avoid the obstacles on the track.
2) Dash through the clover tunnel collecting the scattered bonus gold coins.
3) In the leprechaun's hat-shuffle quiz, concentrate and work out which hat hides the magic charm.
4) Level by level, win back all the magic charms and outrun the villain leprechaun.
pe-00871:
1) Look at the two pictures shown side by side on the screen and concentrate on finding the differences for 15 seconds.
2) Check the bodyweight exercise assigned to the answer choice you think is correct (tail, cloud, glasses, etc.).
3) For the 30-second time limit, give your all to the exercise for that choice (jumping jacks, high knees, etc.).
4) Add up the points from each round to see your final fitness and observation rank.
pe-00872:
1) When a this-or-that question appears on the screen (running like Sonic vs. flying like Tails, etc.), choose the side you like.
2) Move left or right to match your choice, or get ready in the exercise stance for that option.
3) When the screen changes, do the exercise for your side during the countdown.
4) In the mid-game race mini-game, run in place at full speed and cheer so the racer you picked comes in first.
pe-00873:
1) Choose which of the two Grinch characters on the screen you want to cheer for as your racer.
2) When the race starts, run hard in place and cheer loudly for your character.
3) In the mini-games between races, find the one picture that is different and use your powers of observation.
4) Over several race rounds, build cardio endurance and whole-body quickness.
pe-00874:
1) Choose the character you think will win: Team Elsa or Team Olaf.
2) When an arrow rising from the bottom of the screen reaches the line, stomp or jump in that direction.
3) Move with exact timing to the beat to fill your team's energy gauge first.
4) Earn points by taking part in the race cheering and spot-the-difference mini-games that appear in between.
pe-00875:
1) Copy exactly the yoga poses shown by the cute Stitch on the screen.
2) Once in the pose, calm your mind and breathe deeply and slowly.
3) Following the announcements, switch to the opposite side to balance left and right.
4) Go in turn through a full-body stretch, a one-leg stand, and a seated meditation pose to build flexibility and relaxation.
pe-00876:
1) Students become Santa's elves and run in place through the forest path on the screen.
2) Jump when a fence appears, and quickly duck when a branch appears.
3) Reach out to grab the gift boxes that appear in the air or on the ground.
4) When the yeti appears, freeze at once, and in the snowball-fight stage, duck out of the way of the incoming snowballs.
pe-00877:
1) Start by jumping lightly on the trampoline with the Basic Bounce.
2) Next, do the Scissors move (feet crossing front and back) and Knee Tucks (pulling the knees up to chest height).
3) Holding the balance bar, continue with Split Jumps (legs wide apart) and in-and-out jumps.
4) Finish with the Skier (jumping side to side like skiing), a jumping turn in place, and the Firewalk move.
pe-00878:
1) Warm up with basic jumps in place on the trampoline, then do interval training for each move.
2) During the rest time after each 20-second exercise (Switch or Rest), bounce lightly and get ready for the next move.
3) When a Shane Games mission appears, turn around on the call (Reverse) or jump on cue.
4) In the Crab Attack mission, dodge the crab's attacks by quickly ducking while in the air.
pe-00879:
1) In Stage 1, punch the incoming fruit, crouch to dodge the junk food, then block and hit the heart boss.
2) In Stage 2, throw uppercuts at the bananas, do low punches in a squat for the watermelons, and defeat the eyeball boss.
3) In Stage 3, throw hammer fists at the limes and rapid speed punches at the blueberries.
4) In the final Stage 4, defend your house by throwing tornado and helicopter punches at the swarming junk food zombies.
pe-00880:
1) Watching the screen, keep running in place as the basic move.
2) Jump over small monsters as they approach, and duck to dodge the purple monsters.
3) When a smiling monster appears, freeze on the spot like ice.
4) In higher levels, do extra missions such as dropping to the floor under the monsters, spinning, and holding the dead bug pose.
pe-00881:
1) On a personal trampoline, do the jumping moves guided on the screen for the set time.
2) Go through a variety of moves for 20 seconds each, such as basic jumps, one-foot jumps, toe jumps, and shoulder-rotation jumps.
3) Rest or switch to another move during the mission, and do the combo jump and dodging missions.
4) Keep your balance and land on the rhythm until the time limit ends.
pe-00882:
1) Pick one of the numbered boxes from 1 to 15 to open a mission.
2) When the animal inside the box is revealed, copy that animal's movement for 20 seconds as exercise.
3) Accurately perform the full-body imitation moves shown, such as the penguin walk, crab walk, frog jump, and duck walk.
4) When a quiz box opens, choose and do the stretch or strength move that matches the quiz answer.
pe-00883:
1) Escaping from the helicopter, jump and stretch both arms and legs to catch the falling equipment.
2) At the fork in the road, choose the volcano or the sea and do the exercise assigned to it for 20 seconds.
3) At the dinosaur nest, tiptoe quietly, and lie down on the floor when the mother dinosaur comes.
4) When the giant dinosaur chases you, sprint in place and jump over or duck under the obstacles.
pe-00884:
1) Warm up the body by jumping lightly in place to the music.
2) When an animal appears on the screen, copy its characteristic movement or arm-flapping motion.
3) Keep up the jumping in place and arm movements to the rhythm.
4) By moving steadily like this, build basic fitness.
pe-00885:
1) In the first part, warm up with flamingo stretches such as one-leg balancing and bending the upper body forward.
2) When the main workout starts, do fitness moves in order to the timer, such as Knee Tucks, Mountain Jacks, and Mountain Climbers.
3) Continue with surfing moves (paddle, pop-up) and ocean-obstacle dodging (jumping, ducking, changing direction) intervals as directed on the screen.
4) After a set time of exercise, finish with flutter kicks and cobra-pose stretches to train the whole body evenly.
pe-00886:
1) Along with the two hosts in the video, do the set exercise as fast as you can for 30 seconds in each round.
2) Round 1 is Heel Clicks, and Round 2 is Shoulder Taps in a plank position.
3) Round 3 is Heel Touches (touching the heels with your hands), and Round 4 is Mountain Climbers.
4) Count your own successful reps during the 30 seconds, and compare them with the score on the screen after each round.
pe-00887:
1) To grow the Grinch's shrunken heart, do heart-rate-raising moves as directed on the screen.
2) During each 30-second timer, link a variety of interval moves such as running in place, jumping, dodging flying objects, kicks, and squats.
3) When the "Freeze" signal appears on the screen, stop moving at once and hold a freeze pose.
4) The heart gauge fills with each exercise completed, and you succeed when it reaches 100%.
pe-00888:
1) To clear the stages in the Minecraft game, move as directed by the instructions on the screen.
2) In levels 1 to 3, dodge obstacles by jumping, ducking, lying on your stomach, and lying on your back, and dance in the dance sections.
3) In level 4, perform fighting moves in a row, such as stomping spiders, kicking creepers, and slashing Endermen with a sword.
4) The goal is to react in time with the on-screen character, survive to the end, and complete the level.
pe-00889:
1) With the whole room turned into lava, move safely using the trampoline and stepping-stone pads.
2) Do a variety of jumps, steps, and kicks on the trampoline to the music.
3) Hop across to the step pads on the floor, do a squat, lunge, or burpee, and then return to the trampoline.
4) When the giant snake and a "FREEZE" warning appear on the screen, stop in place or crouch to dodge the flying flames.
pe-00890:
1) Sit up straight on a chair and get ready when the on-screen countdown signal appears.
2) Do arm circles, crossing and circling both arms left and right, for 20 seconds, then rest for 10 seconds while catching your breath.
3) Next, while seated, do in-out steps, quickly opening both feet outward and bringing them back in, for 20 seconds.
4) Repeat the set of two moves once more to build whole-body circulation and coordination.
pe-00891:
1) Place one hula hoop or a circle of rope on the floor and stand in front of it.
2) Following the on-screen timer and instructions, do stepping and jumping moves in and out of the hoop for 20 seconds.
3) Go through a variety of moves in turn, such as forward hops, backward hops, bear circles, gallops, crab circles, and lava jumps, and catch your breath in the 7-second transition or rest between moves.
4) In the overtime section near the end, keep up with the fast rhythm through split jacks, single steps, and crossover moves.
pe-00892:
1) Each student holds a favorite stuffed toy and stands with plenty of personal space.
2) For 20 seconds, do the up-down move, raising the toy overhead and lowering it close to the floor in a squat, then the circle move, holding the toy with both hands and drawing a big circle.
3) Lift one foot and pass the toy under that leg, or hold the toy between your legs and jump in place.
4) Jog in place with the toy on your shoulder, or sit and repeat leg lifts, picking the toy up with your feet.
pe-00893:
1) Sit up straight on a chair and follow the arm exercises to the on-screen moves and beat.
2) First, do "Arm Angles," crossing both arms to make angles, for 20 seconds.
3) After a 5-second rest, do the "Cabbage Patch" dance move, making fists and swinging them in circles, for 20 seconds.
4) Repeat the set of two moves with rests in between to build upper-body flexibility and a sense of rhythm.
pe-00894:
1) Two students stand back to back or face to face and do cooperative stretching and core exercises using a stuffed toy as the link.
2) Standing back to back, pass the toy over your heads and between your legs in "Overs and Unders" for 35 seconds.
3) Next, still back to back, twist your upper body left and right and hand the toy over in "Twist Switches."
4) Then, sitting face to face, pass the toy while doing sit-ups, and in push-up or plank position, touch the toy with one hand in turn.
pe-00895:
1) Following the on-screen character's moves, swim in place and make your way forward.
2) When shells approach along the floor, time your jump and hop lightly over them.
3) When flying pelicans or jellyfish appear, quickly crouch so they pass over your head.
4) As levels rise, avoid dolphins in a belly-down position (plank/swim) and sharks lying on your back, until you reach the treasure chest.
pe-00896:
1) To defeat the viruses popping up around the world, such as in deserts and train stations, sprint in place to move ahead.
2) Destroy approaching red viruses with kicks and blue or purple viruses with karate chops.
3) Make the motion of eating healthy food when it appears to refill your energy, and avoid candy and other obstacles.
4) When the final boss virus appears, beat it by using superpowers in a row, such as a strong jump and a power kick.
pe-00897:
1) The floor turns into bubbling lava, so follow the screen and jump across stepping stones (spot markers or safe platforms).
2) When a ring of fire appears, jump through it with both feet, and on shrinking stones, balance on one foot.
3) Sit down to dodge incoming fireballs, and hold a push-up plank on the floor against the dragon's fire-breath attack.
4) In the final bonus game, listen for the calls "the floor is lava" and "the sofa is lava" and quickly move to the designated safe zone.
pe-00898:
1) Following Mario and Toad, dodge obstacles, collect coins, and cross safe platforms without touching the lava.
2) Duck to dodge flying flames and obstacles, and balance on one foot on narrowed platforms.
3) Block approaching villains with punches or kicks, and take on the boss with an ice shield and ice-ball throwing motions.
4) In the later bonus round, follow the calls (the floor/sofa is lava) and move quickly without getting caught in the traps.
pe-00899:
1) Follow a video set in world cities such as Chicago, London, Hong Kong and New York, jogging in place and squatting to ride trains and cross terrain.
2) Defeat red viruses with kicks and blue or purple viruses with karate chops.
3) Crouch in a deep squat under bridges, duck flying candy, and mime eating healthy vegetables and fruit.
4) Throw ninja stars at green viruses and finish the final boss with repeated lightning super-power moves.
pe-00900:
1) Imagine you have shrunk and move through a giant garden, dodging huge insects and water drops.
2) Following the video, jump and land on the flower spot of the named color (green, light green, etc.).
3) When a threat such as a giant centipede or spider appears, hop on one foot or hold your balance until it passes.
4) In the bonus game, listen to random color calls like "red" or "green" (ignoring trick words such as "Pickles") and jump quickly to the correct colored flower.
pe-00901:
1) Run energetically in place and jump over approaching baby dinosaur eggs at the right moment.
2) When arrows fly in, duck quickly to dodge them and sprint to the goal star.
3) In Level 2, run in a belly-down position to dodge a pterodactyl overhead; in Level 3, lie on your back to avoid a giant brontosaurus.
4) In Level 4, jump back and forth between rocks on both sides and kick to defeat the boss.
pe-00902:
1) Become an astronaut and sprint across a planet's surface with running-in-place motions.
2) Sit down to dodge meteors falling overhead, and jump with both feet over shooting-star beams sweeping the ground.
3) In Level 2, lie on your stomach to pass a satellite; in Level 3, lie on your back to avoid a giant UFO attack.
4) In Saturn City, glide in a flying pose and punch or kick drones and aliens to rescue your crewmates.
pe-00903:
1) Set your own personal space, stand on a spot marker and face the screen.
2) Pop balloons that float up with high kicks, front kicks or punches matched to their position; when a ladybug appears, score a point and keep stepping in place.
3) After kicking a blue balloon, hold the kicking foot in the air and balance on one leg during the "Freeze!" 3-2-1 countdown.
4) At higher levels, link fast combinations such as two-hand punches, jumping headers and double pops.
pe-00904:
1) Use a sturdy chair, sofa or mat as the pirate ship and clear obstacles from the area before moving.
2) Sit or climb aboard and move the ship forward by running in place and kicking, then mime climbing the anchor rope with upper-body climbing motions.
3) Lean or lie flat to dodge cannonballs, tilt your body to one side to avoid the giant kraken without falling off the ship, and paddle hard with both arms if you fall into the sea.
4) In the final stretch, jump repeatedly with both feet together over rolling barrels to land safely ashore.
pe-00905:
1) Prepare a mat for rolling and candlestick moves, and stretch beforehand to protect the neck and back.
2) Sprint in place to escape a T. rex and jump over obstacles: hop lightly over rocks and cliffs, and duck your head under low caves or branches.
3) Sidestep quickly to avoid falling pillars and obstacles, and perform a floor roll.
4) When a pterosaur swoops overhead, lie on your back and hold a candlestick pose, supporting yourself on your shoulders with legs extended straight up.
pe-00906:
1) Stack buckets vertically into a tall tower in the center of a square zone, and have group members wait on spot markers outside the square.
2) On the signal, throw balls into the bucket tower or hit it to reach the goal.
3) After each success, run in turn to add one more bucket to make the tower taller.
4) Adjust the distance of the spot markers to set the throwing difficulty for each student level.
pe-00907:
1) Mark a haunted-house zone with cones in the center of the gym, place beanbag "candies" around its edge, and have a few taggers wait inside holding pool noodles.
2) On the signal, team members run one at a time from the start line and circle the zone's edge, without entering the inside, to try to grab one beanbag.
3) A runner who brings a beanbag back untagged puts it in the team basket and the next runner goes; a tagged runner must drop the beanbag and return.
4) Play for a set time or until the candies run out, then switch the tagger roles.
pe-00908:
1) Keep a safe distance from classmates and desks, and face the screen.
2) Choose the one you like from the two Fortnite dance moves shown on screen.
3) When the music and timer start, copy your chosen dance to the rhythm for 30 seconds, then catch your breath and get ready for the next move during the 10-second rest.
4) Pick a new dance every round and keep going through the final bonus round.
pe-00909:
1) Check the locomotor movements (walking, marching, fast walking, skipping, crab walking, etc.) given by music, screen and voice.
2) While the music plays, move freely around the space using the instructed movement.
3) When the whistle sounds with a "FREEZE" signal or voice, stop immediately and hold a frozen pose.
4) When a new instruction comes, switch to that movement and keep traveling to build body control.
pe-00910:
1) Two spring-themed choices appear on screen (for example, flying a kite vs. going for a walk, or jump rope vs. jumping jacks).
2) Pick the one you like better, then check the exercise shown below that choice.
3) While the 30-second timer runs, do your chosen exercise with effort.
4) Choose again each round and keep going through a variety of full-body exercises.
pe-00911:
1) Choose the one you like better from the two summer-activity options on each screen.
2) A moment later, see the exercise assigned under each choice (toe touches, running in place, push-ups, etc.).
3) Follow the countdown timer and do your chosen exercise for 30 seconds.
4) Go through the set rounds in order to build cardio endurance and full-body strength together.
pe-00912:
1) When a simple addition problem appears on screen, work out the answer in your head within the 10-second limit.
2) Each answer choice has a different character exercise next to it (stretching, jumping jacks, running, etc.).
3) Copy the exercise that matches the answer you calculated and keep moving during the countdown.
4) When time is up, the correct answer and a check mark appear so you can check it, then move on to the next problem.
pe-00913:
1) Two basketball-related choices appear on screen (for example, left-hand dribble vs. right-hand dribble).
2) Check the exercise assigned next to the choice you prefer (squats, running in place, etc.).
3) Do that exercise energetically to the music for the set time.
4) When the screen changes, check the next question and exercise, and repeat in Tabata style to warm up.
pe-00914:
1) Follow the teacher's demonstration and the on-screen timer, doing each exercise in place for 30 seconds; warm up with cardio and step exercises such as jumping jacks, side leaps and boxer shuffles.
2) Loosen the upper-body joints with arm circles, the washing machine (knee-to-elbow twist), swimmer stretch and shoulder stretch.
3) Sit on the floor and build lower-body flexibility with a one-leg-extended forward fold, butterfly stretch and ankle circles.
4) Finish by strengthening major muscles with knee or toe push-ups, curl-ups and squats, 30 seconds each.
pe-00915:
1) Lay jump ropes out straight on the floor and practice jumping back and forth over the rope with feet together and with double bounces.
2) Straddle the rope and practice spin jumps, turning 180 degrees with each jump.
3) Without jumping, learn the rope-turning motion by swinging the arms slowly and widely behind the back so the rope lands on the floor in front of the feet.
4) Once the rope reliably lands in front of the feet, jump over it slowly, and when skilled, try continuous jumps or turning the rope backward.
pe-00916:
1) Prepare one pull-out tissue (or 3 squares of toilet paper) and drop it from head height.
2) Try to snatch the falling tissue with the opposite hand below belly-button or knee height.
3) Take on variation missions such as tossing it high with one hand, spinning 360 degrees and catching it, or reaching between your legs to catch it.
4) Try harder challenges in a row, like catching it on the top of your foot or with your head without using hands, or doing a push-up after the toss and then catching it.
pe-00917:
