1) Group members line up behind the start line and receive stepping stones (spot markers) and logs (step boards or boxes) matching the number of members.
2) By placing the spot markers and logs on the floor (the river) and stepping on them, every group member must reach the blue island at the midpoint or the far riverbank. The stones are very heavy, so they cannot be thrown or slid and must be placed by hand.
3) If any body part touches the floor (the radioactive river water), the whole team goes back to the start (the previous checkpoint) and begins again.
4) In later rounds, one stepping stone is removed, so teams use creative cooperative strategies such as carrying a teammate on the back or sharing one marker with both feet.
pe-00918:
1) Lie on a floor mat, raise one leg straight up, and balance one shoe upside down on the sole of that foot.
2) Keep the sole level so the shoe does not fall, and slowly roll your torso over to a face-down position.
3) While face down, keep the shoe in place and roll the opposite way to return to the original lying position.
4) If the shoe falls, start again from the first lying position; the goal is to complete the full 360-degree roll within 1 minute.
pe-00919:
1) Each student receives a hula hoop and waits sitting inside it in an open space of the gym.
2) Practice the step-by-step challenges the teacher presents (waist spinning, spinning on the knees and standing up, neck spinning, arm spinning, jumping it like a jump rope, knee spinning, etc.) for 1 minute each; when the music stops or the signal sounds, stop without touching the hoop and listen to the explanation.
3) At the end of the lesson, choose a trick to keep practicing or play "Hula War" with a partner.
4) In Hula War, two students spin hoops at the same time and move toward each other so the hoops bump; whoever keeps their hoop going to the end without dropping it wins.
pe-00920:
1) Lay mats at both ends of the gym as swamps, split into two teams and start a dodgeball game.
2) A player hit by the other team's ball must go onto the opponent's mat (swamp); a trapped player who catches a ball thrown by a teammate without a bounce is rescued and returns to their own side.
3) If a player catches a ball thrown by an opponent directly, the thrower goes into the swamp.
4) The team that sends every opposing player into the mat swamp wins.
pe-00921:
1) Split into two teams facing each other at opposite ends, give each member a number starting from 1, and place a scarf or towel as the "bacon" in the center of the gym.
2) When the teacher calls a number, the player with that number on each team sprints to the center.
3) A player who grabs the scarf first and returns to their own side without being tagged scores; if the grabber is tagged before reaching home, the defending team scores.
4) Call different numbers and repeat for more rounds.
pe-00922:
1) Mark a pirate-ship defense zone in the center with cones, place beanbag "treasures" around it, and have each pirate team stand in a corner hoop.
2) One defending team stands inside the central ship while the other three teams infiltrate for 2 minutes, stealing one treasure at a time and carrying it back to their own hoop.
3) An attacker tagged by a defender inside the zone returns to the team hoop, does 5 jumping jacks, then rejoins, and any beanbag being carried goes back to its original spot.
4) When time is up, count each team's treasures, rotate the defending team and continue with the next round.
pe-00923:
1) Each student takes off one shoe and puts it in a central circle or hoop, then lines up behind the team start line.
2) On the start signal, the first runner of each team sprints to the center, finds their own shoe and puts it on.
3) A runner who has fully put on the shoe returns to the team, high-fives the next runner and goes to the back of the line.
4) The first team whose members have all found and put on their shoes and returned wins; change the way of moving (hopping, skipping, galloping) each round.
pe-00924:
1) Place a long bench at each end of the gym; one player from each team climbs onto the bench at the back of the opposing court to start.
2) Instead of hitting opponents, each team passes the ball to their own teammate standing on the bench at the far end of the opposite court.
3) If the teammate on the bench catches the ball safely without dropping it, the passer also moves over and climbs onto the opposite bench.
4) The first team to get 5 teammates onto the bench wins the round.
pe-00925:
1) Stand mats up to build a box (container) on the opposing court side, and lay a prison mat flat on the floor in each team's territory.
2) From their own side, students throw foam balls into the opponent's container, or cross into the opposing side to throw from close range.
3) A player tagged by an opposing defender holding a ball is trapped on the prison mat; a prisoner who catches a ball thrown by a teammate without a bounce escapes and may return, throw at a container, or shoot at a basketball hoop.
4) If the escaped player makes a basket, their team takes all the balls inside the opponent's container.
pe-00926:
1) The swimmers line up on one end line while the shark (tagger) stands in the center circle zone of the court.
2) When the shark shouts "Shark Attack!", all swimmers sprint to the opposite end line, avoiding the shark.
3) A swimmer tagged on the way across sits down where they were caught and waves both arms while waiting.
4) On the next crossing, another surviving swimmer who high-fives a seated friend rescues them immediately, and they rejoin the game.
pe-00927:
1) A thrower (it) stands in the center circle while everyone else runs clockwise around the edge of the gym dodging the ball; mats are placed in the corners as safe zones.
2) A student hit by the center thrower's ball is out, moves into the center circle and becomes another thrower.
3) The corner mats are safe zones where a hit does not count, but you may stay only 5-10 seconds and must then get out and keep running.
4) Throwers may fetch balls that roll away, but must return inside the center circle before throwing.
pe-00928:
1) Everyone sits on the floor with eyes closed and head down while the teacher quietly walks around and taps heads to assign roles: one tap makes you a villain (tagger), two taps make you a secret agent who rescues citizens.
2) When the game starts on the signal, villains chase the fleeing citizens and tag them by hand.
3) A tagged player sits down on the spot immediately and can only get up when a secret agent comes and taps their shoulder.
4) The round ends when all the secret agents have been tagged and are sitting.
pe-00929:
1) Place big exercise balls (power balls) in the center of the court and line up each team inside its own zone.
2) On the start signal, both teams throw foam balls (dodgeballs) at the center balls to push them over the opponent's goal line.
3) When a big ball fully crosses the opposing team's goal line, that team scores 1 point.
4) Students may step over the line briefly only to pick up a stopped dodgeball and must return to their own zone right away; balls must be released when thrown, and hitting a big ball while holding the ball is a foul.
pe-00930:
1) The kicking team waits in batting order, and the fielding team takes baseball positions such as pitcher, catcher, basemen and outfielders.
2) The pitcher rolls the ball along the ground, and the kicker kicks it and runs hard toward first base.
3) A runner is out if a fielder catches a fly ball before it touches the ground, throws to a base ahead of the runner, or tags the runner between bases by touching them with the ball held in hand.
4) A kicker who safely rounds all the bases and returns home scores 1 point; teams switch roles after 3 outs or when the batting order is finished.
pe-00931:
1) Set an end zone at each end of the field; the defending team starts in the middle of the field and the attacking team gathers in its own end zone.
2) Before starting, the attackers huddle and secretly pass a small eraser to one teammate, hiding it from the defenders.
3) On the signal, all attackers scatter and sprint toward the opposite end zone, dodging the defenders' tags; a tagged player sits down on the spot.
4) After the play ends, if any player who safely reached the far end zone is holding the real eraser, the attacking team scores 1 point.
pe-00932:
1) Make four helipads (landing zones) from 16 cones in four colors, 4 of each; two taggers holding pool noodles stand in the middle while everyone else waits at any helipad they choose.
2) When the teacher calls a move signal such as "Green helipad moves to orange," students in that zone must travel without being tagged.
3) A student tagged while traveling goes back to the helipad they just left.
4) The teacher keeps calling moves between zones one after another to continue the activity.
pe-00933:
1) Scatter colored beanbags on the floor, cover each with a flying disc or ball, and divide students into 4 teams by beanbag color, lined up in single file.
2) On the start signal, the first runner of each team runs out and lifts a cover to check whether it is a beanbag of their own team's color.
3) If it is their color, bring it back to the team; if not, cover it up again and return.
4) The next runner continues, and the first team to collect all the beanbags of its color wins.
pe-00934:
1) Students scatter around the whole space, and each gets a unique number starting from 1.
2) The caller throws the ball up and shouts one number; that student runs to get the ball while everyone else runs far away.
3) When the student with the ball shouts "Stop," everyone freezes on the spot; the ball holder calls out S-P-U-D at a chosen player, takes 4 steps toward them, then throws to hit them.
4) After a hit or a miss, throw the ball up again and call a new number to continue the game.
pe-00935:
1) Mark a jail zone with a line on one side of the court, place a freedom cone at a set distance, and scatter foam balls on the floor.
2) Choose 2-4 taggers; the other runners dash around the play area avoiding them.
3) A student tagged by a tagger is trapped in the jail zone.
4) A free student picks up a foam ball, goes to the freedom cone and throws a pass to a friend in jail; if the friend catches it safely without a bounce, they escape from jail.
pe-00936:
1) Set a start line and a finish line, and divide students into groups of about 5.
2) Each group member keeps one hand on a hula hoop, and the group runs together toward the finish line on the signal.
3) When the teacher shouts "Shipwreck!", the group drops the hoop on the floor and all members race to jump inside it; the first team with everyone inside scores 1 point.
4) Resume running and repeat the process; the team that crosses the finish line first earns bonus points.
pe-00937:
1) Stand a mat up in a square in the center of the gym to make a goal target, and scatter spot markers around it.
2) One student goes inside the mat target to bounce the balls back out.
3) The other students pick up foam balls at the spot markers and shoot basketball shots into the standing mat.
4) The student inside pops each ball back out in all directions like popcorn, while the others move between markers, collect scattered balls and keep practicing shooting with correct form.
pe-00938:
1) Split into two teams on either side of the net, with team members waiting seated on the floor on the opposite side of the court.
2) Each team first chooses one server to stand on the serving line across the net.
3) The server serves toward a teammate seated on the floor across the net; if the seated teammate receives the ball accurately before it touches the ground, that student stands up, moves to the serving line and becomes a new server.
4) The team in which every member has received a serve and become a server wins.
pe-00939:
1) Runners scatter inside a set area (such as half a court) while everyone else lines up in single file at the start line.
2) On the whistle, the first student in line becomes the tagger and dashes into the area.
3) The tagger tags as many runners as possible during about 10 seconds; tagged students go to the back of the waiting line for their next turn.
4) When the whistle blows after 10 seconds, taggers switch quickly and the next student in line comes in as the new tagger.
pe-00940:
1) Place 8 hula hoops in the play area as houses, with one student guarding a key (cone) in each house.
2) The other students are thieves who roam between the houses and try to steal the keys inside.
3) A thief tagged by a homeowner while trying to steal a key immediately moves on to another house and tries again.
4) A thief who steals a key without being tagged swaps roles with the homeowner; the new homeowner guards the key and the former homeowner becomes a thief.
pe-00941:
1) Divide a basketball court in half so each team stays in its own territory and cannot leave it.
2) Players pass or move the ball by rolling it; once holding the ball, a player must pass or roll it within 10 seconds.
3) Rolling the ball across the opposing team's end line scores 1 point; as an option, set up cones behind the end line and award extra points for hitting or knocking them over.
4) When the ball goes out of the court, the first student to reach it raises a hand to claim possession and restarts by rolling it to a teammate.
pe-00942:
1) Split the gym in half with a team on each side, and make targets on the center boundary line by placing a volleyball on top of each cone.
2) Give every student one tennis ball and, on the start signal, throw at the targets in front of the opposing team.
3) The first team to knock off all the volleyballs on the cones by hitting them with balls wins.
4) When going to the center zone to retrieve scattered balls, avoid getting hit, and bring each retrieved ball back to your own throwing zone before throwing.
pe-00993:
1) Line up in teams, put on team pinnies, and set up the 3-tier ladder target at a designated throwing distance.
2) One player from each team steps up to the starting line and tosses 3 bolas toward the ladder target within 30 seconds.
3) Score 3 points for the top blue rung, 2 points for the middle red rung, and 1 point for the bottom white rung, earning 1 bonus point if all three land on the same rung or across all three distinct rungs, racing to reach exactly 21 points.
4) If a team exceeds 21 points their score drops back to 15 points, or modify the game for younger students by playing a simple highest-total-score format after everyone throws.
pe-00994:
1) Line up in teams wearing pinnies and mark a throwing line 3 to 5 meters away from the target mat on the floor.
2) Decide the throwing order with rock-paper-scissors, and players take turns rolling or tossing the weighted toss balls toward the target.
3) Tally the points where the balls come to rest, counting borderline balls toward the closer area, to calculate the team total score.
4) Use an arithmetic math mat requiring 2 numbers and 1 operator symbol to calculate scores, or switch to a race to reach 50 points first.
pe-00995:
1) Set up home plate and bases on the field with a double safety base at first base, dividing students into two teams of 7 to 10 players.
2) Batters hit the ball off the batting tee within 10 seconds using a level, downward, or upper swing and run toward first base.
3) Whenever a hit lands in fair territory, base runners advance around the bases to score 1 point each time they safely cross home plate.
4) Switch offense and defense after all batters in the lineup have batted once through 3 innings, or adjust outfield fielders based on class size.
pe-00996:
1) Divide the court into infield and outfield zones, send one starting outfielder to the opposing side, and put on team pinnies.
2) Start the match with a center jump ball, and the team gaining possession must throw or pass within 5 seconds to hit opposing infielders.
3) Players hit in the infield immediately move to the outfield to attack from behind, and the team with more infielders left after 5 minutes wins each set in a best-of-three match.
4) Restrict teams to a maximum of three consecutive passes before attacking, or adapt the game for younger students using size 4 soft foam balls.
pe-00997:
1) Set up stations for speed ladder, hurdle relay, cross hop, squat forward jump, javelin, and target throw across the gym.
2) Team members rotate through stations performing runs, jumps, and throws safely with foam equipment.
3) Teams accumulate points based on race times, jump counts, total distance, and target accuracy.
4) Conclude the session with the Formula One obstacle course relay combining tumbling, hurdles, and slalom sprinting.
pe-00998:
1) Set up a 7m by 3m (4m for doubles) court with a 40cm net, rackets, and rubber balls.
2) Determine serve by rock-paper-scissors and serve diagonally behind the baseline after one bounce.
3) Players hit the ball on a single bounce alternately into the opponent's court to score in a best-of-three 11-point match.
4) If tied at 10-10, play continues until a 2-point lead, or adjust match targets to 15 or 21 points.
pe-00999:
1) Mark two 5.5m square courts separated by a 12.8m gap without any net in between.
2) Players serve from the 2.5m back service zone using an underhand or smash stroke toward the opposite square.
3) Serves alternate every 3 points regardless of score, scoring by landing the speeder inside the opposing square.
4) Play a best-of-three match to 16 points, utilizing wind rings for windy outdoors or speedlights for night play.
pe-01000:
1) Set a throwing line 3 meters from the Yut board, wear team bibs, and decide the throwing order via rock-paper-scissors.
2) Players take turns throwing a flying disc through the holes on the Yut board to determine how many spaces to advance their tokens on the game board.
3) Catching an opponent's token or hitting Yut/Mo grants a bonus throw up to three times, taken from 1 meter further back.
4) The team that successfully guides all four tokens around the game board back to start wins the match, with throwing distances adjustable by skill level.
pe-01001:
1) Two holders pull both ends of a 40–50 meter rope baton taut, and runners wearing team bibs line up behind the starting line.
2) The first runner grips the sliding baton attached to the rope and sprints along the track around the cones.
3) The runner must firmly strike the plastic touch peg at the end to make an audible sound, officially passing the baton turn.
4) The relay can be modified into one-way sprint, shuttle run, or a 4-sided square track depending on space and group size.
pe-01002:
1) Set up the Velcro target board, mark a throwing line 3 to 5 meters away based on skill level, and wear team bibs.
2) Players take turns throwing Velcro hook balls to stick them onto specific numbered target sections.
3) Teams score points through highest total score, hitting designated assigned numbers, or forming lines on a bingo sheet.
4) The game can be varied by adding physical challenges such as throwing on one foot, with the non-dominant hand, or backwards.
pe-01003:
1) Set up the ramp, strike zone, and bases, then divide players into two teams to assign kicking and fielding.
2) The pitcher rolls the ball up the ramp in a bowling motion, and the kicker kicks the bouncing ball before it hits the ground.
3) Kickers advance around bases to score runs on safe hits, while the fielding team switches sides after making three outs.
4) Adjust the pitching distance according to skill level and use the center perfect strike zone rule for added challenge.
pe-01004:
1) Set up a net on a badminton doubles court and divide players into two teams of 4 to 6 wearing vests.
2) Start play from behind the service line using an underhand hit; players may use any body part including heads and feet.
3) Teams score by sending the ball into open spaces within a maximum of five touches, winning the best 2 out of 3 sets of 15 points.
4) Modify rules by prohibiting instant one-touch returns off serves or requiring minimum passes to encourage team cooperation.
pe-01005:
1) Stand a fun stick upright inside a stacking cup as a target, and mark a starting throw line at an appropriate distance.
2) Players hold another foam stick and throw it forward like a javelin to knock down the standing target stick.
3) A hit only counts if struck directly in the air; any hits resulting from a bounce off the floor are considered invalid.
4) Once mastered, players step further back to increase difficulty or set up multiple target sticks like bowling pins.
pe-01006:
1) Place a target bucket on the floor, mark a throwing line at a set distance, and give each player 4 wooden chopsticks.
2) Players take turns standing behind the line with both feet planted on the floor to toss chopsticks one by one.
3) Count the chopsticks successfully landed inside the bucket across rounds to determine the winner.
4) Adjust the challenge by increasing the throwing distance or requiring players to balance on one foot.
pe-01007:
1) Pair up students facing each other, assigning one as the catcher and the other as the runner or pitcher.
2) The catcher squats in a defensive stance and quickly stands up into a throwing motion toward second base upon the signal.
3) The runner attempts to lead off and steal a base, while the catcher quickly simulates an accurate throw to tag them out.
4) Switch roles and count the number of successful pick-off and throw motions achieved within one minute.
pe-01008:
1) Form lines across the gym or classroom and learn the basic stepping principles of Dutch klompen dancing.
2) Step on the left foot while kicking the right foot diagonally, combining forward-and-backward steps with rhythmic hand claps.
3) Nod your head side-to-side, stomp the beat, and spin in place like a windmill in sync with the folk rhythm.
4) Pair up or transition into circular formations to perform the complete 8-step routine together as an ensemble.
pe-01009:
1) Set up 5 to 10 target pins (such as water bottles) about 5 to 10 paces away and mark a clear foul line.
2) Place a ball inside an eco-bag and practice pendulum swings along with a 4-to-5-step synchronized approach.
3) Lower your knees at the foul line, align your eyes with the target lane, and roll the ball smoothly to knock down targets.
4) Vary the challenge by increasing the distance or placing obstacles like chair legs to aim for high-scoring pins.
pe-01010:
1) Learn the cultural origin of Indian Kathak storytelling dance, adopting the basic skirt-holding posture and foot alignment.
2) Practice the signature 'Indo-Kathak' footwork by alternating foot taps at a 45-degree angle with heel-grounding rhythms.
3) Perform expressive hand gestures (mudras) depicting the sun, moon, stars, river, and lotus blossom alongside slow spins.
4) In small groups, creatively sequence the natural storytelling gestures to perform an Indian myth narrative dance.
pe-01011:
1) Learn bodyweight Tabata movements inspired by cooking actions like grilling meat, chopping octopus, and pounding rice cakes.
2) Follow the teacher's rhythmic counts while performing stationary footwork, arm reaches, and small hops.
3) Students who maintain proper form and keep moving throughout each timed interval complete the challenge.
4) Let students suggest their own favorite cooking actions to create a customized workout routine.
pe-01012:
1) Sit upright on a stable chair with chin tucked and back straight in the ready position.
2) Perform seated exercises sequentially including torso twists, chair dips/lift-offs, and alternating leg raises.
3) Follow the teacher's counts to hold positions or complete target reps to build muscular endurance.
4) Progress the activity by increasing the chair lift hold time or lifting both legs simultaneously.
pe-01013:
1) Learn disc mechanics and practice the pivot movement by keeping one pivot foot firmly planted.
2) Drill overhead catches for high discs and two-handed pancake catches for chest-level discs.
3) Use a towel or soft disc to repeatedly practice backhand and forehand wrist snaps for accurate release.
4) Partner up, gradually increase distance, and execute passes using pivot footwork and designated catching techniques.
pe-01014:
1) Each player takes one paper cup and sets up a basket or target box as the final putting hole.
2) Throw the paper cup from the starting line, move to where it lands, and make subsequent throws from that exact spot.
3) Navigate around obstacles and sink the cup into the target basket; the player with the lowest total stroke count wins.
4) Add a one-stroke penalty rule that resets the throw from a safe spot if the cup lands in an unplayable hazard.
pe-01015:
1) Learn full-body fitness movements adapted from unique careers such as mammoth hunters, firework designers, and divers.
2) Follow the teacher to perform sequential exercises including lunges with spear throws, jump squats, and prone swimming kicks.
3) Complete designated repetitions and hold proper form during each career interval to enhance endurance.
4) Let students design and share their own bodyweight exercise movements based on their dream jobs.
pe-01016:
1) Learn the basic dance steps of sliding back to move forward while waving hands back and forth.
2) Divide into male and female roles to practice forward steps and turns with adjusted postures and graceful hand gestures.
3) Practice the group parade dance responding with call-and-response chants after the lead dancer.
4) Vary the tempo faster or introduce facing cheer formations for group parade performances.
pe-01017:
1) Sit comfortably to roll the neck and shoulders, then clasp hands behind the back and bend forward.
2) Stretch the shoulders and lengthen the obliques on both sides from a seated posture.
3) Extend legs forward to reach for toes, then press hands back to lift hips into a reverse tabletop pose.
4) Lie on the back to twist the bent knee across the body and conclude with complete relaxation in Savasana.
pe-01018:
1) Spread out evenly across the space and step to the beat while getting ready.
2) Perform the funny beginning choreography depicting the surprise of stepping on poop.
3) Synchronize arms and kicks to match the catchy chorus dance together as a whole group.
4) Modify into group battles by staggering entrance cues or adding custom comical motions.
pe-01019:
1) Learn how to hold the Sogo and stick, practicing basic striking motions on both drum face and rim.
2) Master syncopated strikes and the 4-beat sequence hitting head, face, and chest levels.
3) Coordinate drum strikes with rhythmic walking steps, bending knees gently on heel-first landings.
4) Perform a complete synchronized group dance combining all strike patterns to the K-pop song Dynamite.
pe-01020:
1) Stand in place with enough clearance around to ensure safe full-body movement.
2) Perform varied animal actions such as gorilla chest thumping, eagle one-leg balancing, and crab walking to the count.
3) Build core strength and endurance by completing all target repetitions and balance hold durations.
4) Vary the challenge by speeding up movement cadence or competing with peers for extra repetitions.
pe-01021:
1) Stand safely on a mat or flat floor and perform light mobility warm-ups.
2) Execute full-body exercises themed around cooking recipes like kneading pizza dough, burger patty push-ups, and boiling pasta.
3) Complete each designated set and repetition count to build muscular strength and cardiovascular endurance.
4) Modify by inviting students to invent their own creative movements based on favorite dishes.
pe-01022:
1) Prepare five rolled sock balls, place a target basket ten paces away, and stand behind the throwing line.
2) Position the forward foot on the throwing side and align the elbow straight toward the target in dart stance.
3) Release each sock ball in sequence by extending the forearm smoothly from the stationary elbow into the basket.
4) Progressively increase distance or use smaller target containers to challenge throwing accuracy.
pe-01023:
1) Clear surrounding obstacles and stand upright while warming up joints.
2) Follow along with animal movement patterns including frog hops, earthworm crawls, fire hydrant lifts, and flamingo balances.
3) Hold balances and match repetitions to the rhythm and verbal cues to build core stability.
4) Increase difficulty by shortening rest intervals or chaining multiple animal transitions together.
pe-01024:
1) Learn about Maasai tribal culture and form a performance circle with sufficient spacing.
2) Rebound off the balls of the feet with upright posture, leaping straight up as high as possible.
3) Take turns stepping into the center to showcase peak vertical jumps while group members chant rhythmically.
4) Progress from vertical stationary hops to lateral movements, directional shifts, and straddle aerial leaps.
pe-01025:
1) Put on a glove, hold a rolled sock or towel, and warm up your shoulders.
2) Practice overhand and submarine pitching mechanics step-by-step using body rotation.
3) Catch virtual balls from high, chest, and low zones five times each by securing the glove with the bare hand.
4) Switch to a 50-second reaction drill where you jog in place and catch toward randomly called directions.
pe-01026:
1) Each student prepares a scarf and throws it straight up into the air by its corner or center.
2) While it descends, complete designated tasks such as spinning, clapping, or closing eyes before catching it with one hand.
3) Attempt record challenges by kicking it up with the instep, heading it, or keeping it airborne by blowing continuously.
4) Advance to a higher-level challenge by placing it on the face, blowing it upward, clapping, and catching it before it lands.
pe-01027:
1) Understand the background of the Mandingo dance and maintain a joyful facial expression.
2) Master Part 1 movements: basic marching while leaning forward, pushing the floor, eagle wing flaps, and hand reaches.
3) Practice Part 2 movements: swimming steps, shaking hot sand off feet, turns with shoulder shakes, and dusting dirt.
4) Combine all eight movements into a full dance routine and perform together to African rhythmic music.
pe-01028:
1) Sit firmly in the middle of the swing seat and grip the chains wrapping hands inward at shoulder height.
2) Walk backward with feet on the ground and lift legs to feel the natural swinging motion until it stops.
3) Practice pushing and pulling the ropes: pull forward as the swing advances and push back as it retreats.
4) Coordinate leg extension: bend knees at the highest forward point and straighten them at the highest backward point.
pe-01029:
1) Sit in a circle or team layout and learn the words and rules related to traditional Chuseok holidays.
2) Warm up with a cumulative memory word game and a 3-syllable word-chaining quick-response drill.
3) Play seated wrestling on the floor with interlocking grips and maintain a non-contact circle dance holding toilet paper without tearing it.
4) Compete in teams with elephant-trunk spins to attach sticky notes and charades acting out holiday foods without speaking.
pe-01030:
1) Set up four base cones in a diamond layout in the gym or field and divide players into offense and defense.
2) The batter selects toe kick, instep kick, or inside kick based on game situations to kick the rolled ball.
3) After kicking, the batter sprints toward first base, scoring an automatic home run if crossing the designated outfield boundary line.
4) Practice step drills without a ball first or substitute with balloons for progressive kicking mastery.
pe-01031:
1) Each participant holds a plastic straw and balances it horizontally across two fingers to start.
2) Follow the leader's cues to squat, turn a full 360-degree circle, and jump without dropping the straw.
3) Step up to the throwing line and flick the lightweight straw as far forward as possible.
4) Modify by balancing the straw on your head or hand back, or throw it aiming at target hoops and baskets.
pe-01032:
1) Set up a cone as an imaginary defender and warm up with stationary dribbling using wrist snaps.
2) Practice low dribbling with both hands while keeping eyes forward, followed by 180-degree hip-turn direction changes.
3) Execute chest passes pushing from the sternum and shoulder passes stepping forward toward a partner or wall.
4) Apply basketball pivot rules by planting one pivot foot firmly and rotating 90 and 180 degrees to protect the ball.
pe-01033:
1) Firmly stick a post-it note on each participant's forehead or facial area.
2) On start, players try to dislodge the note without hands, using only facial muscles first.
3) If it persists, escalate to shaking the head and then shaking the whole body to drop it first.
4) Change placement spots to cheeks or chin to adjust the difficulty level.
pe-01034:
1) Pairs form houses (sauce) holding hands around one player (fried chicken), with a tagger in the center.
2) When tagger calls "Fried", insides run; when "Sauce", houses must reform with a new partner at another spot.
3) When "Half & Half" is called, everyone scrambles to form completely new trios, and the left-out player becomes tagger.
4) Theme and call-outs can be altered to Sweet & Sour Pork, Jajangmyeon, or other food sets.
pe-01035:
1) Choose one tagger and give all players stacking cups, with the tagger holding a different color.
2) Each player balances a cup upside down on the back of four fingers kept flat together.
3) Flee from the tagger while carefully balancing the wobbly cup on the hand without holding it.
4) Players are out if tagged or if their cup falls, and the last surviving player becomes the next tagger.
pe-01036:
1) Players stand in a circle with two facing players each holding a ball of different sizes.
2) On start, players rapidly pass both balls in the same direction around the circle to their right.
3) The trailing ball acts as the cat trying to catch up with the leading ball acting as the mouse.
4) If a ball drops, that player picks it up, and the round ends when both balls reach the same person.
pe-01037:
1) Fielders sit in a circle on the floor with legs spread wide, while runners stand inside the circle.
2) Sitting fielders slide or pass soft flying discs along the floor to tag the runners below the waist.
3) Runners dash through the fielders' open legs, loop around the outer boundary, and sprint back inside.
4) Successfully circling back scores a point, while being hit by a flying disc results in an out.
pe-01038:
1) Set up 5 hula hoops on the gym floor labeled with traditional target points (1 to 5 points).
2) Divide students into two teams and take turns tossing soft flying discs toward the hoops from a line.
3) Points inside the hoops are added up, and the team that hits the exact target score (30 points) wins.
4) If a team's total score exceeds 30 points, the round's points are voided and the turn passes to opponents.
pe-01039:
1) Mark a wavy floor track leading to a desk and line up students into relay teams.
2) Runners extend both arms like a scarecrow, balancing a stacking cup on each palm and on the head.
3) Follow the wavy track, place the balanced cups on the desk, and collaboratively build a cup pyramid.
4) Clap hands upon placing the cups to signal the next runner, and the team that completes a 4-3-2-1 pyramid first wins.
pe-01040:
1) One player is chosen as the tagger facing the wall, others stand at the starting line, and spot markers are placed on the floor as safe zones.
2) Players advance while the tagger chants, freezing as the chant ends, and players stepping on a spot marker cannot be tagged.
3) Players imitate assigned poses like a frog or walking cane while approaching to touch the tagger and run back safely.
4) Gradually decrease the number of safety markers or change movement themes to increase challenge and engagement.
pe-01041:
1) Students pair up facing each other and practice the fundamental clapping rhythm sequences.
2) Clap to the song tempo, alternating between personal claps and high-fiving partners to match the beat.
3) Execute highlighted accent actions such as high overhead claps or fist touches in sync with the chorus lyrics.
4) Increase tempo gradually or form a four-person circle to attempt criss-cross hand clapping routines.
pe-01042:
1) Arrange stacks cups in a cross pattern on a table with a center cup and assign colors to each team.
2) On the start cue, teammates take turns bouncing a ping-pong ball once onto the table toward the cups.
3) When a ball lands in a cup, flip it upright immediately, even if it lands in an opposing team's cup.
4) The team that flips all their assigned colored cups and successfully lands a ball in the center cup wins.
pe-01043:
1) Each student tucks a scarf lightly into the back of their waistband like a tail and spreads out across the designated area.
2) On the starting signal, students run around trying to pull scarves from their peers while protecting their own tail.
3) Players are not eliminated when tagged; instead, the player who collects the most scarves within the time limit wins.
4) The game can be varied by having each student wear two scarves or by playing in pairs.
pe-01044:
1) Students pair up on yoga mats facing each other or lying side by side to prepare for stretching movements.
2) Follow the teacher's instructions to perform sequential core exercises including bridge poses, cat stretches, and leg lifts.
3) Partners brace against each other's feet or hands to maintain balance and hold correct posture for 10-20 seconds.
4) The difficulty can be adapted by extending hold times or playing rock-paper-scissors where the loser holds an extra set.
pe-01045:
1) Arrange various colored spot markers on the floor at regular intervals and have two students face each other.
2) On the signal, students execute rapid footwork and sprint toward the specific colored spot marker called by the teacher.
3) The student who reaches the designated marker first and accurately steps on or tags it earns a point.
4) The activity can be modified into marker-flipping battles or integrated with dribbling footwork relays.
pe-01046:
1) Position a sturdy classroom chair in an open space and stand with proper posture facing or in front of the chair.
2) On the start signal, repeatedly perform chair squats by lightly touching the chair seat with the hips and standing back up.
3) Count and record how many correct repetitions are completed within a 10-second limit to beat personal bests.
4) The challenge can be modified by extending the time to 15-20 seconds or pairing up with a partner who counts.
pe-01047:
1) Warm up thoroughly by marching in place and performing full-body joint stretches.
2) Follow the upbeat rhythm while executing basic squats, squat kicks, and punch squats.
3) Build muscular endurance through wide squats, jump squats, and alternating lunge knee-ups.
4) Increase the challenge by expanding repetitions from four to eight or integrating side lunge combos.
pe-01048:
1) Set up agility cones with suitable intervals to secure ample space for lateral movement.
2) Perform rapid side-steps back and forth for 20 seconds, counting each cone touch to test agility.
3) Run a quick shuttle sprint to touch the cone and return immediately to record reaction time.
4) Increase running distances or add multi-directional turning cones to enhance the agility challenge.
pe-01049:
1) Warm up thoroughly for four minutes with full-body stretches to prepare your heart and muscles.
2) Learn eight distinct exercises: jumping jacks, high knees, mountain climbers, planks, push-ups, butt kicks, side steps, and short pitches.
3) Perform each exercise for 20 seconds of maximum effort followed by 10 seconds of active recovery.
4) Modify intensity by resting knees during push-ups or adjusting jump tempo based on individual stamina.
pe-01050:
1) Place exercise mats flat on the floor and begin with gentle breathing and joint loosening exercises.
2) Practice cat-cow poses and deep shoulder needle-threading twists to mobilize your spine.
3) Engage your core with glute kickbacks and bird-dog extensions before transitioning into downward dog and half-moon balance poses.
4) Progress by increasing the holding duration from 5 to 10 seconds or coordinating poses in pairs.
pe-01051:
1) Grip the spoband loops firmly and warm up with in-place marching and light full-body rotations.
2) Hold both ends overhead to perform full shoulder pass-throughs and overhead lateral side stretches.
3) Step firmly onto the band center to execute front kicks, side kicks, seated band rows, and leg lifts.
4) Increase resistance by gripping inner loops or holding terminal extensions for longer counts.
pe-01052:
1) Teammates stand side-by-side holding hands in a straight line with three beanbags placed on an upturned disc cone at each end.
2) On the start signal, the student on the far left picks up one beanbag and the whole connected line moves together to place it on the opposite cone.
3) Once all three beanbags are transported across, the person on the opposite end carries them back one by one in the same cooperative way.
4) The team that transports all beanbags back and forth without breaking hands wins, and larger team sizes increase the turning radius and challenge.
pe-01053:
1) Students pair up and face each other across the activity space to prepare for rock-paper-scissors.
2) The loser crawls through the winner's straddled legs and attaches behind them by holding their shoulders to form a small train.
3) The front leaders of the trains meet and duel; the losing train's members all crawl through the winning train's legs and join the back.
4) The game continues until all players merge into a single massive caterpillar line, praising the leaders at both ends.
pe-01054:
1) Set up boundaries where each player balances a spot marker (pizza) on their open palm and wears two wristbands to represent three lives.
2) Move around the area trying to knock off opponents' spot markers while keeping your own balanced on your palm.
3) Each time a pizza drops to the floor, players discard one wristband, and losing all three lives results in elimination from the playing area.
4) The game can be adapted by shrinking the play zone over time or playing in teams to see which group keeps the most players alive.
pe-01055:
1) Form a large circle where all students face forward toward their classmate's back with hands ready.
2) Tap the shoulders of the classmate in front a specified number of times (e.g., 8, 4, 2, 1 taps) in rhythm, then turn around to tap the opposite person.
3) Reduce the tap count progressively, and immediately after the final single tap, everyone quickly crouches down together to stop the clock.
4) The teacher can set a target record to beat or have small groups compete against each other to foster teamwork.
pe-01056:
1) Select 1-2 taggers while all other runners balance a spot marker (pizza) on their palm and walk within the court boundaries.
2) When a tagger knocks off a runner's pizza, that runner must freeze in place holding one arm high overhead.
3) A teammate must approach, pick up the dropped pizza, and place it back on the frozen player's hand without dropping their own to unfreeze them.
4) If more than a target number of players remain frozen by the end of the round, the group performs a joint fitness challenge like jumping jacks or squats.
pe-01057:
1) Warm up the whole body by performing arm walks, taking five hand steps forward into a plank and five steps back.
2) Move around on all fours keeping knees and bellies off the floor while trying to tag opponents' backs of hands.
3) Score 1 point each time you successfully tap a peer's hand, then immediately look for a different partner to challenge.
4) Play as 1-on-1 pairs or count total touches within a team over a 1-minute period for group competition.
pe-01058:
1) Set spot markers at the starting line and turning point, divide students into teams of about four, and distribute cones to each runner.
2) The first two runners sprint to place and stack their cones on the marker one by one before tagging the next teammate.
3) The remaining runners run out sequentially to unstack and retrieve the cones one by one back to the base.
4) The team that finishes placing and retrieving all cones first wins, and cone distance or stacking sequence can be adjusted.
pe-01059:
1) Two teams form concentric circular paths facing opposite directions, each designating a lead runner.
2) On the start signal, the first runner sprints one and a half laps around the outside of the group formation.
3) Upon completing the lap, the runner stands facing the reversed direction, and the next teammate sprints out.
4) The team whose members all successfully finish running and turn around to face backwards wins the game.
pe-01060:
1) Four students form a group where the center two link arms tightly and the two outer students grasp their shoulders.
2) The group begins walking in a circle in sync, establishing steady rotational rhythm and momentum together.
3) As rotation speeds up, the outer two lift their legs off the ground simultaneously while center runners spin them safely.
4) The team succeeds if they maintain full grip for several complete rotations without tripping or separating.
pe-01061:
1) Form teams behind the starting line and place numbered spot markers on the floor like stepping stones.
2) On the signal, the runner advances toward the turning point by stepping only on spot markers placed ahead by teammates.
3) After touching the turning line, return to the starting line using the same relay method.
4) Rank teams by finish order, or introduce variations like wider marker spacing or one-legged hopping.
pe-01062:
1) Form groups of four where three players hold a hula hoop (one central VIP and two bodyguards) while the remaining player becomes the tagger.
2) The tagger attempts to tag the VIP's back within a time limit of 15 to 20 seconds while bodyguards rotate to defend.
3) The tagger scores by successfully tagging the VIP before time runs out, after which roles rotate among players.
4) Vary the challenge by restricting movement around a cone or having defenders hold the hoop behind their backs.
pe-01063:
1) Place a 30-egg tray in the center of the table and give two opposing players or teams different colored ping pong balls.
2) Determine player order with rock-paper-scissors and bounce balls off the tabletop into the carton cups.
3) The first player to align three of their balls horizontally, vertically, or diagonally wins the round.
4) Retrieve missed balls immediately to continue, and increase difficulty by separating the throwing desks.
pe-01064:
1) Teams form two separate circles holding hands on the court while starting runners line up holding a baton.
2) On the signal, runners sprint around their own team circle first, then cross over to circle the opposing team in a figure-eight path.
3) Teammates shrink their circle tightly to shorten their runner's path, while the opposing team expands wide to lengthen the runner's path.
4) The runner returns to pass the baton to the next teammate, and the first team whose runners all finish wins.
pe-01065:
1) Two players face each other standing with their heels and toes completely touching together.
2) Play rock-paper-scissors, and the loser must step one foot outward as wide as possible keeping feet grounded.
3) Repeat rounds until a player falls, touches the floor with their hands, or cannot widen their stance any further.
4) Once mastered horizontally, vary the game into a front-to-back stride challenge where comebacks are possible.
pe-01066:
1) Place three spot markers at the starting line with the runner standing on them.
2) Move forward to the goal without touching the floor by picking up and placing the rear marker ahead.
3) The player or team that reaches the turnaround point first scores.
4) Vary the challenge by playing as a team relay or extending the distance.
pe-01067:
1) Set up six cones in an inverted bowling pin layout with a defender standing astride over them.
2) Attackers take turns quickly slapping or rolling the ball without catching it to pass through the legs.
3) The attacker scores 1 point if the ball successfully passes through the defender legs.
4) Expand the game with multiple defenders or turn it into a timed group rotation challenge.
pe-01068:
1) Two turners swing the long jump rope smoothly at an even pace and height.
2) Students time their run in the direction the rope moves as it hits the floor.
3) Each student sprints through in turn on every single rope cycle without tripping to build streak points.
4) Increase difficulty by having students do one jump inside or having pairs run through together.
pe-01069:
1) Students spread out facing the instructor with sufficient personal space.
2) Follow the instructor rhythmically tapping shoulders, clapping overhead, and placing hands on hips.
3) Add stationary jumping or side-to-side hops while coordinating upper-body movements.
4) Challenge coordination by hopping forward and backward while reversing or offsetting the arm patterns.
pe-01070:
1) Arrange desks as 1st (1pt), 2nd (2pt), and 3rd base (3pt) targets and set a boundary line for home runs.
2) A batter stands on the spot marker while a teammate gently tosses a soft oversized ball upward.
3) The batter hits the ball with an open palm or fist toward desks to score points or clears the boundary for a home run (4pts).
4) Out occurs if the ball hits the ceiling or lands directly on the floor; modify to award bonus points for hitting multiple desks.
pe-01071:
1) Scatter numbered spot markers across the gym floor at varying distances.
2) The lead runner chooses and stands on a target marker, while the roller rolls the ball accurately toward their feet.
3) If the catcher secures the ball without lifting their feet off the marker, they collect the spot marker for their team.
4) Sum up the points written on retrieved markers to determine winners, or modify by assigning bonus values to distant spots.
pe-01072:
1) Defending players sit on the floor holding foam sticks near desks, while the batter stands on the home marker.
2) The batter tosses the ball up independently and strikes it forward toward the desk targets.
3) Sitting defenders swing their foam sticks to touch or deflect the ball in mid-air to record an out.
4) The batter earns points by hitting empty desks or clearing the home run line, with defenders shifting positions each turn.
pe-01073:
1) Set up a row of traffic cones in front of each team and give four disk cones to the lead runner.
2) On the signal, the runner dashes forward and places one disk cone atop each traffic cone before sprinting back.
3) The next runner sprints out to retrieve all the stacked disk cones one by one and hands them to the following teammate.
4) Modify so that each runner places and collects the disks in a single trip, or arrange cones in a zigzag slalom pattern.
pe-01074:
1) Defenders wait on spots while challengers line up at the starting line with soccer balls.
2) On the whistle, challengers dribble forward to face the first defender in rock-paper-scissors.
3) Winners dribble to the next defender, while losers must dribble back to start over from the beginning.
4) Passing all defenders scores a point, and rules can be modified using foot or whole-body gestures.
pe-01075:
1) Form groups of three where outer pairs hold hands as 'buns' and the middle player stands as 'meat'.
2) A tagger stands in the center and calls out either 'Meat', 'Bread', or 'Burger'.
3) On 'Meat' inside players swap, on 'Bread' outer players swap, and on 'Burger' all three dissolve to reform.
4) The tagger steals a vacant spot, and the remaining player becomes the next caller.
pe-01076:
1) Teammates stand on sturdy stools arranged in a circle, with the first passer raising a free hand.
2) On start, players throw the lightweight ball across the circle, skipping immediate adjacent neighbors.
3) Once a player successfully catches and passes the ball, they immediately sit down on their stool.
4) The relay finishes when the starting player catches the final return pass, recording the team's total elapsed time.
pe-01077:
1) Set up a low net across classroom desks using a jump rope and divide students into two small court teams.
2) Serve the ball underhand over the net so that it bounces once inside the opponent's court boundary.
3) Players must allow the ball to bounce once before catching it; catching it directly in the air or failing to catch results in an opponent's point.
4) Teams may pass up to three times before sending it back, and variations include using different ball types such as rugby or larger reaction balls.
pe-01078:
1) Students stand in rows with sufficient personal space facing the teacher in ready positions.
2) The teacher chants "With one hammer" swinging one arm like a hammer, and students echo the chant while mirroring the motion.
3) Progressively increase hammer counts to two (both arms), three (arms plus one foot), four (both arms and legs), and five (whole body with head nodding).
4) Vary movement tempo and rhythm to challenge full-body coordination and enhance student engagement.
pe-01079:
1) Each student holds one soft juggling ball in each hand and stands in a balanced, ready posture.
2) Toss the first ball in an arc, and as it reaches its peak and begins to drop, toss the second ball inward underneath it.
3) Catch each incoming ball cleanly with the opposite hand, ensuring the two balls do not collide in midair.
4) Chant the rhythm aloud like 'one, two, three, four' and progressively practice alternating which hand tosses first.
pe-01080:
1) Place two chairs with their seats facing together as a landing zone and set players behind a designated line.
2) Take turns gently tapping the balloon ball upward with open palms toward the chair seats.
3) Score a point whenever the balloon comes to a complete rest on top of the chair seats without falling off.
4) Increase difficulty by extending the throwing distance or adding a consecutive landing challenge.
pe-01081:
1) The entire class stands in a large circle, interlocking crossed hands with neighbors to create an arm rail.
2) Place a giant kin-ball on the starting arms and begin rolling it clockwise upon the whistle.
3) Roll the ball along the connected arms using wave-like body motions without grabbing or tossing it until it completes a full lap.
4) If the ball drops, quickly lift it back onto the arms from that spot and challenge the class to break their best time record.
pe-01082:
1) Each student holds a lightweight juggling scarf in each hand at chest height.
2) Toss the first scarf diagonally upward into the air, followed immediately by the second scarf crossing underneath it.
3) Watch the floating paths of both slow-falling scarves and catch them cleanly one by one with opposite hands.
4) Follow a rhythmic count like 'one, two, three, four' and progress to an 8-beat continuous catching routine.
pe-01083:
1) Two rope holders swing a long jump rope in a steady rhythm in the same direction.
2) The first runner times the rope swing to dash straight through to the opposite side without getting caught.
3) For the return trip, an additional runner joins in so they pass through together, adding one more runner on each consecutive pass.
4) Teams compete against the clock to see how quickly all group members can complete the full passing sequence together.
pe-01084:
1) Arrange 9 hula hoops in a 3x3 grid on the floor and place number spot markers (1-10 points) inside each hoop.
2) Players take turns standing behind the foul line and bowling a foam ball along the floor toward the target hoops.
3) If the ball comes to a complete stop inside a hoop, the player earns that hoop's points; balls rolling outside score zero.
4) Teams bowling from four different sides accumulate points over set rounds to determine the winning team.
pe-01085:
1) Set up 16 dish cones of four different colors in a mixed 4x4 grid and mark a starting line at a distance.
2) On signal, the first runner sprints to the grid and swaps the positions of exactly two cones.
3) The runner sprints back to tag the next teammate, who then dashes out to swap two more cones.
4) The relay continues until one team successfully arranges all four horizontal rows into matching single colors.
pe-01086:
1) Teammates stand in a straight line with uniform spacing between two boundary cones set at the front and back.
2) On signal, players pass a foam ball backward overhead from the front of the line to the rear.
3) The last player catches the ball, sprints around to the very front of the line, and starts passing backward again.
4) By continuously passing and leapfrogging the rear runner to the front, the team that advances past the finish line first wins.
pe-01087:
1) Place one foam ball in the center and let all students scatter freely around the play area.
2) The player who retrieves the ball shouts 'Scatterball' and all other players must instantly freeze in place.
3) The thrower takes up to three steps and throws the foam ball targeting another player.
4) If the throw misses, the closest student grabs the ball immediately to shout and attack until someone is eliminated.
pe-01088:
1) Set up diamond bases with an extended outer cone track for boys and an inner base path for girls.
2) The batter hits the foam ball off the tee and sprints continuously around 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and back to home.
3) Fielders field the batted ball and relay it sequentially to 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and home bases to beat the runner.
4) The runner scores 1 point upon reaching home and can keep running an extra lap to score a 4-point grand run.
pe-01089:
1) Two turners hold each end of a long jump rope and turn it steadily in an incoming forward motion.
2) The first jumper enters the rope just as it reaches the peak above their head and begins swinging down.
3) The jumper executes a single centered jump over the rope and immediately dashes forward out of the zone.
4) The next jumper enters seamlessly the moment the previous person jumps, aiming for unbroken continuous passes.
pe-01090:
1) The entire class lines up along the starting lane behind empty desks arranged across the classroom floor.
2) On the teacher's starting cue, all students take one deliberate synchronized step forward simultaneously.
3) Upon reaching the classroom perimeter, students loop around and begin squeezing into the gaps between desks.
4) The whole class wins if every student completely plugs all the empty desk gaps within the 1-minute time limit.
pe-01091:
1) Set up game stations along a long table with cups, a balloon, a table tennis ball, and a paper plane.
2) Start the timer and consecutively complete 7 knee push-ups, 7 squats, and tissue juggling.
3) Clear tabletop skills including balloon cup transport, cap flicking, cup flip, bounce-in, and paper plane throw to record total time.
4) Compete in small relay teams to clear all nine missions under the 99-second limit.
pe-01092:
1) Form a team of 4 to 6 students and line up while firmly holding hands side by side.
2) Place a hula hoop on the first runner's arm and pass it along the human chain without releasing hands.
3) Once the hoop reaches the last student, the whole group circles the cone marker and races back across the finish line.
4) Add multiple hoops or launch hoops from both ends simultaneously to increase physical difficulty.
pe-01093:
1) Tape printable sheets showing random left/right hands and feet in a 3-by-14 grid along the floor.
2) Each runner visually identifies the pattern and advances by placing matching hands and feet simultaneously on all three spots.
3) Any incorrect limb placement or loss of balance results in a foul where the runner rejoins the line, and completion time is timed.
4) Set up parallel tracks for head-to-head team relay matches or add timer challenges.
pe-01094:
1) Students spread out with double-arm intervals facing the instructor to maintain safe exercise personal space.
2) Begin stretching from lower body ankles and hamstrings up to shoulder presses and single-leg knee hugs.
3) Perform upward full reaches with heel raises, side torso bends, forward flexions, and lunges timed to upbeat music.
4) Hold each posture dynamically for about 5 to 6 seconds following the musical rhythm.
pe-01095:
1) Set a hula hoop on the floor in front of the starting line and prepare in pairs or small groups.
2) Take turns rolling the foam ball along the floor toward the hoop.
3) Score 1 point if the ball stays safely inside the hoop without rolling out.
4) Increase the rolling distance or aim along the inner rim to add challenging curves.
pe-01096:
1) Fold a jump rope in half and tie one end securely around the ankle.
2) Swing the tied leg forward to spin the rope loop and jump over it with the opposite foot.
3) Count consecutive successful jumps without tripping over the spinning rope.
4) Switch the rope to the other ankle or increase rotational speed to challenge coordination.
pe-01097:
1) Hold the jump rope handles with both hands and stand in a ready position.
2) Hook the rope over one arm and cross the handles through the loop to create a spider-web pattern.
3) Hold the intricate pattern securely and attempt to jump over the rope while maintaining the shape.
4) Progress from slowly weaving the rope to swinging it upward in a single fluid motion.
pe-01098:
1) Set up 3 numbered cones in a triangle and have 3 players sit around the play area.
2) Take turns rolling the ball along the floor aiming between opponents' cones or knocking them over.
3) Conceding a ball through the cones adds penalty points, and the player with the lowest score wins.
4) The scorer designates the next roller or the cone spacing is widened to vary difficulty.
pe-01099:
1) Place 7 beanbags on the center spot marker and position players at four outer home bases.
2) On start signal, sprint to the center to retrieve one beanbag at a time back to the base.
3) Once the center is empty, players can steal beanbags from opponents to reach 3 beanbags first.
4) Assign one player as a defender or increase the winning target to 4 beanbags for variety.
pe-01100:
1) Arrange 9 cones inverted in a 3x3 grid as targets and prepare flying discs and stacking cups at the throw line.
2) Players take turns throwing flying discs from the line to hit one of the target cones.
3) Hitting a cone allows the player to run up and place their team's cup on it to make a line of three.
4) Play in a fast-paced relay where teammates continuously retrieve discs and throw until a line is completed.
pe-01101:
1) Prepare decorated paper plates, set up wall targets or a hula hoop, and mark a throwing line 2-3 meters away.
2) Grip the paper plate firmly with fingers along the rim and align your body sideways toward the target.
3) Throw the plate toward the target hoop or wall scoring zone using a wrist snap and record your accuracy score.
4) Gradually increase the throwing distance or reduce target size for progressively harder challenge rounds.
pe-01102:
1) Each student holds two beanbags or juggle balls in one hand while standing with a balanced stance.
2) Toss the first ball upward and throw the second ball slightly to the side just as the first reaches its peak.
3) Catch the first falling ball with the same hand and continuously receive the second ball counting the rhythm.
4) Practice with the non-dominant hand or challenge students to increase their maximum consecutive catches.
pe-01103:
1) Place several cones in a row along each team's track, set a turning point cone, and line up the teams.
2) On the starting signal, the first runner sprints forward and knocks down every standing cone along the lane.
3) After rounding the turning cone, the runner restores all fallen cones upright on the way back and tags the next teammate.
4) Modify the rule by requiring runners to knock cones down with elbows or upright them using only their feet.
pe-01104:
1) Place spot markers 3-4 steps away from each student desk as throw spots and distribute mini saucer cones.
2) Players toss saucer cones like flying saucers toward their desk tops aiming for a successful landing.
3) Upon a successful landing on the desk, the player must touch a designated classroom wall or complete 5 squats to earn points.
4) Challenge players to touch all four room walls in sequence after successive landings to see who finishes first.
pe-01105:
1) Pair up students, with each holding a cone balancing a foam ball in one hand and a fun stick in the other.
2) On the signal, players move within the designated boundary, guarding their own ball while targeting the opponent's.
3) A player scores a point by using their fun stick to tap and knock the ball off the opponent's cone.
4) The game can be varied by shrinking the boundary area or playing in 2-on-2 tag team matches.
pe-01106:
1) Place a red target beanbag in the center of the court and divide students into green and blue teams.
2) Determine the order with rock-paper-scissors, then alternate tossing team beanbags toward the target from behind the throwing line.
3) After all throws are finished, the team with beanbags closest to the red target earns points for each winning beanbag.
4) Variations include tactically knocking away opponent beanbags or shifting the target distance farther back.
pe-01107:
1) Sit opposite each other across a desk and place three stacking cups upright in front of each player.
2) Bounce a bouncy ball once on the desk table, aiming to sink it cleanly into one of the opponent's cups.
3) Each time a ball successfully lands in a cup, retrieve the ball and stack that cup onto the baseline cup.
4) The first player to successfully stack all three cups wins the round, with distance adjustable for challenge.
pe-01108:
1) Create a small circular boundary about two shoe-lengths wide on the floor using rolled towels or newspapers.
2) Stand inside the circle and tap the balloon above head level without letting either foot step outside the ring.
3) Successfully keep the balloon airborne 5 times with the dominant hand, 5 times with the other, and 5 times alternating hands.
4) Increase difficulty by replacing the balloon with a crumpled scrap paper ball to practice controlling irregular bounces.
pe-01109:
1) Prepare a paper ring folded from scrap paper and stand in place with feet shoulder-width apart.
2) Quickly execute one jumping jack, then immediately toss the paper ring straight up into the air.
3) Dart your hand smoothly through the airborne ring hole like a diving dolphin to catch it around your wrist.
4) Repeat the entire movement continuously for 60 seconds to reach the target goal of 12 to 16 repetitions.
pe-01110:
1) Each student prepares a jump rope and listens to the music beat while observing the teacher's 16-beat demonstration.
2) After the teacher completes 16 beats of a designated jump step, all students perform the same step for the subsequent 16 beats.
3) Students master six fundamental footwork patterns including basic bounce, alternating step, and boxer bounce to the rhythm of the music.
4) For an advanced variation, students attempt to perform all steps consecutively without pauses or switch turns with a partner.
pe-01111:
1) Each student takes a jump rope and practices the tilted circular path of the rope moving from overhead down to the feet.
2) Keep one hand stationary in front while turning the rope overhead in continuous rotations with the other hand.
3) As the rope sweeps toward the ground, lift the left foot and then the right foot consecutively to let the rope pass through.
4) Advance the challenge by aiming for ten consecutive successful passes or taking turns with a partner to match counts.
pe-01112:
1) Form equal teams behind the starting line and place target hoops at the opposite end of the course with one beanbag per runner.
2) Each runner travels to the hoop while balancing the beanbag on a designated body part, such as behind the knee, between thighs, on the belly, or on the head.
3) The runner drops the beanbag safely inside the target hoop without using hands, rushes back, tags the next teammate, and the team finishing first wins.
4) Adjust difficulty by introducing advanced carrying postures like the airplane balance or toe carry, or having pairs travel together while holding hands.
pe-01113:
1) Each student stands at the starting line inside a hula hoop placed flat on the floor.
2) Lift the hoop upward, pass it completely over the body from feet to head, and place or toss it onto the floor within jumping distance ahead.
3) Perform a standing long jump to leap forward and land stably with both feet inside the newly placed hoop, repeating to advance toward the finish line.
4) Turn the drill into a personal time challenge or a paired relay where one partner lays down the hoop and the other performs consecutive jumps.
pe-01114:
1) Players stand in a circle maintaining social distance, each holding a foam stick with a chair placed in front of them.
2) Play rock-paper-scissors with the entire group, and the final winner shouts out a target exercise count.
3) On the count of "One, two, three, Arrow!", every player points their foam stick simultaneously at one target opponent.
4) The player with the most arrows pointed at them becomes 'it' and performs that number of jumping jacks or squats, or conversely, all safe players do the exercise as a fun rule switch.
pe-01115:
1) The teacher stands at the front as the leader, and students line up facing forward with personal space around them.
2) On the chants of "Cham, Cham," all students perform two preparatory vertical hops in place to establish rhythm.
3) On the final "Cham!", students instantly jump to turn 90 degrees left or right, or choose vertical poses like raising both arms up or squatting down.
4) Students who match the teacher's exact directional jump or body pose get a strike, sitting down after two strikes until the last survivor wins.
pe-01116:
1) Prepare one inflated balloon tied securely after clearing furniture and obstacles around the personal activity space.
2) Start at level 1 (foot) and tap the balloon upward sequentially through level 2 (knee), level 3 (elbow), level 4 (shoulder), and level 5 (head).
3) Catch the balloon cleanly with both hands after the final head tap to achieve a successful elevator ascent.
4) Progress by descending from head down to foot, or attempt a full round-trip ascent and descent without letting the balloon touch the ground.
pe-01117:
1) Fold the jump rope in half and hold both handles firmly together with one hand while standing upright.
2) Spin the rope horizontally above your head like a helicopter propeller to build up consistent centrifugal momentum.
3) Lower your body into a kneeling or deep crouching posture while keeping the rope smoothly spinning around you.
4) Bring the rotating rope close to floor level and execute a single hop over it as it swings beneath your feet, progressing to reverse spinning.
pe-01118:
1) Insert a cotton swab into a bendable straw and place paper cups as targets across the floor.
2) On the start signal, blow through the straw forcefully to shoot the cotton swab toward the cup.
3) If you miss the target, sprint back and forth to the designated return line before reloading another swab.
4) The player who hits and knocks over the opponent target cup first wins, and target distance can be increased.
pe-01119:
1) Prepare three circular rings made from A4 paper and place three cans on the floor as targets.
2) Set a 1-minute timer, run from the starting line to touch a towel marker, and return to throw a ring at the cans.
3) If the ring fails to hook onto a can, sprint back to the marker again before retrieving and throwing the next ring.
4) The challenge is completed when all three rings are hooked onto the cans within the 1-minute time limit.
pe-01120:
1) Set up a low net in the center of the court and divide students into teams of four to five players each.
2) Serve the balloon ball and have every teammate touch the ball at least once before returning it over the net.
3) Award 2 points when the designated target player completes the touch, and have the conceding team perform squats.
4) Adjust variations such as allowing floor bounces or double hits to extend rallies and maximize participation.
pe-01121:
1) Place hula hoops on the ground along the starting line and set cones at the turning point.
2) On the start signal, step inside the hoop and lightly tap-kick its inner rim forward with your feet to move.
3) The first runner to navigate around the turning cone and cross the starting line wins.
4) As students improve, extend the running distance or run it as a continuous team relay.
pe-01122:
1) Set up a 2-meter square area using cones and spot markers, placing one runner inside and three taggers guarding outside.
2) On the signal, the runner attempts to dash out of the square through the openings between taggers.
3) The runner scores 1 point upon successfully escaping without being touched, while taggers score 1 point if they tag the runner.
4) Rotate roles so that either the successful runner or the tagger who made the tag enters the center next.
pe-01123:
1) Mark movement zones with cones between the start line and the tagger, positioning one tagger ahead and players at the start.
2) Players advance toward the tagger only while the tagger chants 'The [Action] Flower Has Blossomed'.
3) When the tagger turns around, players who fail to perform and freeze in the specified posture must return to the start line.
4) The first player to reach and tag the leader while properly executing the freeze poses becomes the next tagger.
pe-01124:
1) Line up spot markers numbered 1 through 6 on the floor and prepare a die (or mobile dice app).
2) Roll the die, flip over the marker showing the rolled number, and perform that exact number of push-ups or squats.
3) If a previously flipped number is rolled again, the marker stays flipped and the participant must repeat the exercises.
4) Clear the challenge by flipping all six numbers while alternating between upper-body and lower-body movements.
pe-01125:
1) Build a 6-cup pyramid (3 on bottom, 2 in middle, 1 on top) on a flat desk.
2) Grip the two middle-tier cups with both hands and slide them downward simultaneously onto the outer base cups.
3) If the top cup drops straight down directly into the central base cup, shout 'Goal' and score 1 point.
4) Quickly collect the cups back into a single stack and rebuild to race toward a target score (e.g., first to 3 goals).
pe-01126:
1) The representative runner of each team rolls a giant dice to determine the number.
2) The runner sprints to teammates and donates (distributes) the rolled number of jump rope counts among them.
3) Teammates complete their assigned jump rope reps before the next runner dashes to roll the dice.
4) The team that first completes the designated total count or donates the most within the time limit wins.
pe-01127:
1) Check the 6 fitness exercises displayed on the dice ball: squats, jumping jacks, burpees, tuck jumps, mountain climbers, and high knees.
2) Roll the dice ball within each group to reveal the fitness movement and number.
3) All team members perform the indicated bodyweight exercise for the shown repetitions or duration.
4) Use the dice ball as a scoring variant during ball games (e.g., bonus points upon scoring).
pe-01128:
1) Scatter non-slip spot markers across the court slightly exceeding the number of players.
2) Players must maintain contact with a spot marker with at least one foot at all times during play.
3) Move between markers only by jumping to avoid thrown foam balls or catch and throw back at opponents.
4) If both feet lose contact with a marker or a player is struck, they are out and move to the outfield; add multiple balls as time progresses.
pe-01129:
1) Each team forms a straight single-file line, facing one designated leader holding a ball.
2) The leader passes to the first player in line, who catches and returns the ball, then immediately squats down.
3) Each player in line repeats this pass-and-squat sequence until all members are sitting; the first player then steps out to become the next leader while the previous leader joins the back of the line.
4) The team where every member completes their rotation as the leader first wins the challenge.
pe-01130:
1) Students form a circle or train line with both hands placed lightly on the shoulders of the person in front.
2) According to the leader's call, 'Apple' jumps forward, 'Banana' jumps backward, and 'Orange' performs a 180-degree turn jump.
3) All players must chant the called fruit name aloud while jumping simultaneously in unison.
4) The leader gradually increases difficulty by chaining multiple commands together in sequence (e.g., Apple-Banana, Orange-Orange-Apple).
pe-01131:
1) Set up a small round rebound net in the center with two teams of two players (4 players total) positioned around it.
2) One player serves by hitting the soft volleyball down onto the rebound net toward the opposing team.
3) The receiving team can make up to three touches between partners before spiking the ball back down onto the net.
4) If a team drops the ball on the floor, hits the frame, or fails to return it onto the net, the opposing team scores a point.
pe-01132:
1) Each student takes one play scoop and one soft foam ball, spreading out across the activity space.
2) Trap the ball on the floor with one foot to scoop it up, then toss it upward and catch it after a single bounce.
3) Increase successful catches by bouncing the ball off the back of the scoop or threading it between the legs before catching.
4) Challenge students with an advanced variation by tossing the ball from behind the back and catching it in front.
pe-01133:
1) Form a circle of 5 to 6 students with one soft volleyball per group.
2) The starting player bounces the ball once on the floor and gently sets it upward with their hands.
3) A teammate catches the airborne ball directly and immediately bounces it toward another player.
4) The team cooperates to reach the target number of consecutive catches without letting the ball hit the floor twice.
pe-01134:
1) Align an odd number (9) of cones in a central row and position 2-3 players per team on opposite sides.
2) On the signal, each team's first roller rolls a foam ball along the floor to knock down the target cones.
3) Whenever a cone is knocked over, the player quickly retrieves it to their team's base and tags the next runner.
4) Continue until all cones are cleared, and the team that collects a majority of cones (5 or more) wins the round.
pe-01135:
1) Form teams of 3 to 4, giving each team 6 to 7 spot markers, a basket, and scattering beanbags at the far end.
2) The front player lays down markers to form a stepping path, and teammates step strictly onto the markers to advance.
3) The rear teammate picks up passed markers and relays them to the front to continuously extend the bridge toward the treasure.
4) Once a beanbag is retrieved, the team maneuvers back to the starting line on their markers to collect the most treasure.
pe-01136:
1) Students pair up, facing each other with one soft foam ball per pair.
2) On a single whistle blow, partners pass the foam ball back and forth continuously.
3) When a double whistle sounds, the student holding the ball immediately becomes the tagger and chases their partner.
4) Once the runner is tagged by the ball holder, both resume their starting positions and return to passing the ball.
pe-01137:
1) Set up four spot markers in a square formation and assign group members to each corner and diagonal running position.
