2) On the signal, pass the disc sequentially along the perimeter while the end player sprints along the diagonal line.
3) Track the total time required for all players to complete the pass rotation and return to their starting positions.
4) Compete against another squad simultaneously or require teams to retry any dropped pass until caught cleanly.
pe-01138:
1) Lay out hula hoops as stepping stones leading to a treasure pile of beanbags at the far end of the court.
2) Each team runner carrying a fun stick navigates the path by performing consecutive two-foot jumps or one-foot hops.
3) Pick up one beanbag at the turning point using the fun stick or hands, leap back through the hoops, and deposit it into the home base.
4) Vary the challenge by requiring single-leg hops or spreading hoops further apart to practice broad jumping skills.
pe-01139:
1) Provide each student with two stacking cups, holding one upright and resting the other in hands facing each other.
2) Level 1: Align the narrow bottom bases together, flip the lower cup one full rotation upward, and catch it nested inside.
3) Level 2: Align the wide open rims together, toss the lower cup in a single flip, and nest it cleanly into the upper cup.
4) Level 3: Execute a split motion by tilting the cup horizontally first and then launching it smoothly into the final nested catch.
pe-01140:
1) Arrange disc cones in a 2 to 3-meter diameter circle and place two facing players on opposite sides of the perimeter.
2) One player attaches a long tail ribbon behind their waist while the opposing player prepares as the chaser.
3) On the start whistle, both sprint along the circular boundary as the chaser maneuvers to snatch the runner's tail.
4) Switch roles after each tag and modify the circle's diameter to challenge agility and rapid directional footwork.
pe-01141:
1) Place two spot markers 1 to 1.5 meters apart on the floor with safe baseline zones marked behind both players.
2) Two players jog forward toward each other, step on their respective markers, and play Rock-Paper-Scissors simultaneously.
3) The winner instantly becomes the tagger and attempts to chase down the loser before they cross back over their safe zone.
4) The runner scores if they reach safety untouched, while the tagger scores if a successful tag is made before the line.
pe-01142:
1) Scatter dozens of holed dome cones in the center and place spot markers around the perimeter to mark each player's home base.
2) On the signal, each player runs to the center holding one foam stick and inserts the stick tip into a dome cone's center hole to hook it.
3) Without touching the cone with hands, carry exactly one caught cone on the stick back to the home base and use feet to slide the cone off onto the floor.
4) Once all center cones are collected, count the total number or color-coded values of the caught cones to determine the winner.
pe-01143:
1) Set up a straight line on the floor and stand lightly on the balls of your feet with heels lifted.
2) Clap to the music beat and practice basic jump steps in place including forward, side two, side-and-side, split, and cross jumps.
3) Once the rhythm is mastered, jump forward along the line without stepping on it for 20 beats.
4) Advance the challenge with complex variations such as turn jumps, heel touches, one-leg jumps, and side squats.
pe-01144:
1) Place a hula hoop on the floor at a set distance and place a cone upside down inside it as a target.
2) Team members line up behind the throwing line and take turns rolling the ball toward the target.
3) Score 1 point if only the cone is knocked down, 2 points if the ball stays inside the hoop without hitting the cone, and 3 points if the cone is knocked down and the ball stays inside.
4) Teams rotate rolling within a 1-minute time limit to score the most points, or switch to kicking the ball with feet.
pe-01145:
1) Form groups of three where two students hold either end of a foam fun-stick low near the floor and one student stands in the middle as the jumper.
2) On the signal, the stick holders walk forward keeping the stick low while the middle jumper frog-hops over it consecutively.
3) The team advances to the turning cone while continuously jumping, circles the cone, and heads back to the starting line.
4) Teammates rotate roles so each member takes a turn jumping in the middle, or race against other teams.
pe-01146:
1) Set up an egg carton on a desk or floor while players line up at throwing spots with containers of balls.
2) Players take turns bouncing table tennis balls once on the table surface toward the carton cups.
3) Compete in various mini-games such as Tic-Tac-Toe, Gomoku sandwich capture, or numerical target scoring.
4) Increase fitness intensity by requiring 2 push-ups or 3 squats before each bounce attempt.
pe-01147:
1) Place two different sets of 5 colored table tennis balls along opposite starting edges of a 30-hole egg carton on a desk.
2) Two facing players engage in simultaneous Rock-Paper-Scissors duels.
3) The winner moves one ball straight (forward, backward, left, right) by 1 space for Rock, 2 for Scissors, and 3 for Paper.
4) Landing directly on an opponent's ball captures it, and the player who eliminates all opposing balls wins.
pe-01148:
1) Place two desks facing each other with a mini center net/barrier and give each player a paper cup and a ping-pong ball.
2) The server starts play by bouncing the table tennis ball on their own desk before sending it across.
3) The receiver catches the ball inside their cup before it bounces twice, immediately flicking it back onto the opponent's desk.
4) Failing to catch the ball or hitting it out results in a point for the opponent, playing up to 5 points.
pe-01149:
1) All students sit in a large circle, and one chosen tagger stands in the center to begin.
2) The tagger runs up to any seated player and quickly chants that player's name three times in a row.
3) The targeted player must defend by shouting the tagger's name once before the tagger finishes all three repetitions.
4) If the tagger succeeds, the seated player becomes the new tagger; if defended, the current tagger must immediately challenge someone else.
pe-01150:
1) Students move around freely, pair up facing each other, and introduce their names clearly.
2) Each pair plays rock-paper-scissors; the winner becomes the 'Star' and the loser becomes their loyal 'Fan'.
3) The fan attaches behind the star like a train carriage and enthusiastically chants the star's name aloud.
4) Stars challenge other stars, with the entire losing train attaching behind the winning star until one grand champion emerges.
pe-01151:
1) Form groups of four where two students anchor an elastic jump band around their ankles and two act as jumpers.
2) Jumpers execute synchronized rhythm step patterns in and out of the bands along to the background music.
3) The team scores by successfully completing all choreographed footwork sequences without tripping over the elastic band.
4) The activity can be varied by swapping jumper-holder roles or speeding up the tempo of the music.
pe-01152:
1) Set up groups of four with two holders stretching the elastic band between their ankles and two jumpers poised inside.
2) Both jumpers coordinate inside-and-outside step jumps along with the rhythm and lyrics of the background song.
3) The group succeeds by completing their designed jumping routine without stepping on the elastic band.
4) Modify the game by introducing rotational turns or exchanging positions while hopping between the bands.
pe-01153:
1) Organize four students per team where two members anchor the jump band and two practice footwork routines.
2) Jumpers execute synchronized rhythm hopping patterns in sequence according to the song's verse and chorus.
3) Points are scored by completing all designated steps consecutively without missing any rhythmic beats.
4) Increase difficulty by narrowing the elastic width or adding turn-around footwork combinations.
pe-01154:
1) Set up marker cones in a circle and station four to five students near their respective cone bases.
2) Practice fundamental punchball fielding by throwing the ball sequentially to moving teammates along the perimeter.
3) Teams score a point every time the ball circulates through all players without any catching drops or fumbles.
4) Vary the challenge by increasing the passing distance or alternating between fly balls and grounders.
pe-01155:
1) Teams put on colored pinnies at the starting point while a hula hoop target is placed downfield as a hole.
2) Team members take turns throwing the flying disc, advancing the entire group to where the disc lands after each throw.
3) The team with the lowest total throws to sink the disc inside the hula hoop target wins the round.
4) Change hole locations, add physical obstacles, or set different Par targets for subsequent rounds.
pe-01156:
1) Fielders stand on their assigned spot markers while four batters line up to hit the ball in turn.
2) When a batter hits the ball with a fist, all four attacking runners run around the bases together.
3) Fielders field the ball, tag their spots, and complete the defense mission by passing to all fielders.
4) Points are scored based on the bases reached by the last runner before defense finishes, then teams switch.
pe-01157:
1) Fielders cover each base while a batter hits the ball and runs around the outside of the bases.
2) The fielder who retrieves the ball runs to the nearest base while others spread out to each base.
3) Fielders pass the ball counterclockwise through every base until it reaches the final designated base.
4) Attack scores points according to the number of completed laps and extra bases reached before the last throw.
pe-01158:
1) Place beanbags in a center hoop and position each group behind their own base hoop marked with cones.
2) On the whistle, the first runners sprint to take one beanbag back to their base and tag the next runner.
3) Once the center pool is empty, players can sprint to rival team bases to steal one beanbag at a time.
4) When the timer (2-3 minutes) expires, the team with the most beanbags in their base wins the game.
pe-01159:
1) Form groups of four where two students anchor the elastic band with ankles while two act as jumpers.
2) Perform rhythmic jumping steps inside and outside the band aligned with the beat of the song Ah-Choo.
3) Earn success points when the pair completes the choreographed jump sequence without tangling the band.
4) Rotate jumper and holder roles or raise band height to knees to adjust difficulty levels.
pe-01160:
1) Form teams of four where two holders secure the band at ankle level and two jumpers stand in the center.
2) Perform creative choreography including side steps, cross jumps, and turns synchronized to the song.
3) Score points by completing the routine rhythmically without tripping on the elastic band.
4) Modify the difficulty by integrating custom arm movements or switching jumping directions midway.
pe-01161:
1) Build a 5-4-3-2-1 pyramid castle using 21 jumbo cups and mark the throwing line using cones.
2) Two throwers from each team launch flying discs at the castle, retrieve them quickly, and pass to teammates.
3) Score points based on knocked-down tiers excluding the bottom base layer (15 points for a total clear).
4) Compete for the highest cumulative team score within 3 minutes, adjusting distance for varied difficulty.
pe-01162:
1) The kicking team forms four-runner squads while the fielding team spreads out across the field.
2) When the kicker kicks the ball, the entire squad runs around the bases together around designated cones.
3) The fielding team lines up behind the fielder who caught the ball and passes it alternately over and under.
4) If the squad's slowest runner crosses home plate before the last fielder runs in, the batting squad scores.
pe-01163:
1) Tape square scoring zones (inner 30 pts, outer 10 pts) and a sliding line on a smooth floor, then divide players into two teams.
2) Players take turns sliding one flying disc along the floor toward the target house.
3) Team members can mock-sweep the floor with brooms to cheer, aim for high points, or knock opponent discs out.
4) After everyone has slid their disc, calculate total points based on discs resting inside the marked lines.
pe-01164:
1) Prepare cardboard tiles (twice the size of A4, one fewer than team members) and gather the team at the start line.
2) Team members hold hands continuously and stand on the cardboard stepping stones to cross the floor lava.
3) Pass the rearmost stone forward to build the path, but if a stone is left completely unattended, it drifts away.
4) Touching the floor with one foot loses that foot's use, while touching with both feet resets the team back to start.
pe-01165:
1) Set up team bases (stealing posts) on both ends of the field with all players starting at '10 years old'.
2) Older players can tag younger players to gain 10 years, and players of the same age resolve encounters with rock-paper-scissors for 10 years.
3) Infiltrating and touching the opponent base awards 30 years, while defenders touching their own base possess infinite age to tag intruders.
4) After gaining or giving age, players must run back to touch their own base ('eat rice') to reset, and teammates can hold hands to combine ages.
pe-01166:
1) Divide into two teams sitting opposite each other separated by a held blanket, with spot markers placed in front.
2) Each team secretly sends one representative forward to sit quietly right in front of the blanket screen.
3) Everyone counts together "One, two, three, peek-a-boo!" as facilitators quickly drop the blanket to the floor.
4) The player who yells out the facing opponent's correct name first wins a point for their team.
pe-01167:
1) Form a team of 4, assign numbers 1 to 4, set up 10 bowling pins, and have Player 1 at the throw line while Player 4 waits next to the pins.
2) Player 1 rolls the ball to knock down pins, and Player 4 retrieves the ball, hands it to Player 2, and goes to the back of the line.
3) Player 1 runs forward to reset the knocked-down pins and remains by the pins as the next ball retriever.
4) Continue the rotation for a 3-minute time limit and count the total number of pins knocked down by each team.
pe-01168:
1) Create a 4-lane spiral snail track on the classroom floor using books and divide the class into two teams.
2) In trios, sit in a line holding the ankles of the person behind and scoot on hips starting from opposite ends.
3) Follow the curved lines, and when encountering the opposing trio, the lead players play Rock-Paper-Scissors.
4) The winner advances while the loser returns to start, allowing their next trio to launch, aiming to reach the opponent's starting end.
pe-01169:
1) Rope holders stretch 3 to 5 jump ropes horizontally across the room at varying heights from ground to waist level.
2) The challenger carefully observes and memorizes the layout, heights, and spacing of all the ropes.
3) The challenger puts on a blindfold and crawls or steps carefully to reach the destination box without touching any rope.
4) Touching a rope ends the attempt, and as a fun variant, helpers silently remove the ropes for the final runner to test their memory and trust.
pe-01170:
1) Prepare Play Stick long/short tubes with connectors and divide the class into two teams wearing team vests.
2) Each team holds a strategy discussion to design and construct their own custom soccer goal post using the tubes.
3) Set up the assembled DIY goal posts at opposite ends of the field and play a mini soccer match following basic soccer rules.
4) Scoring rules can be customized based on goal structure, and teams compete while developing engineering collaboration and teamwork.
pe-01171:
1) 4-5 students in a group form a circle and hold a straw in their mouths.
2) On the signal, a balloon is launched in the middle and players blow through straws to keep it afloat.
3) The team that keeps the balloon airborne without touching the floor for the longest time wins.
4) Difficulty can be adjusted by changing the straw size or adding more balloons.
pe-01172:
1) Groups of three wear pinnies and line up behind the start line, with three target points marked ahead.
2) On the whistle, the three runners dash together and neatly stack dish cones at each marked station.
3) After tagging the turning line, they run back together to retrieve each cone one by one.
4) The game can be varied by placing tennis balls as toppings on top of spot markers.
pe-01173:
1) Teammates sit on the floor in a straight line, with each front player firmly holding the ankles of the person behind them.
2) Players practice sliding forward on their hips by extending and pulling their legs to a shared rhythm.
3) On start, teams row forward simultaneously, and the first team whose whole line crosses the finish line intact wins.
4) Teams can be challenged to solve a group word puzzle immediately after crossing the finish line.
pe-01174:
1) Set up four 3-2-1 pyramid castles using 24 Jumbo Stacks inside the restricted key at each end [00:00:44].
2) Teams advance solely through passing within 10 seconds without dribbling, while defenders stay at least 1 meter away without physical contact [00:01:09].
3) A team scores a point by throwing the ball and completely collapsing the second tier or higher of the castle [00:01:43].
4) Modify by allowing teams to creatively design their castle structure or stacking all 24 cups into one towering pyramid [00:03:11].
pe-01175:
1) Groups of 5-7 form a train holding shoulders; everyone closes their eyes except the very last conductor at the rear.
2) The conductor navigates silently by tapping shoulders (left/right/forward/stop), which is passed forward sequentially.
3) The train weaves through obstacles like desks, chairs, and seated human obstacles to reach the finish line against time.
4) Increase difficulty with an evolution rule where brushed obstacles evolve by standing up or extending arms.
pe-01176:
1) Each group selects a song, analyzes the lyrics, and designs a storyboard for movements.
2) Students practice expressive body movements matching the rhythm and film each scene.
3) Groups edit their clips on tablet devices to synchronize actions with the background music.
4) The whole class watches the finished music videos together and conducts peer evaluations.
pe-01177:
1) Four students split into 2-on-2 teams and stand on opposite sides of a gym floor line.
2) One team starts the rally by tapping a balloon over the dividing line with their hands.
3) A team scores a point whenever the balloon lands on the floor within the opponent's court.
4) The game can be modified by increasing team size to 3-on-3 or setting a 3-touch limit before crossing.
pe-01178:
1) Arrange an inner circle of outward-facing chairs around a center king and an outer standing circle.
2) The outer circle walks around singing until the king signals a stop, facing their partner over a bib.
3) Following body part commands (head, shoulders, knees), players race to grab the floor bib on the cue.
4) The winner sits on the chair, the loser rejoins the outer circle, and 3-win streaks challenge the king.
pe-01179:
1) Place 4 cones at the corners and 9 spot markers in the center, assigning each team behind a corner cone.
2) Players advance through stepping hoops to place one team beanbag onto an available spot marker.
3) Only one beanbag is placed per turn before visiting another spot, and the majority color claims that marker.
4) The game can be varied by linking team members together as a full train or adjusting round times.
pe-01180:
1) Set up five chairs on each side where fielders sit with gloves while one helper stands by the basket.
2) When a batter tosses the soft ball, fielders catch it and relay it along the chair line to their helper.
3) The fielding team scores an out by passing the ball rapidly until the helper deposits it in the basket.
4) Upon success, the helper moves to the first chair and all seated teammates rotate forward by one seat.
pe-01181:
1) Select one tagger while the other students gather and await the verbal signal.
2) When the tagger shouts "It's a raccoon!", players flee, but if another phrase is called, everyone must freeze immediately.
3) In reverse magic mode, players freeze on "raccoon" and run on any other words, with mistakes leading to becoming the tagger.
4) Vary the game by integrating classroom vocabulary categories where players move only on matching concepts.
pe-01182:
1) Mark the court with cones and split the class into two teams wearing scrimmage vests.
2) Give each team one dodgeball and start the game with all players positioned inside the inner court.
3) Pass the ball to teammates and tag opposing players by touching them with the ball in hand rather than throwing.
4) The team with the most surviving inner court players when time expires, or the team that eliminates all opponents, wins.
pe-01183:
1) Draw a 3x3 grid of nine equal squares on each side of the net and place one player in each zone.
2) Serve the ball and have the player whose zone the ball enters make the initial contact before passing it over the net.
3) Whenever a rally ends or a rotation signal is called, players shift one space sequentially to change positions.
4) Begin with a single-bounce allowed rule to build confidence, then progress to volleying without any bounces.
pe-01184:
1) Pair up students facing each other at a safe distance (15–20 cm apart) with knees slightly bent.
2) Position one hand as a shield covering one's own knees and the other hand ready to reach and tag the opponent's knees.
3) Keep feet grounded while defending and attempting to touch the opponent's knee; each successful touch scores 1 point up to 3 points.
4) Advance the game by allowing lateral one-step movements or turning it into a whole-room mixer aiming for 5 points.
pe-01185:
1) Line up jumbo stacking cups along the center line and have both teams line up behind their starting boundaries.
2) On the whistle, dash to retrieve cups one by one and cooperatively construct a tiered castle from bottom-left to top-right (1st scoring round).
3) Once castles are built, throw dodgeballs from behind the throwing line for 5 minutes to knock down upper cups (2nd scoring round).
4) Completely collapsing the opponent's castle triggers an instant win; otherwise, sum retrieved and demolished cup points to decide the winner.
pe-01186:
1) Line up four classroom desks on their sides to form side walls, and have two players per team sit behind each end line holding indoor shoes.
2) Decide first possession with rock-paper-scissors, then slide the ring toward the opposing side either directly or by rebounding it off the desk barriers.
3) A team scores one point whenever their shot passes the opponent end line or hits an opposing defender.
4) Substitute in two waiting teammates each time a point is conceded (or every two minutes), competing over a four-minute match to see who scores more.
pe-01187:
1) Set up one fielding home plate, two batting home plates, and bases 1 to 3, splitting students into teams of six.
2) Two offensive runners stand at home, the right batter kicks a volleyball off a cone, and each runs toward first and third base.
3) Both runners meet near second base, high-five each other, and sprint back to step on their designated home plates before fielders throw home to score a point.
4) Teams switch roles after all batters kick for two innings, with teachers narrowing base distances if fielders dominate.
pe-01188:
1) Line up opposite each other at the entryways of an S-shaped meandering pathway on an outdoor court.
2) Move along the designated pathway toward the opponent by either running or executing continuous two-foot jumps.
3) Stop immediately when meeting the opponent midway and play rock-paper-scissors; the loser resets to start while the winner advances.
4) Score one point by reaching the opponent's starting mark, and introduce kangaroo-style hopping variants to increase physical exertion.
pe-01189:
1) Place beanbags inside hula hoops in the center court, designating Heungbu and Swallow bases on opposite ends with four Nolbu taggers holding foam sticks.
2) Heungbu players run freely on two feet while Swallows hop on one foot, but Swallows may run on two feet once paired by holding hands with Heungbu.
3) Taggers chase and tag them with foam sticks sending them back to base, while surviving pairs reach the center, shout the chant, and retrieve one beanbag.
4) The round finishes after the set time limit or once all beanbags are harvested, awarding victory to the village team with the most seeds collected.
pe-01190:
1) Students pair up and play rock-paper-scissors, where the losers each hold a basketball to become taggers, making half the group taggers.
2) Taggers carry their basketballs and chase any runner across the gym to tag them with the ball.
3) When tagged, the runner receives the ball, performs a designated ball-handling penalty such as ten figure-8s around the legs, and becomes the new tagger.
4) The penalty task can be varied to waist circles, knee circles, or neck wraps.
pe-01191:
1) In groups of four, students pair up into two teams of two and sit facing each other on mats.
2) Partners interlock their feet and ankles together for mutual support and lie back.
3) On the starting signal, both partners curl up simultaneously to high-five each other with both hands, counting total reps completed over 3 minutes.
4) When tired, partners can quickly switch with the other resting pair in their group to keep going.
pe-01192:
1) Tape a square target on the classroom floor and divide students into teams of four, deciding order by rock-paper-scissors.
2) Team members establish throwing order, with each player holding one plastic ring (4 per team, 8 total).
3) Teams alternate sliding their rings across the wooden floor aiming for the target center or bumping opponent rings out.
4) After all 8 rings are delivered, the team with the ring closest to the target center scores one point for each ring closer than the opponent's best ring, playing up to 3 ends.
pe-01193:
1) Prepare a whole-class supply of Speed Stacks cups (around 28 sets) on the classroom floor.
2) Warm up by challenging students to stack cups vertically in a single line and create creative group structures.
3) Tape a baseline on the floor and engage students in a math calculation to determine the optimal base layer (25 cups).
4) Take turns by groups placing cups layer by layer to construct a massive 25-floor pyramid without toppling it.
pe-01194:
1) Set up a rectangular half-court area placing 8 spot markers at the four corners and the midpoints of each side.
2) Four players stand at the corners, and player 1 steps to the midpoint with the ball to initiate the drill.
3) Player 1 delivers a lead pass to the adjacent side's midpoint while player 2 times their run to catch and pass to the next midpoint.
4) Students attempt to complete 20 consecutive passes along the diamond route without mistakes, advancing to using two balls simultaneously.
pe-01195:
1) Mark throwing and catching lines on the classroom floor using masking tape and provide 10 rings per group.
2) In groups of 4, two partners face each other and toss the rings horizontally using a frisbee-style wrist flick.
3) The receiver catches the incoming ring onto their arm (stage 1) or hooks it onto a playstick or broomstick (stage 2).
4) Scoring is based on the number of catches out of 40 throws, or timed by how fast a team can reach 30 successful catches.
pe-01196:
1) Arrange chairs in a large circle with all students seated except one 'it' standing in the center.
2) Assign each student in sequence one of three words ('Pee', 'Poop', or 'Booger'), assigning one to the tagger as well.
3) A seated student asks a creative question, and the tagger must humorously answer with their designated word (or two words).
4) Students assigned the spoken word must immediately stand and switch chairs, and if the tagger shouts "All of them!", everyone switches seats.
pe-01197:
1) Set up two bases in the center of the field with a cone 15 meters behind home plate for the kicking team lineup.
2) The kicker kicks the ball in any 360-degree direction toward open space and runs 3 to 4 laps around teammates before sprinting to home plate.
3) Fielders line up behind whoever fields the ball first and tunnel the ball through their legs to the final player who throws it home.
4) The kicking team scores 1 point if the kicker reaches home before the throw, earning extra points for additional laps if fielding is delayed.
pe-01198:
1) Arrange spot markers in a baseball diamond shape with a center pitcher spot, dividing 8 to 12 students across the bases.
2) The player at home throws the ball to first base and immediately sprints into the center pitcher spot.
3) The first baseman passes the ball back to the player in the center and shifts toward the next designated base position.
4) The center receiver passes across diagonally to the opposite base and runs diagonal, keeping the ball moving in a 90-degree pinwheel while counting successful passes.
pe-01199:
1) Form groups of four and distribute 12 Speed Stacks cups between pairs based on fitness level (e.g., 6:6 or 8:4).
2) Two partners face each other in a push-up position, placing their designated stack of cups directly beneath their chest bones.
3) Both partners perform a push-up simultaneously until their chests gently tap the cups, then high-five opposite hands at the top.
4) Teams perform for 2 minutes, tagging out with the resting pair whenever tired, competing for the highest total group repetitions.
pe-01200:
1) Form groups of 3 to 4 students, where one student holds a steady forearm plank on the floor.
2) A runner continuously jumps side-to-side over the planking partner's lower legs, counting each successful leap.
3) Whenever either the planker or the jumper tires, they immediately rotate roles with waiting teammates.
4) Compete over a set time limit of 1 to 3 minutes to achieve the highest cumulative group jump count.
pe-01201:
1) Tape a rectangular court on the floor and place four rings per team inside the baseline with players taking turns from one to four.
2) Players take turns sliding their ring across the floor to knock the opponent rings out of the boundary.
3) Rings pushed outside the court or self-eliminated are removed, and the team that knocks out all opposing rings wins the round.
4) Adjust the total number of rings to match group sizes or modify whether rings touching the boundary line count as out.
pe-01202:
1) Clear space in the classroom for safety and prepare a follow-along cardio workout video on the main screen.
2) Follow the screen alongside the teacher, performing 20 minutes of full-body cardio and core-strengthening exercises in place.
3) Conclude the session by reflecting on physical exertion and checking heart rate and movement completion.
4) Adapt the routines to target physical fitness test components like curl-ups and push-ups, or assign monthly home workout logs.
pe-01203:
1) Set up two adjacent diamond fields shaped like butterfly wings using 8 bases and a line marker to separate running paths.
2) A batter hits the ball off the tee, and all attacking teammates run together around their designated bases toward home plate.
3) Fielders field the ball and run to hand it to a nearby teammate like a relay baton, circling all bases to finish their mission.
4) The batting team scores if they finish before the fielding team, and rules can advance from hand-offs to throwing and catching.
pe-01204:
1) Mark the field with cones and lines into left, center, right, and three distance zones: infield (1 pt), outfield (2 pts), and home run (3 pts).
2) The batter loudly predicts and announces their intended target direction before hitting the ball off the tee.
3) The player earns zone points, and if the ball lands in the declared direction, their scored points are doubled.
4) Each member takes 3 turns to accumulate team points, with variations adding fielders who can reduce points by catching balls.
pe-01205:
1) Students form a large circle at arm's length, and 7 rings are placed on the starting player's left arm.
2) On the signal, the starter shifts rings from left to right arm and slides them onto the next player's left arm.
3) Each player repeats the arm-to-arm transfer in sequence around the entire circle while the teacher times the lap.
4) Divide into two competing groups or increase laps and ring count to challenge records.
pe-01206:
1) Set up a kickball diamond with a hula hoop beside home plate and divide players into two teams of seven.
2) The batter kicks the pitched volleyball and sprints around 1st, 2nd, 3rd bases toward home plate.
3) The fielding team catches the ball and passes it consecutively among players at least 2 meters apart, scoring 1 point per successful catch before the runner reaches home.
4) Duplicate catches by the same player are disallowed, and the final pass must reach the target hoop safely to validate total points.
pe-01207:
1) Stand upright next to your desk in the classroom aisle and prepare for stretching.
2) Balance on one foot while pulling your opposite ankle backward to stretch the quadriceps, then switch sides.
3) Hug one knee toward your chest while flexing your ankles up and down, then rotate your hips outward to mobilize the joints.
4) Take a wide stance, lower into a horse stance with hands on knees, and drop one shoulder inward to deeply stretch the inner thighs and torso.
pe-01208:
1) Begin in place with side lunges without creating floor noise to warm up the leg muscles.
2) Move into a plank position to perform cross-body mountain climbers, then stand up for squat-and-punch combinations.
3) Alternate lateral skate jumps touching the opposite floor, followed by elbow planks and crab-walk squats for core strength.
4) Complete 30-second intervals of alternating hand-leg planks, superman extensions, and side-plank leg raises on the floor.
pe-01209:
1) March lightly in place within the classroom space in time with the classical music accompaniment.
2) Spread both arms wide like swan wings and flutter gracefully while lifting one leg outward and forward alternately.
3) March briskly with pumping arms, then mimic smooth breaststroke swimming motions while twisting the upper torso left and right.
4) Stretch sides deeply with arms overhead, bend forward to touch opposite toes alternately, and finish with a graceful lunge bow.
pe-01210:
1) Lie down in a hip bridge or plank position and place 12 cups beside your body to prepare.
2) In the hip bridge position, pass the cups one by one under your hips from the right hand to the left hand, then reverse.
3) In the plank position, take cups from both sides alternately to stack a 4-3-2-1 pyramid in front and then disassemble it.
4) Students who struggle can modify by dropping knees to the floor or timing themselves for a challenge.
pe-01211:
1) Sit upright on a classroom chair with good posture and stabilize your breathing.
2) Follow the music to stretch your neck, bend forward to reach your legs, and march rhythmically in place while seated.
3) Pull knees toward your chest, do 90-degree robot arm rotations, and lift both legs while gripping the seat to build strength.
4) Modify the activity by increasing the tempo or pairing up with a partner for a mirror-following challenge.
pe-01212:
1) Students stand beside their desks facing the screen with proper posture.
2) Follow low-impact bodyweight exercises such as butt kicks, side lunges with knee lifts, modified squats, and reverse lunges for 30 seconds each.
3) Complete the entire circuit without giving up to build endurance and lower body strength.
4) The difficulty can be adjusted by adding brief rest intervals or increasing movement tempo with a partner.
pe-01213:
1) Students stand safely beside their desks or in the gym with ample personal space.
2) Swing both arms horizontally twice to the rhythm, then express Scissors (crossed arms over chest), Rock (arms curved above head), or Paper (arms spread wide) on the final call.
3) Compete against a partner or small group to score points through consecutive wins.
4) Integrate this into tag games or classroom pyramid tournaments to expand physical movement.
pe-01214:
1) Students sit upright on their classroom chairs with good posture and relaxed breathing.
2) Follow guided upper-body movements sequentially: interlacing fingers to stretch arms forward and upward, gently pulling the neck to each side/front/back, rolling shoulders, and bending the torso sideways.
3) Focus on tension release and muscle relaxation across the neck and shoulders.
4) Use as a quick warm-up before class or a restorative break during prolonged desk study.
pe-01215:
1) Set up a cardboard box as a hoop and mark 9 shooting spots at 1, 2, and 3-pace distances across straight, 45-degree, and side angles using paper cups.
2) Players shoot 3 rolled-up sock balls from each of the 9 marked spots toward the box.
3) Total points are calculated by counting the number of successful shots out of 27 attempts.
4) Challenge a partner by timing the circuit or having a partner hold the hoop box dynamically.
pe-01216:
1) Mark designated grid squares on the floor where each player stands with at least one foot inside, holding a balloon.
2) On start, tap the balloon up repeatedly while strictly keeping at least one foot anchored inside the square.
3) A round ends when a player steps completely outside the square or lets the balloon hit the floor; the opponent scores a point, playing first to 3 points.
4) Increase the challenge by adding a second balloon per player or requiring alternating left and right hand hits.
pe-01217:
1) Join the live Zoom session and follow the teacher's guidance to perform whole-body warm-up stretches along with the home gymnastics video.
2) Follow the teacher's shared workout video to perform full-body bodyweight aerobics and muscular endurance training together in real time.
3) After a brief rest, open the shared URL individually to complete another full round of the aerobic workout to maximize cardiovascular fitness.
4) Access the shared Padlet board to reflect on personal physical endurance, write feedback notes, and comment on peers' experiences.
pe-01218:
1) Stand at the starting line and do a reverse lunge to place a stack of 12 cups beside your foot.
2) Alternate front and reverse lunges while moving cups one by one to build a 3-6-3 pyramid.
3) Once the pyramid is built, switch legs and perform lunges to collect the cups one by one back to the starting stack.
4) As you get used to the movement, try side lunges to build a 6-6 pyramid or challenge your completion time.
pe-01219:
1) Stand at the end of the 2-meter Sjoelbak board and prepare all 30 wooden pucks.
2) In the first round, slide all 30 pucks toward the 4 scoring slots (worth 2, 3, 4, and 1 point from left to right).
3) Collect the pucks that failed to enter and slide them in rounds 2 and 3, then calculate the score based on pucks in each slot.
4) Earn a 10-point bonus for every full set of pucks distributed evenly across all four slots, and the player with the highest total wins.
pe-01220:
1) Divide players into two teams across a volleyball net and decide the serving order.
2) Catch the opponent's serve or throw and either pass it among teammates or immediately throw it over the net.
3) Score points equal to the number of teammates who touched the ball before clearing the net (e.g., 4 points if all 4 touched), playing up to 30 points.
4) Strategically vary between a surprise quick attack for fewer points and multi-pass teamwork for big points.
pe-01221:
1) Mark a rectangular area with 4 cones, divide into two teams, and have all players tuck a scrimmage vest into their waistband as a tail.
2) On the start signal, run around the area trying to snatch the tails of the opposing team members.
3) Players whose tails are pulled become scarecrows where the tail fell, keeping one pivot foot fixed while reaching out to snatch opponent tails.
4) The team with the most surviving runners when time expires wins the round.
pe-01222:
1) Pair up students and place two spot markers facing each other approximately 15 meters apart.
2) On start, players walk toward each other and halt to play rock-paper-scissors upon meeting.
3) The winner continues walking forward, while the loser sprints back to tag their own start marker before walking forward again.
4) If a player wins rock-paper-scissors while the opponent is standing on their own marker, they score 1 point.
pe-01223:
1) Set up your personal space and stabilize your body's central axis without moving your feet.
2) Follow the instructor through 11 fundamental non-locomotor movements including twisting, shaking, bending, and stretching.
3) Combine two or more body parts simultaneously and vary levels and directions to master expressive control.
4) Work in pairs to link selected non-locomotor movements into a creative stationary movement sequence.
pe-01224:
1) Arrange students in classroom aisles with adequate personal exercise space and stand ready.
2) Rotate through 10 quiet exercises including silent jumping, crunch knee lifts, and reverse lunge twists.
3) Perform each station for 30 seconds of active work followed by 5 seconds of transition and rest.
4) Maintain a continuous rhythm without lifting feet forcefully, repeating the entire circuit for higher intensity.
pe-01225:
1) Set up two circular team bases using spot markers or cones, placing one traffic cone flag next to each base.
2) Players start inside their home base at full energy, with energy depleting immediately upon leaving the base.
3) Players who left base later have higher energy and can tag out earlier opponents, who must return home to recharge.
4) Evade defenders to snatch the opposing team's cone flag to score 1 point, then reset positions for the next round.
pe-01226:
1) Prepare six everyday objects such as t-shirts, plastic bags, small balls, tissues, water bottles, and umbrellas.
2) Practice fundamental manipulative skills including throwing, catching, striking, bouncing, and swinging with each object.
3) Challenge students with object-specific tasks like clapping multiple times before catching a floating tissue.
4) Combine rhythms, directional changes, and creative prop manipulation to choreograph a short expressive sequence.
pe-01227:
1) Set up a 50m straight track on the field or a 15m shuttle course with cones in the gym and line up students in pairs by height.
2) Students sprint on the whistle to measure 50m sprint times or shuttle run times and memorize their score without decimal points.
3) Arrange students in rank order and have lower-ranking runners challenge the peers just above them in 1-on-1 races to take their spot.
4) Adjust course length according to available space and use the final assessment results to form balanced mixed-ability teams for upcoming ball games.
pe-01228:
1) Set up badminton nets on two courts, divide the class into 5 teams of 4 players with team pinnies, and set up a round-robin schedule.
2) Use a 50cm big volleyball and allow players to serve from the closer badminton service line instead of the far baseline.
3) Permit one bounce between hits and allow saves outside the sideline boundary, giving each team up to 5 touches to return the ball into the opponent's court.
4) Rotate teams so that while four teams play matches on two courts, the fifth team serves as referees and video recorders in a sport education model.
pe-01229:
1) Form small groups of 4 to 5 students and choose a specific song section (e.g., Mamamoo's 'Yes I Am') to express creatively.
2) Explore song lyrics and themes to brainstorm key signature moves, intro formations, level changes (sitting/standing), and eye contact.
3) Practice connecting individual gestures with synchronized group dance while transitioning between line and spread formations to dynamic beats.
4) Present the completed dance routine on stage while peer groups assess synchronicity, expressiveness, and movement creativity.
pe-01230:
1) Set up a badminton net, form 4-player teams wearing pinnies, and assign each player numbers 1 (server), 2 (receiver), 3 (setter), and 4 (spiker).
2) Practice circle spiking drills first, then run a 3-repetition drill of serve-receive-set-spike before rotating positions clockwise.
3) Play a head-to-head match using a one-bounce rule and an 'all-touch' rule where every teammate must touch the ball within 5 total hits before spiking over.
4) The first team to score 15 points wins, with options to expand allowed touches to 6-7 hits or waive the all-touch rule depending on skill level.
pe-01231:
1) Form groups of six on either side of the net and place five hula hoops in open spots on the opponent court.
2) The server executes an underhand serve and all defending players on the opposite side take turns touching the ball in relay.
3) Attack the ball back into the empty court without hitting the hula hoops to score one point.
4) Rotate server turns and shift hoop positions to challenge students with varied defensive spaces.
pe-01232:
1) Set one spot marker in the center and place one spot marker with a soft dice ball in each of the four compass directions.
2) The participant balances on one foot on the center marker while keeping the opposite foot completely off the floor.
3) Bend down to pick up one dice ball at a time in any order and stack all four onto the other hand.
4) Compete in group relays where players who successfully stack four dice and balance for three seconds earn points for their team.
pe-01233:
1) Choose a popular song within each group and analyze the lyrics to extract key themes and words.
2) Create unique point choreography matching key lyrics and organize formations like lines and V-shapes.
3) Practice over several sessions and conduct a mid-term showcase to receive constructive feedback from peers.
4) Perform the final dance using simple props in the gym and produce an explanatory video reflecting on the creative process.
pe-01234:
1) Determine offense and defense by a kicking contest, facing the pitcher and batter with runners and fielders spread around.
2) The pitcher tosses the shuttlecock (soft ball) toward the batter who kicks it into the open field to begin play.
3) The batter or teammates run, pass, and kick the shuttlecock repeatedly to gain additional lives for every extra kick.
4) Fielders tag the shuttlecock holder or intercept the ball with a direct kick to reverse offense and defense instantly.
pe-01235:
1) Form a group of four dancers and stand in an initial facing formation on the stage.
2) Perform synchronized point choreography matching Mamamoo's 'Decalcomanie' mirroring each other's gestures.
3) Transition smoothly between face-to-face and horizontal line formations while aligning motions with the lyrics.
4) Execute the signature chorus dance moves together and conclude with a crisp ending pose.
pe-01236:
1) Set up an oval track with cones and position two teams wearing pinnies in pairs at opposite starting points.
2) On the signal, the first pair of each team runs in the same direction around the track while passing the ball to each other.
3) After completing one full lap, they pass the ball to the next pair to continue the relay until the final pair finishes.
4) The team that catches up to the opposing team or completes all laps first wins, with variations including wider passing distances or required pass counts.
pe-01237:
1) Place spot markers from center to perimeter, set up three portable nets at 120-degree intervals, and position three 6-player teams in each zone.
2) Determine the first server via rock-paper-scissors, allowing them to serve the ball into any opponent's court to begin play.
3) Teams may hit the ball up to 6 times using direct hits or one bounce before sending it over a net into an opposing court.
4) Scoring an attack moves the net by 30 degrees to expand that team's territory, and the team with the largest area at time limit wins.
pe-01238:
1) Form groups of three, assigning numbers 1, 2, and 3, with players 2 and 3 standing opposite each other.
2) As players 2 and 3 begin exchanging passes, player 1 acts as defender, moving continuously in a figure-8 pathway between them.
3) Player 1 intercepts the moving pass, immediately dishes the ball back to the passer, and pivots around to intercept from the other side.
4) Roles rotate once player 1 completes 20 successful interceptions, with variations including bounce passes or faster passing tempos.
pe-01239:
1) Preparation: Students form groups of three where two hold hands to make a clam and one stands inside as a pearl, while one tagger stands in the center.
2) Progression: When the tagger calls out 'Pearl', 'Clam', or 'Starfish', students with that role must quickly leave their group and find new partners.
3) Scoring: The tagger also rushes into an open spot, and the student left without a group becomes the new tagger and completes a simple physical task.
4) Variation: If class numbers are an exact multiple of three, the teacher joins in, or two taggers can be assigned if there are two extra students.
pe-01240:
1) Preparation: Students pair up, place spot markers 1 meter apart as starting bases with cones marking safe zones, and each hold a foam dice.
2) Progression: Facing each other, they roll their dice simultaneously on cue, grab their dice, and the player with the larger number chases to tag the player with the smaller number.
3) Scoring: The player with the larger number scores 1 point by tagging the opponent before they reach the safe zone, and the first to reach 5 points wins.
4) Variation: Players can roll two dice each to compare sums or race to call out the multiplication product first to earn tagger rights.
pe-01241:
1) Set up a box hoop on the classroom window and place spot markers numbered 1 to 6 in a zigzag path from the goal.
2) The first player rolls a foam dice ball, runs to the corresponding numbered spot marker, and shoots into the hoop.
3) If the shot goes in, the team scores points equal to that number; then the runner carries the ball back to hand off to the next player.
4) As a variation, if a player misses, the next teammate must continue attempting from that exact number until it is made before rolling again.
pe-01242:
1) Form attack and defense groups in the gym, with every student holding a playstick.
2) In the circle drill, 6 attackers form a perimeter while 2 defenders in the middle try to intercept the moving ring using their sticks.
3) When a defender successfully intercepts a sliding ring, they switch roles with the attacking player who made the error.
4) Advance into a team pass game where teams score 1 point per successful pass, competing to reach a target count (e.g., 20 passes) first.
pe-01243:
1) Form small groups lined up in front of mini goals (or cone goals), with each student holding a playstick.
2) Practice stationary shooting by placing the stick inside the ring and sliding it toward the goal, then retrieving your own ring.
3) Award 1 point per goal, or assign one student as a goalkeeper who can block shots using feet and stick.
4) Progress to a dynamic 2-player drill where partners advance across the court by passing to each other before taking a running shot.
pe-01244:
1) Face your partner 1 meter apart on spot markers and place cones behind each player to mark finish lines.
2) Play rock-paper-scissors where the winner instantly becomes the chaser and the loser becomes the runner sprinting away.
3) The chaser scores 1 point by tagging the runner before the finish line, while no point is awarded if the runner crosses safely.
4) Modify the game by having the runner turn into a chaser immediately upon touching the turning point for a reverse tag.
pe-01245:
1) Take a play stick and ring, form pairs or trios, and practice passing in place by inserting the stick into the ring center.
2) Advance to dynamic pair passing where partners slide the ring ahead of each other while jogging down the court.
3) Practice 2-on-1 keep-away drills where a defender intercepts passes, and target drills passing through a partner's legs.
4) Progress into a 5-player star formation passing drill, moving cohesively while maintaining the passing pattern.
pe-01246:
1) Place balls in a center circle marked by spots, set hoop bases at four corners, and divide into four teams with pairs.
2) On start, one runner dashes to the center to grab a ball and passes it back and forth with their partner toward their base.
3) Players cannot travel while holding the ball, and if dropped, the ball must be carried on foot back to its origin.
4) Once center balls run out, teams can steal balls from opponents' bases, and the team with the most balls wins.
pe-01247:
1) Set up nine spot markers in a straight line, place a bowling pin on the center marker, and position one student from each team next to the pin while others line up behind base lines.
2) Teams take turns rolling a dodgeball toward the center pin to knock it down.
3) When a player knocks the pin down, the teammate next to the pin moves it one spot closer to the opponent's side and returns the ball to the next roller.
4) The team that pushes the pin farther toward the opponent's territory when time runs out wins the game.
pe-01248:
1) Two players sit facing each other on the floor with their feet touching and grasp each other's hands firmly.
2) On signal, both players pull each other's hands simultaneously while driving with their legs to stand up together.
3) Upon successful attempts, increase group size to three, four, and eight players sitting in a circle with feet together.
4) Finally, challenge the entire squad or class to form one large circle and stand up all at once.
pe-01249:
1) Scatter spot markers across the floor equaling two-thirds of the total number of students.
2) Two-thirds of students stand on a marker as defenders, while the remaining one-third without markers become challengers.
3) Challengers approach any defender to play rock-paper-scissors; winning challengers take the marker while defeated defenders become challengers and run to another spot.
4) If the defender wins they hold their ground, and when time expires, all remaining challengers perform a brief fitness task like frog jumps.
pe-01250:
1) Place bowling pins on spot markers along both baselines, mark a centerline, and set up a revive zone on the sideline.
2) When play starts, students roll dodgeballs across the centerline to knock down the opponent's bowling pins.
3) Players may block balls with their bodies to protect pins, but getting hit eliminates them to the revive zone where they must do three jumping jacks to rejoin.
4) Once time expires, the team with more upright bowling pins remaining on their markers wins the match.
pe-01251:
1) Mark the playing area and have each student draw a locomotor movement card to assign their initial movement skill.
2) On the start signal, students travel around the area performing only the specific movement shown on their card (e.g., hopping, leaping, skipping).
3) When tagging another player, both announce their movements and play rock-paper-scissors.
4) The loser adopts the winner's movement skill, and the movement shared by the most students at the end of the round wins.
pe-01252:
1) Pair up students side by side, allowing the left partner to use only their left hand and the right partner only their right hand.
2) Work collaboratively using 12 cups to perform 3-6-3 or Cycle stacking routines as if moving as a single body.
3) In classroom group matches, all pairs compete simultaneously and earn points based on their finishing order.
4) In relay format, pairs run from a 2.13m starting line to the desk to complete the stack before tagging the next pair.
pe-01253:
1) Set up a rectangular playing area with cones and form groups of six (4 attackers and 2 defenders wearing pinnies).
2) Attackers move across the area by running with the ball or passing it to open teammates to evade defenders.
3) Defenders attempt to disrupt the offense by tagging the ball carrier with a hand or intercepting passes in mid-air.
4) Any attacker tagged or intercepted swaps roles with that defender after a brief pause, restarting with a pass.
pe-01254:
1) Set stacked Jumbo Cups 10 meters from the start cone with a turning cone 2 meters behind it, organizing each team into 3-player squads.
2) On the signal, the trio sprints together to build a designated pyramid (15 cups for grades 3-4, 21 cups for grades 5-6).
3) Once the pyramid is built, teammates circle around the turning cone and cooperatively downstack all cups back into a single vertical tower.
4) The squad runs back to loop around their waiting team line and tag the next trio, with scoring adapted across multiple rounds.
pe-01255:
1) Set a batting tee at home base and place 3 dish cones each at 7m, 10m, and 13m distances, dividing the class into hitting and fielding teams.
2) The batter hits the ball off the tee, runs to grab one treasure cone, and sprints back to the offensive home plate.
3) Fielders field the ball and relay it to the catcher at defensive home plate; if the runner arrives before the ball, the team scores 1 point.
4) If the ball reaches the catcher first, the runner is out and returns the cone, with variations offering 1, 2, or 3 points based on cone distance.
pe-01256:
1) Set up three plastic bins spaced 50cm apart starting 3m from the shooting line, with each 4-player team holding sticks and floorballs.
2) Players take turns placing a ball on the line, striking it toward the buckets, and immediately retrieving their own ball for the next player.
3) The team scores hits collectively, capturing the first bucket at 8 hits, the second at 6 hits, and the third bucket at 4 hits.
4) The squad that cooperatively clears all hit quotas and retrieves all three buckets first wins the match.
pe-01257:
1) One tagger faces the gymnasium wall while all other students stand on the starting line, each with their own soccer ball.
2) While the tagger calls out the phrase twice, players dribble their balls forward toward the tagger's wall.
3) Any student failing to bring their ball to a complete stop when the tagger turns around is caught and holds hands beside the tagger.
4) When an active dribbler tags the tagger's back, all trapped players dribble back to the start, and whoever the tagger tags while dribbling becomes the next tagger.
pe-01258:
1) Set spot markers down the badminton court center line; divide players so each team supplies half as active court players and half as stationary 'human nets' facing the opponent.
2) A player serves the big volleyball across the line, and teams may use up to five hits and one floor bounce to return the ball.
3) A team scores a point if the opponent hits out or lets the ball bounce twice, while human net players score a point if they catch an opponent's airborne ball.
4) When one team reaches 10 points, players rotate and swap roles between court fielders and the human net for the next round.
pe-01259:
1) Set a target box and mark levels 1 to 5 at 1-step to 5-step distances using numbered cups.
2) Start the timer and throw 3 sock balls from level 1 until making 5 successful shots into the box.
3) Retrieve the balls and advance through level 2 (4 shots), level 3 (3 shots), level 4 (2 shots), and level 5 (1 shot) for 15 total goals.
4) Repeat for 2 to 3 rounds to challenge and improve your overall completion time.
pe-01260:
1) Fold colored paper to craft a wrinkled paper caterpillar and mark start and finish lines on a desk.
2) On signal, blow through a straw targeting the ridges or tail of the caterpillar to propel it forward.
3) Measure the time taken to reach the finish line or race simultaneously against a peer to score.
4) Modify the game by setting up curved tracks or playing as a back-and-forth relay.
pe-01261:
1) Assemble a chopstick launcher with rubber bands, stack 10 paper cups into a 4-tier pyramid, and set a firing line 3 steps away.
2) Load a rubber band behind the line, aim at the cup tower, and fire one band at a time.
3) Count the number of shots and time taken to knock down all cups on tiers 2, 3, and 4 to determine the score.
4) Increase shooting distance or assign numerical points to each cup to vary the competition.
pe-01262:
1) Prepare 1 to 3 small juggling balls and secure sufficient personal practice space.
2) Stage 1: Toss 1 ball in an arc from outside inward, clap hands, and catch it smoothly.
3) Stage 2: Hold 2 balls and practice toss-toss-catch-catch in an alternating rhythm or two-in-one-hand catches.
4) Advance to Stage 3 by maintaining a continuous 3-ball cascade pattern in the air.
pe-01263:
1) Set up cones in front of a wall to mark obstacles and prepare a soccer ball.
2) Practice inside, outside, toe, and heel passes against the wall while stopping the rebound with the sole of your foot.
3) Pass the ball toward the wall from one side of a cone, sprint to the other side to trap the ball, and count your successes.
4) Increase difficulty by narrowing the space or alternating feet on each pass.
pe-01264:
1) Set up four cones in a square and designate stations 1 through 4 at each corner.
2) Perform 10 two-hand ball tosses at station 1, then move to station 2 to complete 10 two-hand bounces.
3) Complete 10 right-hand dribbles at station 3 and 10 left-hand dribbles at station 4, then record the total elapsed time.
4) Progress from catch-and-bounce drills to alternating hands rapidly or lowering the target time limit.
pe-01265:
1) Place four numbered hula hoops at varying distances across the badminton net.
2) Stand behind the service line, hold the feathers with cork facing inward, and serve with an underhand stroke.
3) Serve shuttlecocks into hoops 1 through 4 in sequence and record the total time taken to clear all targets.
4) Turn it into a team relay where players alternate serves or award point values to each hoop for competitive scoring.
pe-01266:
1) Mount a tablet on a stand, launch the HomeCourt app Reaction drill, and align your body within the on-screen silhouette.
2) Maintain an athletic stance for 60 seconds and use rapid side steps to reach out and tap green targets appearing randomly on the screen.
3) Score points by touching green circles while avoiding red X marks that penalize points, then review the final score.
4) Increase movement speed to build combos or switch to battle mode to compete against a partner.
pe-01267:
1) Assume a plank position on a mat and roll a soccer ball in circles around each supporting hand 5 times.
2) Hold the plank while lightly tossing and catching the ball with each hand for 5 repetitions.
3) Lie flat on the mat holding the ball overhead, perform a V-up to transfer the ball from hands to feet, and lower down for 5 reps.
4) Increase the number of repetitions or practice facing a partner while rolling the ball back and forth.
pe-01268:
1) Prepare a badminton racket and shuttlecocks, then set a starting line and a turning point using cones.
2) Bounce the shuttlecock straight up on the racket face ten consecutive times in place.
3) Once mastered, walk toward the turning cone while tapping the shuttlecock and time completing three round trips.
4) If the shuttlecock drops, quickly restart and gradually increase the distance between cones for a greater challenge.
pe-01269:
1) Establish a central home base and arrange spot cones in six designated court zones around it.
2) On the start signal, sprint from the center to zone one, place a shuttlecock on the cone, and return to home.
3) Continue sequentially through zones two to six, placing one shuttlecock at each cone while timing the total sprint.
4) As an advanced variation, run back to each cone to retrieve all six shuttlecocks back to the center one by one.
pe-01270:
1) Stand behind a spot marker holding a soccer ball in both hands in an athletic stance.
2) Drop the ball to bounce on the floor, gently kick it upward with the shoelace area, and let it bounce or catch it.
3) Drop the ball directly and volley it up into your hands, gradually stringing together consecutive juggles up to ten.
4) Advance from instep juggling to thigh juggling with the knee parallel to the floor, and eventually attempt head juggling.
pe-01271:
1) Visually divide the goal into four numbered quadrants and mark three shooting distances using cones.
2) Approach the ball, plant the support foot one fist-width beside it with a bent knee, and lean forward into the strike.
3) Start at level one close range, calling a target zone (such as bottom corners or top corners), and shoot accurately.
4) Move back to cones at level two and level three upon success, testing accuracy and shooting power from distance.
pe-01272:
1) Perform jumping jacks continuously for 5 repetitions using a standard four-count movement.
2) Complete 5 repetitions of cross jacks by crossing the feet forward and back while alternating arm extensions.
3) Learn rhythm coordination movements such as limb separation exercises and baby seal clapping drills.
4) Complete the full 12-movement national gymnastics routine twice following rhythmic verbal cues.
pe-01273:
1) Place 4 cones in a square circuit pattern and position a toilet paper roll in the third station.
2) Complete 10 jumping jacks at station 1, then advance to station 2 to perform 10 cross jacks.
3) Tap the toilet paper roll 10 times alternating feet at station 3, then run to station 4 for 10 two-foot jumps.
4) Measure the total elapsed time using a stopwatch and encourage students to beat their personal records.
pe-01274:
1) Warm up thoroughly by stretching the neck, wrists, ankles, and waist for 10 seconds each on the mat.
2) Crouch with knees bent, tuck the chin firmly toward the chest, and place both hands flat on the mat.
3) Push off with the feet, letting hands, upper back, and hips touch the mat sequentially to complete the forward roll.
4) For backward rolls, place palms next to ears facing backward, roll over, and push firmly against the mat to stand up.
pe-01275:
1) Set up 4 cones in a square formation to establish training zones and place 1 soccer ball in play.
2) Jump over the stationary ball with feet together 10 times at zone 1, then dribble to zone 2 to perform 10 alternating toe taps.
3) Lightly tap the ball toward zone 4 from zone 3, sprint ahead of the ball, and trap it before it passes the boundary.
4) Repeat the kick, sprint, and stop sequence 3 times between zones 3 and 4, timing the full drill to beat previous records.
pe-01276:
1) Set up zigzag marker cones along a lane with a hula hoop placed at the turning point.
2) In Step 1, students gently push the soccer ball to the first cone and control it back without kicking it away.
3) In Step 2, students dribble into the hula hoop, bring the ball to a complete stop, circle around it, and dribble back.
4) In Step 3, dribble through zigzag cones, stop and loop inside the hoop, and weave back through the cones in a team relay.
pe-01277:
1) Adjust rope length so handles reach chest height when stepping on the middle of the rope with one foot.
2) Practice basic rhythm using the 2-bounce step (two hops per turn) and standard two-foot basic bounce.
3) Progress to alternate foot steps mimicking a jogging motion, followed by the double bounce on each foot.
4) Challenge students to perform side-straddle steps and 3-beat front-to-back cross steps continuously to music.
pe-01278:
1) Hold jump rope handles together in one hand and ensure a safe clear space away from peers.
2) Learn the basic swing (figure-eight motion) by rotating the rope continuously from side to side without jumping.
3) Practice the double swing rhythm by letting the rope tap the floor twice on each side in succession.
4) Connect the criss-cross wrap swing and the arm-wrapping release maneuver into a creative rhythm routine.
pe-01279:
1) Each student draws a 4x4 bingo grid on paper while the teacher secretly picks three undercover spies using software.
2) The teacher points vaguely toward the classroom areas where the spies sit as radar hints.
3) Students write down the names of 16 classmates on their grid, attempting to avoid the suspected spies.
4) When the teacher reveals the spies, players must cross them out with an X, and the first to complete 3 clear bingo lines wins.
pe-01280:
1) Select three taggers and five mafias from the class, and have the taggers face the blackboard holding whiteboard slates.
2) Display two citizen words and one mafia word on the screen, then prompt all students to express their assigned words through body gestures.
3) For 10 seconds, the taggers observe the full-body movements of the classroom to distinguish authentic gestures from mafia distractions.
4) If at least two taggers correctly write down both citizen words while avoiding the mafia word, the citizens win; otherwise, the mafia wins.
pe-01281:
1) Push classroom desks to the walls and tape across the floor in a cross pattern to form a 4-square raised net.
2) Divide the class into four squads seated in each square, with diagonal squads teaming up (Team A vs Team B).
3) Set a 3-minute timer, distribute an odd number of balloons, and hit balloons across the net while keeping bottoms on the floor.
4) The team with fewer balloons in their territory when time expires wins, with variations including playing seated on chairs or adding more balloons.
pe-01282:
1) Pair up students facing each other in the classroom either standing or seated.
2) Conduct a 5-activity sequence: palm strike balance, Cham-Cham-Cham face turn, handshake RPS hand-tap, thigh wrestling, and RPS leg-stretch.
3) In each game, the first player to lose balance or miss an attack/defense yields a point, playing best of three rounds.
4) Use as a quick warm-up or brain-break and rotate partners in a mini-tournament format.
pe-01283:
1) Arrange desks in groups of four facing each other, fold paper into 8 sections, and write 8 words to act out.
2) Determine turns by rock-paper-scissors; the presenter tears off an end word and acts it out silently.
3) Teammates raise hands to guess the answer, and whoever guesses correctly becomes the next presenter.
4) Finger count or initial letter hints can be given when difficult, continuing until all teammates finish all words.
pe-01284:
1) Sit at the classroom desk and hold both hands out as if gripping a car steering wheel.
2) When the teacher shouts "Bung-bung-bung!", students respond together with "Bureung-bureung!" and focus.
3) When the teacher commands "Right!", students turn the wheel right while leaning their body to the left in opposite coordination.
4) Once mastered, add extra commands like "Forward" (lean back), "Brake" (lean forward), and "Speed Bump" (seat jump) for reaction training.
pe-01285:
1) Students form two concentric circles with an inner circle of 6 players and an outer circle of 8 players standing within arms reach.
2) Inner players pass a balloon among themselves while outer players pass a ball around their own circle.
3) An outer player succeeds and swaps positions with an inner player if they strike and drop the inner team's balloon.
4) With more participants, add two balls and two balloons or reverse the passing direction dynamically.
pe-01286:
1) All students start as individual cavemen, play best-of-three rock-paper-scissors with peers, and the loser attaches behind the winner as a train.
2) When a group grows to 4-5 students, they form a tribe and create a unique tribal chant and signature gesture together.
3) Tribes meet, perform their chants, and engage in survival rock-paper-scissors where the losing tribe merges into the winning tribe's federation.
4) The game progresses with 1-on-1 matches between federations until the entire class is unified into a single nation.
pe-01287:
1) Desks are arranged facing each other in two team rows with boys and girls sitting alternately side by side.
2) Attackers stand in the center aisle and throw a soft foam ball toward the seated opposing team.
3) A girl is out if hit by a girl's throw and a boy is out if hit by a boy's throw, while players hit by the opposite gender are safe, allowing neighbors of the other gender to extend their arms as bodyguards.
4) Standing up or hiding underneath the desk counts as a foul, and the team with more surviving players wins.
pe-01288:
1) Arrange classroom chairs in a tight circle facing sideways after clearing the central space.
2) On cue, all students lie back simultaneously using the person behind them as a lap pillow.
3) The teacher gradually pulls out all chairs one by one, leaving students supporting each other.
4) Maintain the human-bridge circular formation without chairs for the target countdown to complete the mission.
pe-01289:
1) Arrange chairs in a circle with one less chair than the total number of students and place one 'it' player in the center.
2) The tagger picks an emotion word displayed on screen and shares a personal story of why they felt that emotion.
3) Classmates ask "Why?" and only those who empathize with the shared experience must stand up and dash to a different empty chair.
4) The student left without a seat becomes the next tagger, and becoming 'it' three times requires a fun short talent show.
pe-01290:
1) Students stand in a large circle and hold hands with their peers on both sides.
2) The teacher calls out directional commands (Right, Left, Forward, Backward, In-place, Shake), and students jump in unison while keeping hands held.
3) Without eliminations, the goal is to maintain the circle formation and rhythm without tripping or letting go of hands.
4) For variation, increase the tempo gradually or apply the 'opposite rule' where students jump in the reverse direction of the call.
pe-01291:
1) Form small table groups with assigned player numbers while the facilitator prepares a covered word card list in the corner.
2) Player one from each team rushes to check the first hidden prompt and acts it out silently using only body motions.
3) Once teammates guess correctly, the next player runs to whisper the answer to the proctor and receives the next prompt to act out.
4) The team whose members successfully guess all prompts and complete the final group chant mission first wins the challenge.
pe-01292:
1) Students start by lying flat on the floor beside their desks.
2) Players play rock-paper-scissors or answer quizzes against the teacher, moving up one level upon success: sitting on the floor, sitting on the chair, standing on the chair, and sitting on the desk.
3) When reaching the top desk level and raising both arms shouting hooray, the player scores 1 point, and then reverses the sequence down to the floor to earn another point.
4) Rules can be modified by altering winning conditions (e.g., tying or losing) or using cham-cham-cham mini-games to provide more opportunities.
pe-01293:
1) Fold and cut paper into strips, write target words such as animals or objects on each, fold them, and place them into a basket.
2) A quiz presenter draws one paper strip in secret and rolls a die.
3) Depending on the roll (1-2 for body gestures, 3-4 for verbal clues, 5-6 for drawing), the presenter describes the word, and the first guesser earns 1 point and becomes the next presenter.
4) In pairs, add a 30-second time limit per word to compete on how many words can be solved within the time.
pe-01294:
1) The teacher stands at the front as the conductor while students sit upright at their individual classroom desks.
2) The conductor performs a continuous sequence of 4-beat body percussion actions (e.g., knee tap 4 times, clap 4 times, shoulder tap 4 times, head tap 4 times).
3) Students must not copy immediately, but must perform the conductor's previous movement one sequence behind while observing the conductor's new movement.
4) To increase difficulty, speed up the tempo, divide the 4 beats into 2-beat combinations, or invite proficient students to take over as conductors.
pe-01295:
1) Students wear masks and stand or sit at their designated classroom desks maintaining personal distance.
2) The teacher explains the movement rules focusing on non-contact coordination and visual interaction.
3) Students perform target physical responses or coordination cues according to the teacher's signals.
4) The difficulty increases progressively by changing movement patterns and response speed without physical contact.
pe-01296:
1) Participants stand or sit comfortably facing the screen or leader with enough personal moving space.
2) The leader performs a specific body movement for four beats and transitions immediately to the next movement.
3) Students observe carefully and mirror the leader's previous movement exactly one sequence behind.
4) Increase the challenge by shortening the interval to three or two beats or rotating student leaders.
pe-01297:
1) Two partners sit or stand facing each other and choose a reaction rule set such as block or tag.
2) Both players perform rock-paper-scissors simultaneously and instantly identify the outcome.
3) The winner immediately executes the attack action while the loser performs the required block or evasive maneuver.
4) Introduce variations like mental addition, reverse shout calls, or finger coordination for added complexity.
pe-01298:
1) A group steps into the hallway and secretly designates one member to only mime playing the recorder.
2) The group stands in front of the classroom and performs a learned tune together while the secret player pretends.
3) Seated classmates listen closely and observe players' finger movements, breath, and expressions to deduce the imposter.
4) The audience discusses in small groups to guess the hidden player, then positions are swapped for the next round.
pe-01299:
1) Pair up students facing each other across a desk or standing face-to-face.
2) Choose one mode such as Cheers RPS, Lose-to-Win RPS, Quick Hand-Tag RPS, Addition RPS, or Toy-Hammer RPS.
3) Students compete to score points by shouting the outcome first, tagging the opponent's hand, or summing numbers faster.
4) Increase difficulty by inverting the verbal cues or switching attack and defense roles.
pe-01300:
1) Students stand in front of their webcams facing the screen.
2) While the tagger turns away and chants the countdown phrase, players clap rhythmically in front and behind their body.
3) If a player moves when the tagger turns back, their count resets to zero; the first player to reach 30 claps and press the raise-hand button wins.
4) Add character pose missions such as Spider-Man or elephant stances during freeze moments to increase engagement.
pe-01301:
1) Arrange classroom desks in a horseshoe layout and place stage 1–9 quiz sheets at designated desks.
2) Roll a large die at the blackboard to jump directly to that stage and point to a question for the desk examiner.
3) Answering correctly advances the player to the next stage and scores a point, while answering incorrectly swaps roles with the examiner.
4) Clearing all stages allows rolling the die again, and the team with the highest accumulated score wins.
pe-01302:
1) Divide the class into two opposing teams holding hands in a circular formation, placing a paper cup on a chair between the end players.
2) At the start signal, the front player squeezes the next player's hand to send a tactile "electric pulse" down the line.
3) The moment the last player feels their hand squeezed, they snatch the cup off the chair, scoring a point for the faster team.
4) After each round, the end players rotate to the very front of the line so all students cycle through the grabbing position.
pe-01303:
