3) If the leader throws a bounce pass, the partner throws a chest pass; if the leader throws a chest pass, the partner bounces it.
4) As an advanced drill, one partner tosses their ball vertically, receives and returns the leader's pass, then re-catches the aerial ball.
pe-01473:
1) Partners stand back-to-back, jump with a half-turn, and instantly call out the number flashed on the partner's fingers.
2) Keep one pivot foot anchored inside a floor ring while rotating and dodging to snatch the opponent's tail belt.
3) Scatter spot markers on the floor; when the teacher shouts "Moving day!", students quickly sprint to occupy a different marker.
4) Progress by calling specific colors, requiring students to identify and dash only to a differently colored spot marker.
pe-01474:
1) Pair up with one partner holding a newspaper sheet taut while the other stands in front.
2) On the signal, punch through the center of the newspaper sheet with full focus.
3) Progress from punches to front kicks, chops, and creative strikes to break the paper.
4) Switch roles and compare which striking technique tears the sheet most cleanly.
pe-01475:
1) Prepare soft Dodgebee discs for each student and maintain safe personal spacing.
2) Balance the disc on the head while walking, squatting, and standing without dropping it.
3) Toss the disc upward to catch after clapping, or pass back and forth with a partner.
4) Progress into target games by sliding discs along the floor or tossing into a basket.
pe-01476:
1) Roll and tie a hand towel into a soft ball and pair up with a partner.
2) One partner lies on the floor while the other drops the towel ball to dodge by rolling.
3) Stand up and toss the towel ball solo, clapping or touching the head before catching.
4) Play catch across 1-2 meters using non-dominant hands, behind-the-back tosses, or dodge rules.
pe-01477:
1) Stand tall with elbows at shoulder height and raise knees to touch elbows for 10 reps.
2) Extend arms sideways and kick toes upward toward the palms for 10 repetitions.
3) Lower into a deep sumo squat, lift one leg sideways, and hold balance for 3-5 seconds.
4) Assume a plank position and bring each knee forward to touch the elbow for 10 reps.
pe-01478:
1) Two partners sit facing each other on the floor and place a ball securely between their feet.
2) Without using their hands, they lift the ball using only their leg strength and pass it directly to each other's feet.
3) Both players rotate their bodies clockwise or counterclockwise while continuously passing the ball without dropping it.
4) Increase the challenge by lying back to tap the ball overhead or by using different ball sizes.
pe-01479:
1) Partners stand facing each other while maintaining a safe distance.
2) Both players play Rock-Paper-Scissors on the count of three.
3) The winner spreads both legs wide to create a tunnel, and the loser crawls completely through the legs.
4) Switch the rule so the loser makes the tunnel or play using feet to play Rock-Paper-Scissors.
pe-01480:
1) Start in a stable split-stance lunge position with one foot forward and the opposite foot back.
2) Jump vertically and swiftly switch the positions of both feet in mid-air before landing softly.
3) Repeat the foot-swapping jump continuously in rhythm while bending knees to absorb the impact.
4) Advance by jumping higher to switch feet twice or three times in a single aerial phase.
pe-01481:
1) Form pairs where one student holds a small soft ball and the partner holds a plastic bucket or container.
2) The thrower tosses the ball in an arc, while the receiver quickly tracks the trajectory and moves under the landing spot.
3) The receiver catches the ball directly into the bucket without letting it bounce out to score one point.
4) Increase difficulty by starting with backs turned before spinning around to catch, or by switching to smaller cups.
pe-01482:
1) Set up cones at the start and finish lines, then assign specific running modes like forward, sideways, or backward.
2) On the teacher's starting signal, sprint toward the target cone while quickly adjusting footwork and body orientation.
3) The runner who stabilizes balance and safely touches the turnaround cone first without stumbling wins a point.
4) Progress by having runners instantly switch running directions, such as transitioning from a forward sprint to a backward pedal upon a clapping cue.
pe-01483:
1) Mark the playing boundaries with cones, select one or two taggers, and let all other runners scatter within the court.
2) When a player is tagged by the tagger, they must freeze completely in place like a block of ice.
3) Two free runners must join hands around the frozen teammate and shout "Ding!" together to defrost and release them.
4) Increase difficulty by requiring three runners to defrost a player or by having taggers link hands to encircle runners.
pe-01484:
1) Place safety mats on the floor, and pair a student with a teacher or parent standing securely side-by-side.
2) Warm up with an elephant swing by supporting under the child's torso and gently swaying side-to-side to adapt to lateral movement.
3) The adult safely grasps the child under the armpits and waist, gently rotating them sideways in a full circular cartwheel motion to land.
4) Transition advanced students into practicing independent hands-on-mat side cartwheels and rolling challenges.
pe-01485:
1) Form pairs where one student sits firmly on a towel gripping the front edges with both hands while preparing to slide.
2) The standing partner holds the opposite edge of the towel and pulls slowly while maintaining a safe pathway.
3) Pairs successfully complete the challenge by gliding around a turn marker back to the start line, then switch roles.
4) You can advance the activity by guiding through curved courses or swapping towels for gym mats.
pe-01486:
1) The assistant sits on the mat while the learner lies face-up on the mat facing the partner.
2) The partner firmly grasps the learner's ankles to provide stable support and balance.
3) The learner lifts the hips in a bridge position and pulls the lower abdomen close to the partner.
4) The learner kicks the legs backward and upward overhead to develop backward rotational awareness for chin-ups.
pe-01487:
1) The partner kneels down, and the child lies stomach-down across the partner's thighs.
2) The partner firmly secures the child's waist and legs to prevent slipping off.
3) Rock back and forth rhythmically on the count of three to build rotational momentum.
4) Roll the child backward over the knees onto the soft floor mat to experience backward inversion safely.
pe-01488:
1) Two turners swing the long rope while two lines of students stand behind markers on opposite sides, with the front runner holding a ball.
2) The first pair from opposite sides enters the turning rope in sync as it hits the floor.
3) Both jumpers jump together in the center while hand-to-hand transferring the ball smoothly.
4) After the successful pass, both exit smoothly and the next runners repeat the relay without stopping the rope.
pe-01489:
1) Warm up with partner core-strengthening activities like the V-sit balance, vacuum cleaner game, and fish flipping game.
2) Practice rolling variations on the gym mat such as teacher-assisted hand-pull rolls and cross-armed rolls.
3) Challenge forward rolls with walking or running approaches to use forward momentum to stand up without touching hands.
4) Progress to a tail-tag roll game where the roller must immediately stand up and sprint before the chaser grabs their tail ribbon.
pe-01490:
1) Lay a long rope flat on the floor and have students practice two-foot hops over the rope without stepping on it.
2) Have students run straight and diagonally toward the still rope on the ground to jump over, practicing figure-8 rope entry paths.
3) Wiggle the rope side-to-side like a snake or up-and-down like small hills so students time their run and leap over the moving rope.
4) Progress to a swinging wave jump where students run into the swinging rope arc, jump over it in rhythm, and exit immediately.
pe-01491:
1) Two partners face each other in a standard push-up or plank hold position.
2) Lift one hand off the floor simultaneously to play rock-paper-scissors against each other.
3) The loser performs a quick movement penalty such as spinning around once in place, bear walking, or bunny hopping, then resumes position.
4) Vary the challenge by having the winner form a high bridge tunnel while the loser crawls through underneath for three laps.
pe-01492:
1) Place mats vertically over the gym stage edge for protection and set a springboard in front.
2) Run forward and perform a single-leg hop just before stepping onto the springboard.
3) Rebound off the board with both feet, place both hands firmly on the stage mat, and push off forcefully to land on two feet.
4) Gradually widen the springboard distance or emphasize quick hand repulsion to enhance airborne flight.
pe-01493:
1) Students take a personal jump rope and spread out across the area to maintain safe spacing.
2) Jump continuously to music following 8 designated skills including two-beat hops, basic single hops, jogging steps, straddle/scissor hops, cross hops, and double unders.
3) Completing the full 3-minute sequence without tripping achieves a 'Complete Clear', while students who trip immediately resume jumping to finish.
4) Beginners may substitute double unders with regular single hops or partner up to complete the 3 minutes as a relay challenge.
pe-01494:
1) Students stand safely beside their classroom chairs with sufficient clearance for arm movement.
2) Follow the counts through wrist stretches, shoulder rolls, rocket reaches, single-leg balances, tiptoe holds, soft hops, and shallow squats.
3) Successfully sit on the chair for the final 30 seconds to complete mindful deep breathing with closed eyes.
4) Modify for restricted mobility by performing movements entirely seated or mirroring a partner across the desk.
pe-01495:
1) Students scatter freely around the activity area ensuring safe personal space between peers.
2) When the teacher announces an animal prompt and gives one signal, students instantly act out that animal's movement and sound across the floor.
3) When two signals sound, students must immediately freeze and return to an upright human standing posture to earn points.
4) As students gain confidence, let individual learners take turns stepping up to announce creative new animal or insect prompts.
pe-01496:
1) Students start crouching low and stand up on cue, checking adequate distance from nearby peers.
2) Play 3 rounds of full-body Rock-Paper-Scissors against the teacher (squat for rock, split legs for scissors, star jump for paper), followed by arm circles, single-leg balances, tiptoe holds, behind-back clasps, and high star jumps.
3) Score points by beating the teacher in rock-paper-scissors rounds and holding balance poses steadily for 5 seconds.
4) Progress into peer-versus-peer matches or increase the number of star jumps to elevate energy levels.
pe-01497:
1) Two bases kneel on one knee and lock wrists underneath the flyer's armpits to prepare.
2) On the count, both bases stand up pushing inward while the center flyer jumps lightly upward.
3) The flyer locks their body completely straight forming a cross shape in the air to balance.
4) Land safely on command and gradually extend the aerial hold time from three to five seconds.
pe-01498:
1) Pair up so that one student acts as the dart floating face-down and the partner holds their feet.
2) The launcher gently but firmly pushes the partner forward to glide across the water surface.
3) Score points by keeping the body streamlined like a dart and passing through a floating hula hoop target.
4) Switch roles each turn and challenge longer gliding distances by moving the target hoop further away.
pe-01499:
1) Place starting cones and a central target cone on the floor, then have a runner and a tagger face each other.
2) The runner feints movements to test the tagger's balance, taps the center cone, and sprints back toward their goal line.
3) The tagger immediately reacts upon the touch to chase down the runner, scoring a point by tagging them before the line is crossed.
4) Expand the game into a 2-on-2 team matchup where runners execute diversion tactics and defenders cover open spaces together.
pe-01500:
1) Inspect the landing zone around the playground jungle gym and organize students into orderly small squads.
2) Students take turns tackling graded balance stunts including climbing up and down, sitting with legs extended, and releasing one hand and one foot.
3) Safely execute advanced stunts such as lateral shifting followed by landing, or hanging by the knees, scoring personal accomplishment points.
4) Modify the activity by introducing safe height boundaries or challenging squads to invent and present their own creative poses.
pe-01501:
1) Hold the jump rope horizontally in front of the body with one hand positioned below between the legs and the other above.
2) Keep the bottom hand stabilized between the legs while smoothly spinning the rope in a side-to-side planar motion with the top hand.
3) Lift the approaching leg with the knee brought forward to step over the incoming rope, immediately followed by the other leg.
4) Transition smoothly by swapping the upper and lower hand positions following a steady count of 'swing, 1, 2, switch' for continuous jumps.
pe-01502:
1) Line up behind the starting line facing marker cones set at the turnaround point.
2) Gallop forward rhythmically on signal by leading with one foot while the trailing foot chases.
3) Earn success points upon completing a clean turn around the target cone and bounding back.
4) Vary the challenge by alternating the lead leg or aiming for higher leap extensions.
pe-01503:
1) Stand in open space inside the classroom or gym keeping safe distances between peers.
2) Perform rhythmic warm-ups starting from the neck, wrists, ankles, and trunk rotations to the beat.
3) Score form points by accurately performing advanced hop-touch movements like elbow-to-knee and under-thigh touches on tempo.
4) Finish strong with dynamic wide-squat jumps and star jumps while keeping up with speed variations.
pe-01504:
1) Mark a defined square activity boundary using cones and select one player to be the tagger.
2) On the teacher's rhythmic count, all fleeing players take exactly five walking steps to reposition themselves.
3) The tagger also takes exactly five walking steps and attempts to step on a fleeing player's shadow.
4) Any player whose shadow is stepped on becomes the next tagger, with running strictly prohibited.
pe-01505:
1) Each student takes one soft foam ball and finds an open personal space.
2) Players gently toss the ball upward and catch it securely in front of their chest using both hands.
3) Progress through challenges such as making dish hands, clapping before catching, or catching after a bounce.
4) Keep score based on consecutive catches or expand by tossing the ball into boxes and hoop targets.
pe-01506:
1) Place cones at the start and finish lines and line up with ample personal space.
2) Assume designated positions such as sitting or lying face down, then sprint to the finish cone on signal.
3) Rank finishes and give handicaps by moving the first runner two steps back and the last runner two steps forward.
4) Apply a variation where runners keep arms crossed until a middle cone and vigorously swing their arms afterwards.
pe-01507:
1) Form pairs and face each other keeping a distance of two meters.
2) The controller moves two fingers, and the partner moves their whole body according to the finger directions.
3) Successfully reflect the motions using fingertips, toes, and facial expressions in coordination with the partner.
4) Switch roles to mirror each other's body movements or vary the speed and scale of actions.
pe-01508:
1) Draw a start line, an 'it' marker, and a pass line behind 'it' on the playground, then select one 'it'.
2) Players advance while 'it' chants the phrase, freeze when 'it' turns, and return to start if caught moving.
3) Once any player crosses the line behind 'it', all runners turn around and sprint back to the start line.
4) The player who crossed the line is safe, while the slowest runner to return becomes the next 'it'.
pe-01509:
1) Pair up with a partner and stand side by side holding individual jump ropes or sharing ropes.
2) Jump along to the rhythm of children's folk songs using basic two-foot bounces and side steps.
3) Perform designated foot crosses or direction changes on specific lyrics or accented beats of the song.
4) Advance by exchanging rope handles with each other or jumping synchronously inside a single shared rope.
pe-01512:
1) Set up cones on both sides about 1-1.5 meters from center line and place markers in a center basket.
2) Side shuffle rapidly across the lines to pick up markers from center and place them onto side cones.
3) Side shuffle back and forth to retrieve all markers from the outer cones and return them to the center basket.
4) Progress by increasing the marker count or doing head-to-head mirror drills with a partner opposite the line.
pe-01513:
1) Each team lines up behind the starting line with turning cones set up, and the first pair ties their ankles with a headband for a three-legged run.
2) On the signal, they run around the cone chanting in rhythm, return to the start, and add another teammate to tie together into a four-legged group.
3) Teams score a win by successfully adding runners round by round and having the entire group cross the finish line first.
4) You can adjust difficulty by increasing to larger groups or placing cones in a slalom pattern to maneuver around.
pe-01515:
1) Set up agility ladders in parallel lines or a square formation and position runners at opposite ends.
2) On start, players sprint through the ladder rungs simultaneously from both sides using varied footwork patterns.
3) When meeting at the center or corners, runners coordinate footwork carefully to cross without colliding.
4) In the square variation, four runners navigate the circuit continuously in a relay challenge.
pe-01517:
1) Set turning cones ahead and place scooter boards along the starting line with pairs.
2) Level 1: Kneel on the board and propel forward using hands on the floor to loop the cone.
3) Level 2: Place feet on the board in a push-up plank pose and crawl forward using hands.
4) Level 3: One partner holds the other's legs wheelbarrow-style while the front partner grips the board and drives forward.
pe-01518:
1) A thrower rolls a hula hoop upright across the floor while runners wait in line.
2) On cue, the runner sprints toward the path of the moving hoop, timing their approach.
3) The runner dives or leaps swiftly right through the moving circular frame without touching the edges.
4) Progressively increase hoop rolling speed or attempt passing through two consecutive rolling hoops.
pe-01519:
1) Place spot markers in a straight line on the floor and have group members line up behind one another.
2) Jump in and out of the markers to a three-beat rhythm cue while steadily moving forward.
3) Successfully complete the course by keeping the rhythm without stepping on or missing the markers.
4) Increase the challenge by starting from opposite sides toward each other or incorporating arm gestures and turns.
pe-01520:
1) Set up agility ladders on the floor and have students line up behind the starting line with proper spacing.
2) Move through the ladder spaces stepping inside and outside to the musical rhythm and count.
3) Succeed by having all team members complete the ladder continuously without tripping or missing a beat.
4) Advance through levels by adding side steps, arm swings, and crossing footwork patterns.
pe-01521:
1) Arrange two agility ladders in a cross shape (+) and place students at the four outer ends.
2) Start simultaneously from all four directions, stepping through the rungs toward the center intersection.
3) Earn team points by crossing through the busy central junction safely and reaching the other side.
4) Add variations by having runners turn 90 degrees at the center or increasing simultaneous runners.
pe-01522:
1) Set up double dutch turning ropes and place a hoop filled with beanbags at the turning point.
2) On the signal, each runner sprints, enters the turning ropes, jumps once or twice, and exits cleanly.
3) Pick up one beanbag from the hoop, bring it back to the home basket for a point, and tag the next runner.
4) If a runner gets caught, they must retry that jump, or variations can require additional jumps.
pe-01523:
1) Form groups of three where one student is the jumper and two partners hold a short jump rope low to the floor.
2) The jumper performs a standing long jump over the rope, after which the partners quickly move the rope forward.
3) The jumper repeats consecutive long jumps across the floor, aiming to reach the destination in the fewest jumps.
4) Increase difficulty by setting greater jump distances or having partners hold the rope slightly higher off the floor.
pe-01524:
1) Form a team of 5-6 students where two swing the long rope and the jumpers line up in front and back positions.
2) Jumpers begin leaping over the turning rope in unison starting from the basic Level 1 stage.
3) The team scores and completes the level by successfully making continuous jumps together without catching their feet on the rope.
4) Advance through Levels 1 to 5 by switching front and back orientations or increasing rope turning tempo.
pe-01528:
1) Crumple newspaper into 1–2 paper balls each and clear some space around you to sit or stand.
2) Sit on the floor with legs apart and roll the ball around your toes and behind your back to stretch, then lie down, catch the ball with your feet, and throw it up over your head.
3) Standing, bounce the ball up alternately with your palm and the back of your hand, and count how many times in a row you can keep it from dropping.
4) Once you are comfortable, add a second ball and keep both in the air, or face a family member or friend and compete at kicking the ball toward a target.
pe-01529:
1) Crumple a sheet of newspaper into a ball and roll it back and forth on the floor to get accustomed.
2) Have one player make a 'magic cave' first by standing with legs apart, then sit on the floor spreading their legs wide open as the magic door.
3) The thrower rolls the ball into the open space and sprints in to retrieve the treasure before the gate snaps shut.
4) Vary the challenge by having the seated defender close their eyes and listen closely before slamming the door shut to catch the retriever's hand.
pe-01530:
1) Inflate and tie a plastic grocery bag into a balloon shape, then gently tap it upward with hands to keep it airborne.
2) Toss the bag up and catch it after clapping hands or tapping designated body parts like head, shoulders, and hips.
3) Kick or launch the bag high, drop to the floor, and challenge yourself to catch it between your feet.
4) Progress to spinning a full turn in place or striking a unique frozen pose before securing the bag safely.
pe-01531:
1) Keep an inflated grocery bag in the air using dynamic striking techniques including punches and high kicks.
2) Toss the bag high, rapidly complete a 4-part coordination sequence of 'head-shoulders-knees-floor', and catch it cleanly.
3) Hold two inflated bags, launch them simultaneously, and catch them either simultaneously or with crossed arms.
4) Advance by tossing two bags, sprinting to touch the gym wall and returning to catch, or catching one by hand and one with a foot.
pe-01532:
1) Set up mini-hurdles and folded boxes at regular intervals to create rhythmic courses for each group.
2) Runners sprint and leap over each hurdle according to designated cadence beats like step-step-jump.
3) Earn points by clearing all hurdles consecutively without touching any hurdles or cardboard boxes.
4) Vary the spacing between hurdles or add obstacle boxes to create diverse stepping rhythms.
pe-01533:
1) Divide the class into 4 teams with bibs and assign runners along an open-course track.
2) The lead runner sprints on the starting whistle toward the exchange zone of the next teammate.
3) Pass the baton without slowing down using opposite hands between incoming and outgoing runners.
4) Have incoming runners deliver with the right hand and immediately peel off inside the track.
pe-01534:
1) Gather at the pool deck and demonstrate two kickboard holding methods: head-up and face-in-water.
2) Push off the wall holding the front of the board with straight elbows and flutter-kick forward.
3) Rest hands on the near edge, dip the face into the pool, and practice rhythmic breathing while kicking.
4) Students evaluate and select their preferred kicking technique to complete lane lengths independently.
pe-01535:
1) Divide students into teams on a netted court with soft volleyballs.
2) Allow the ball to bounce once before receiving, and require all team members to touch the ball.
3) The second player can catch the ball and toss it smoothly to the third player for an attack.
4) Adapt rules by allowing up to five hits or underhand passes so every team can rally easily.
pe-01536:
1) Spread both arms out to the sides and lift one foot off the ground upon the signal.
2) If the lifted foot touches the floor or balance is lost, the student sits down immediately.
3) Top survivors from the preliminary rounds advance to the final championship match.
4) Increase difficulty in the finals by closing eyes or timing the record with a stopwatch to determine the winner.
pe-01537:
1) Prepare an obstacle zone by placing foam blocks or noodles horizontally or vertically on gym mats.
2) Move forward across the mat using a seal crawl or wheelbarrow walk before reaching the foam block.
3) Raise the hips high and execute a forward roll over the aid while tucking the head safely to earn a completion point.
4) Progress to a jump forward roll or raise the obstacle height to increase the movement difficulty.
pe-01538:
1) Set up four 5-meter goals along each sideline of a 30m by 15m court and divide players using pinnies.
2) Introduce 4 soccer balls simultaneously onto the pitch for an 8-versus-8 match lasting 5 minutes.
3) Score 1 point by kicking any ball into any of the four open goals, while reserve players serve as ball retrievers and scorekeepers.
4) Vary the challenge by decreasing the number of balls or requiring players to pass with their non-dominant foot.
pe-01539:
1) Stand by classroom desks and practice four evolution poses: Rabbit (crouching), Kangaroo (sitting), Human (standing), and Giant (standing on chair).
2) Jump in rhythm to the teacher's call and execute whole-body rock-paper-scissors gestures.
3) Players advance one stage upon winning, revert to the initial rabbit stage upon losing, and score by reaching the god stage.
4) Modify by having students roam to challenge peers or changing to chair-seated leg-spread stag beetle RPS.
pe-01540:
1) Each student inflates and ties a balloon and gets ready to keep it in the air using various body parts like hands, head, or feet.
2) Students challenge themselves with individual missions such as consecutive taps, balancing on a finger or forehead, and moving to a goal line while tapping.
3) In pairs, students hold balloon nozzles and engage in a gentle balloon duel to see who can tap the partner's head three times first.
4) Groups can advance to a cooperative challenge where they keep the balloon airborne while taking turns playing a word-chain game.
pe-01541:
1) Each student holds a 70cm plastic ribbon and spreads out across the area ensuring plenty of personal space.
2) Students wave the ribbon like a swimming fish, crumple it into a lightweight ball to toss and catch repeatedly, and practice throwing mechanics.
3) Without using their hands, students place the ribbon flat against their stomach and sprint through straight or zigzag courses using wind pressure.
4) Three braided ribbons are tucked into waistbands as tails, transforming the drill into a tag game with movement constraints like skipping.
pe-01542:
1) Attackers each take a ball and wear two waist tags, while defenders position themselves inside the playing zone.
2) On signal, attackers sprint toward the end goal area while dodging defenders trying to pull their tags.
3) Attackers score 1 point by placing the ball in the goal area without losing either tag, while tagged runners must fetch a tag from a hoop and restart.
4) For upper grades, reduce balls so untagged teammates can receive lateral or backward passes to advance strategically.
pe-01543:
1) Each student prepares a 100g soft volleyball, and numbered pinnies/bibs are hung on the gym wall as targets.
2) Students lower their hips, bend knees, face the ball squarely, and practice consecutive wall receives either no-bounce or one-bounce.
3) Students execute underhand serves aimed directly at the hanging bib target on the wall to hone accuracy and flight control.
4) Progress by catching the wall rebound on one bounce to execute an immediate receive, and step back across court lines to increase difficulty.
pe-01544:
1) Divide each 15-player team into roles (1 King, 1 Hero, 3 Warriors, 3 Mages, 2 Priests, 5 Slimes) and publicly reveal each team's King.
2) Play like standard dodgeball, but Warriors only get out by Hero or Mage throws, and any touch on a Mage's ball results in an immediate out.
3) When a Priest hits an opponent, an eliminated teammate is revived, and Slimes link shoulders to become an invincible King Slime until hit.
4) Teammates must protect their King from getting hit, and the team that successfully eliminates the opposing King wins the match.
pe-01545:
1) Divide the class into partnered team pairs and set up three target stages with cones on stands along with designated throwing lines.
2) On the start signal, the throwing team launches balls to knock down or dislodge the cones to clear each stage sequentially.
3) Record the total elapsed time until all stages are cleared, competing to improve and beat the team's best time record.
4) The partner team supports by retrieving balls and giving advice, with options to adjust throwing distances or target layouts as progression.
pe-01546:
1) Set up two goals side-by-side and organize students into 2 attackers and 1 goalkeeper using a flat, non-bouncing soccer ball.
2) The single goalkeeper defends both goals while the two attackers face the goals and exchange passes to shift the keeper side-to-side.
3) An attacker shoots directly if their facing goal is unguarded, or passes to the teammate at the open goal if the keeper moves to block.
4) Once mastered, widen the passing distance between attackers to increase keeper movement, or adjust time limits and defender constraints.
pe-01547:
1) The fielding team places two out-boards in the field, keeping the catcher area and the pitcher-to-home lane clear for safety.
2) The batter hits the ball off a tee or from a pitcher and runs around the bases without leading off.
3) The fielding team gets an out if they hit an out-board with the ball before the runner touches the base; otherwise the runner is safe.
4) The batting team scores one point when a runner safely returns to home plate, while balls failing minimum distance count as fouls.
pe-01548:
1) Mark an S-shaped boundary with safety cones placed at each team's home base at opposite ends.
2) Players hop on one foot inside the path once they leave the safety of their designated base area.
3) When opposing players meet along the curves, they push palms together trying to make the rival drop their raised foot.
4) Knocked-down players must reset to their home base, and the first team to push through and topple the opposing cone wins the round.
pe-01549:

pe-01550:

pe-01551:

pe-01552:

pe-01554:

pe-01555:

pe-01556:

pe-01557:

pe-01559:

pe-01560:

pe-01561:

pe-01562:

pe-01563:

pe-01564:

pe-01565:

3) Scoring: Score one point for each knocked-over bottle, basketed ball, or hit plate target within a one-minute round while retrieving and resetting.

pe-01566:

3) Alternate tapping heels and toes in rhythm for 20 seconds, followed by another 5-second rest.

2) Follow onscreen cues by jumping over enemies, ducking obstacles, and sprinting in place.
3) Transition through levels performing Boo freeze stops, mountain jacks, swimming arm strokes, punches, and kicks.
4) Complete all 8 stages including boss dodging and stomping squats to successfully finish the workout challenge.
pe-01705:
1) A student steps onto the center of a mini trampoline and establishes a stable upright posture.
2) Perform fundamental jumps including in-and-outs, torso twists, and side-to-side runs in 15-second intervals.
3) Progressively execute higher-level hops like fast feet, star jumps, bell jumps, high knees, and scissors in rhythm.
4) Vary the activity by lowering jump heights or practicing floor-based footwork so the whole class can rotate through.
pe-01706:
1) Set up multiple jumping stations around the gym using pool noodles, hula hoops, crash mats, and spot markers before dividing students into small groups.
2) On the teacher's signal, groups practice their assigned station by jumping over swinging noodles, leaping onto mats, or hopping along spot markers.
3) Students count successful consecutive jumps without touching obstacles to earn points for themselves or their teams.
4) Rotate to the next station after a set duration and increase the difficulty by switching between two-foot jumps and single-leg hops.
pe-01707:
1) Divide the class into teams of 3 or 4, stacking 6 hula hoops over a cone at each team's base while placing a die at the opposite turning cone.
2) On the start signal, the first runner sprints across the gym to roll the die and unlocks one hoop from the cone if they roll an even number.
3) Runners sprint back to tag the next teammate in line, continuing the relay until all six hoops are successfully unlocked.
4) Once all six hoops are released, the team collaborates to build a freestanding hula-hut igloo and crawls through it to finish.
pe-01708:
1) Place a large pile of bean bags in the center of the gym and scatter six hula hoops around the perimeter, assigning each team to a hoop.
2) On the start whistle, one runner from each team dashes safely into the center circle, grabs a single piece of treasure, and returns it to their hoop.
3) Teammates take turns in a continuous relay fashion to collect treasure until the center pile is completely cleared.
4) Count the collected bean bags to calculate team points, or modify the game by allowing students to steal one bean bag from opponents' hoops.
pe-01709:
1) Scatter poly spots across the gym floor like stepping stones and establish start and finish areas.
2) Students balance and step only on the spots without touching the floor to navigate the lava river.
3) Each time a student successfully crosses to the end, they collect a counter block to track their score.
4) Increase difficulty by widening spot intervals or timing the crossing in team relays.
pe-01710:
1) Equip team scooters with pool noodle handles and buckets at the start line, and scatter beanbags at the far end.
2) On the signal, each lead runner pushes their scooter cart across the gymnasium toward the beanbag area.
3) The runner grabs one beanbag, drops it into the cart bucket, rushes back, and handsoff to the next teammate.
4) Teams count their collected beanbags for total score, or slalom around cones to adjust the challenge.
pe-01711:
1) Scatter hula hoops across the gym floor to serve as bounce pass targets between partners.
2) Pairs stand facing each other across a hoop and perform crisp bounce passes aiming inside the circle.
3) After completing three consecutive bounce passes, the partner without the ball hustles to find a new teammate.
4) Players holding the basketball raise it overhead to signal for a new partner, and passing distances can be extended.
pe-01712:
1) Teams line up behind their colored cone facing six snowman bowling pins set in a straight line marked by spot markers.
2) The first runner selects an item (gator ball, koosh ball, or bean bag) from their team bucket to roll, toss, or slide toward the first snowman.
3) If knocked over, the runner collects the snowman and their throwing item to bring back to the team, but if missed, they only retrieve the item and return.
4) Teams progress through each tier sequentially, and the team that successfully knocks down and collects all six snowmen first wins.
pe-01713:
1) Students form small groups of 2-3 with a die, and six colored rainbow cones are laid flat on the floor (lights off) across from them.
2) On the start signal, the first runner rolls the die, checks the rolled number, and sprints to the corresponding colored cone.
3) If the cone of that number is down, the runner turns it on by setting it upright; if it is already standing, they must turn it off by knocking it flat.
4) Teammates take turns rolling and running until one team successfully turns all six cones (lights) upright to win.
pe-01714:
1) Bowling pins (ghosts) are placed on spot markers and hula hoops are scattered in the center line, while teams line up on opposite sides of the gym.
2) The first player steps with the opposite foot and smoothly rolls a ball along the floor toward the center targets.
3) Knocking down a ghost earns one candy beanbag (after resetting the pin), while landing the ball completely inside a hula hoop awards three candy beanbags.
4) Players retrieve their ball and candies, hand off to the next teammate, and the team with the most candies collected at the end wins.

3) Students then lift the hoop to practice hula hoop jump roping, arm twirling, and classic waist hooping coordinated movements.
4) Finally, students roll the hoop forward with backspin so it reverses direction and rolls back to be caught cleanly.

2) On the leader's signal, everyone lifts the parachute high overhead together to create a large floating dome.
3) When the leader calls out a specific shirt color, students wearing that color walk underneath to the opposite side.
4) For variation, players can take a giant step inside to pitch a tent or add tossing numbers on top for a math challenge.
pe-01777:
1) Students scatter across the playing area, and half of the players hold a 7-inch coated foam ball of different colors.
2) The ball carrier quickly completes three passes to a partner who signals with open hands.
3) After completing three passes, the player relinquishes the ball, becomes an open receiver, and seeks out a different colored ball.
4) Add variations such as requiring all three throws to be bounce passes or prohibiting receiving the same color consecutively.
pe-01778:
1) Students pair up facing each other behind a line of numbered cones spaced across the gym.
2) One partner tosses the ball underhand, and the opposite partner volleys it back out of the air using the inside of the foot into their hands.
3) After completing a successful volley with both right and left feet, partners swap positions and advance to the next numbered cone.
4) Teams race to cycle through cones 1 through 6, then conclude with a continuous zigzag dribbling challenge through the course.
pe-01779:
1) Two players take positions at opposite ends of the Nok Hockey board holding a mini stick.
2) When the puck is on your half, strike it toward the opposing goal in a single hit without stick-handling.
3) Score a point by shooting directly or banking the puck off the side cushions into the goal.
4) Switch to a two-on-two tag team format where partners alternate taking shots.
pe-01780:
1) Each student stands beside their desk holding juggling scarves in both hands.
2) Move your arms in large circles and trace alphabet letters in the air as instructed.
3) Solve calling math problems while tossing and catching the scarf to match the rhythm.
4) Progress into quick-reaction drills by dropping and snatching scarves out of the air.
pe-01781:
1) Students each hold a pool noodle and space out facing the gym wall.
2) Throw the noodle overhand toward the wall target using a javelin throwing technique.
3) Pair up to roll, toss, and balance a soft foam ball together along the noodles.
4) Transition into team noodle hockey by holding both ends of the noodle to strike the ball into the wall.
pe-01782:
1) Set up a rebound frame and a semicircular forbidden zone at each end line, and divide the class into two teams.
2) A player holding the ball may not take more than 3 steps, and the team must connect passes within 3 passes to shoot at a frame.
3) If the ball rebounds off the frame and lands on the court floor outside the forbidden zone, the team scores; if a defender catches it directly, no point is scored.
4) Players may not intercept an opponent's pass or shot directly, and the two-way rule applies, so either frame may be attacked.
pe-01783:
1) Divide players across the center line or net, each holding an eclipse ball paddle with a firm wrist.
2) Serve the ball over the net after letting it bounce once on the floor.
3) Set up passes among teammates allowing one bounce between hits before returning it over.
4) Play multi-player games where consecutive hits by the same player are prohibited.
pe-01784:
1) Teams line up in a single file between the water source disc and the fire target disc.
2) The front player picks up a bean bag and passes it over the left shoulder to the teammate behind.
3) After passing, the runner sprints along the side to the very back of the line to continue receiving.
4) The first team to transfer all bean bags to the final target disc to extinguish the fire wins.
pe-01785:
1) Students pair up with one sitting on the scooter board and the other standing behind to push.
2) On the start signal, the pusher navigates the scooter forward toward a target cone.
3) The rider must grasp and lift the cone using only their feet without touching it with hands.
4) The team races back to the start holding the cone and tags the next pair to finish first.
pe-01786:
1) Players set up in doubles on opposite sides of a low portable net holding pickleball paddles.
2) The server executes an underhand serve striking the ball below the navel into the diagonal court.
3) Both the serve and the return must bounce once on each side before any volley is allowed (Double Bounce Rule).
4) Players continue the rally with flat paddle strikes, scoring points when opponents commit a fault.
pe-01787:
1) Nine players enter the elevated 3x3 grid structure, each occupying a designated square numbered 1 to 9.
2) The player in the center square (#9/King) serves the ball up and over the top frame into another square.
3) Players use volleyball overhead sets or hits to keep the ball airborne and direct it out of their square on one touch.
4) When a player misses or hits out of bounds, they rotate to square 1 while others move up toward the center.
pe-01788:
1) Each student takes up to three scarves and holds the center pinch to form a ghost shape.
2) With one scarf, lift gently upward and catch on the descent using a downward palm claw catch.
3) With two scarves, practice the criss-cross X-pattern calling out 'throw, throw, catch, catch' alternately.
4) Progress to three scarves, starting with the hand holding two, maintaining a rhythm with only one scarf in the air at a time.
pe-01789:
1) Mark a 15m or 20m running course across the gym and pair up students into two-person teams.
2) The first runner jogs across to the opposite line in sync with the audio beeps, tags their partner's hand, and switches roles.
3) Partners alternate laps to manage fatigue, with stronger runners allowed to take consecutive turns to give their partner a rest.
4) The test ends when the team fails to cross the line before the beep twice, recording the total successful laps completed.
pe-01790:
1) Fold and create three paper airplanes and place a laundry basket or bucket 5 to 10 feet away from the throwing line.
2) Start a 1-minute timer and throw the three paper airplanes one by one from behind the throwing line toward the basket.
3) Score 1 point if an airplane hits the outside of the basket and 2 points if it lands inside, quickly retrieving and re-throwing within the time limit.
4) Adjust the challenge by moving the basket further away or using a smaller target bucket to increase difficulty.
pe-01791:
1) Students line up at an appropriate distance around the basketball hoops with small arcade basketballs.
2) Review and practice the four core shooting cues of B.E.E.F. (Balance, Eyes, Elbow, Follow-through).
3) Follow the leader's demonstrated form and shoot toward the back of the basketball rim.
4) As a modification for more power, students bend their knees and jump during the shot instead of standing still.
pe-01792:
1) Set up eight stations across the gym including traveling mat, vault, rock wall, rope swing, balance, jump boxes, balance beam, and partner balance.
2) Divide students into small groups at each numbered station and review the challenge task cards.
3) Practice each skill while music plays, and rotate along the gym lines to the next numbered station when music stops.
4) Modify difficulty by adjusting vault mat height, jumping tricks, or balancing with a bean bag on the head based on grade level.
pe-01793:
1) Students take off their shoes and line up in orderly fashion behind the sit and reach box.
2) Sit with one leg straight against the box, the other foot flat next to the knee, and fingertips aligned together.
3) Reach forward along the measuring scale as far as possible and hold the stretch for three seconds while the teacher records the score.
4) Switch legs to complete the second trial, then move over to the scale and stadiometer for private height and weight recording.
pe-01794:
1) Divide the gym into two courts, place a mat trashcan in each backcourt, and designate one student per team as Oscar inside the trashcan.
2) Scatter foam balls (trash) across the playing area and have students pick up only one ball at a time.
3) Players throw balls into the opposing team's mat using overhand or underhand throws, while Oscar continuously tosses balls out of the can.
4) If a player crosses the center line, they step aside to recite the ABCs before returning, and the team with the least trash in their can wins.
pe-01795:
1) Select two taggers holding pool noodles while other students scatter across the open gym space.
2) When music plays, taggers chase runners and tag them gently with their noodles to freeze them.
3) Tagged runners, runners stepping out of bounds, or those falling must stay in place doing a fist pump dance without being unfrozen.
4) The round continues until the music stops, after which new taggers are chosen to begin a new round.
pe-01796:
1) Assign one player to each of four marked squares (1-4) and have waiting students line up behind square one.
2) The server in square 4 bounces the ball once behind the service line and strikes it underhand into another player's square.
3) Players must allow the ball to bounce once before striking it into another square; hitting inside lines, double bounces, or hitting out results in an out.
4) The eliminated player moves to the end of the waiting line, players advance up a square number toward square 4, and the next challenger enters square 1.
pe-01797:
1) The turner stands at the center with a thunderstick while students form a circle or stand along court boundary lines.
2) The turner sweeps the thunderstick rope along the floor in a low circle around their feet.
3) Students jump over the incoming rope with timing; anyone whose foot gets struck by the rope is temporarily out.
4) Eliminated students move to an outside station to hula hoop or jog until a final winner remains to reset the game.
pe-01798:
1) Position two rope turners while students line up single file facing the entry side of the long jump rope.
2) Turners rotate the rope outward from the runners, and students continuously enter the rope the moment the runner ahead leaps.
3) Each student performs exactly one jump and exits smoothly; touching the rope or letting the rope complete an empty turn results in elimination.
4) Eliminated students move to a secondary practice rope to keep active, while top finalists from multiple heats advance to a championship round.
pe-01799:
1) Each student spreads out across the gymnasium with one soccer ball ready to dribble.
2) When designated bumpers approach playing light defense, students shield and protect the ball with their body.
3) If a student's ball is bumped out of bounds, they perform 5 push-ups before returning to play.
4) Bumpers pass the role to a quiet hand-raising student to rotate defenders while keeping defense intensity moderate.
pe-01800:
1) Students line up spread out along the gym sideline and observe teacher demonstration laps.
2) On the starting signal, students run straight and slow across the modified short distance before the beep.
3) As test levels increase in speed, students keep pacing; making two consecutive mistakes ends their test.
4) Finished students sit down immediately to cheer silently for peers aiming for 25 to 30 total laps.
pe-01801:
1) Adjust the jump rope length by stepping on its center so handles reach armpit height.
2) The teacher stands behind the student and guides their hands to make a big overhead circular turning motion.
3) The student waits for the rope to hit the floor in front of their feet before jumping over it.
4) Once single jumps are mastered, progress to backwards jumping and consecutive jumps of two to five reps.
pe-01802:
1) Spread out into open space with safe personal boundaries across the room.
2) Perform four rounds of the 4-count chicken dance consisting of beaks, wings, tail feathers, and claps.
3) During the musical movement break, travel around the open area performing locomotor skills like skipping, sliding, and galloping.
4) Progress by having students square dance with partners or use ribbons and scarves during movement breaks.
pe-01803:
1) Scatter a deck of 60 silly task cards face down inside the center circle of the gym.
2) On the start signal, students run in, grab one card, and complete the movement or social interaction challenge with peers.
3) Once completed, hand the card face up to the teacher and immediately grab another card to beat the target time.
4) When the central pile is empty, students without cards actively seek out and assist classmates still finishing tasks.
pe-01804:
1) For chest passes, stand 2 steps from a wall; for bounce passes, stand back-to-back with a partner, take 2 steps apart, and face each other.
2) Push the chest pass straight forward from chest level, and push the bounce pass toward the floor about three-quarters of the way to your partner.
3) Extend both arms with thumbs pointing down upon release, and catch incoming balls firmly using both hands.
4) Begin with individual chest passes against the gym wall, then transition into cooperative partner bounce passing practice.
pe-01805:
1) Set up 18 diverse activity stations across the gym and field, including javelin throw, noodle tower, cup stack relay, and sack race.
2) Divide the class into squads to rotate through stations every 6 minutes upon hearing the air horn signal.
3) Teams score by throwing the farthest, building the tallest self-standing tower, or finishing relay races fastest.
4) Practice game rules with early grades first, then progress to competitive team challenges and championship throw-offs.
pe-01806:
1) Pair students up in groups of two or three facing each other in front of a basketball hoop.
2) Both players simultaneously dribble 5 times (or slap the ball 5 times for early grades), then tap their balls together.
3) Immediately following the ball tap, both players sprint to shoot, continuing until someone successfully makes a basket.
4) The first player to score earns a point and resets to the starting mark; the first to reach 3 points wins the match.
pe-01807:
1) Pair students up with one longer jump rope designated for two jumpers.
2) In 'Face to Face', one partner turns the rope while both jump together facing each other, or the second runner enters mid-turn.
3) In 'Side by Side', each partner holds one handle with their outside hand and coordinates a simultaneous swing and jump.
4) Progress from basic jumps to advanced challenges such as spinning, touching the floor, or jumping in and out of the turning rope.
pe-01808:
1) Students receive a bingo sheet and marker, then gather in the central square.
2) When music plays, ask a classmate about an adventure activity on the card (one question per person).
3) If they answer yes, have them initial the square, then run to tag the cone and jog one lap before asking another person.
4) Each classmate can sign only once, and players aim to complete 4 or 6 boxes in a row before time runs out.
pe-01809:
1) Students sit on their mats in a pike position and view two balance options shown on screen.
2) On signal, try both balance poses within 30 seconds while engaging core muscles.
3) Hold each balance like a statue for at least 5 seconds to feel the required strength, flexibility, and stability.
4) Progress from basic balances to smaller bases of support and inverted poses, voting and discussing which was more challenging.
pe-01810:
1) Set up nine hula hoops in a 3x3 grid and place team cones with three colored scarves at the start line.
2) On go, the first runner takes one scarf, sprints forward, places it inside a hoop, and runs back.
3) The next runner can only leave the cone once tagged by the returning runner, placing another scarf strategically.
4) After all three scarves are played, subsequent runners sprint up to move one of their own scarves to an open hoop until one team aligns three in a row.
pe-01811:
1) Stand at an appropriate distance facing a gym wall marked with a target area, holding a foam ball.
2) Point your non-throwing side toward the wall target and bring your throwing arm back into an uppercase L shape.
3) Step with the opposite foot, twist your torso, and throw the ball overhand at the target, catching the rebound.
4) Catch the ball off the wall three times in a row, then jog one full lap around the gym before returning for another round.
pe-01812:
1) A small group of 3–5 students lines up facing a wall, and the first thrower hurls a tennis ball (or bouncy ball) against the wall so that it bounces back.
2) Another group member catches the rebounding ball, no matter how many times it has bounced on the floor, and immediately throws it back at the wall to keep play going.
3) A player who misses the catch must sprint and touch the wall before another player picks up the ball and hits the wall; if they get there first, they are safe.
4) Vary the difficulty and speed with underhand throws, no-bounce catches, or by adding more balls.
pe-01813:
1) Divide players into Lion and Tiger teams and line them up facing each other along the center markers.
2) When the teacher calls out one team's name, that team turns and sprints toward their safe zone while the other team chases.
3) Players tagged before crossing the safe zone line switch to the opposing team for the next round.
4) Modify by pairing specific partners, playing touchless, or having students start from fitness positions like planks or animal crawls.
pe-01814:
1) Divide players into two teams on a basketball court and determine initial possession with rock-paper-scissors at center court.
2) The offensive team advances by passing only without taking steps, scoring points by throwing the football into the opponent's hoop.
3) If a pass hits the floor or an airborne ball is swatted down by defenders, possession switches immediately to the opposing team.
4) Defenders must maintain a buffer of 1 to 2 feet without stripping balls from hands, with variations allowing adjusted team sizes or multiple half-courts.
pe-01815:
1) All students start inside the basketball court boundaries while multiple dodgeballs are tossed into the playing area for a free-for-all match.
2) Players pick up balls and attempt to hit any opponent, and anyone struck by a ball must immediately exit to the outer boundary lines.
3) Out-of-bounds players remain active by retrieving balls rolling outside and throwing them at remaining players inside the court.
4) The game continues until only one survivor remains inside, with optional variations allowing outer throwers to re-enter upon scoring a hit.
pe-01816:
1) Divide the court into two halves with end zones at each boundary, placing several teammates wearing flag belts into the opposite end zones.
2) Players throw football passes from their home court across to trapped teammates waiting in the opposing end zone.
3) Upon catching a pass in the end zone, that player chooses between punting the ball back for a teammate to catch or sprinting across the court without getting their flag pulled.
4) If a runner's flag is pulled they must return to the end zone, and the first team to successfully bring all end-zone teammates back wins.
pe-01817:
1) Divide into teams of four or five, with every player holding at least one hand on their team's hula hoop.
2) Scatter a large collection of foam balls in the center of the gym and wait for the starting whistle.
3) Move together as a unit holding the hoop and use only feet to kick and pass one ball back to your base at a time.
4) Count the collected balls or sum up point values assigned to different ball colors at the end to determine the winner.
pe-01818:
1) Arrange four gym mats like baseball bases and divide runners so no more than three occupy a single mat.
2) Assign two taggers equipped with dodgeballs in the center while runners continuously circulate the bases forward.
3) Runners are safe while standing on a mat but can be hit by a thrown dodgeball whenever they move between mats.
4) Any runner hit becomes a tagger while the thrower becomes a runner, and an arriving runner forces the lead runner off the mat.
pe-01819:
1) Place hula hoops with an equal number of bean bags at each corner and divide students into teams at their home bases.
2) On go, players run to steal one bean bag at a time from any opposing team's hoop and return it to their own hoop.
3) The team with the most bean bags inside their hoop at the end of the time limit wins.
4) As a variation, tag rules can be introduced so defenders can protect their hoops.
pe-01820:
1) Divide the playing field into multiple distance zones and assign higher point values to zones further away.
2) The first player of each team stands as the thrower while the second player positions themselves in a chosen target zone to catch.
3) Successfully catching the thrown disc scores that zone's points, after which the thrower becomes the catcher and the catcher returns to the back of the line.
4) Variations include racing to a target score or switching the equipment to footballs or baseballs.
pe-01821:
1) Set up equal numbers of plastic pins as targets in each team's end and mark exclusive goalie zones.
2) Introduce multiple foam soccer balls for continuous passing and kicking action across the court.
3) Players shoot to knock down opposing pins; successfully downed pins are claimed and added to their own side until one team captures them all.
4) Expand to a four-corner team elimination format or vary ball counts to boost participation.
pe-01822:
1) Divide students into teams behind the starting line and place a cone at the turning point for each team.
2) The first runner places a pool noodle between their knees without using hands and waddles around the cone.
3) Upon returning, they pass the noodle to the next teammate, and the team that finishes first wins.
4) For variations, returning runners can add teammates to hold the noodle together like a train, or try balancing it vertically on their palms while running.
pe-01823:
1) Choose one student as the tagger (Tatanka) in the middle while the remaining players (buffaloes) line up along one end line.
2) When the center tagger shouts "Tatanka, Tatanka!", all runners sprint across to the opposite end without getting tagged.
3) Any runners tagged before reaching safety join the taggers in the middle for the subsequent rounds.
4) Continue playing as the tagger pack expands until everyone is caught, or reset with the last remaining runner as the new Tatanka.
pe-01824:
1) Scatter all students across the playing area, appoint 2–3 initial taggers with soccer balls, and place extra balls in a sideline bin.
2) Taggers dribble around and pass or gently kick their balls to tag fleeing runners strictly on their feet.
3) Any runner whose foot gets hit goes to the bin, grabs a new soccer ball, and becomes an additional tagger.
4) The game progresses as more players become taggers until everyone has been tagged, or plays as a timed survival challenge.
pe-01825:
1) Students spread out across the gym as the teacher throws multiple foam balls into play.
2) Players pick up balls and throw or roll them to hit opponents strictly below the knee.
3) Any hit player must sit down immediately and can only re-enter when grabbing a different ball rolling toward them.
4) If hit while holding a ball, players must surrender it and sit, while teammates may roll balls to revive seated peers.
pe-01826:
1) Students form a circle while objects ranging from large to small are lined up beside them.
2) Place the largest ball in the center, challenging all students to touch the object simultaneously without touching each other.
3) Once the group successfully touches the object without any body contact, replace it with the next smaller object.
4) As objects scale down to tennis balls and coins, students must strategize using single fingertips to complete the challenge.
pe-01827:
1) Set up two goal nets facing backwards and divide students into two competing teams on the court.
2) Field players are not allowed to kick the ball and must strike or swat the ball strictly using their hands.
3) Goalies operate under reverse rules and cannot use their hands, defending the net solely with their feet and body.
4) Carrying the ball is prohibited, and teams score points by maneuvering the ball into the backward-facing nets.
pe-01828:
1) The teacher announces a target alphabet letter and chooses one or two taggers.
2) Players scatter around the gym and taggers chase them to tag anyone they can reach.
3) Tagged players must sit down until they say aloud a word starting with the designated letter to rejoin.
4) Introduce a rule that students cannot repeat any word previously spoken to increase difficulty.
pe-01829:
1) Place alphabet paper cards across the gym and line up teams behind the start line.
2) On start, the first runner sprints across, grabs one letter card, and returns to the team.
3) Teammates take turns running one at a time to retrieve additional letter cards for the group.
4) The first team to assemble a valid target word or score the highest point total wins.
pe-01830:
1) Set up six cones to mark a large circle, place a bottle and rubber toys in the center, and seat groups between cones.
2) The teacher spins the bottle in the center, and the group pointed at by the bottle becomes the taggers.
3) Taggers grab rubber chickens while all other runners enter the circle area to avoid being tagged.
4) Tagged runners move to the circle perimeter to wait until all players are caught, then reset.
pe-01831:
1) Divide the court with a volleyball net and place a hula hoop along each team's back boundary line.
2) Players pick up foam dodgeballs and continuously throw them over the net into the opponent's court.
3) If a player catches an incoming ball before it hits the ground, they store it directly into their hoop.
4) The team that collects the most caught balls into their hoop when time expires wins the round.
pe-01832:
1) Players line up along the end line facing away while the teacher scatters coins across the playing area.
2) On the go signal players run to locate a coin and stand directly on top of it.
3) Any players who fail to secure a coin must perform designated exercises such as push-ups or jumping jacks.
4) Remove one coin each round to gradually increase the number of students exercising until a champion remains.
pe-01833:
1) Divide the court into two halves and set up a ball on a cone inside each three-point key with hula hoops as safe zones and corner jails.
2) Offensive players cross into the opponent's territory while evading defenders and resting safely inside the hula hoop zones.
3) Tagged players are sent to the opponent's jail and can be rescued when a teammate safely runs in and tags them.
4) Score a point by grabbing the ball and successfully carrying or passing it across the center line without being tagged.
pe-01834:
1) Mark a throwing circle with cones in the gym center and place four folding mats standing upright along the perimeter.
2) One student starts as the thrower inside the central circle while all other runners jog in one direction around the mat course.
3) Runners can take cover behind the standing mats for up to 10 seconds before being forced to advance to the next mat.
4) Any runner hit below the waist must join the throwers in the center until all runners have been tagged out.
pe-01835:
1) Lay out a long line of hula hoops on the floor and designate the second-to-last hoop on each side as the scoring goal.
2) Two teams line up at opposite ends and the first runners bunny-hop forward through the hoops toward each other.
3) When runners meet in a hoop they play rock-paper-scissors, with the loser stepping out to the back of their team line.
4) The winner continues hopping forward while the losing team immediately sends their next runner, scoring a point upon reaching the opponent's goal hoop.
pe-01836:
1) Students line up in a single file facing forward and give the lead runner a ball.
2) The entire line jogs together around the gymnasium perimeter maintaining a steady pace.
3) While moving each runner passes the ball overhead backward until it reaches the last player.
4) The last runner sprints past the line to become the new leader and teams can vary the pass between legs.
pe-01837:
1) Divide the court into defense midfield and forward zones assigning players and goalies to each section.
2) Players must strictly stay inside their assigned zones and only play when the ball enters their area.
3) Teams score points by passing the ball through zones and kicking it into the opponent goal net.
4) Rotate players periodically between defense midfield and forward positions so everyone practices each role.
pe-01838:
1) Designate two taggers as broken arrows and one cupid carrying mission cards while others are hearts.
2) Broken arrows chase and tag hearts turning them into frozen broken hearts standing on one foot.
3) Cupid delivers a card from the bucket to frozen players who rejoin after performing the listed exercise.
4) Taggers win if everyone is frozen or you can add extra cupids to increase game flow.
pe-01839:
1) Pairs receive a basketball and 10 to 15 bowling pins to build custom pathways like an S pattern.
2) The first player dribbles the basketball smoothly through the obstacle pin pattern without knocking any down.
3) Partners count successful laps in a 30-second round or award points to the partner if pins fall.
4) Progress by enforcing weak-hand dribbling simultaneous pair dribbling or running it as a team relay.
pe-01840:
1) Scatter 50 to 100 question cards in the center, assign one guardian team holding foam balls, and line up runners behind cones.
2) On go the lead runner sprints into the card field to grab one card while avoiding guardian tags.
3) Runners who safely return place the card onto the correct answer slot on their team board for points.
4) If tagged by a ball runners drop the card and return empty-handed, and guardians rotate each round.
pe-01841:
1) Three taggers hold one hula hoop together as a jellyfish while the other runners spread out in the playing area.
2) Tagged runners freeze in place, and the jellyfish taggers lower the hula hoop over their head to the floor and lift it back up.
3) Eaten players move outside the perimeter, where they can tag any runners wandering too close to the boundary lines.
4) Every time three players are eliminated they form a new jellyfish team with a hoop until three survivors remain.
pe-01842:
1) Two or three students start as pirates without a ball, while every other student dribbles a basketball around the gym.
2) Pirates move around the court trying to steal or knock away a basketball from any active dribbler.
3) When a player loses their ball, they immediately become a pirate and must pursue someone else's basketball.
4) Immediate takebacks from the player who just stole the ball are forbidden, and basketballs can be gradually removed to increase difficulty.
pe-01843:
1) Scatter hula hoops as fishing holes, placing paper fish and blank cards inside them covered up by poly spots.
2) Students form relay teams behind the starting line, with the first runner holding a pool noodle as a fishing rod.
3) On the whistle, one runner races out to flip over a single poly spot, retrieving the fish if found and flipping the spot back before returning.
4) Score by the total weight written on the fish, or add letter tiles, math equations, or movement penalties under the spots for creative variations.
pe-01844:
1) Place four cones at the corners of the play area and designate four distinct locomotion movements for each boundary line.
2) All students begin traveling around the perimeter in the same designated direction (clockwise or counter-clockwise).
3) Runners perform actions like jogging and galloping along the long sides, and switch to crab walks and hopping on the short sides.
4) After several laps, reverse the running direction or swap in new locomotive movements such as side-stepping, skipping, or high knees.
pe-01845:
1) Two teams wearing pinnies line up on opposite baselines, with one player from each team starting in the center as sharks.
2) A player rolls the foam ball to the opposite baseline who kicks it, triggering all minnows from both teams to sprint across to the other end.
3) Sharks attempt to catch the fly ball or throw the loose foam ball below the waist to eliminate fleeing minnows.
4) Minnows who are struck or hit a caught fly ball become sharks for the next round until one team's minnows are fully eliminated.
pe-01846:
1) Divide the play area in half, set up 2-point mats in corners and 1-point mats in the center rear, and scatter hula hoops as safe zones.
2) Players cross into the opponent's territory avoiding defenders, gaining temporary safety when inside hula hoops or point mats.
3) Tagged players must sit frozen on the spot until a teammate safely touches them, granting a free walk back to their half.
4) When the 3-5 minute round ends, everyone freezes and each team calculates total points based on players occupying the opponent's scoring mats.
pe-01847:
1) Place numbered cones in a line across the center and have two teams line up facing each other behind their starting lines.
2) The teacher calls out a math equation, prompting the first runner from each team holding a baton to sprint toward the correct cone.
3) The runner taps the correct answer cone with the baton and races back to their team line, with the first returner scoring the win.
4) The losing team performs jumping jacks equal to the answer value, after which batons pass to the next pair for a new equation.
pe-01848:
1) Arrange players into foosball-style rows (defenders, midfielders, forwards) with 2-4 players per row holding onto shared pool noodles.
2) Drop one or more soccer balls onto the court, requiring players in each row to slide together strictly side-to-side.
3) Teams pass the ball forward through rows and shoot into the opponent's goal using only their feet without letting go of noodles.
4) If a player lets go of the pool noodle or breaks formation to reach a ball, play halts to reattach and possession is given to the other team.
pe-01849:
1) Mark two parallel team lines about 10 feet apart with goal lines at both back ends, having Team X and Team Y line up facing each other.
2) The teacher tosses a beanbag labeled 'X' on one side and 'Y' on the other high into the air like a coin toss.
3) Whichever letter faces up when it lands designates the chasing team, who immediately sprints to tag members of the opposing team.
4) The fleeing team tries to sprint across their back goal line to safety, and the chasing team earns one point for each runner tagged before crossing.
pe-01850:
1) Establish safe lines at opposite ends, divide the class into two teams, and have each team secretly huddle to choose Gorilla, Man, or Gun.
2) Teams line up facing each other at the centerline, jumping into their designated pose when the teacher calls "Gorilla, Man, Gun, Shoot!".
3) According to the hierarchy (Gorilla beats Man, Gun beats Gorilla, Man beats Gun), the winning team chases the losing team.
4) Fleeing players dash toward their end safe line, and any player tagged before reaching it must join the opposing team for subsequent rounds.
pe-01851:
1) Students partner up and stand back-to-back without using their hands.
2) On the signal, partners push against each other and slowly lower themselves into a seated position without using their hands.
3) Once seated, they work together pushing back-to-back to stand completely upright again.
4) As they succeed, combine pairs into groups of four or more to attempt the same challenge together.
pe-01852:
1) Place three hula hoops in the center as submarines with two foam balls and a captain in each, while the rest line up at one end.
2) On the go signal, runners sprint across to the other side avoiding balls rolled or thrown by the captains inside their hoops.
3) Hit runners lay down on their stomachs to become mines who can pivot in place to tag runners moving back and forth.
4) The last three surviving runners become the new captains for the next round, and the number of hoops can be varied.
pe-01853:
1) Select two taggers with pool noodles and two freers holding foam balls, while other students scatter across the gym.
2) When tagged, a runner must freeze on the spot and raise a hand high to signal they need rescue.
3) Freers must stand stationary with the ball and throw accurate passes to frozen players; catching the pass earns 1 point for both players and frees the runner.
4) The catcher becomes the new freer, and variations include using bounce passes or switching to basketballs and footballs.
pe-01854:
1) Four teams position in the four corners behind protective mats, while one team stands inside the center circle holding all dodgeballs.
2) On the whistle, runners from corner teams run in a set direction around the perimeter dodging balls thrown from the center.
3) Successfully completing a full loop back to the base scores one point for the team, while hit runners join the center throwers.
4) The round ends when time expires, the team with the most points wins, and the winning team rotates into the center for the next round.
pe-01855:
1) Attach skipping ropes to scooter boards, place a plastic bowling pin on each, and divide students into tugboats (pullers) and throwers.
2) Tugboats carefully pull their cargo across the gym while throwers roll or throw foam balls from side zones to knock the pins down.
3) Points are scored each time a cargo reaches the opposite wall, and players whose pins fall drop their ropes to become blockers for teammates.
4) The game can be varied by allowing throwers to kick the balls or use hockey sticks to shoot at the moving targets.
pe-01856:
1) Place four exercise mats in the corners, position one tagger (the Chef) in the center, and have all other players (Gingerbread Men) lie down on the mats.
2) The Chef calls out the chant, which signals all players to get up quickly and sprint to a different mat.
3) Any runner tagged by the Chef before reaching another mat joins the tagging team as an extra Chef for subsequent rounds.
4) Modify the layout British Bulldog-style by placing mats along one end wall and having everyone sprint across to the other end.
pe-01857:
1) Set up three cones in a line for each 3-player team, assigning roles as a thrower, a noodle holder, and a retriever.
2) The middle player shapes a pool noodle into a loop, and the thrower tosses the frisbee attempting to fly through the loop.
3) When successful, the team shouts their score, the retriever collects the disc, and all players rotate positions.
4) Footballs or foam balls can be substituted for frisbees to practice various throwing and targeting skills.
pe-01858:
1) Divide the class into two equal teams, Bridges and Rivers, scattered freely across the gymnasium.
2) Students jog around to music; when the teacher shouts "Bridges!", the Bridge players form bridges while Rivers crawl underneath them.
3) When "Rivers!" is called, the River players lie flat on the floor and Bridge players leap over them.
4) The activity can be modified by having students roll balls under the bridges or bounce balls across the rivers.
pe-01859:
1) All students disperse across the playing area, where every single player acts simultaneously as a tagger and a runner.
2) On signal, players run and tag others; any player who is tagged must sit down immediately on the spot.
3) A sitting player is freed and rejoins the game the moment the person who tagged them gets tagged by someone else.
4) If two players tag each other at the exact same moment, they play rock-paper-scissors to determine who sits down.
pe-01860:
1) Divide the play area into three zones and place bowling pins in the middle zone separated into individual sections using skipping ropes.
2) Defenders stay inside their assigned middle section protecting one pin each, while attackers line up along the outside zones with balls.
3) Attackers kick balls simultaneously to knock down the pins, shouting out their cumulative score each time a pin falls while the teacher resets knocked pins.
4) After playing for a set time limit or reaching a target score, switch the roles of attackers and defenders.
pe-01861:
1) Place one hula hoop per student on the gym floor, have each student stand in a hoop, and let them practice communicating and switching spots.
2) Remove two hula hoops to begin the game, turning the two students without hoops into the 'Hunter Hawks'.
3) Students in hoops communicate using winks or gestures and attempt to sprint and swap places with each other.
4) The Hawks attempt to dive into an open hoop before the runners arrive, and the displaced runner becomes the new Hawk.
pe-01862:
1) Divide players into two teams (green cars and red cars) lined up shoulder-to-shoulder along opposite sidelines facing each other.
2) Blow the whistle and count down from eight seconds as both teams run across toward the opposite team's starting line.
3) Any players who collide with anyone or fail to reach the other side before time expires must freeze on the spot as stationary 'roadblocks'.
4) Repeat the crossing rounds while progressively reducing the countdown time to 7, 6, and 5 seconds as more roadblocks clutter the court.
pe-01863:
1) Have the entire class line up standing with their backs flat against the gymnasium wall and hand a ball to the first student.
2) Players pass the ball down the line, and immediately after passing, each player sprints to the far end of the line to become the new leader.
3) The team works together to maneuver the ball along all four gym walls until they return completely to their original starting point.
