4) Increase difficulty by having players do a continuous wall-sit during passing, or lying on their backs using their feet against the wall to pass an exercise ball.
pe-01864:
1) Set up six base mats in a wide perimeter with a collection basket in the center, dividing players into kickers and fielders.
2) The pitcher rolls the ball in, the kicker boots it into the field, and runners attempt to round all six bases sequentially to score.
3) With no foul balls, catch-outs, or tag-outs, the sole way to record an out is for fielders to toss the ball into the central container while runners are between bases.
4) For larger classes, allow multiple base-runners to stack safely on a single base, or switch sides after everyone has kicked once.
pe-01865:
1) Scatter various colored spot markers or hula hoops randomly across the gym floor and split students into four groups.
2) The teacher calls out a specific color pattern sequence such as red, blue, yellow, blue, and green for students to memorize.
3) On the go signal, all students run simultaneously touching each designated color marker in that exact order and sprint back to their group base.
4) Vary movement locomotor skills using skipping, galloping, or hopping, or place jump ropes on the floor for students to leap over.
pe-01866:
1) Place two collection boxes about 50 meters apart and give every player wearing team pinnies a flag tucked into their waistband.
2) Players run into the open area to pull flags from opponents and safely carry them back into their team's collection box.
3) A player whose flag is pulled must return to their team box to retrieve a new flag; if the box is empty, they must wait until teammates bring flags.
4) If a player carrying stolen flags loses their own flag, they must forfeit all carried flags to the tagger, and a team wins by capturing all opposing flags.
pe-01867:
1) Divide the class into two equal teams, placing one team as goalies along the wall and the other team as attackers throughout the court.
2) Set up a restriction line using cones or gym floor lines so attackers cannot get too close to the goalies along the wall.
3) During a 2-minute round, attackers shoot multiple foam balls toward the wall attempting to score as many goals as possible.
4) Whether a shot scores or is saved, goalies constantly kick and throw balls back into play, and teams switch roles after two minutes.
pe-01868:
1) Students spread out across the entire open area while the teacher starts music or sets a 20 to 30 second timer.
2) Throughout the countdown, students continuously jog, skip, hop, or gallop around the area changing directions freely.
3) Once time is called, the teacher shouts a specific number (e.g., "Six!"), prompting students to instantly form groups matching that exact count.
4) Any leftover students who cannot complete a group perform quick exercises such as six jumping jacks or push-ups before restarting.
pe-01869:
1) The teacher prepares a secret path key and arranges poly spots in a 6x6 grid.
2) The first student begins on the start spot and steps one spot forward, sideways, or diagonally.
3) If the step is correct they keep moving, but if incorrect they return to the back of the line.
4) The next teammate enters, recalling previous steps, and continues attempting to navigate all the way to the finish.
pe-01870:
1) Students spread out on the gym court lines and one player is chosen as the starting Pac-Man.
2) On the go signal, all players and taggers must move exclusively along the lines.
3) The Pac-Man moves their arms like an opening mouth and tags runners, turning them into additional Pac-Mans.
4) Survivors must navigate intersections and dodge an increasing swarm of taggers to stay alive.
pe-01871:
1) Mark a center zone using cones, scatter 50 beanbags as cheese, and select two cats to guard the middle.
2) Mice line up on one side and dash across to the opposite end, picking up exactly one beanbag along the way.
3) Any mouse tagged by a cat or crossing without a beanbag transforms into an extra cat for the next round.
4) Surviving mice must cross back each round accumulating more beanbags (two, then three) to determine winners.
pe-01872:
1) Form groups of three, place cones to mark boundary lines, and assign the middle player to hold a skipping rope as the net.
2) Players on opposite sides start a rally by serving and passing a soft volleyball over the rope.
3) Teams score points through simple volleyball rules with no spiking allowed, rotating the net holder every 3 points.
4) Adapt rules according to skill level by allowing one bounce before passes to encourage longer rallies.
pe-01873:
1) Set up boundaries with cones and assign dinosaur tagger roles such as T-Rex, throwers, and scooter-riding Triceratops.
2) Runners evade taggers across the gym while taggers use their specific tagging mechanics like tagging or rolling balls below the waist.
3) Tagged players freeze until freed by teammates or scooter rescues via a high-five tag.
4) Progress through the video's 10 featured tag game variations across rounds to sustain variety and engagement.
pe-01874:
1) Set up two goals with a goalie at each end and divide players into two teams with dodgeballs.
2) Players try to hit opponents, and anyone tagged by a ball is out and moves to the side.
3) When an active player throws the ball past the goalie into the net, all sidelined teammates revive back into the game.
4) A team wins by eliminating all opposing field players or holding the lead when time expires.
pe-01875:
1) One player is chosen as the cat inside the circle while other students form a ring as little birds.
2) The birds rotate in a circle chanting a playful rhyme to tease the sleeping cat.
3) As soon as the chant finishes, the birds scatter away and the cat chases to tag them.
4) The first student caught by the cat becomes the new cat for the next round.
pe-01876:
1) One student starts as the octopus in the center while all other runners line up at one baseline.
2) Runners chant the rhyme together and sprint across the gym toward the opposite safe line.
3) Anyone tagged must sit down right where they were caught, acting as seaweed/tentacles who can tag passing runners with their arms.
4) Rounds continue back and forth until everyone is tagged, and the last surviving runner wins.
pe-01877:
1) Players line up single file behind the foul line, with the first two shooters holding basketballs.
2) Shooter one shoots, and as soon as it releases shooter two shoots, both racing to score their own rebounds.
3) If the trailing shooter scores before the lead shooter makes a basket, the lead shooter is eliminated.
4) Successful shooters pass their ball to the next player in line and rejoin the queue until the last survivor wins.
pe-01878:
1) Scatter bean bags across the entire gym floor while all students spread out freely into open spaces.
2) With everyone playing simultaneously, students grab bean bags and slide them along the floor targeting others' feet.
3) Any runner struck on the foot by a slid bean bag must sit down immediately on that spot.
4) Seated players who collect sliding bags can shoot at standing runners' feet to revive back into the game.
pe-01879:
1) Write warm-up tasks like laps or jumping jacks on the board using math equations.
2) Students enter the gym, check the board, and mentally solve each equation.
3) Each student completes the designated number of repetitions matching their calculated answers.
4) Vary the math level from simple addition to multi-step operations depending on student grade.
pe-01880:
1) Form groups of three and assign players as pitcher, kicker, and catcher.
2) The pitcher rolls a foam ball along the floor toward the kicker.
3) The kicker kicks a high pop fly, and the team scores a point if the catcher catches it.
4) Rotate positions after each kick so everyone cycles through pitching, kicking, and catching.
pe-01881:
1) Set up agility ladders and poly spots in an X shape with six perimeter stations.
2) Disperse students evenly across the fitness stations and agility paths to begin.
3) Perform designated exercises such as ten burpees then traverse the agility lines continuously for two minutes.
4) Rest for 30 to 60 seconds after each two-minute bout, then reverse running directions or switch activities.
pe-01882:
1) Divide players into two equal teams on either side of the court with dodgeballs.
2) Players throw foam dodgeballs across the center line to eliminate opponents.
3) Hit players step off to the sideline and remember the specific person who hit them.
4) When that particular opponent gets hit and eliminated, the waiting player instantly rejoins the game.
pe-01883:
1) Dump various toy items on one side of the gym and set up starting cones and collection hula hoops for each team on the opposite side.
2) On the signal, the first runner sprints across, retrieves one treasure, places it inside their team hoop, and high-fives the next teammate.
3) The team that collects the three secret treasures pre-selected by the teacher, or gathers the highest total number of items, wins.
4) Vary the movement by requiring locomotor skills like skipping, galloping, or backpedaling instead of simple sprinting.
pe-01884:
1) Divide the gym into Danger Land, Water, and Fun Land, placing mats as islands and providing each team with one scooter board and one rope.
2) Teams must transport all members across the water using only their scooter boat, mat islands, and rope without touching the gym floor.
3) If any student touches the floor, they must return to the starting area, and the team wins once all members safely reach Fun Land.
4) Increase difficulty by setting a time limit or restricting how many students can use the scooter at once.
pe-01885:
1) Divide students into small teams of 2-3 facing their respective basketball hoops in a half-court setup.
2) On the go signal, the first player in each line dribbles toward the hoop and shoots from a comfortable distance.
3) Players must rebound and shoot continuously until making a basket, then shout out their score and dribble back to hand off.
4) The first team to reach a target score (e.g., 10 points) or the team with the most baskets when time expires wins.
pe-01886:
1) Place 4 players (doubles) or 2 players (singles) on each court and line up extra students along the court sidelines.
2) Players rally or play mini-games continuously for 1 to 2 minutes upon the starting signal.
3) When the whistle blows and the teacher calls switch, all students rotate one spot clockwise so waiting players step onto the court.
4) Vary the activity by focusing on specific stroke drills or playing short competitive scoring matches each round.
pe-01887:
1) Students pair up, spread out across the gymnasium, and receive one soft foam ball per pair.
2) While music plays, partners continuously toss and catch the ball back and forth at an appropriate distance.
3) The moment the music stops, the student holding the ball becomes the tagger and must chase and tag their partner with the ball.
4) Variations include tagging with the ball held in hand or gently tossing the ball below the waist to hit the partner.
pe-01888:
1) Divide the play area into four team zones and prepare a list of various physical challenges.
2) For each round, one representative from each team steps into the center circle to receive and compete in the announced challenge.
3) The player who completes or holds the challenge the longest earns a point for their team.
4) Challenges can be played equipment-free or modified to use balls, jump ropes, and beanbags based on available gear.
pe-01889:
1) Pair up two teams at each available basketball hoop in the gym with one ball per team.
2) The first player shoots, retrieves their own rebound, passes to the next teammate in line, and goes to the back.
3) Whenever a basket is made, the entire team yells out the score, racing to reach five baskets first.
4) The winning team rotates to the next hoop clockwise, while the losing team stays to face a newly arriving opponent.
pe-01890:
1) Half the class sits around a center circle as bouncers, the other half spreads out as rollers, and buckets are placed in the center and with the teacher.
2) The teacher scatters whiffle balls representing popcorn all over the gym floor, and rollers scramble to collect them.
3) Once a roller reaches a ball, they must stop and roll it to a bouncer, who bounces it once into the center bucket.
4) When all balls are gathered into the bucket, teams swap roles, and younger grades can directly toss into the bucket without bouncing.
pe-01891:
1) Preparation: Divide students into three or four teams wearing colored pinnies and give every player one foam ball.
2) Progression: Players run with their ball in hand to tag opponents from other teams, causing tagged players to sit down immediately.
3) Scoring: Sitting teammates are rescued when a teammate touches their ball with another ball, and a team wins when all players on an opposing team are seated.
4) Modification: Set a specific chase order where each team only tags one target color or require tagged teams to do jumping jacks to return.
pe-01892:
1) Preparation: Split the gym into two halves, placing about 20 bowling pins, a mini net guarded by 1-2 goalies, and a basketball hoop on each side.
2) Progression: Players roll or throw foam balls across the centerline to attack opponent pins, mini nets, and basketball hoops without crossing over.
3) Scoring: Direct hits down one pin, scoring into the net removes one opponent pin, making a basket removes two pins, and the team that clears all pins wins.
4) Modification: Allow kicking the ball for older grade levels or let each team strategically arrange their pins before the round begins.
pe-01893:
1) Preparation: Set up running perimeters around the gym or field and pair up students standing across from each other.
2) Progression: One partner sprints along the outer perimeter toward the other while the second partner waits in place.
3) Scoring: Upon tagging up, the runner walks across the court width to rest while the waiting partner sprints along the perimeter in a continuous cycle.
4) Modification: Stagger running distances according to differing fitness levels so partners can complete their intervals comfortably.
pe-01894:
1) Preparation: Gather students within a designated court boundary and prepare a special object such as a bean bag or trophy.
2) Progression: While music plays, students move around using various locomotor skills like running, skipping, or hopping while trying to stay as far from others as possible.
3) Scoring: When the music stops, everyone freezes, and the student found to be furthest from all other peers receives the special object to carry next round.
4) Modification: Vary the movement skills during music playback, such as galloping, crab walking, or moving at different tempo levels.
pe-01895:
1) Divide the field into two zones with a center path and give teams 30 seconds to hide their flags visibly.
2) Infiltrate the opponent zone to find the flag, moving to the jail bench for 2 minutes if tagged by defenders.
3) Score and win the round by successfully carrying the opposing team's flag across the center line.
4) Introduce hidden immunity beanbags to grant tag immunity, or call a free-for-all mode if the round stalls.
pe-01896:
1) Mount an exercise ball onto a laundry basket to stabilize it and form small groups of 4 to 6 players.
2) Throw a smaller ball so that it rebounds off the exercise ball and have teammates quickly catch it.
3) Score points by counting the total number of consecutive successful catches completed within one minute.
4) Adjust throw distance or switch the throwing object to different balls like foam balls to vary difficulty.
pe-01897:
1) Set up mats against the walls as goals and have teams of three link together by holding pool noodles.
2) Move cooperatively while maintaining hold of the noodles and strike the large exercise ball with feet or bodies.
3) Score goals by kicking or hitting the exercise ball into the opponent mat goal without breaking the noodle link.
4) Adapt the game to pairs with one noodle or add multiple exercise balls to increase activity levels.
pe-01898:
1) Have all players disperse along gym floor lines and designate two taggers and two freers using colored pinnies.
2) Everyone must travel strictly on the floor lines, and anyone tagged must sit down immediately as a roadblock.
3) A sitting player is liberated and returns to active running once tagged by one of the designated freers.
4) Keep freers immune from tags and run short rounds so all students get frequent turns in special roles.
pe-01899:
1) Construct castles using mats with pillars holding balls, and send one knight from each team to the opposing side.
2) Teams race to complete objectives in order: throw 3 balls into opposing towers, then knock down 2 pillar balls.
3) Once pillars are cleared, the knight sits on the throne chair and must catch a thrown ball without standing up to win.
4) Integrate dodgeball elimination rules where hit players go to jail behind the wall until rescued by a catch.
pe-01900:
1) Students line up at the baseline each with a ball, while the teacher stands at the opposite end of the gym.
2) On the teacher's 'green light' command, students advance forward while continuously dribbling the ball.
3) On the 'red light' command, players must halt their forward motion but keep dribbling in place; losing control sends them back to the start.
4) The game can be varied by using whistle counts, adding a slow-down yellow light, or racing competitively to the finish line.
pe-01901:
1) Set up 6 to 8 exercise stations such as jump rope, sit-ups, and squats around the perimeter of a volleyball court.
2) Partners split up so that one runner performs laps or line sprints while the other performs the station exercise.
3) After a 45-second music interval, the teacher signals switch, and partners immediately swap their running and exercise roles.
4) Once both partners complete a station, pairs rotate to the next workout area until all stations are completed.
pe-01902:
1) Form relay lines behind a starting line and place numbered posters 1 through 5 (or 10) at varying distances ahead.
2) The teacher calls out an age-appropriate arithmetic problem (for example, '2 plus 1') to the whole class.
3) The first runners in each line race to the correct answer poster (number 3), touch it, and run back to tag the next teammate.
4) Vary the movement by having students hop, gallop, skip, or dribble a ball to the correct answer.
pe-01903:
1) Scatter hula hoops across the gym floor to serve as tree nests, placing each student inside their own individual hoop.
2) In part one, students practice verbal communication by making eye contact, asking to switch nests out loud, and trading spots.
3) In part two, talking is banned and students must use non-verbal cues like eye contact, hand gestures, and nodding to agree and swap nests.
4) In part three, remove several hoops to create Hunter Hawks who attempt to swoop in and occupy open nests during transitions.
pe-01904:
1) Teams line up in single file behind the starting line with all players standing with their feet spread wide apart.
2) The last player in each line crawls through the legs of all teammates until reaching the very front of the line.
3) Once at the front, that player stands up with feet spread and shouts 'Next!' to signal the next rear teammate.
4) Continue this caterpillar crawl sequence consecutively until the entire team crosses the designated finish line.
pe-01905:
1) The tagger (wolf) faces the wall on one side, while all other players line up on the opposite starting side.
2) When players shout "Roll the dice!", the wolf rolls the foam die and counts out loud to that rolled number.
3) Players advance across the gym during the count and must freeze completely once the count ends; anyone caught moving is sent back to the start.
4) The first players to safely cross to the wolf's side win, and the game can be played for multiple rounds or time limits.
pe-01906:
1) Each student spreads out across the basketball court with their own soccer ball (or basketball).
2) Players actively dribble within boundaries while trying to kick or knock away opponents' balls without losing control of their own.
3) If a player's ball crosses the boundary line or they lose possession, they are knocked out and move to the sideline.
4) Eliminated players stay along the perimeter lines trying to knock active balls out, while the teacher gradually shrinks the playing area to determine the final survivor.
pe-01907:
1) Most players spread across the gym as butterflies, while two taggers designated as bees hold pool noodles, with a safe circle marked in the center.
2) When a bee tags a butterfly using the pool noodle, the tagged butterfly must instantly freeze in place.
3) To rescue a frozen butterfly, two other free butterflies must link arms with the teammate and escort them safely into the center circle.
4) Once inside the safe zone, the rescued butterfly counts to five before re-entering the game, and tagger roles can rotate periodically.
pe-01908:
1) Have students form a large circle (or small teams) in the activity area and join hands with their neighbors.
2) Place a hula hoop over the arms of two students before they reconnect hands to form an unbroken circle chain.
3) Without breaking hand grips at any point, players must manipulate their bodies through the hoop to pass it along the entire circle.
4) Use a stopwatch to time how long it takes to complete a full circuit, then challenge the group to beat their record or compete against another circle.
pe-01909:
1) Scatter hula hoops as lily pads across the court, mark caves and a belly area with cones, choose two gators, and line up the frogs on one side.
2) On start, frogs hop across toward the safe zone, and when the teacher calls "Go Gators!", gators hunt and tag frogs outside hoops for 30 seconds.
3) Tagged frogs enter the belly area, gators return to caves on "Freeze!", and frogs resume hopping for a total of three rounds.
4) Frogs remaining in hoops after round three are counted as caught, and successful frogs score a win before rotating new gators.
pe-01910:
1) Divide students into four groups along the four boundary lines of the court, give each student a ball, and prepare a large foam dice.
2) The teacher rolls the dice, and if 1 through 4 is rolled, the corresponding side performs a full-court dribbling wave there and back.
3) When a 5 is rolled, all groups dribble and rotate clockwise to the next side, and when a 6 is rolled, they rotate counter-clockwise.
4) Vary the challenge during waves by requiring weak-hand dribbling, low dribbles, cross-overs at midcourt, or tricky dribbling moves.
pe-01911:
1) Scatter all students across the gym, assign a blue tool to one tagger (freezer), and give a red tool to one rescuer (melter).
2) The blue tagger chases and tags runners, who must immediately freeze into frozen ice statues upon being touched.
3) The red melter moves around the gym to touch frozen statues to melt them, allowing rescued players to rejoin the game.
4) Challenge the freezer to catch everyone within a time limit, then rotate the blue and red roles among different students.
pe-01912:
1) Designate a jail area preferably near climbing structures, choose two players as cops, and assign all other players as robbers.
2) Robbers disperse and hide around the obstacle course while the cops count down aloud from thirty to zero in the jail.
3) Once the countdown ends, cops chase and tag robbers, immediately sending any tagged robbers into the designated jail.
4) Captured robbers stay active inside the jail structure, and after a few minutes, tally the arrests before rotating new cops.
pe-01913:
1) Students pair up facing each other around the room, while one extra player without a partner is designated as 'It'.
2) When 'It' calls out a physical prompt such as "Back-to-back!", each pair must immediately connect back-to-back.
3) When 'It' calls out a different prompt such as "Front-to-front!", partners quickly change their body positions accordingly.
4) When 'It' shouts "Switch!", everyone including 'It' must sprint to find a new partner, leaving the unpaired player as the next 'It'.
pe-01914:
1) Prepare sticky notes numbered 1 to N, hand one to each student, and keep numbers strictly secret while spreading out.
2) The teacher calls out a specific number and starts a 1 to 2 minute timer, prompting that secret student to reveal themselves as the tagger.
3) The tagger chases and tags as many classmates as possible within the time limit to score tag points.
4) For variation, write called numbers on a whiteboard, recall previously used numbers, or call multiple numbers simultaneously.
pe-01915:
1) Divide the gym into two halves, place three King's Cones targets on each side, and distribute multicolored foam balls across the court.
2) Players hit by a thrown dodgeball head to the sideline jail and wait in order of elimination.
3) A team wins the round instantly by knocking down all three enemy cones, sinking a designated special ball into the opposing basketball hoop, or eliminating all opponents.
4) Catching a flying ball frees the first player in jail, while sinking any shot into the basketball net instantly frees all jailed teammates.
pe-01916:
1) Set up mats, benches, and obstacle tunnels on both halves of the court to create trenches and barricades, then distribute dodgeballs.
2) Players take positions behind barriers on their half and throw dodgeballs while ducking behind cover.
3) Any student hit by a dodgeball must exit to the gym sideline, remaining out until the round concludes when one team is completely eliminated.
4) Adapt the game into capture-the-flag paintball mode where teams dodge incoming throws while attempting to retrieve the enemy flag.
pe-01917:
1) Form an energy charging station in the center using hula hoops and a side repair shop using cones, designating several students with dodgeballs as bad robots.
2) Good robots roam the playing area while bad robots attempt to tag them using the held dodgeballs.
3) Tagged robots become broken, moving to the repair shop to count out loud to 30 before re-entering play.
4) Good robots may take refuge in the center charging station for up to 10 seconds (counting to 10) where bad robots are not allowed to enter.
pe-01918:
1) Set up goals at opposite gym ends using mats or nets, divide students into two teams, and assign starting goalkeepers.
2) Begin the match with an initial kickoff using the first soccer ball under standard no-hands soccer rules.
3) Toss a second and third soccer ball into the court unexpectedly after play gets underway to have all three balls active simultaneously.
4) Whenever a goal is conceded, that goalkeeper must immediately switch positions with an active field player.
pe-01919:
1) Set up four cones with two teams facing each other across the middle where a target cone is placed.
2) On the signal, each team rolls their basketball back and forth trying to knock over the center target cone first.
3) The team that knocks over the cone immediately lines up to perform layup shots while the opposing team runs to the corner to complete 20 chest passes.
4) Once the 20 passes are finished, reset the target cone and tally the made layups before starting the next round.
pe-01920:
1) Define the playing area, designate one or two taggers, and have the remaining players scatter across the gym.
2) When tagged, players must freeze in a banana pose with their arms raised overhead and bending sideways.
3) An untagged teammate can rescue them by gently pulling down their raised arm as if peeling a banana.
4) Switch taggers after a set time or increase difficulty by requiring both arms to be peeled to rejoin the game.
pe-01921:
1) Set up mats as hospitals at each endline and designate two doctors equipped with scooter board ambulances per team.
2) Players throw dodgeballs across the center line, and anyone hit must sit down immediately where they were tagged.
3) The team doctor rides the scooter over to the downed player, transports them back to the hospital mat, and heals them.
4) Vary the game for older grades by allowing doctors to be hit and eliminated, ending the round when a team is wiped out.
pe-01922:
1) Place beanbags as food on one end line, line up critters with flag tails on the opposite end, and place fox taggers in the middle.
2) Critters strategize to sprint across the playing area either individually or together while dodging the foxes.
3) Any critter reaching the food zone safely grabs one beanbag and brings it back to their home line without losing their tail.
4) If a player's tail is pulled by a fox, they must sit down at that spot and can only reach out to pull tails of passing critters until everyone is caught.
pe-01923:
1) Set up cones in a large loop with one cone designated as a starting station for each player.
2) The teacher announces a running direction, the number of laps, and a target completion time such as one lap in exactly 40 seconds.
3) Players pace themselves by choosing when to walk, jog, or sprint around the perimeter cones.
4) The student who crosses back to their starting cone at the exact target time wins, and the challenge repeats with varied laps and times.
pe-01924:
1) Designate two players as personal trainers wearing pinnies and scatter multiple soft dodgeballs throughout the gym.
2) Only the trainers are allowed to pick up and throw dodgeballs to tag the running classmates.
3) Any student hit by a thrown ball must step out to the perimeter fitness zone and perform predetermined exercises such as push-ups or jumping jacks.
4) Once the student finishes their prescribed repetitions, they immediately rejoin the active dodgeball game in the main area.
pe-01925:
1) Students form a large circle or line up along the court boundary, with one leader starting in the center.
2) The leader performs a chosen physical movement (such as tuck jumps, push-ups, or silly dance stretches) for 20 seconds.
3) All surrounding classmates must follow along and mirror the leader's action for the entire 20-second duration.
4) Once the 20 seconds expire, that leader joins the perimeter and the next designated student steps in to lead a new movement.
pe-01926:
1) Players pair up with one ball between them and stand facing each other approximately 10 to 15 feet apart.
2) Partners practice tossing and catching the ball back and forth using overhand or underhand throws.
3) The instant the teacher blows the whistle, the partner without the ball immediately turns into the tagger and chases the partner holding the ball.
4) The ball carrier flees using open space, and after a short chase period both reset to their distance to resume throwing and await the next whistle.
pe-01927:
1) Divide the gym into four corners, set up two stacked mats in each corner as skyscrapers, and split students into four teams.
2) Distribute dodgeballs to each team, and on the signal, players throw balls to knock down opposing skyscrapers.
3) Players may defend and block shots targeting their own skyscraper, and a team is eliminated when their mat tower falls.
4) Eliminated players disperse to join surviving teams, continuing the battle until only one standing skyscraper remains.
pe-01928:
1) Split the class into two teams positioned behind their respective service lines on a full volleyball court.
2) One team receives volleyballs and all members serve simultaneously over the net aiming for in-bounds territory.
3) The team scores points equal to the total number of successful serves landing inside the boundaries.
4) The opposing team gathers all balls to take their turn serving, rotating between underhand and overhand serves until reaching 20 points.
pe-01929:
1) Mark a large center circle in the gym or with jump ropes outside, and pair up students behind designated marker cones.
2) On the whistle, the first runner sprints to touch the perimeter of the center circle and sprints back.
3) Once the first runner returns and tags their partner, the second runner immediately takes off to repeat the cycle.
4) Modify the movement patterns from basic running to side-stepping, hopping, dribbling a ball, or performing five jumping jacks at the circle.
pe-01930:
1) Line up all students along one baseline of the gym with sufficient safety spacing between peers.
2) Prompted by teacher guided questions, students suggest movement ideas and walk across to the opposite wall before jogging back.
3) Progressively advance movement patterns by having students perform running, single-leg hopping, skipping, and galloping across the gym.
4) Introduce imaginative movement variations such as animal walks, arm swing rhythms, and alternating lead feet during galloping.
pe-01931:
1) Organize students into small groups of 4 to 5 members and assign each team their own designated practice space.
2) Provide a dramatic scene prompt such as firefighters, medieval knights, or sporting events, or allow groups to choose their own topic.
3) Group members collaborate to choreograph physical movements and expressive poses where every individual plays an active role without words.
4) Groups perform their dynamic pantomime scene in front of the class while peer audiences guess the theme and evaluate creativity.
pe-01932:
1) Students spread out in the classroom or gym and stand stationary at their spots.
2) Players toss a soft ball to each other silently without letting it bounce.
3) Any student who drops the ball, throws a bad pass, or speaks must perform an exercise like 5 jumping jacks to rejoin.
4) Increase the challenge by adding two or three balls into play simultaneously.
pe-01933:
1) Set up a hula hoop and two cones in a triangle, placing three balls inside the hoop.
2) One kicker kicks all three balls into the field one by one while three fielders prepare to retrieve them.
3) The kicker circles the two cones back to home as many times as possible, scoring one point per completed lap until all balls are returned.
4) Players rotate positions after each turn and teams can compare their accumulated points.
pe-01934:
1) Students start inside a designated large boundary, each wearing a flag tucked into their pocket or waistband.
2) On the signal, players run around trying to pull opponents' flags while protecting their own.
3) Players whose flags are stolen or who step out of bounds move to the sidelines, where they can swipe flags from nearby active runners.
4) Shrink the court boundary progressively as fewer players remain until the last survivor wins.
pe-01935:
1) Players face the wall with eyes closed while the teacher secretly taps one student to be the Spy.
2) Everyone walks around making continuous eye contact while the Spy attempts to poison players by winking at them unseen.
3) Any player who is winked at must lie down or hold a fitness plank, and players try to deduce and accuse the Spy.
4) Incorrect accusations also result in holding a plank, and the game ends when the Spy is found or eliminates everyone.
pe-01936:
1) Place six gym mats around the gym floor, naming each after a Mario world land.
2) Two taggers start in the middle while the remaining students distribute themselves across the six mats.
3) When taggers call out "Find a new land!", all runners must sprint to a different mat without getting tagged.
4) Tagged players become the taggers in the center for the next round, and runners cannot return to their previous mat.
pe-01937:
1) Designate a few attackers who start with hula hoops on the floor and spread the rest of the players as runners.
2) On the go signal, attackers kick their hoops across the gym floor aiming to hit the runners on their feet.
3) Any runner struck on the foot must exit and run a perimeter lap before re-entering or face elimination.
4) The game can be modified by using floor hockey sticks and pucks or by rolling foam balls toward feet.
pe-01938:
1) Line up players along the designated start line and place cones topped with grab objects along the far wall.
2) The teacher calls out line colors, prompting all students to quickly sprint and relocate to that specific line.
3) When the teacher shouts out the target object command, players race to grab an available object from the cones.
4) The round can be varied by repeating colors as trick calls or removing one object each round.
pe-01939:
1) Position one or two bakers in the gym center and divide runners into groups of holiday cookie names.
2) When the baker calls out a cookie name, those specific runners must cross to the far side without getting tagged.
3) Players tagged by the baker must enter the oven area along the side and wait inside while baking.
4) The baker can shout a rescue phrase to let all trapped cookies run over to the waiting table safely.
pe-01940:
1) Drape bed sheets over the volleyball net so that both teams cannot see across to the opposing court.
2) Divide the class into two teams positioned on opposite sides without any view of opponents or setup.
3) Teams play standard volleyball rules, reacting quickly as the ball suddenly appears over the covered net.
4) Adapt play using lightweight beach balls, permitting one bounce, or adjusting the team size per side.
pe-01941:
1) Divide the gym into four playing areas with a long runner zone down the center using pylons.
2) Teams in each corner area throw dodgeballs at opposing zones to hit other players.
3) A tagged player enters the middle zone and must run from one end to the other without being hit to get back in.
4) If hit inside the middle zone, the runner must keep attempting to cross safely to revive.
pe-01942:
1) Mark hospital zones in opposite court corners with cones, and designate two taggers and two ambulance drivers.
2) Tagged players become sick patients and must lie down on the floor where they were caught.
3) Ambulance drivers push the scooter mat to collect up to two patients and transport them to the nearest hospital.
4) Patients complete a fitness task such as five push-ups at the hospital before returning to the game.
pe-01943:
1) Scatter 50 to 100 beanbags (fish) in the lake center and place hula hoops (nests) at opposite sidelines.
2) The agile Seahawks receive a 5-second head start to dash in and collect fish into their nest.
3) The stronger Eagles enter to gather fish or tag Seahawks to force them to drop fish to steal.
4) Players carry only one fish at a time without throwing, and the team with the most fish wins.
pe-01944:
1) All students act as robots with a beanbag placed on their head while two players are chosen as mechanics.
2) On the signal, robots walk around the gym maintaining their balance without using their hands.
3) If a beanbag falls off, that robot freezes in place until a mechanic arrives.
4) Mechanics pick up the fallen beanbags and place them back on heads to repair them, switching roles periodically.
pe-01945:
1) Stand several folding mats upright in the gym center to form obstacles, set up start and finish lines, and choose one tagger.
2) The tagger yells face the wall and counts down from five to zero while hiding behind one of the mats.
3) Once zero is reached, runners dash toward the opposite finish line trying to avoid getting tagged.
4) Tagged runners, peekers, or anyone touching a mat become taggers for the next round until everyone is caught.
pe-01946:
1) Scatter bingo chips, pennies, or small objects widely across a grassy field and organize students into teams of four or individuals.
2) On the start whistle, students sprint across the field to collect as many objects as possible within a 3 to 5-minute time limit.
3) Collected items are brought back to the designated team base continuously before the timer expires.
4) Teams count their collected items at the end to determine the highest score, and play again with different locomotor movements.
pe-01947:
1) Students spread out across the gym moving in various directions using locomotor skills like running, hopping, or skipping to music.
2) The teacher stops the music and calls out an alphabet letter loudly.
3) Students quickly pair up with the nearest partner, lie down on the floor, and cooperate to form the shape of that letter.
4) Once confirmed, students stand up to resume moving, and variations can expand to 3–4 players spelling entire words.
pe-01948:
1) Place poly spots around each basketball hoop with assigned point values (1 to 4 points) and divide players into small teams.
2) On the clock, the first shooter takes as many shots as possible within a one-minute time limit from any spot.
3) Teammates act as active rebounders under the hoop, catching misses and quickly passing the ball back to the shooter while tallying points.
4) After one minute, players rotate roles until every teammate completes their shooting round, crowning the highest cumulative team score.
pe-01949:
1) Set up multiple holes across the gym or field using cones for tee-offs and targets, assigning groups of 2-3 to each hole.
2) The first player throws a disc from the tee cone toward the target cone and continues throwing from where it lands until hitting the cone.
3) Upon hitting the target, the player records the total number of throws and brings the disc back to the next teammate to compete for the lowest strokes.
4) Once all teammates finish the hole, groups rotate to the next hole simultaneously, with variations using soccer balls or hockey sticks.
pe-01950:
1) Designate one student as Santa wearing a red pinnie while all other students scatter across the gym as reindeer.
2) Santa chases and tags the runaway reindeer while the reindeer dodge into open spaces to avoid being caught.
3) Once tagged, a reindeer must run to touch one wall of the gym and then sprint to touch the opposite wall before re-entering play.
4) Depending on group size and stamina, add helper elves as extra taggers or modify the wall-running movement to side-shuffles.
pe-01951:
1) Scatter lily pad spot markers on the floor around basketball hoops and place a hula hoop collection chamber for each team.
2) Players from 2-4 teams dribble to an available spot marker and take a basketball shot from that exact position.
3) If made, the shooter retrieves that spot marker and brings it back to their team's hula hoop; if missed, they must attempt from a different spot before returning.
4) The first team to collect 10 spot markers or the team with the most markers within the time limit wins, with scoring weight adjustable by shooting distance.
pe-01952:
1) Divide the activity space into two designated areas: Inner Space and Outer Space, assigning satellites (runners) and meteors (taggers).
2) Satellites must hop in Inner Space and jump in Outer Space, while meteors must do the opposite by jumping in Inner Space and hopping in Outer Space.
3) When a meteor tags a satellite while maintaining the required locomotion, they immediately switch roles and continue the game.
4) Locomotion rules can be modified to crab walks, backward walking, or skipping across zones to vary coordination challenge.
pe-01953:
1) Line up 20-40 plastic pins along one side of the gym and establish a throwing line tailored to students' grade levels.
2) Place containers filled with various balls (foam balls, tennis balls) behind the line and have all throwers line up ready.
3) Players collaborate for 3 minutes to throw one ball at a time and knock down all pins before the ball bins run empty.
4) Students are strictly forbidden from crossing the throwing line to retrieve balls during play, and the activity can be modified into a team relay contest.
pe-01954:
1) Pair students up facing each other and give each pair one ball to start.
2) When a player successfully catches a thrown ball without bouncing, that catcher takes one step backward.
3) If a catch is missed, the player who missed it must step forward to reduce the distance.
4) Switch throwing techniques between underhand and overhand, or use water balloons for advanced rounds.
pe-01955:
1) Have all runners line up along one side of the gym and place one or two catchers in the middle.
2) When the catchers shout "British Bulldog!", runners must sprint across to the opposite end line.
3) Any runner tagged while crossing joins the center team as a catcher for the next round.
4) Continue until the last bulldog is caught, and the final survivor becomes the starting catcher next game.
pe-01956:
1) Divide the gym into two halves, placing 7 bowling pins and one hula-hoop castle in each half.
2) Players throw foam balls to knock down enemy pins, with a maximum of one defender per pin.
3) Teams must knock down all 7 target pins before they are allowed to attack the hoop castle.
4) Accidentally knocking down the opponent's castle before eliminating all 7 pins results in an automatic loss.
pe-01957:
1) Arrange the class in a grid (e.g., 5x5) and assign one student as a cat and another as a mouse.
2) When the caller shouts "Streets!" or "Alleys!", grid players pivot 90 degrees and join hands to alter paths.
3) The cat chases the mouse through open pathways strictly using fast power-walking without running.
4) If the cat tags the mouse or time runs out, switch roles; head-balancing items can be added as a handicap.
pe-01958:
1) Choose three students to be bandits wearing pennies and scatter multiple foam balls inside the gym.
2) Regular players dribble and pass the balls to one another to keep possession away from the bandits.
3) Bandits steal balls and kick them against the perimeter wall to permanently eliminate them from play.
4) The game continues until all balls are eliminated, after which new bandits are selected for the next round.
pe-01959:
1) Divide the court into two yards using a volleyball net and spread dodgeballs and beanbags evenly on both sides.
2) On the start signal, throw dodgeballs over the net and slide beanbags under the net across the floor into the opponent yard.
3) When time is called, count the items in each yard, and the team with fewer items wins the round.
4) Players may only handle one item at a time, and music can be played and paused to signal start and stop.
pe-01960:
1) Students form lines by placing hands on shoulders to make snakes, with the last person holding a collection bag.
2) Scatter thirty to fifty small items such as beanbags, small balls, and cones all over the playing area.
3) On the whistle, snakes move together; only the head picks up items and passes each item down the line into the tail bag.
4) The team with the most collected items in their bag wins, and players can change snake lengths or head roles.
pe-01961:
1) Set up boundaries with cones; runners line up at one baseline while rollers position along the sidelines with dodgeballs.
2) Runners attempt to dash across to the opposite end while rollers roll soft balls across the floor aimed at runners' feet.
3) Any runner contacted on the foot joins the sideline rollers to roll balls during subsequent crossings.
4) Rounds continue back and forth until all runners are caught, with extra balls added to adjust challenge.
pe-01962:
1) Teams line up behind starting cones with a turnaround marker set ahead, giving the first runner a beanbag.
2) On start, runners balance the beanbag on their head or arm, walk around the turning cone, and return without dropping it.
3) The runner passes the beanbag to the next teammate and sits at the back; the first team all seated wins.
4) Variations include balancing on shoulders, flipping and catching, or tossing the beanbag to the next runner from the marker.
pe-01963:
1) Divide the gym into two halves, stand up mats at each end to form target areas, and place cones to create throwing lines.
2) When play starts, students throw footballs into the designated mat target area strictly from on or behind their throwing line.
3) Each quarter lasts two to three minutes, after which the balls inside each target area are counted to calculate team points.
4) In subsequent rounds, you can move the throwing line farther back or allow blockers to defend the target.
pe-01964:
1) Set up benches, scooter boards, hula hoops, and standing mats across the gym, placing a hoop with bean bags at the far end.
2) Half the students become creatures (snakes on benches, crocodiles on scooters, frogs on hoops, lizards behind mats) while the other half are humans.
3) Humans attempt to cross the gym without getting tagged to collect one bean bag and safely return it to their team's stash.
4) If tagged, humans must return to the start and try again; teams switch creature and human roles after a set time.
pe-01965:
1) Pair up or form small groups and place a cone in the center between players.
2) Follow the teacher's called-out movement commands such as toe touches or balancing.
3) Race to touch the cone when the teacher says 'Go', scoring one point for being first.
4) Vary the game by having students circle the cone to music and touch it when it stops.
pe-01966:
1) Set up defensive zones in front of both goals using cones and assign attackers, defenders, and goalies.
2) Defenders must strictly remain inside their assigned defensive zone during play.
3) Attackers move the ball through zones via passing combinations to score into the opponent goal.
4) Modify the activity by using a basketball or handball with modified court rules.
pe-01967:
1) Disperse students across the play area and designate a couple of players as taggers.
2) Tagged players must lie on their backs with arms and legs raised like a dead ant.
3) Four free players must each touch one limb simultaneously to revive the teammate.
4) For smaller groups, modify the revival rule so a single high-five frees the player.
pe-01968:
1) Spread out all players across the playing area to move around freely.
2) When two players encounter each other, they stop and play rock-paper-scissors.
3) The loser must line up directly behind the winner and follow them as a train.
4) When trains meet, the lead champions battle until the entire class forms one long train.
pe-01969:
1) Set up gym stations using mats, hula hoops, scooters, skipping ropes, cones, and tunnels.
2) Have the next student in line start once the front student finishes the first few stages.
3) Complete each challenge sequentially including log rolls, single-foot hopping, scooter riding, and rope jumping.
4) Switch the running direction or have students design their own obstacle configurations.
pe-01970:
1) Set up gym mats in an octagon at waist height and place all students inside.
2) The teacher tosses in a soft bouncy ball and players strike the ball with their hands.
3) Any player hit below the knee is eliminated and steps outside the mat boundary.
4) Eliminated players re-enter when the teacher calls jailbreak or extra balls are added.
pe-01971:
1) Place one exercise mat per team along the gym baseline and have all members stand on it.
2) On the go signal, teammates work together to move the mat without touching the floor.
3) The first team to navigate their mat across the gym to the opposite end line wins.
4) Scatter cones or beanbags as treasures on the floor to collect the most within a time limit.
pe-01972:
1) Divide the area into grids using cones and introduce 10 games including Bandits and Pinball Soccer.
2) Students rotate through stations practicing ball control, one-touch passing, and target shooting.
3) Teams score points by knocking down pins or kicking opponents' balls out of bounds.
4) Modify by introducing irregular balls like foam dice or adding active defenders in circles.
pe-01973:
1) Form circles of 6-8 students with soccer balls and setup cones in designated areas.
2) Players call a teammate's name across the circle and deliver accurate inside-foot passes.
3) Score by knocking down target cones in the center or swap places when a defender intercepts.
4) Progress to all outer players holding balls and executing rapid one-touch passes with a center pivot.
pe-01974:
1) Place one hula hoop per team opposite their relay line and scatter colored beanbags in the center.
2) On the go signal, the first runner dashes to grab one topping beanbag and places it in their hoop.
3) Runners return to high-five the next teammate who then sprints to deliver another topping.
4) Once all toppings are collected, teams sit down together to count and compare their ingredients.
pe-01975:
1) Set up 10 plastic pins in a line along the center court line, placing goalkeepers in the middle, throwers and rollers on opposite sidelines, and ball retrievers on the endlines.
2) Throwers and rollers attempt to knock down the pins using foam dodgeballs while the goalkeepers block the balls from hitting the pins.
3) Teams score one point for each pin knocked down during a 3-minute round, and knocked-down pins are immediately stood back up by the goalkeepers.
4) Rotate positions after each round so every student experiences each role, or modify the game to end only when all pins are knocked over.
pe-01976:
1) Mark a long lengthwise zone across the gym floor with cones, place 3-4 wolves holding scarves inside the den, and line up the rest of the players as bunnies along the sides.
2) Bunnies attempt to run across the den to the opposite side while wolves must stay within their designated zone and tag them with their free hand.
3) When a bunny is tagged inside the den, they retrieve a scarf from the crate and transform into a wolf for the next crossing.
4) Increase the width of the den or the starting number of wolves to scale the game difficulty for large groups up to 50+ students.
pe-01977:
1) Designate opposite ends of the gymnasium as 'Army' and 'Navy' boundaries, and have all students begin by lining up along the center line.
2) When the caller shouts "Army!" or "Navy!", players run toward that designated side, immediately turning back if the opposite command is called mid-stride.
3) If "Hit the deck!" is called, every player must instantly drop flat on their stomach and remain completely still until the caller gives the command "At ease!".
4) Add an elimination or fun exercise challenge for players who react prematurely to trick commands or who are the last to reach the wall.
pe-01978:
1) Students pair up, find an open space anywhere in the gym, and take one soft foam ball per pair.
2) The player without the ball gets a 5-second head start to sprint away and gain as much distance as possible.
3) Once the 5 seconds expire, the thrower chases their partner and attempts to tag them by throwing the foam ball at safe target areas like the feet or legs.
4) The thrower can retrieve and re-throw the ball until a hit is scored, after which the partners immediately swap roles and start a new 5-second countdown.
pe-01979:
1) Students form a circle of 6 to 10 players, and one starting player holds a stuffed cow (or soft ball).
2) Players pass the stuffed cow around the circle from person to person without dropping it onto the floor.
3) Every time the toy successfully completes a full rotation around the circle, all players take one small step back to expand the circle.
4) If anyone drops the toy, everyone shouts "Moo-shake!" and performs a silly whole-body shaking wiggle dance before stepping back in to reset the circle.
pe-01980:
1) The teacher starts as the leader and students spread out across the gym or classroom with enough personal space.
2) When the leader calls out an item good for the heart, students continuously perform an action like jumping on the spot.
3) When an item that is bad for the heart is called out, students must immediately freeze and stand completely still.
4) There is no elimination, and students discuss why an item is unhealthy while varying exercise movements such as high knees or jumping jacks.
pe-01981:
1) Scatter numerous cones across the area and divide the class into Messies who knock down cones and Cleanies who upright them.
2) Start with hands only, then progress to using feet only where players gently tip cones over or upright them without kicking.
3) In the soccer version, Messies dribble soccer balls and gently kick them into cones to knock them over while Cleanies fix them.
4) Progress into paired passing challenges against aligned cones or a slalom dribbling relay shooting at a final target cone.
pe-01982:
1) Set up goals at opposite ends of the gym, divide the class into two teams, and have all players assume a crab walk position.
2) Players must maintain the crab walk stance throughout the entire match without standing up or using their hands and arms.
3) Teams pass and kick the beach ball toward the opposing net using only their feet, knees, or head to score goals.
4) Introduce multiple beach balls simultaneously onto the court to increase engagement and keep all participants active.
pe-01983:
1) Section off a designated lane using cones or gym floor lines, placing half the students inside as targets and half outside as throwers.
2) Target players move continuously back and forth inside the gallery performing assigned locomotive skills like crab walking or hopping.
3) Throwers practice rolling, underhand, or overhand throwing soft foam balls at the moving target players from behind the line.
4) When a target is hit, they immediately swap roles with the thrower, or play with a rule where targets cannot dodge and must move at a steady pace.
pe-01984:
1) Place four cones in the corners to form a rectangle, and have students divide themselves among the four corners facing clockwise.
2) Players at each corner pair up to play rock-paper-scissors, and the winner immediately sprints clockwise to the next cone.
3) The player who loses stays at the same cone and matches up with another waiting classmate to play again.
4) Players who lose three consecutive times advance automatically, and completing a full four-cone lap earns a scoring popsicle stick.
pe-01985:
1) Runners gather in the center circle as horses while four taggers start outside holding hula hoops as lassos.
2) On the signal, runners gallop out of the center and spread out across the gym while cowboys attempt to tag them.
3) Tagged runners must return to the center circle and perform exercises such as jumping jacks.
4) To ensure safety, students gallop rather than sprint, or play with simple hand tags instead of hoops when running.
pe-01986:
1) Set up five cones in a designated area and assign four defenders and one attacker to the group.
2) On the whistle, all players move around the play area looking for open angles and positions.
3) The attacker tries to capture a cone by placing a hand on top, while four defenders move quickly to touch and protect the cones.
4) A round immediately ends when the attacker successfully touches an open cone, after which a new attacker is rotated in.
pe-01987:
1) Divide the court into two halves, line up team players along the end walls as goalkeepers, and start with three field players per side.
2) Throw a foam soccer ball into the center to begin the fast-paced three-on-three match.
3) Players attempt to kick the ball past defenders into the end wall below head height to score, with infractions penalized by free kicks.
4) Whistle blows every one to two minutes to rotate field players to the end wall line while three fresh players immediately sprint in.
pe-01988:
1) Set up four corner bases using four colored cones representing Pokemon teams, and have students wear matching colored pinnies.
2) Designate one color team to be the taggers to start the round while all other students scatter across the gym floor.
3) Any tagged student must go to their team's home cone area and complete a designated movement skill before returning.
4) Once the movement challenge is finished, the student re-enters play, and tagger roles rotate to another color team after several minutes.
pe-01989:
1) Have students gather in the center of the gym while the teacher introduces a creative theme like a jungle or desert.
2) When signaled, students imagine an animal living in that habitat and spread out across the entire open space.
3) Each student travels around the room mimicking the unique movements and physical behaviors of their chosen animal.
4) The whistle blows for all students to return to the center circle, after which the class can explore a new theme.
pe-01990:
1) Organize students into teams in straight lines and place 3-4 hula hoops in front of the lead jumper.
2) On the whistle, the first jumper (the frog) leaps forward into the hoops one by one.
3) Teammates behind quickly pick up the cleared hoops from the back and lay them down in front of the frog.
4) Stepping outside the hoop requires returning to the start, and upon reaching the far wall, a new jumper takes over for the return trip.
pe-01991:
1) Disperse students across the gym and designate one or two players as taggers.
2) On the start signal, runners scatter while the taggers chase and tag them with a gentle touch.
3) Tagged runners must freeze and bend their backs forward with curved arms to form a candy cane shape.
4) Free runners unfreeze tagged players by ducking under the candy cane hoop, and roles switch after a set time.
pe-01992:
1) Set up goals with cones at each end, divide the class into two teams with assigned numbers, and place beach balls in the center.
2) The teacher calls out specific numbers, and the called players must enter the center playing area using a crab walk.
3) Called players (crabs) can only use their feet to kick the beach balls toward the opposing team's goal to score points.
4) Uncalled players (lobsters) guard the goal line using only their hands to push or punch the balls away without catching them.
pe-01993:
1) From a standing position, bend your knees and place both hands on the floor.
2) Step back one foot at a time into a plank position without jumping.
3) Keep your hips and back from sagging, then step forward one foot at a time.
4) Straighten your back first and stand up using the strength of your legs.
pe-01994:
1) Move only by passing without dribbling, taking no more than three steps while holding the ball.
2) Pass or shoot at the frame within three seconds of receiving the ball.
3) Complete a maximum of three consecutive passes within the team before attempting a shot.
4) Score 1 point when a ball shot at the frame bounces off and lands on the floor outside the forbidden zone.
pe-01996:
1) Float in the water using a comfortable posture such as shrimp float, star float, back float, or jellyfish float.
2) Press down on the water with your arms and lift your head above the surface to inhale when breathing is needed.
3) As the body sinks after breathing, resume the floating posture and wait to surface again.
pe-01997:
1) Choose the most comfortable floating posture, such as shrimp float or prone star float, and enter the water.
2) Periodically push down on the water with both arms and raise head to breathe while floating.
3) Continuously check your surroundings and maintain the same spot to stay afloat for 5 minutes.
pe-01998:
1) Perform a back float posture and gently move hands to maintain balance.
2) Without kicking legs, move arms like rowing oars to turn and move in the desired direction.
pe-01999:
1) Practice alternating foot step and side-to-side two-count step.
2) Master jumping with feet opening and closing, and criss-cross arm jumping.
3) Combine the learned basic steps with foot movements to choreograph a routine in groups.
4) Perform the completed routine together in sync with music.
pe-02000:
1) When holding a life buoy, lean chest against it and hook both arms over it rather than climbing on top.
2) Hug kickboards tightly against the chest and lie back to stay afloat.
3) If there is no immediate danger and land is far, look toward rescuers and wait in place.
4) If a safe refuge is nearby, gently kick feet to navigate toward it.
pe-02001:
1) Players from both teams take turns using long cues to slide disks into the scoring zones.
2) If a disk is more than halfway inside a scoring area (10, 8, 7), points are awarded; landing in 10-OFF deducts 10 points.
3) Players strategically aim to position their disks in scoring areas or knock away opponent disks.
4) After playing all designated rounds, the team with the higher cumulative score wins.
pe-02002:
1) Warm up with 1 minute of light jogging in place on an exercise mat.
2) Perform overhead clapping steps without jumping for 1 minute.
3) Execute standing elbow-to-opposite-knee crunches for 1 minute.
4) Complete slow burpees maintaining a flat back plank, followed by phantom air rope skipping.
pe-02003:
1) Roll newspapers tightly into rigid rods, secure with tape, and trim the ends evenly.
2) Practice balancing the stick horizontally and vertically on palms, fingers, back of hands, and forehead.
3) Toss and catch the stick in the air, or release it vertically and catch the bottom before it falls.
4) Two partners place stick ends between their index fingers and cooperate to move, turn, and bend without dropping it.
pe-02004:
1) Learn low block (Arae Makki) by bringing the blocking wrist to the opposite shoulder and sweeping down.
2) Perform middle block (Momtong Makki) by rotating the forearm inward to chest level.
3) Practice high block (Olgul Makki) by raising the wrist along the center line in front of the forehead.
4) Practice middle punch, face punch, and low punch by twisting the fist forward from the waist.
pe-02005:
1) Place 2 storybooks side by side on the floor and stand upright facing them.
2) As step 1, perform double-tap footwork alternating two touches per book over 16 beats.
3) As step 2, alternate single touches over 16 beats, and as step 3, step both feet up and down alternately onto the books.
4) As step 4, perform the advanced alternating switch jump step across the diagonal position over 16 beats.
pe-02006:
1) Rest hand on the floor and flick a bottle cap using thumb, index, or middle finger.
2) Place caps facing each other and take turns flicking to hit opponent caps or land within a hand span to capture them.
3) In wall rebound mode, bounce the cap off the wall to hit opponent caps.
4) The player who captures all or the most opponent bottle caps wins.
pe-02007:
1) Hold the handle straight with thumb positioned under the big cup and balance the ball.
2) Practice gently lifting the ball and resting it onto the cup.
3) Toss the ball upward and catch it softly without making noise by bending your knees.
4) Flip the wrist so the small cup faces up, and practice tossing and catching the ball the same way.
pe-02008:
1) Hold around the base cup, toss the ball to chest height, and catch it in the base cup.
2) From the standard grip, toss the ball and rotate the kendama inward to catch on the base cup.
3) Practice shifting the ball consecutively between big cup, small cup, and base cup.
4) Toss the ball upward without spin using knee recoil and land it onto the spike.
pe-02009:
1) Perform high-intensity exercise for 20 seconds.
2) Rest for 10 seconds.
3) Execute jumping jacks, narrow push-ups, squats, plank, burpees, wide push-ups, jump squats, and mountain climbers in order.
4) Complete all 8 movements over a total of 4 minutes.
pe-02010:
1) Players wear 3 wristbands chosen from 6 colors, and 6 to 12 players hold hands in a circle.
2) A player tosses the dice ball into the circle; only the player matching the top color retrieves the ball while others scatter.
3) When the thrower calls 'Stop', all running players freeze facing the ball; the thrower may pivot on one foot and throw within 5 seconds.
4) Hit players surrender one wristband to the thrower, but if a player catches the throw, they take a band from the thrower; collecting 5 different colored bands wins.
pe-02011:
1) Observe picture cards of classroom items and select objects to represent.
2) Imitate shapes using bodily movements to highlight traits like big, small, sharp, round, wide, or narrow.
3) Express movements of functioning items like electric fans through variations in speed, curves, and straight lines.
4) Cooperate with peers to complete creative bodily expressions of classroom objects.
pe-02012:
1) Set starting and finishing lines and decide within groups how to move.
2) Move along the designated path using various steps such as walking, skipping, and galloping.
3) Follow teacher signals using flags or whistles to change movement directions between left and right.
4) Students who need extra support can hold hands with peers or teachers while practicing.
pe-02013:
1) Divide roles into throwers and target holders facing each other.
2) Target holders stand still without moving while holding a basket in front of their waist.
3) Throwers toss balls or objects into the basket from a set distance.
4) The player or group that lands the most objects into the fixed target at varying distances wins.
pe-02014:
1) Mark the playing area and set up safety zones.
2) Each player holds a sticker and waits with adequate space inside the boundary.
3) At the start signal, players chase each other and place stickers on friends' backs.
4) Players must not run out of the field while fleeing, and anyone with a sticker on their back moves to the waiting area.
pe-02015:
1) Divide into teams and assign the fielding team to pitcher and fielders.
2) The kicker calls out the score zone where the ball will be kicked and kicks the ball.
3) If the ball lands in the designated zone, the team gets the points.
4) Landing elsewhere or being caught results in an out, and teams switch after three outs; the team with the most points after 3 innings wins.
pe-02016:
1) Form fielding and batting teams.
2) When a batter steps up, the fielding team calls out a batting direction such as 1st base, 2nd base, or 3rd base.
3) If the batter hits toward the designated direction, they score 1 point; failing to do so awards no points.
4) Each student receives 3 batting chances.
pe-02017:
1) Mark scoring zones from 1 to 3 points around the goal according to shooting locations.
2) Offensive players take turns dribbling from the starting line and shoot from their chosen zone.
3) Goalkeepers must stay within the goalkeeper area while defending.
4) The team with the highest total score at the end wins.
pe-02018:
1) Hold a paddle in one hand and bounce a ball upward without letting it hit the floor.
2) Hold a paddle in each hand and alternate hitting the ball upward.
3) Two players sit facing each other and rally the ball without letting it drop.
4) From a designated distance, hit the ball with the paddle into a target box with or without a bounce.
pe-02019:
1) Face each other in pairs behind cone markers to practice underhand passing and catching forward and in indicated directions.
2) Practice long-distance overhand passes and catches.
3) Shoot at the tchoukball net frame from outside the semi-circle crease and catch the rebound.
4) Practice jump shooting from 45-degree angles and sides, then rotate into defensive positions to catch rebounding balls.
pe-02020:
1) Keep the balloon airborne to a rhythm using various body parts including head, shoulder, knee, and foot.
2) Stand facing a wall and practice 20 underhand serves by hitting the lower diagonal side of the balloon upward.
3) Practice 20 stationary overhand serves against the wall by swinging your arm back and forward.
4) Practice 20 alternating single-hand passes, 20 underhand passes with straight elbows, 20 overhead passes with hands forming a triangle above the forehead, and 10 alternating underhand-overhead passes against the wall.
pe-02021:
1) Students sit in a circle in a cross-legged position with hands on their knees.
2) Everyone bends forward tapping the floor while the teacher chooses a leader, and a guesser sits in the center.
3) Once started, the leader changes hand or body motions, and all other students quickly mimic them without staring directly.
4) The guesser in the middle rotates in place without standing up to observe and guess who the leader is.
pe-02022:
1) Set up a mini net by placing obstacles such as boxes or books in the center of the desk.
2) Decide turns by rock-paper-scissors and strike a bottle cap with hands over to the opponent's side.
3) If the bottle cap flies off the desk or hits the net barrier, the opponent scores a point.
4) Accumulate points, and the player reaching the target score first wins the game.
pe-02023:
1) Set up obstacles in the center of a desk or table to serve as a net.
2) Flick a bottle cap with your finger over to the opponent's side avoiding the obstacles.
3) Score a point when the opponent fails to return the cap or knocks it out of bounds.
4) Hitting or getting stuck on the obstacle net results in giving up a point.
pe-02024:
1) In pairs, one student stays outside the mat and rolls a die showing rolling movements and repetition counts.
2) The student on the mat performs the designated roll to tag an opponent with their hand.
3) Tagged students swap roles with their partner waiting outside the mat and return to the game.
4) Continue playing; the team that swapped roles the fewest times wins.
pe-02025:
1) Students pair up, and one person tosses a ball or shuttlecock toward the partner.
2) The receiving partner strikes the tossed ball with a racket to return it.
3) Move toward the path of the incoming ball, hit it, and return to the starting spot to get ready.
4) As players improve, toss the ball or shuttlecock faster and into various directions.
pe-02026:
1) Team members get down on all fours to form a leg tunnel, keeping gaps between players within 10 cm.
2) On the start signal, the front runner sprints to the back and rolls the ball forward through the tunnel.
3) The player who rolled the ball immediately assumes the tunnel position, and the player at the end catches the ball and sprints forward to repeat.
4) If the ball rolls out behind, the last person retrieves it, and the team whose members reach the destination line first wins.
pe-02027:
1) Divide roles into balloon holders and balloon kickers.
2) Balloon holders stand at set intervals holding balloons at progressively increasing heights.
3) The kicker takes a light run-up, takes off from one foot, and kicks the balloon with the opposite foot using a scissors kick motion.
4) Switch roles and repeat the drill.
pe-02028:
1) Divide into two teams and determine the running order.
2) On the start signal, runners set off one by one, performing assigned vault movements at each station.
3) Measure the total time taken to complete all stations and return to the starting line.
4) Every member completes the course; team times are summed, and the team with the faster overall time wins.
pe-02029:
1) In the lead-up activity, a thrower launches the disc, collects scattered disc cones from the field, and steps on base to score 1 point per cone.
2) The fielding team tags their base with the disc to get the runner out, and teams switch sides after 3 outs or 3 fouls.
3) In the main 7v7 game, teams line up in their end zones and advance the disc exclusively through passing without running with it.
4) Catching a pass inside the opponent's end zone scores 1 point, and the team with the most points when time expires wins.
pe-02030:
1) Set up starting and finish lines, placing spot markers as stepping stones to begin.
2) The bridge crosser balances on one foot on a spot marker and advances by stepping onto markers laid down by a teammate.
3) The teammate placing the bridge carries and lays down only one spot marker at a time from the start line.
4) Upon reaching the finish line, switch roles and the team that returns to the starting line first wins.
pe-02031:
1) One player acts as the batter while the other students play defense.
2) The batter hits the ball over the foul line with a fist and walks around one of the cones on either side to return to the start without running.
3) Fielders catch the ball and bring it inside the foul line before the batter returns to the starting position.
4) After the batter hits the ball three times, the next student takes a turn on offense.
pe-02032:
1) With a partner, gently kick the ball using the inside of the foot to pass and trap the rolling ball with the foot.
2) Dribble the ball by gently tapping it with the foot while keeping it close.
pe-02033:
1) Keep the ball from hitting the floor in place by adjusting the racket angle and hitting power.
2) Walk in a straight line while continuously bouncing the ball upward with the racket without letting it drop.
3) Move around while bouncing the ball on the racket and dodging various cones placed on the floor.
pe-02034:
1) Takeoff: Run quickly and jump forcefully off the beat board with both feet to land standing on top of the vault.
2) Straddle sit: Step on the board, place both hands on the vault, and straddle your legs to sit on it.
3) Straddle vault: Approach from 3–5 steps back, push off the springboard with both feet, place hands on two-thirds of the vault, straddle legs over, and land with knees softly bent.
pe-02035:
1) Students sit with their backs facing the center against the classroom walls, assigned numbers 1 through 5 in each group.
2) When the teacher calls a number, players with that number quickly scramble to grab the beanbag from the center marker.
3) The student who grabs the beanbag throws or passes it through another team's vacant space to take 1 point from that team.
4) Teams lose a point if players lift their bottoms or move before their number is called.
pe-02036:
1) Tightly wind the string of the top-spinning stick around the top.
2) Release and spin the top on the floor by pulling the stick.
3) Continuously whip the body of the top with the string to keep it spinning.
4) In competitive play with two or more players, strike or bump the opponent's top to make it stop first.
pe-02037:
1) Each player prepares 2 or more paper folded ddakji tiles.
2) Play rock-paper-scissors; the loser places their ddakji flat on the floor.
3) The winner strikes the opponent's ddakji on the floor using their own ddakji.
4) If flipped, the striker claims it; if not, turn passes to the opponent.
pe-02038:
1) Grip the stick with the dominant hand lower, knees bent in a low stance.
2) Place a disc cone between the feet and dribble side to side for 10 seconds, then repeat with a floorball.
3) Dribble around a cone placed 5 meters away and return in a relay format.
4) Dribble toward the goal, take a shot, retrieve the ball, and tag the next runner.
pe-02039:
1) Line up at the cone starting point.
2) Run forward on signal and stack 3 jumbo cups.
3) Run to the next spot and stack 3 jumbo cups.
4) Turn around the cone and run back.
pe-02040:
1) Blow up a balloon to an appropriate size.
2) Drop the balloon and kick it upward with the inside of the foot.
3) Practice kicking once and catching, then progress to consecutive kicks.
4) Take turns with a partner kicking the balloon without letting it fall.
pe-02041:
1) Play 3 sub-quarters per set using 30 pucks.
2) Slide the pucks by hand into the 4 target gates on the board.
3) Collect unentered pucks after each quarter to use in the next quarter, while entered pucks remain stacked inside the gates.
4) Tally points after the 3rd quarter; filling 1 puck in every gate earns 20 points with a 2x bonus instead of 10 points.
pe-02042:
1) Players stand behind the throwing line and divide red and blue boccia balls (6 each).
2) The starting player throws the white jack onto the court and follows with their first colored ball toward the jack.
3) The side whose ball is further away from the jack continues throwing until they are closer or run out of balls.
4) After all 12 colored balls are thrown, the team with the ball closest to the jack scores points equal to the number of balls closer than the opponent's best ball.
pe-02043:
