1) Form two teams of 5 players each on a court or artificial turf field.
2) Wear flat-soled sneakers without studs suitable for hard gym floors.
3) When the ball goes out of bounds, restart play using a kick-in with the foot instead of a throw-in.
4) The kick-in must be executed within 4 seconds, or possession is awarded to the opponent.
pe-02044:
1) Roll newspapers and fringe the end to craft 3 newspaper arrows.
2) Place a basket as the target and throw the arrows from increasingly distant stages (1 to 4).
3) Challenge variations such as using the non-dominant hand or balancing the arrow on fingers before throwing.
4) Execute movement challenges such as throwing backwards or spinning 3 times in an elephant-nose pose before tossing.
pe-02045:
1) Divide into four groups, create a beanbag zone for each group, and place beanbags evenly.
2) Pick up one beanbag, run, and accurately place it in the next group's zone.
3) The group with the fewest beanbags remaining in their zone wins.
pe-02046:
1) Divide into two teams and wait in a line outside the court boundary.
2) On the signal, rush to grab the 5-6 balls placed along the center line.
3) Players hit by a ball are eliminated and stay outside the court to pass stray balls back to their teammates rather than playing in an outfield.
4) If a player catches an opponent's throw, the thrower is eliminated; players can also deflect or block incoming balls using a ball they hold, and only one player can be eliminated per throw.
pe-02047:
1) Two teams stand in a single line facing opposite directions and hold hands.
2) On signal, the first runners at both outer ends circle around and run into the center.
3) Once a runner arrives in the center, the next runner runs in the same way.
4) The team whose final runner reaches the center first wins.
pe-02048:
1) Students pair up holding hands to act as 'trees' positioned around the classroom.
2) The mouse is chased by the cat and grabs the hand of one student forming a tree.
3) The student on the opposite side of the tree detaches and becomes the new mouse who must run away.
4) When the cat tags the mouse, the tagged player becomes the new cat, while the previous cat completes a meowing transformation motion before fleeing as the new mouse.
pe-02049:
1) Sit facing each other on chairs placed 1m apart.
2) Pass the ball back and forth 4 times with a partner.
3) Move the chairs one step backward after every successful set to increase distance.
4) Pass the ball using various methods such as throwing high, rolling, or bouncing.
pe-02050:
1) Lie flat on a mat and cross one leg over the pelvis, pinning it to the floor.
2) Twist the upper body to the opposite side and move beanbags across one by one.
3) Perform 3 repetitions on each side for 2 sets.
pe-02051:
1) Set up 10 bowling pins across three distance zones (1 pt: 4 pins, 2 pts: 3 pins, 3 pts: 3 pins).
2) Hit the foam baseball with a fist toward the pins.
3) Only the score of the highest value pin knocked down is awarded.
4) Reset pins after hitting, rotate through 3 sets, and the team with the most points wins.
pe-02052:
1) Stand facing each other 1.5m apart and play rock-paper-scissors on signal.
2) The winner chases and attempts to tag the loser before reaching the finish line.
3) The loser runs toward their designated finish line to avoid being tagged.
4) If tied or tagged, perform the designated fitness mission (e.g., 3 squats).
pe-02053:
1) Pairs face each other holding sticks to balance a ball between two sticks.
2) Bounce the ball on the floor and catch it securely between the two sticks.
3) Toss the ball upward, let it bounce off the floor, and catch it with the sticks.
4) Bounce or toss the ball across to transfer it to the next team's sticks.
pe-02054:
1) Set up desks in the center of the classroom as a dividing net and split 6 players into two teams facing each other.
2) Lift and volley the finger light ball with legs or feet within 5 touches to send it over to the opponent's side.
3) A team loses a point if the ball touches the floor.
4) The first team to score 5 points wins.
pe-02055:
1) Walk in four directions and perform step jumps to the music.
2) Push legs while walking forward and backward, then perform bilateral jegichagi kicks.
3) Rub hands, fold arms, do hesitant steps, and clap hands.
4) Wash hair motions, stretch and pull shoulders, rotate hips, and high-five partners.
pe-02056:
1) Place a shuttlecock on your head and squat without letting it fall.
2) Place a shuttlecock on your instep or thigh and lift your leg to balance.
3) Kick the shuttlecock up from your instep and catch it with your hands.
4) Place a shuttlecock on your head, tilt your head backward or forward, and catch the falling shuttlecock with your hands.
pe-02057:
1) Hold 4 cups in each hand, gather them into a single stack, and separate them back into two hands.
2) Stack cups into a single vertical tower and take them down.
3) Perform the Cup Elevator by moving top cups to the bottom one by one until a different colored cup reaches the top.
4) Grab the exact same number of cups simultaneously from two separate stacks using both hands.
pe-02058:
1) Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, raise arms sideways, lift one leg to the side, and balance for 5 seconds.
2) Raise arms forward, bend and lift one knee forward, and hold the position for 5 seconds.
3) Place 4 spot markers on the floor, assume a plank position on all fours, and lift right hand, left hand, right foot, and left foot one at a time for 3 seconds each.
4) Walk along straight and S-curved lines on the floor with arms held horizontally, staying precisely on the lines across a 3-meter round trip.
pe-02059:
1) Perform warm-up stretches including wrist/ankle rotations and leg stretches.
2) Complete single-leg leg rotations and single-leg forward bends (12 reps, 2 sets each).
3) Perform squat with side leg lifts (15 reps, 3 sets) and lunges lifting a mini gym ball (10 reps, 3 sets).
4) Complete side lunges (10 reps, 3 sets), plank row taps (20 reps, 3 sets), sit-ups lifting a mini gym ball (15 reps, 3 sets), and cool-down stretches on mats.
pe-02060:
1) Throw-ins must be taken within 15 cm of the line by the designated player.
2) Defenders must stand at least 0.9 meters away from the player with the ball.
3) Players cannot take more than two steps, dribble, or roll the ball along the ground.
4) Play begins with a center pass delivered within the center third upon the whistle.
pe-02061:
1) Inflate the Kin-Ball using an air blower and tie the bladder opening tightly.
2) Divide 4 to 8 players into two teams facing each other across a standing gym mat.
3) Lift the Kin-Ball overhead with both hands and throw it over the mat to the opposing court.
4) Exchange throws for 30 seconds to 1 minute, and the team without the ball in their court when time expires wins.
pe-02062:
1) Set up a divider across joined desks and hold one speed cup each on opposite sides.
2) The server bounces the ball from the cup onto their own side of the desk before it travels to the opponent's desk.
3) For regular returns, launch the ball directly to bounce once on the opponent's desk without touching your own.
4) A point is lost if a player fails to catch the incoming ball on a single bounce or allows it to bounce twice.
pe-02063:
1) Divide the class into two teams and practice 8 animal movements in advance.
2) Place 5 animal slips into each team's basket.
3) When the runner starts, the next runner draws a slip from the basket to determine which animal to mimic.
4) Run mimicking the drawn animal around the cone and tag the next runner, and the team completing 10 runs first wins.
pe-02064:
1) Explore the goalball by touching it with hands to get familiar.
2) Stand with feet twice shoulder-width apart, bend the waist, and extend hands downward.
3) Place the ball in front of the legs and pick it up with both hands.
4) Swing the ball side to side and release it smoothly to roll along the floor.
pe-02065:
1) Stand at the starting cone holding a badminton racket and a shuttlecock.
2) Begin bouncing the shuttlecock upward repeatedly with the racket in place.
3) Walk forward toward the turning cone while continuously bouncing the shuttlecock.
4) Loop around the turning cone and return to the starting line without dropping the shuttlecock.
pe-02066:
1) Stand with feet together and rotate wrists and ankles smoothly in both directions.
2) Place hands on knees to rotate them, then spread legs to perform shallow and deep knee presses.
3) Spread legs wide in a squat stance, rest hands on knees, and twist the torso side to side.
4) Step forward to stretch the Achilles tendon, then finish by rotating the waist, shoulders, and neck.
pe-02067:
1) Hold the jegi by resting its heavy head on the palm of your hand.
2) Toss it lightly upward and kick it with the inside of your foot as it falls.
3) Start by kicking once and catching, then progress to kicking twice while tapping your foot on the floor.
4) Advance to kicking continuously without touching the ground (heullaengi) or alternating feet (jigijigi).
pe-02069:
1) Set up hula hoops and spot markers on the floor to secure exercise areas.
2) Round 1: Jump on the spot with both feet together on the marker.
3) Round 2: Alternate feet tapping the marker, followed by jumping twice on each foot in Round 3.
4) Round 4: Jump feet together on the marker then spread outside the hoop, and Round 5: Jump alternating feet front and back.
pe-02070:
1) Two turners swing a long rope at both ends while the remaining ten runners line up.
2) Runners enter the moving rope one by one in rhythm with the rope strikes.
3) Each runner jumps once inside and exits smoothly along a figure-eight pathway.
4) The team counts the total number of successful passes achieved within 2 minutes.
pe-02071:
1) Place a thick mat or blanket on a flat floor and clear nearby obstacles.
2) Lie on your back and perform leg raises, seated leg lifts, and glute bridges for 10 seconds each.
3) Lie face down and lift opposite arm and leg, then lift both arms and legs together (superman pose) for 10 seconds each.
4) Hold a bird-dog plank balance with opposite arm and leg raised horizontally for 10 seconds.
pe-02072:
1) Lie on the floor with knees bent and curl up your upper body, holding for 10 seconds.
2) If lacking strength, reach hands toward knees and lift upper body slightly to hold for 10 seconds.
3) Grip the edge of a stable chair with hands and extend legs forward to hold for 10 seconds.
4) Perform 3 repetitions of chair dips by bending and straightening arms, then hold extended posture.
pe-02073:
1) Face each other, place hands on partner's shoulders, step back, and press upper body down.
2) Stand side by side holding partner's shoulder and pull own ankle backward to stretch quadriceps.
3) Sit facing each other with legs spread and feet touching, then hold each other's hands.
4) One partner gently pulls backward so the other leans forward to stretch inner thighs, then switch.
pe-02074:
1) Each player runs carrying one jumbo stack cup to build a team castle and line up
2) Players take turns throwing (or kicking) balls to knock down the opponent's castle
3) The team that knocks down the opponent's entire castle first wins (ground floor excluded)
4) Quickly tidy up the fallen jumbo stacks and form a team line
pe-02075:
1) Divide students into equal teams according to group size (e.g., 4 teams of 6).
2) Place a spot marker at an appropriate distance from the jar based on student skill level.
3) Team members take turns throwing 2 pitch-pot arrows each from the marker.
4) Record the total number of arrows scored by each team to tally points (e.g., 20 points per score).
pe-02076:
1) Hold the stick properly and practice tap dribbling, long dribbling, and turn dribbling in place.
2) Dribble forward around marker cones pretending they are defenders.
3) Pair up to practice pushing passes along the floor and receiving by cushioning the ball backward.
4) Practice shooting towards the goal and apply the skills in a mini-game.
pe-02077:
1) Form two teams of 4 to 7 players, decide the first attacker via rock-paper-scissors, and start with an entry pass across the center line from behind the endline.
2) Once the ball crosses the center line through passing, players can shoot at either rebounder frame.
3) The attacking team scores if the ball rebounds off the frame and touches the floor or hits a defender below the knee without being caught.
4) The defending team scores if the rebound falls into the forbidden zone, lands out of bounds, or touches an attacking player; the first team to reach 10 points wins.
pe-02078:
1) Organize teams of three players and decide the hitting order behind the start line.
2) The first student hits the shuttlecock toward the target (jumbo cup) using a handler racket.
3) From the exact spot where the shuttlecock lands without stepping forward, the next player hits toward the target.
4) The team that successfully sinks the shuttlecock into the final 3rd target and sprints back to the start line with the cup and shuttlecock wins.
pe-02079:
1) Learn how to grip the handler paddle with forehand (palm facing up) and backhand (back of hand facing up).
2) Practice bouncing the shuttlecock upward repeatedly in place using forehand and backhand grips without dropping it.
3) In pairs, practice hitting by taking turns tossing the shuttlecock by hand and striking it with the paddle.
4) Practice serving over the badminton net into target cups or baskets by gently dropping the shuttlecock and hitting it from below.
pe-02080:
1) Two teams of two players face each other across a badminton court.
2) Play rock-paper-scissors to decide the first serve; serve diagonally from the right when the score is even (or 0) and from the left when odd.
3) Return the shuttlecock over the net on either one bounce or in the air in a single hit.
4) If the serving team wins the rally, the same server continues, and the first team to reach 15 points wins.
pe-02081:
1) Form three teams wearing colored pinnies and set up a forbidden zone with mats around the tchoukball rebounder.
2) Determine the starting team by rock-paper-scissors, and the attacking team calls out the color of the target defending team.
3) Complete three passes among teammates, then shoot the ball against the rebounder.
4) If the called defending team fails to catch the rebounding ball, the other two teams earn points, and the first team to reach 10 points wins.
pe-02082:
1) In pairs, practice shoulder passes, push passes, and underhand passes.
2) Throw the ball against the rebounder and catch the bouncing ball individually.
3) Throw the ball at the rebounder and have the next student in line catch the rebound.
4) Practice combined attack and defense with 1 attacker and 2 defenders, rotating positions after each catch.
pe-02083:
1) Set a team order, and from the spot marker, each player takes turns hitting a shuttlecock with a handler paddle into the jumbo stacks in the center.
2) If the shuttlecock misses, retrieve it and hand it over to the next teammate in line.
3) If successful, bring that jumbo cup to your team's designated spot and stack it.
4) The team that successfully builds the 4-3-2-1 (10 cups) pyramid first wins.
pe-02084:
1) Divide into two teams, hold floorball sticks, wear team pinnies, and position across the court.
2) Start the match with a face-off in the center, passing and dribbling the ball with sticks.
3) Shoot the ball into the opponent's goal to score points.
4) Play through the designated periods (periods 1 to 4).
pe-02085:
1) Create a paper target on the wall and throw newspaper balls 10 times to calculate the total score.
2) Use a broom or implement to hit a ball through a cardboard box goal over 10 attempts.
3) Mark 1-point to 5-point zones on the floor and putt the ball 10 times to earn target scores.
4) Suspend a newspaper ball with string between chair legs to swing and hit it with thrown balls.
pe-02086:
1) Place a desk in the center of a dodgeball court and place a cone (treasure) on top.
2) Play standard dodgeball rules while throwing balls to knock the opponent's cone off the desk.
3) Players hit by the ball are out and move to the outfield.
4) Even if players remain inside, a team loses immediately if their treasure falls to the floor.
pe-02087:
1) Split into two teams and kick balls from behind cones toward an open goal.
2) Earn 1 point for scoring inside the goal and 5 points for hitting the crossbar.
3) Missing scores 0 points, and the kicker must immediately retrieve the ball.
4) Tally all points after every player completes their turn to determine the winner.
pe-02088:
1) Place a balance beam and set a kicking line at a set distance using cones.
2) Players from both teams kick balls on cue to hit or pass under the beam.
3) Passing under the beam scores 1 point, while hitting the beam directly scores 5 points.
4) Players retrieve their balls, and the team that accumulates more points wins.
pe-02089:
1) Set up a circular court with cones, placing a hula hoop and a cone (treasure) in the center.
2) One defender stands in the center to guard the treasure cone.
3) Attackers stationed outside the outer circle kick soccer balls to knock down the treasure.
4) The defender kicks balls away; defending for 1 minute scores 1 point, while the treasure falling causes a role switch.
pe-02090:
1) Set up a rectangular court using cones.
2) On the start signal, defenders roll or throw balls from both sidelines.
3) Attackers sprint across to the safe zone while dodging balls.
4) The team earns points for each player reaching safety, and the team with the higher score wins.
pe-02091:
1) Connect balance beams to form a path, divide into two teams, and start from opposite ends.
2) Walk forward maintaining balance and play rock-paper-scissors upon meeting an opponent.
3) The winner advances while the losing team immediately sends the next runner.
4) A team wins by entering the opponent's final defense area and winning rock-paper-scissors.
pe-02092:
1) Line up 5 desks in a row.
2) Take turns within the team to bounce a ping-pong ball along the desks.
3) Catch the ball with a cup before it hits the floor to earn points equal to the number of desks bounced over.
4) Teams take turns and the team with the higher score wins.
pe-02093:
1) Balance a treasure (candy) on the back of your hand.
2) Protect your candy from falling while trying to knock off others' candy.
3) If your candy drops, you are eliminated and return to your seat.
4) Continue until the last player remains.
pe-02094:
1) Set up the balance beam and turning cones in the gym, then decide the running order.
2) On the signal, run toward the balance beam and either crawl under or jump over it.
3) Touch the turning cone and head back, passing through the balance beam again.
4) The person who returns to the starting line first wins.
pe-02095:
1) Divide into two teams facing each other across the net.
2) Serve overhand across the net to score 1 point.
3) Scoring is 0 points if failing to clear the net, while the receiving side earns 2 points for catching the ball.
4) Earn 3 points by bumping the ball back over the net with an underhand pass.
pe-02096:
1) Divide into two teams across a center line marked by a cone, holding hands in front and gripping teammates' waists behind.
2) At the start signal, both teams pull backwards with all their strength.
3) The team whose grip breaks or gets pulled further across the line loses.
4) If neither team wins within 5 seconds, it is a tie or decided by rock-paper-scissors.
pe-02097:
1) Two players hold the corners of a towel facing each other.
2) Place a bouncy ball in the center of the towel.
3) Simultaneously snap the towel taut to bounce the ball into the air.
4) Challenge to achieve the highest number of bounces within a set time limit (if using a balloon, out of bounds ends the attempt).
pe-02098:
1) Set up 10 empty plastic bottles in a triangle mark and set a throwing line at a fixed distance.
2) Participants take turns rolling the ball from behind the throwing line to knock down the bottles.
3) Knocking all down on the first roll scores a strike (10 points); if any remain, a second roll is given and knocked pins are summed.
4) Play through the designated frames (10 frames) and the player with the highest total score wins.
pe-02099:
1) Write the most regrettable thing from the first semester and the habit to break on two scrap papers.
2) Crumple both papers tightly to make two paper balls.
3) Place 5 jumbo cups in a line on the classroom floor and assign 2 to 6 points increasing by distance.
4) Throw one paper ball at a time twice; score the cup's points if it goes in, or 1 point if it misses.
pe-02100:
1) Prepare two shuttlecocks per person and hold one in each hand.
2) Toss one shuttlecock at least 1m above your head and catch it with the other shuttlecock.
3) Practice tossing and catching 10 times to get used to the movement.
4) Within the 2-minute time limit, count the total number of successful catches to reach the challenge goal.
pe-02101:
1) Divide players into two teams using pinnies and set up a center line using cones.
2) Throw the dodgeball according to standard dodgeball rules to hit and eliminate opponents.
3) Players hit by a throw step outside the court and wait.
4) When the specific opposing thrower who eliminated them gets hit and out, the eliminated players immediately revive and return to the court.
pe-02102:
1) Place 32 stones on the intersections of the board, leaving only the exact center spot empty.
2) Choose a stone to jump over an adjacent stone into an empty spot directly beyond it.
3) Remove the jumped stone from the board.
4) Repeat jumping and removing stones until no valid moves remain, aiming to leave only one stone on the board.
pe-02103:
1) In rhythm walking, pairs face each other and walk while clapping hands to the beat.
2) In single-direction hopping, enter, jump to the right and back, while followers mirror the leader.
3) For cross hopping, set up a grid with at least 4 horizontal squares and an even number of vertical rows.
4) Players start from opposite sides and hop through the grid while crossing past each other.
pe-02104:
1) Face a partner and practice gently tossing the bean bag toward the partner's feet.
2) Practice tossing the bean bag toward the hole on the cornhole board from a distance of 4 meters.
3) Divide into boys' and girls' teams to start a cornhole relay game.
4) Team members take turns tossing bean bags, and the team that successfully sinks 4 bags into the hole first wins.
pe-02105:
1) Grip the rim with three fingers, support the top with your thumb, and point the index finger forward.
2) Bring the disc to the opposite shoulder and extend your arm forward while rotating the waist to throw.
3) The receiver opens arms vertically like an alligator mouth to catch the disc.
4) Advance to catching while running in the flight direction or throwing into goals.
pe-02106:
1) Hold a disc individually, flick it upward using wrist snap, clap hands, and catch it safely with both hands.
2) Practice rolling the disc forward with backspin so that it rolls back to your hands.
3) Place mini goal nets on one side of the gymnasium and form team lines behind marker cones.
4) Throw the disc towards the goal net in sequence upon signal, and the team scoring the most goals wins.
pe-02107:
1) Each group sits at their desk area and awaits the starting cue.
2) On the teacher's signal, all members of a group must stand up simultaneously while shouting a number.
3) If two or more groups stand up shouting the same number at the same time, both groups are eliminated.
4) The group that called out 1 in the previous round cannot call 1 in the next round, and the group left with the last number is eliminated.
pe-02108:
1) Set up starting lines using cones at distances of 3 paces (1 point), 5 paces (2 points), and 7 paces (3 points) in front of the disc golf basket, and line up by groups.
2) The first thrower from each group attempts a putt from the 1-point distance toward the basket.
3) Successfully putting into the basket earns progression to the 2-point distance on the next turn, and succeeding at 2 points allows an attempt at the 3-point distance; failing passes the turn to the next player.
4) Sum up all points scored by group members, and the group with the highest total score wins.
pe-02109:
1) Each group selects equipment such as disc golf baskets, mini goals, cones, spot markers, and mats in order of rock-paper-scissors results.
2) Team members collaborate in their designated areas to construct unique disc golf courses featuring baskets, obstacles, and starting markers.
3) Starting from Course 1, players listen to the host team's course explanation before thrower 1 from each team attempts the challenge from the starting line.
4) Teams rotate through every student-created hole in sequence, earning 1 point per successful hole-in to determine the final winning team.
pe-02110:
1) Place a toy egg on the egg spoon and hold the spoon with one hand.
2) Jump over mini hurdles sequentially upon the start signal.
3) Turn around the cone marker and return to pass the spoon and egg to the next runner.
4) If the egg drops or a hurdle falls, reset it in place before resuming.
pe-02111:
1) Hold the handle of the Boundarun racket and practice balancing the ball on the surface without dropping it.
2) Apply volleyball rules across a net to return the ball to the opponent's side within three touches.
3) In Boundarun volleyball, the first team to score 5 points wins.
4) As a variation, play a tic-tac-toe game with 9 hula hoops where teams alternate bouncing balls in to complete a line first.
pe-02112:
1) Step right and clap, step left and clap, then clap down right and clap down left.
2) Step and extend arms and legs outward alternately to each side.
3) Take three steps to the right and clap, then three steps to the left and clap.
4) Tap right foot forward and back, step side, tap the inside of the foot with hand, and jump turning 90 degrees clockwise to repeat.
pe-02113:
1) Inside a 2-3m circle, sit back-to-back or face-to-face with arms wrapped between thighs and calves, using hips to push the opponent over or out of the ring (Pig Wrestling).
2) Sit on the floor holding opposite calves with opposite hands, shuffle on hips, and push or hook legs to topple the opponent.
3) Stand facing each other matching the same foot and hand, and without lifting the planted foot, push and pull hands to unbalance the opponent (Hand Wrestling).
pe-02114:
1) Arrange 12 cups in sets of 3, 6, and 3 on the table.
2) From the side, alternately use right and left hands to stack cups into pyramids of 3, 6, and 3 (upstack).
3) Use both hands smoothly to collapse each stack back down into nested columns (downstack).
4) Stop the timer with both hands to record the time taken to complete the cycle.
pe-02115:
1) Prepare defensively in a very low stance to anticipate the opponent's attack.
2) Turn your body to dodge if the ball flies between you and your teammate and is difficult to catch.
3) Drop flat to the ground to dodge when facing close-range attacks.
4) Jump to dodge when the ball is thrown below knee level.
pe-02116:
1) Outfielders maintain full court vision and distribute passes evenly to front and center infielders.
2) Infield attackers target players with weaker defense or upright stances to secure quick outs.
3) Defenders form a basic straight-line formation 2-3m inside the end line.
4) The defensive line shifts sideways in unison according to the attacker's ball position under the captain's call.
pe-02117:
1) Groups of four line up holding the waist of the person in front (4-18 players per team).
2) Play attack and defense on a standard court following general dodgeball format.
3) Attackers must only aim at the tail player at the end of the line, and middle players are not out if hit.
4) If the tail player is hit, all four members are out and move to the outfield to continue playing.
pe-02118:
1) Line up facing each other to practice throws and passes, and the thrower runs to the back of the opposite line to wait.
2) Three groups form a triangle and pass clockwise, with the thrower moving to the back of the adjacent group.
3) Two groups face each other, rotate clockwise, and pass diagonally, with the leftmost person sprinting to the other side's left.
4) Four groups face each other and pass to any other group without passing to the same group twice consecutively, then the thrower moves to the back of their own line.
pe-02119:
1) Arrange 5 spot markers in a line according to leg length and place both feet on the center marker.
2) Roll the ball along the leg line from the left side to the right side and bring it back.
3) Move each foot outwards one spot marker at a time and repeat the rolling motion.
4) The player who successfully completes the sequence through the outermost markers first wins.
pe-02120:
1) Form 3 teams (Pink, Grey, Black) of 4 players each wearing team pinnies.
2) Three players on the attacking team support the ball while one calls 'Omnikin' and the target team color before hitting the ball with both hands.
3) The called team defends using any body part to keep the ball off the floor and must launch a counterattack within 5 seconds.
4) If the called team fails to catch the ball and it touches the floor, the attacking team earns 1 point; matches are played to 15 points across 3 sets.
pe-02121:
1) Two players face each other across a center marker.
2) If the whistle blows once, flee left; if it blows twice, flee right.
3) The opposing player immediately chases to tag the runner before they cross the safe boundary line.
4) Add variations such as hopping on one foot while escaping and chasing.
pe-02122:
1) Set up target bowling pins (or chair legs) on a flat floor surface.
2) Stand in a comfortable stance holding the ball with knees slightly bent.
3) Take steps (such as a 4-step approach), swing the arm back, shift weight onto the front foot, and roll the ball toward targets.
4) Compete to knock down as many targets as possible with fewer rolls.
pe-02123:
1) Four players form a team and toss markers onto the grid starting from square 1.
2) Hop on one and two feet avoiding marked squares, gathering everyone into the top 'Heaven' zone.
3) Turn around inside the 'Heaven' zone, hop back in reverse, retrieve the markers, and exit.
4) After all four clear level 8, toss markers backward over the head to claim owned territories.
pe-02124:
1) Place a 100-won coin in the bottom center of an opaque plastic bag.
2) Fold the bag upwards by the size of the coin, fold it in half so the coin stays fixed, and tie it with a rubber band.
3) Cut the upper part of the bag into strips with scissors, spread them out by hand, and rub them to finish the jegi.
4) Try challenging steps in order: palm hitting, book hitting, and kicking with the foot.
pe-02125:
1) Choose one tagger while other players line up behind the starting line.
2) The tagger announces two consonants (e.g., B-B) and chants "B-B word flower has bloomed" with their back turned.
3) Players advance, shout a word matching the consonants, and freeze in a pose depicting that word when the tagger turns around.
4) Any player who moves or fails to represent a matching word must return to the start or is out.
pe-02126:
1) Run with a consistent approach run toward the springboard.
2) Jump off the springboard using both feet together rather than one foot.
3) Place both hands wide on the far two-thirds section of the vault box.
4) Straddle legs wide over the box and land with feet together and knees bent.
pe-02127:
1) Step in place lightly to catch the rhythm during the intro of BTS's Dynamite.
2) Perform Movement 1 by clapping hands and extending arms and shoulders outward with step touches.
3) Execute Movements 2 and 3 combining light kicks, steps, and dynamic hand gestures.
4) Step actively through Movement 4 and finish with deep breathing exercises to cool down.
pe-02128:
1) Walk left and right to an 8-count beat, lifting up on odd beats and lowering down on even beats.
2) Circle both arms smoothly as if turning a steering wheel while stepping.
3) Keep the same footwork while modifying arm movements to touch shoulders across the chest.
4) Combine both movements and repeat twice in sync with the music.
pe-02129:
1) Form a straight body line in a push-up position on the mat and hold for 10 seconds.
2) Turn to the side, supporting yourself on one hand with body straight for 10 seconds, then switch sides.
3) Face upward, press the floor with hands behind to lift hips into a straight reverse plank for 10 seconds.
4) Sit on the mat hugging knees, round your back, and roll back and forth smoothly.
pe-02130:
1) Each participant tears a sheet of newspaper along the grain into a single long strip to make a necklace.
2) Everyone wears their newspaper necklace and moves around the classroom.
3) Play rock-paper-scissors with opponents; the loser places their necklace onto the winner's neck.
4) Winners face each other until one finalist collects all necklaces to win the game.
pe-02131:
1) The whole class sits in a circle, closes their eyes, and bows their heads down to the floor.
2) The teacher secretly taps 5 students on the back to designate them as the Mafias (taggers).
3) Only the Mafias raise their heads upon command to identify each other, then bow down again.
4) 3 seconds after the whistle blows, the Mafias start tagging regular players, and tagged players go up to the stage.
pe-02132:
1) Stack fists alternately with a partner.
2) When the teacher calls 'Up', move only the bottom fist to the top, and when calling 'Down', move only the top fist to the bottom.
3) When the teacher calls 'Pot Lid', the player whose hand is below must cover the partner's top fist first to win.
4) When the teacher calls 'Gourd', the player whose hand is above must support the partner's bottom fist first to win.
pe-02133:
1) Select 3-4 taggers who start by wearing pinnies.
2) Runners can rest inside hula hoops placed on the ground when tired.
3) If another classmate arrives and yells 'Swap', the person inside must immediately step out.
4) A player cannot immediately re-enter the hoop they just exited, and if tagged by a chaser, they swap pinnies and become the tagger.
pe-02134:
1) Spread feet shoulder-width, step one foot slightly back, bend knees, flex wrists down, and extend arms into the basic underhand stance.
2) Move feet to the ball without locking hands beforehand, contact the ball on the forearms above the wrists, and lift using arms and legs together.
3) Form a finger triangle with thumbs and forefingers in front of the forehead, practicing tossing and catching the ball overhead.
4) Use the coordinated extension of knees, elbows, and wrists to push the ball upward into an overhead pass.
pe-02135:
1) Grip the handles together and perform figure-8 swings with footwork to the intro music.
2) Skip over the rope with recovery swing and single bounce variations.
3) Connect alternate-foot jumping, slow figure-8 side steps, and SSOO COCO steps.
4) Perform straddle jump, high knee jump, scissor jump variations, and finish with a front stop.
pe-02136:
1) Divide into 4 teams of 6 students and assign a captain for each team.
2) The captain stands at the rear without a blindfold to give verbal directions, while the 5 teammates wear blindfolds and place hands on shoulders.
3) Guided by the captain's verbal instructions, teammates maneuver through zigzag cones without knocking them over.
4) The team that clears the course without touching the obstacles faster than the opposing team wins.
pe-02137:
1) Set up 4 bases (Home, 1st, 2nd, 3rd) on a diamond-shaped field and divide into offense and defense.
2) Batters use their legs like bats to kick the ball.
3) Balls kicked outside the foul line are ruled foul balls.
4) There are no home runs; regardless of kicking distance, batters and baserunners can advance a maximum of 2 bases.
pe-02138:
1) Hold the ribbon stick and take a ready stance matching the music cue.
2) Circle the arm widely to create large loop motions.
3) Wave the ribbon up and down to form wavy lines and figure-eight patterns.
4) Connect zigzag movements, semicircles, and spiral whirls continuously along with the song.
pe-02139:
1) One 'tagger' stands at the front facing away, while the remaining students secretly choose one 'spy'.
2) The spy hides a small hand-held object behind their back.
3) While the tagger chants the phrase, students advance; when the tagger turns around, everyone freezes and conceals the object.
4) The tagger attempts to identify the spy; if unsuccessful, the tagger turns back to chant again while the spy secretly passes the object to another student.
pe-02140:
1) Place 10 balls at 20 cm intervals along the center line of the 2-meter start area on Line 4.
2) Place disc cones at 1-meter intervals from 5 meters to 15 meters past the first gate.
3) Use the stick to hit each ball, practicing passing cleanly through the first gate.
4) Aim to pass at least 8 out of 10 balls through the gate, controlling swing power so balls stop near targeted cones.
pe-02141:
1) Practice tossing DIY juggling balls filled with rice or socks, progressing from 1 to 3 balls.
2) Fold triangle ttakji using 2 sheets of A4 paper and hit a target ttakji 10 times to count flips.
3) Throw paper rings folded from A4 paper at targets such as egg cartons or stacking cups.
pe-02142:
1) Hit the ball placed on the tee bat into fair territory.
2) The batter runs to first base while fielders retrieve the batted ball and throw it to the base ahead of the runner.
3) A fly ball caught before touching the ground or a throw reaching the base before the runner results in an out.
4) Teams switch between offense and defense after all players take a turn at bat, scoring one point per home run.
pe-02143:
1) Divide into two teams, determine kicking and fielding via rock-paper-scissors, and set fielders at 1st, 2nd, 3rd base, home plate, 4 infielders, and 2 outfielders.
2) The kicking team lines up in order, kicks the ball from home plate, and runs to 1st base.
3) A batter is caught out (fly out) if a fly ball is caught, forced out if the ball reaches the base first, or tagged out if touched with the ball held in the fielder's hand.
4) Accumulating 3 foul balls results in 1 out; teams switch sides after 3 outs, playing 2 full innings where the team with more runs wins.
pe-02144:
1) Lay out a target scoring mat with numbered zones (10, 5, 3, 2 points) on the floor.
2) Determine the first thrower by rock-paper-scissors, then alternate sliding floor curling stones toward the mat.
3) Strategically position your stones in high-scoring zones or bump away opponent stones.
4) Sum up the points of all stones remaining on the scoring mat after the end; the higher total wins.
pe-02145:
1) Players holding the same colored spot markers form a team
2) Tagged players call out 'Save me!'
3) Teammates who are not out place their marker on the tagged player's hand to revive them
pe-02146:
1) Hold the play stick to practice balancing and dribble or hit balls on the ground.
2) Move forward while coordinating hands and feet to the rhythm in sports rhythm training.
3) Follow visual demonstrations starting with footwork, then gradually integrate arm movements.
pe-02148:
1) Line up 3 to 4 paper cups on the table to create target goals.
2) Place a coffee stick or pen flat on your palm.
3) Strike the edge of the stick upward with the other hand to flip it toward the cups.
4) Successfully land the sticks into the designated paper cups across multiple attempts.
pe-02149:
1) Form teams of four, running 3 to 5 teams depending on class conditions.
2) The attacking team calls out 'Omnikin [Color]' and hits the ball within 10 seconds.
3) The called defending team cooperates with all four players to catch the ball before it hits the floor.
4) The defending team positions themselves above, below, to the right, and to the left of the ball.
pe-02150:
1) Prepare 12 Speed Stacks cups in a 3-6-3 layout.
2) Upstack and downstack the 3-6-3 formation to the rhythm of the carol song.
3) Transition into upstacking and downstacking the 6-6 formation.
4) Complete the 1-10-1 stack and downstack back into the original 3-6-3 position.
pe-02151:
1) Set up gateball sticks, balls, 4 gates, and place a purple target ball in the center.
2) Team leaders play rock-paper-scissors to determine order of play.
3) Players take turns striking their designated ball with the gateball stick.
4) The team that first hits the purple center ball into any gate wins the game.
pe-02152:
1) Place a spot marker as the target jack in the center and designate team throwing zones.
2) Players from each team alternate sliding floor curling stones toward the target spot marker.
3) Score 1 point for each stone that is closer to the target marker than the opponent's closest stone.
4) Combine scores across all completed ends to determine the winning team.
pe-02153:
1) Stand in front of the vaulting box and place both hands on top of it.
2) Straighten your elbows, lean your upper body forward, and sit on top of the vaulting box.
3) Move both hands forward and lean forward to climb down over the box.
pe-02154:
1) Stand in front of the obstacle course consisting of an incline mat, a tunnel, and landing mats.
2) Get down on all fours with hands and knees on the mat facing the incline.
3) Crawl slowly up the incline and into the cylindrical tunnel by moving opposite arms and legs alternately.
4) After exiting the tunnel down the slope, shift your center of gravity backward to prevent tumbling forward.
pe-02155:
1) Two holders stretch the rubber band at varying heights from ankles, knees, hips, chest, head, to overhead.
2) Jumpers perform designated steps by stepping on, jumping over, or hooking the band to the rhythm of a song.
3) Successfully finishing the song sequence allows the jumper to advance to the next height.
4) If a jumper makes a mistake or touches the wrong line, they switch roles with a holder.
pe-02156:
1) Arrange 9 spot markers of the same color in a 3x3 grid and mark a starting line 10 steps away.
2) Divide students into 2 or 4 teams, lined up in single file, with the first 3 players each holding one beanbag.
3) On start, the first player runs and places a beanbag on a spot marker, runs back, tags the next player, and goes to the back.
4) The first 3 runners place beanbags on empty spots, and from the 4th runner onward, players move an already placed beanbag to complete a line of 3.
pe-02157:
1) Sit straight on a chair and prepare with upper-body and shoulder stretches.
2) Perform arm, chest, torso, and leg movements repeatedly according to the verbal cadence.
3) Take short rests between movements and continue for the set rounds.
4) Cool down with gentle finishing stretches while controlling your breath.
pe-02158:
1) [Beanbag Toss] Run to the spot marker, throw the beanbag into the hoop, loop around the cone, and pass the beanbag to the next runner.
2) If missed, retrieve and re-throw until it lands inside; the first team whose final runner finishes wins.
3) [Beanbag Golf] Take turns throwing at hoops; if missed, throw again from where it landed, racing to complete the 4th hoop first.
4) [Beanbag Race] Run on signal to retrieve one beanbag at a time to the team hoop; the team with the most beanbags within the time limit wins.
pe-02159:
1) Teammates hold hands in a long line facing forward.
2) Place 3 hula hoops next to the first player and a cone next to the last player.
3) On start, the first player steps through the hoop and maneuvers it across their body to the next player without letting go of hands.
4) Once the last player places the hoop over the cone, the first player sends the next hoop, and the first team to transfer all 3 hoops wins.
pe-02160:
1) Crumple a scarf, toss it overhead, and catch it on the way down with both hands or one hand.
2) Toss the scarf up, clap 1-3 times, and catch it or land it on an arm or instep.
3) Place scarves in a row on the floor at regular intervals by color.
4) Jump or hop on one foot along the path, stepping only on the scarves.
pe-02161:
1) Perform 4 double-hand swings to the intro music.
2) Execute 4 single bounces, 2 double bounces, 4 swing steps, and 2 open-cross jumps in order.
3) Perform open-close jumps, scissor-fist jumps, alternate foot jumps, and double swing steps during the chorus.
4) Finish with swing walks followed by front and cross stops.
pe-02162:
1) Fold two sheets of paper to make two ddakji tiles.
2) Practice striking directly at the center or the slightly lifted gap of the target tile on the floor.
3) Play rock-paper-scissors to decide the order, and place the loser's tile on the floor.
4) Take turns striking the target tile, and win by successfully flipping it over.
pe-02163:
1) The fielding team positions players at pitcher, catcher, bases, infield, and outfield, while the batting team waits at home plate in batting order.
2) The pitcher rolls the ball from the mound, and the kicker kicks it into an open area in the field.
3) The runner advances through 1st, 2nd, 3rd bases and scores 1 run upon reaching home plate before being thrown out.
4) Teams switch between offense and defense when 3 outs are made by fly-outs or ground-outs.
pe-02164:
1) Roll up socks tightly to create a softball-sized fistball.
2) Throw the sock ball against a wall and practice catching the rebound securely at chest height.
3) Practice accurate overhand throwing toward a target utilizing hip and body rotation.
4) Toss the ball slightly with one hand and strike it forward accurately using the flat inner part of the clenched fist.
pe-02165:
1) Construct a rubber band shooter using 3–4 wooden chopsticks and rubber bands.
2) Stand 5–6 paces back from the designated target in a stable aiming stance.
3) Align the sights with the target and pull the trigger handle to hit a large water bottle target.
4) Progressively advance difficulty by aiming at smaller targets like paper cups and pen-cap-sized markers.
pe-02166:
1) Make a bow and arrow using a wire hanger, rubber bands, and wooden chopsticks, padding the arrow tip.
2) Insert the arrow through the guide ring and nock it securely onto the rubber band string.
3) Extend the bow arm straight forward, align the arrow in a straight line, and release toward the target.
4) Advance difficulty from large targets down to landing the arrow inside a paper cup.
pe-02167:
1) The pitcher rolls the ball fast and accurately into the strike zone.
2) Fielders catch incoming balls with both hands hugging towards the chest.
3) Kickers place their non-kicking foot beside the ball, kick using inside/instep/outside foot, and sprint directly to first base.
pe-02168:
1) Both teams take turns sliding 5 curling stones each toward the target mat.
2) After all stones are played, calculate the points on the target mat.
3) The team with the higher score wins.
pe-02169:
1) Front Door Pass-through: Run into the turning rope as it swings downward from above and pass through without jumping.
2) Back Door Pass-through: Enter the rope as it swings upward from below, jump once, and exit smoothly.
3) Viking Game (Front Door): One runner enters, passes through to the other side and returns; progressively add runners (2, 3,
4) to pass through and back together.
4) Viking Game (Back Door): Starting with 1 player and adding one more each round, run into the upward swinging rope together, jump, and return successfully.
pe-02170:
1) Sit on a chair barefoot on a newspaper and perform 10-second toe curls and stretches.
2) Fold and roll the newspaper into a stick to tap and massage arms, legs, and soles.
3) Unfold the newspaper, tear it into strips by hand, then crumple, unfold, and tear it using bare feet.
4) Gather torn pieces, compress them firmly into a round ball, toss and catch, then throw into a basket.
pe-02171:
1) Align the foot so that the ball makes contact with the instep (shoelace area).
2) Place the non-kicking plant foot about two fists away from the ball and lean the chest and upper body forward to keep the ball down.
3) Practice kicking from a stationary position close to the ball first to ensure accurate contact with the instep.
4) As you improve, take 3 to 4 steps back to run up and shoot with power, or receive a ball passed by a partner and shoot.
pe-02172:
1) As the first movement, jump as high as possible in place while keeping heels off the ground.
2) As the second movement, perform the same jumping technique moving side to side.
3) As the third movement, jump back and forth.
4) As the fourth movement, spread and close the legs while jumping, and as the fifth movement, jump while turning around in place.
pe-02173:
1) Step 1: Raise hands by the head, step forward, and clap in coordination with foot steps.
2) Step 2: Raise one arm up and hold the other at shoulder level, then take quick footsteps (1-2-3-4) and place hands on hips.
3) Steps 3 & 4: Rotate palms outward from the waist and rotate wrists outward while extending arms in sync with steps.
4) Step 5: Pat clap-shoulder-hip in sequence, stamp feet, and connect all five patterns to musical rhythm.
pe-02174:
1) Form 4 groups of 8 students per class (32 total) and stand in line waiting for their turn.
2) The first group holds each rope of the bounce apparatus tautly.
3) When the teacher places the ball onto the center disc, bounce it above head height; if dropped, the next group immediately steps in to take over the ropes.
4) Sum up the total number of bounces across all groups to determine the ranking.
pe-02175:
1) Follow designated 4-minute cardio Tabata exercise routines along with the music and rhythm.
2) Write down the physiological benefits of cardiorespiratory endurance in study notes during class.
pe-02176:
1) Complete 3-6-3 cycle downstacking with jumbo stacks in Course 1.
2) Throw a flying disc into the hula hoop target in Course 2.
3) Jump rope 10 times in Course 3.
4) Kick a soccer ball into the goal in Course 4, run back, and hand over the vest to the next runner.
pe-02177:
1) Prepare 30 wooden pucks at the start bar of the board and determine the player order.
2) Slide the pucks along the board toward the 4 scoring compartments (1, 2, 3, and 4 points).
3) Retrieve pucks that failed to completely enter the scoring gates and replay them across 3 sub-rounds.
4) Earning one puck in each of the four compartments scores a 20-point strike; total points determine the winner.
pe-02178:
1) Four players per team take positions on a badminton court separated by a low net.
2) The rally begins with a serve, sending the soft foam ball over the net using hands or arms.
3) Teammates use underhand and overhead passes to keep the ball off the floor and return it across the net.
4) The team that scores 15 points first wins the set, and winning 2 out of 3 sets wins the match.
pe-02179:
1) Draw a Sabangchigi court on the ground and prepare flat throwing stones.
2) Toss a stone into the first square and hop through the court on one or two feet without touching the lines.
3) Reach the end section, turn around, pick up the stone on the return path, and hop out.
4) Proceed through consecutive numbered squares by tossing the stone to the next target area.
pe-02180:
1) Players line up at one end line and the tagger stands in the middle.
2) On signal, players dribble floorball balls across to the opposite line avoiding the tagger using short or long dribbles.
3) The tagger steals the ball and knocks it out of bounds, and any player who loses their ball joins the tagger team.
4) Remaining players repeat the crossing against all taggers until the final survivor wins.
pe-02181:
1) Prepare a juggling ball (or rolled socks, or a tennis ball).
2) Practice tossing the ball from one hand to the other in an arc.
3) Throw the ball up to eye level (at least 30 cm high) to get the feeling of catching it cleanly with both hands.
4) Repeat the toss-and-catch drill until you can comfortably make 50 consecutive catches without dropping.
pe-02182:
1) Practice the fundamental shooting form by pressing under the floorball and sweeping it forward with the blade face.
2) Keep the stick blade below waist level during the shot to prevent high-sticking penalties.
3) Apply free-hit rules when body obstruction or fouls occur, connecting passes and shots smoothly.
4) Practice aimed shots on goal and play mini floorball matches.
pe-02183:
1) Control the floorball using only the stick blade without tucking the ball between or behind your feet.
2) Shield the ball by turning your body so your body stays between the defender and the ball.
3) Play a 1-on-1 drill within a designated area trying to maintain possession against a defender.
pe-02185:
1) Review the textbook to identify the components of health-related fitness: cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition.
2) Understand the concept and purpose of the PAPS physical fitness assessment system.
3) Learn the specific measurement methods and guidelines for each fitness component including BMI.
4) Develop a step-by-step exercise plan (measure-plan-practice-verify) tailored to individual fitness levels.
pe-02186:
1) Two teams of 9 players take turns batting and fielding throughout the game.
2) The batter hits the ball and runs as far as possible toward first, second, and third base.
3) The batter is out if the ball reaches the base before the runner arrives, or if a fielder catches the fly ball directly in the air.
4) The offensive team scores 1 point when a runner safely circles all bases and returns home.
pe-02187:
1) Position infield defenders and outfield side attackers, marking movement routes with cones and floor markers.
2) Practice side attacks where the outfield attacker either throws directly after shifting sideways or makes a bounce pass to the infield.
3) Practice passing the ball, quickly moving along the sideline, receiving the return pass, and attacking.
4) Rotate defending and attacking partners sequentially by assigned numbers to repeat the drills.
pe-02188:
1) Divide into a tagger at the front and two teams along the lockers
2) Play rock-paper-scissors with the tagger; winners split legs forward
3) Those who tie or lose must touch fingertips to the floor for 3 seconds
4) When a player reaches the target desk line, they score a point for their team and return to the back of the line
pe-02189:
1) Arrange chairs equal to half the number of students in a circle with one team vest on each, dress one chair with a vest as a marker, and place a bell on a center desk.
2) Pairs play rock-paper-scissors where winners sit on chairs, one student sits at the desk as General Yi Sun-sin, and losers hold hands in front of the chairs.
3) Yi Sun-sin rings the bell once, players rotate singing Ganggangsullae, and when the bell rings again, they stop to face opponents aligned clockwise from the marked chair.
4) Facing pairs compete in three minigames using vests (sitting vest grab, standing vest grab, hand push game), and any student with 5 consecutive wins can challenge Yi Sun-sin.
pe-02190:
1) Fold an old textbook in half and tuck it into the pages to form a curved track.
2) Divide into two teams and align textbooks end-to-end in a line from the start to a paper cup on a chair.
3) The front player rolls a ping-pong ball; once it passes, players sprint to the end of the line to extend the track.
4) If the ball drops, pick it up from that spot and continue; the team that deposits the ball into the cup first wins.
pe-02191:
1) Scatter team bibs (1 per person) widely across the area, and have teams of 6-8 sit in circles holding hands at the start line.
2) The first runner stands inside the circle; on the signal, the entire team moves together holding hands toward the bibs.
3) The first runner picks up one bib and weaves zigzag through the connected teammates for one full lap.
4) The next runner enters the center to repeat; the first team whose members all collect bibs and return seated at the start line shouting 'Success' wins.
pe-02192:
1) Perform individual stretching from legs to upper body (short/long leg stretch, floor reach, arm and neck stretches) holding for at least 5 seconds.
2) Stand facing a partner, place hands on each other's shoulders, and lean upper bodies down to stretch shoulders and backs together.
3) Keep the lower body fixed and twist the torso to high-five the partner in sync with the teacher's whistle.
4) Start with feet together and play Rock-Paper-Scissors; the winner moves their front foot back, and the loser steps forward into a leg split.
pe-02193:
1) The human number team (wearing numbered bibs) plans positions and scatters across the field.
2) Challenge teams (3 teams of 7 students) gather at the starting line to discuss running strategies.
3) On signal, each challenge team runs together in a single file, touching the palms of human numbers to check their hidden numbers.
4) Once identified, the team must touch the human numbers in exact order from 1 to 7, sprint back across the start line, and shout "Success."
pe-02194:
1) Share attitudes of communication and cooperation among team members.
2) Select suitable cooperative activities such as zigzag relays, circle tags, or bounce ball games.
3) Allow sufficient practice time before games to understand the rules.
4) Chant counting voices together to complete the team missions.
pe-02195:
1) Connect desks in a row down the center of the classroom to serve as nets, dividing every 4 desks into a court (3 courts total).
2) Divide 4 to 6 group members across each desk court facing each other.
3) The server tosses the table tennis ball over the desk net, and the receiving side hits the underside of the ball with their open palm after one bounce.
4) Count aloud each successful volley until the ball is missed, and record the highest consecutive count achieved within 5 minutes.
pe-02196:
1) Form a circle of 6 students per team holding hands.
2) The first runner weaves zigzag in and out under the joined arms of teammates around the circle.
3) When the runner returns to their starting spot, the player to their right becomes the next runner.
4) The team whose members all finish running and sit down on the floor first wins.
pe-02197:
1) Sit comfortably at desks and lightly warm up the body.
2) Play rock-paper-scissors simultaneously with the teacher on call.
3) Students who tie or lose must mimic the teacher's dance movements as accurately as possible.
4) Students who win do not have to copy the movements and may rest.
pe-02198:
1) Divide into 4 teams of 5 to 7 students; 2 teams become challenge runners at the starting line, while 2 teams become human number teams seated on chairs in a circle.
2) The human number team secretly assigns numbers 1 through 6 among themselves.
3) On the start signal, challenge runners dash out and tag a seated student, who then displays their secret number using fingers.
4) Runners must find and tag the numbers in strict sequence from 1 to 6; incorrect numbers require running back to tag the next runner, and the team that brings all numbers 1-6 back hand-in-hand first wins.
pe-02199:
1) Reflect on the purpose of physical education by viewing examples of Usain Bolt and Park Ji-sung.
2) Learn to show consideration and avoid alienating others with excessive competitiveness during familiar sports.
3) Pledge to give full effort without giving up even in challenging activities.
4) Promise to participate together harmoniously and enjoyably as a class.
pe-02200:
1) Each student places 12 colored pencils on their desk and waits.
2) When the teacher rings the bell, students stand up one by one calling out consecutive numbers in order.
3) A student is eliminated if they stand up simultaneously with someone else, call the wrong number, or fail to stand before the end.
4) Eliminated students put one pencil into their pencil case, and the player with the most pencils left after multiple rounds wins.
pe-02201:
1) Prepare 10-14 long umbrellas found in the classroom.
2) Form teams of 5-7 players and stand in a circle holding an umbrella upright.
3) One teammate inside or leading the circle counts the beat (one, two, three).
4) Release your own umbrella so it stays balanced and quickly move sideways to catch the next umbrella on the beat.
5) Count successful catches without dropping an umbrella for 1 minute, and the team with the most wins takes the match.
pe-02202:
1) Align front and side rows upon the teacher's call, then sit down in sequence while shouting numbers (jumping variation optional).
2) To form two teams with equal gender ratio, play rock-paper-scissors with same-gender peers and split into winners and losers.
3) To form four teams, play round 1 of rock-paper-scissors, then winners (raising hand) play each other and losers (hands on head) play each other.
4) Divide into 4 teams based on 2 wins, 1 win 1 loss, and 2 losses, line up, and verify team numbers with squat calling.
pe-02203:
1) Divide into two teams with one team wearing vests, and determine each player's age by rock-paper-scissors: 1st (30 yrs/3 rubber bands), 2nd (20 yrs/2 bands), 3rd (10 yrs/1 band).
2) Teams start at opposite sides of the field and move to tag opponents upon the signal.
3) Teammates can join hands in groups of 1 to 3, combining their total ages.
4) When players tag each other, the side with lower total age surrenders 1 rubber band (10 yrs); reaching 0 bands requires 5 jumping jacks in the penalty zone to get 1 band back.
5) Sum the total number of outs for each team at the end; the team with fewer outs wins.
pe-02204:
1) Set up five wrestling stations in the classroom (knee wrestling, arm wrestling, thumb wrestling, palm push wrestling, seated foot push wrestling) and a rock-paper-scissors area.
2) All students gather in the rock-paper-scissors area and play rock-paper-scissors with same-gender peers.
3) The winner chooses a wrestling station and takes the partner there to compete.
4) The winner receives 2 points and the loser receives 1 point, then both return to the rock-paper-scissors area to find new opponents until the highest scorer wins.
pe-02205:
1) Form a team of 5 to 7 students standing in a circle with 1 ball.
2) One player tosses the ball into the center to bounce once, starting the rally.
3) Players hit the underside of the ball with their open palm so it bounces once inside the circle for teammates to hit.
4) Count the consecutive number of successful one-bounces until the ball bounces twice or hits an obstacle, aiming for the highest record.
pe-02206:
1) Cluster desks into group islands ensuring clear walkways, and place 2 revival team vests on top of the desks.
2) Five throwers wear vests and roll 2 balls along the floor aiming at the runners' ankles.
3) A runner whose ankle is hit is out and must sit on a nearby desk.
4) Active runners hand a revival vest to an eliminated player; if that eliminated player throws the vest and hits an attacker, they revive, and teams count total outs over 5 minutes.
pe-02207:
1) Draw the bowstring to shoot 3 arrows at the target and calculate the sum of scores hit.
2) Strike the opponent's ttakji on the floor with one's own ttakji to flip it over for the win.
pe-02208:
1) Two partners stand side by side, each holding one handle of the jump rope with their outside hand.
2) Turn the rope together in sync and jump over the rope using a two-bounce jump.
3) Practice jumping while alternating feet to maintain a steady shared rhythm.
4) Progress into advanced variations such as one jumping, alternating every 4 jumps, continuous alternating jumps, and turns.
pe-02209:
1) Grip the disc with the thumb on the labeled top surface, index finger on the rim, and remaining three fingers supporting underneath.
2) Stand sideways with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the disc at shoulder height.
3) Stand at the marker cone and throw towards the disc catcher on the count of one, two, three.
4) Practice short-range putting into the basket 10 times per player.
pe-02210:
1) Hang a large target banner on the goal net and set a shooting line at a fixed distance.
2) Participants take turns taking 5 shots each toward the target.
3) Record and sum up the points based on which scoring ring the ball hits.
4) The player with the highest total score after 5 rounds wins.
pe-02211:
1) Two teams stand facing each other in parallel lines
2) The first runners of both teams sprint to the center and play rock-paper-scissors
3) The winner walks to the back of the line, while the loser runs a lap around their team line back to the front
4) The losing runner continues running laps until they win, and the first team where all members finish wins
pe-02212:
1) Set up starting lines and mark zones 1 through 3 with cones for each team.
2) Runner 1 carries disc cones one at a time and places them at zones 1 through 3, completing 3 round trips.
3) Runner 2 runs out and collects the disc cones one by one back to the start, completing 3 round trips.
4) Subsequent runners alternate between placing and retrieving cones until the final runner finishes.
pe-02213:
1) Set up nine cones in a 3-by-3 grid.
2) Both teams line up in single file, and the first three runners hold team vests at the starting line.
3) The first runner sprints out and places a team vest over one cone, then runs back.
4) From the fourth runner onward, players move an existing team vest to an empty cone, and the team that completes a straight line first wins.
pe-02214:
1) Students form a wide circle around a tagger in the center.
2) Outside players pass the ball with their feet to keep it away from the tagger.
3) The tagger must intercept the rolling ball using only their feet without using hands.
4) When the tagger intercepts the ball, the player who made the last pass becomes the new tagger.
pe-02215:
1) Set up spot markers on the floor in a long U-shape path.
2) Both teams line up at opposite ends, and the first runners hop across the markers toward each other.
3) When they meet, they play rock-paper-scissors; the winner keeps moving forward while the loser's team sends the next runner.
4) The team whose runner successfully reaches the opponent's starting line wins the game.
pe-02216:
1) The first runner of each team holds two fun sticks and places a ball on the floor.
2) At the starting signal, guide the ball between the two fun sticks around the cone and back to the starting line.
3) Hand over the fun sticks to the next runner upon returning.
4) The team whose final runner finishes first wins.
pe-02217:
1) Crumple a sheet of A4 paper and unfold it onto your head like a hat.
2) Maintain balance while blowing to knock off opponents' paper hats.
3) Protect your own paper hat and do not stay in one spot for more than 3 seconds.
4) Players whose paper falls off must sit in place as obstacles; the last remaining player wins.
pe-02218:
1) Form two teams facing each other behind starting lines.
2) Roll the dice, and when a team's color appears, that team chases to tag while the other team runs toward the cones.
3) Any player tagged before grabbing a cone is eliminated from the playing area.
4) The game can also be played with a rule variation where tagged opponents join the chasing team.
pe-02219:
1) Divide into two teams and play rock-paper-scissors.
2) The winner sprints toward the ball while the loser sprints toward the cone.
3) The player with the ball scores by throwing and hitting the opponent before they return to the starting line.
4) The runner scores by dodging the ball or successfully carrying the cone back to the starting line.
pe-02220:
1) Teams decide a playing order, designating riders to sit on rolling chairs and pushers.
2) From behind the baseline, pushers glide the seated teammate across the floor toward the target line.
3) The team stopping closest and most accurately to the target line wins the round.
4) Rotate roles each round so every student gets a chance to sit and push.
pe-02221:
1) The fielding team disperses across the field while the kicking team kicks in order.
2) A foul is called if the ball lands outside or too short; three fouls result in an out.
3) If a fly ball is caught directly, the kicker is out and runners cannot advance.
4) On ground balls, runners are out if the ball beats them to the base, and safe if they beat the ball.
5) When a runner from third touches home base, 1 point is scored; teams switch sides after all kickers complete their turn.
pe-02222:
1) Grip the ball with the index and middle fingers slightly spread on top, keeping it off the palm.
2) Practice wrist action by flicking the ball upward toward the target direction to feel finger release.
3) Kneel down, rotate the torso, raise the elbow, and release the ball with the fingers facing the target.
4) Stand up, step the front foot toward the target, and throw by sequentially transferring power from the torso, shoulder, elbow, wrist, and fingers.
pe-02223:
1) Put the glove on the non-throwing hand and squeeze fingers to close the glove when the ball enters.
2) For ground balls, spread feet wider than shoulder-width, lower the body, catch in front of the toes, and cover with the right hand.
3) For fly balls, raise the glove and catch slightly to the left of the face, supporting the side of the glove with the right hand.
4) Practice playing catch with grounders and fly balls in pairs facing each other, or throw against a wall to catch rebounds.
pe-02224:
1) Perform wrist stretching and ankle rotations alternately on both sides in place.
2) Place hands on hips and rotate neck and shoulders in sequence.
3) Perform torso/waist twists and knee rotations to loosen up the joints.
4) Do leg stretches (narrow/wide), arm and shoulder stretches, hip joint stretches, and finish with jumping jacks.
pe-02225:
1) Set up the height-adjustable batting tee at home plate and place a T-ball on top.
2) Select an appropriately sized bat and wear the glove on the non-throwing hand.
3) Place rubber bases at 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and home plates.
4) Learn the scoring and out mechanics by having batters run bases while fielders attempt to touch bases with the ball.
pe-02226:
1) The batter hits the ball off the tee and advances only one base; when the ball lands fair, all runners advance one base.
2) Fielders catch the ball and tag or step on the base while holding the ball before the runner arrives to record an out.
3) Three strikes (including three fouls or hitting the tee) results in an out; a runner crossing home plate scores 1 point.
4) Teams switch between offense and defense after every player bats once, and remaining base runners stay on base for the next inning.
pe-02227:
1) Batters hit inside the batting circle and run the bases, advancing up to a maximum of a double (except the final 10th batter who has no limit).
2) Runners must keep their foot on base until contact is made and cannot deviate beyond the 3-foot running lane.
3) Fielders get outs by stepping on the base while holding the ball, tagging the runner, or catching a fly ball (forcing runners to tag up).
4) Three strikes result in an out, and teams rotate through 10-player rosters balanced with boys and girls per half-inning.
pe-02228:
1) Divide the class into two teams and designate a catcher with a basket on the head.
2) Start holding a rubber shoe and put it on at the shooting line.
3) Shoot the rubber shoe over the elastic cord obstacle into the catcher's basket.
4) The catcher catches it inside the defense line, and the shooter returns to high-five the next runner.
pe-02229:
1) Determine the player order through rock-paper-scissors with the last player becoming 'it'.
2) The first-place winner decides and gives a mission type such as Wangdaepo, Picnic, or Teacher Says.
3) The remaining players sequentially give commands of that type and 'it' follows them.
4) When 'it' completes all commanded actions, 'it' is freed and the next round begins.
pe-02230:
1) Form groups of 4 and designate animal tiers using colored vests or paper.
2) Players only chase animals that are stronger than themselves.
3) After tagging, play rock-paper-scissors (muk-jji-ppa); if the weaker animal wins, they swap vests.
4) If the stronger animal wins, count to ten before pursuing again; the group with the tiger scores 1 point at round end.
pe-02231:
1) Set up speed ladders, zigzag cones, and hurdles in order, and have the anchor wear a team vest.
2) On signal, all team members start in single file and navigate through the three obstacles.
3) Record the number of laps completed by the anchor in 3 minutes (1 point per lap, plus 0.5 points for over half a lap).
4) A 0.1-point penalty is given for each infraction such as stepping on ladder rungs or touching obstacles.
pe-02232:
1) Set up a rectangular playing area with cones and place hula hoops (energy refill station and star zone) at the end.
2) Divide players into offense and defense teams, placing offensive players along both sides outside the rectangle and defenders at the start line.
3) If hit by a ball (comet) rolled by the offense, defenders go to the refill station to recharge before returning to the start.
4) Defenders who cross the court collect a small marker and return to the start, switching roles after a set time.
pe-02233:
1) Arrange hula hoops in a 3x3 or 5x5 grid on the floor.
2) Divide into two teams and line up behind the starting line.
3) Each runner carries a team vest, sprints to place it inside a hoop, and returns to tag the next runner.
4) Vests must be placed neatly without throwing, and players can move placed vests until one team completes a line to win.
pe-02234:
1) Two players face each other, wrapping a thick rope around their waists in an S-shape to distribute force.
2) Hold the rope with one hand at the front of the abdomen and use the other hand behind the waist to grip firmly.
3) When the referee raises the flag, pull or release the rope; if an opponent's planted foot moves, score 1 point.
4) Switch sides and compete in a best-of-three match; if tied 1-1, continue in the same spots without switching.
pe-02235:
1) Draw a circular game court with marked paths and designated lanes on the playground ground.
2) Choose one tagger ("tiger") via rock-paper-scissors, who counts to 10 before chasing others.
3) All players must only move along the marked lines; if an evader enters the tiger's exclusive path, they become the tiger.
4) Both the tiger and evaders must stay strictly on their paths; tags made while the tiger is off-line do not count.
pe-02236:
1) Set up only a home base on the field and divide players into kicking and fielding teams.
2) The kicker places the ball on home base, kicks it, and runs around their own team members for a set number of laps instead of running bases.
3) The fielding team lines up behind the player who caught the ball and passes it backward between their legs (tunnel).
4) The last fielder grabs the ball and sprints to touch home base; if they reach it before the runner finishes the laps, the kicker is out.
pe-02237:
1) Ready at center 0 of a cross hop mat (or line tape grid) with 50cm squares.
2) On signal, perform two-foot jumps in the sequence 0-1-0-2-0-3-0-4 to complete one cycle.
3) Jump for 20 seconds per person, scoring points for completed cycles and additional successful steps (1 point each).
4) A 1-point penalty is deducted each time a line is stepped on or the order is broken, and team scores are totaled.
pe-02238:
1) Attach labels for Do, Gae, Geol, Yut, and Mo onto cones and space them out at a distance.
2) Prepare one set of large Yut sticks for each team.
3) Throw the Yut sticks upon the teacher's signal and check the resulting cast.
4) Run around the cone marker matching the cast result and return to the finish line first to win.
pe-02239:
1) Form a circle around one central player, and assign numbers starting from 1 to all surrounding players.
2) The central player tosses the ball high into the air and calls out a number.
3) The player with the called number runs to the center to catch the ball.
4) If caught, that player moves to the center to toss next; if missed, the previous thrower tosses again and calls another number.
pe-02240:
1) Select one tagger while the remaining players step inside a circle drawn appropriately according to the group size.
2) Players inside the circle push each other using their backs chanting "Yeongcha-yeongcha".
3) The tagger runs around the perimeter of the circle attempting to tag players in the center.
4) Anyone pushed out of the circle or tagged joins the tagger's team, continuing until only 1 final survivor remains.
pe-02241:
1) Mark a spiral snail track on the ground with cones, and the defending team enters in single file.
2) The attacking team on the outside cannot throw the ball in the air and must roll it along the ground.
3) Defenders dodge rolling balls along the track without overtaking teammates or stepping on boundary lines.
4) Any defender hit by the ball is eliminated; once all defenders are out, the teams switch roles.
pe-02242:
1) Divide players into two teams across a net using modified volleyball rules.
2) The ball must be sent over the net within 3 touches, and the same player cannot touch it twice in a row.
3) One bounce on the floor is allowed per side, and players cannot touch the net during play.
4) Players may step outside boundaries to hit the ball, and service lines are moved forward due to ball weight.
pe-02243:
1) Divide into two mixed teams with each player having one ball, and mark two concentric circles on the floor.
2) Player 1 of Team A rolls a ball from behind the target line aiming for the inner circle.
3) Scoring 1 point if the ball stops inside the inner circle; leave it in place if in the outer circle, or retrieve it if outside.
4) Team B takes turns rolling to land in the inner circle or knock out Team A's balls for points, highest total wins.
pe-02244:
1) Divide into groups of 4 to 6 players and draw a circle approximately 6 meters in diameter on the floor.
2) Teammates face inward in a circle and link arms over each other's shoulders tightly.
3) Both groups lock shoulders together in the center of the ring and begin on the whistle.
4) Push the entire opposing group out of the circle or force them down to win.
pe-02245:
1) Draw a segmented court on the field marking "Sky" (start), "Earth" (goal), and defense zones in between.
2) The defending team stands in designated middle lanes to block attackers from reaching Earth or returning to Sky.
3) The attacking team starts from Sky, dodges defenders to reach Earth, and then runs back toward Sky.
4) Defenders tag attackers within defense zones to send them back to Sky; the team with the most successful round-trips wins.
pe-02246:
1) Divide into two groups; two turners rotate a long jump rope while others sing and prepare.
2) One player from each group enters the turning rope and plays rock-paper-scissors while jumping.
3) The winner remains inside jumping, while the loser exits the rope.
4) The next player from the losing team enters to challenge the winner, and the team with the last surviving jumper wins.
pe-02247:
1) Divide around 10 players into two equal teams across a net.
2) Start play by serving the flying disc from behind the boundary line service zone.
3) Catch and throw the disc without letting it touch the floor, passing it across the net within a maximum of 3 throws.
4) Players can move freely around the court, but cannot run while holding the flying disc.
5) Play a best-of-3 sets match to 11 points, applying deuce rules at a 10-10 tie.
pe-02248:
1) Form two co-ed teams with male and female students.
