 4) The team relay has a 99-second time limit, and upon failure, players restart from stage 1 or the failed stage.
pe-06550:
1) Form teams of four, with each pair facing each other side-to-side behind the starting line.
 2) One tosses the ball while the other receives with an underhand pass, moving toward the turning point using side steps.
 3) Place the ball into the ball cart (or box) located at the turning point.
 4) Return to the starting line using side steps and tag the next pair.
 5) The first team whose four members all finish wins.
pe-06551:
1) Three students each hold a hula hoop and stand in a circle to form a formation.
 2) The remaining students move freely outside the hula hoop circle.
 3) When music plays, the three hoop holders rotate left or right while maintaining the formation.
 4) Outside players move around the perimeter.
 5) When the music stops and the hoop formation halts, outside players rush to grab the object placed in the center.
 6) The first person to grab the object earns a point.
pe-06552:
1) Place a ball at each corner of the pickleball court.
 2) The participant stands at the center of the baseline.
 3) On the whistle signal, sprint quickly to each corner to retrieve the balls one by one.
 4) Successfully complete the drill by gathering all balls back to the baseline center.
pe-06553:
1) Teams assign runners and judges, setting up a turning cone at a 20-meter distance.
 2) Round 1 is a slow-running challenge where runners run as slowly as possible without walking, while opponent judges add a 1-second penalty for each walking violation.
 3) Round 1 increases team size from 2 to 4 runners, and the team with the longest time wins.
 4) Round 2 is a fast sprint challenge where runners sprint around the 20m cone on the start signal without false starts.
 5) Round 2 increases from 1 to 4 runners, and the team with the fastest time wins.
 6) Both rounds are combined to determine the final winner.
pe-06554:
1) Form three teams of 3; attacking teams stay in zones A and B, while defenders position between zones.
 2) Attackers circulate passes within their zone and switch play to the opposite zone when space opens.
 3) Up to two defenders enter a zone to press and intercept, switching roles with the attackers upon winning the ball.
 4) For high pressing, 5 defenders build up from the goalkeeper while 4 attackers press to intercept and score.
pe-06555:
1) Two teams stand facing each other across parallel lines 14m apart, with teammates stepping aside except the thrower.
 2) The attacking thrower throws the disc strongly without crossing the foul line and within the receiving zone.
 3) The defending team must catch it with only one hand (bobbling permitted); dropping, using two hands, or ground contact yields a point to the opponent, switching courts every 11 total points until one reaches 21 points.
pe-06556:
1) Each team consists of 7 players, with one designated as the goalkeeper.
 2) Players take turns 1-on-1 against the goalkeeper from the 7m penalty line.
 3) Keeping one pivot foot grounded, each team takes 7 shots following the referee's whistle, and the team with the most goals wins.
pe-06557:
1) Crumple scrap paper and wrap it with tape to create a round footvolley ball.
 2) Students stand in pairs, a zigzag, or a circle and pass the ball to each other without letting it bounce.
 3) Use various body parts like inside foot, instep, or head to keep the rally going, with the last player directing it into a trash can.
pe-06558:
1) Kick a footvolley ball directly against a flat wall using the inside of your dominant foot continuously.
 2) Progressively advance by alternating feet, using inside/outside foot, or juggling 1-2 times between wall rebounds.
 3) In pairs, set a boundary cone to exchange wall passes or hold hands while alternating toss and wall strikes.
pe-06559:
1) Warm up with lower-body stretching, back steps, and side steps using balls and cones.
 2) Perform alphabet step drills moving along A, X, and Z paths through nine cones in a low athletic stance.
 3) Play a 1-on-1 mirror game matching the runner's fakes and sprinting to touch them before the finish.
 4) Practice 2-on-1 triangle defense stopping an attacker from escaping the area within 8 seconds.
 5) Drill pass interceptions and finish with a 4-on-2 zone defense game divided into three zones.
pe-06560:
1) Discuss sportsmanship cases, define team core values, and design team jerseys on worksheets.
 2) Participate in a 10-question team basketball true-or-false quiz covering history and rules.
 3) Create paper cup rims and bounce table tennis balls off classroom desks and chairs in a trick shot challenge.
 4) Play the 'Cooperative Zero Foul' game in circles of five by shouting numbers while raising hands.
 5) Shoot two free throws into a central box whenever a team commits five fouls.
pe-06561:
1) Warm up with wrist stretches and a relay carrying a shuttlecock on a racket around cones.
 2) Complete the individual drill bouncing the shuttlecock upward 5 consecutive times on the racket.
 3) In groups of three facing across the net, rally using underhand strokes until the sixth person catches it.
 4) Rally 20 consecutive underhand strokes in a circle around a hula hoop in teams of four.
 5) Play a 60-second game hitting underhand shots from designated distances to be caught in a basket.
pe-06562:
1) Three to five students lie in a line on their backs in a leg raise position
 2) On the start signal the first student lifts and passes the ball with both legs to the next person
 3) The receiver catches the ball with their legs and passes it along and the team succeeds when the ball reaches the last person and returns to the first
pe-06563:
1) In the individual challenge, memorize a play card for 5 seconds and draw it within 15 seconds or explain it to teammates within 25 seconds.
 2) In the team challenge, form a team of 5 where the quarterback calls the play and teammates execute it to make a catch within 25 seconds.
 3) In the essential skills, check the line of scrimmage, deliver quarterback signals, and maintain a 7-yard defensive distance to prevent penalties.
 4) In the play-guessing game, Team A executes 3 plays while the opposing team identifies the plays to score points.
pe-06564:
1) Warm up by tossing and catching alternating hands with 2 balls and tossing 2 balls simultaneously to catch with both hands.
 2) Master the 2-ball claw catch from above, followed by consecutive catches in the 3-ball basic and 3-ball claw.
 3) Pair up, raise arms to shoulder height, and pass balls beneath the arms in the elephant juggling challenge within 5 minutes.
 4) Complete a 2-ball juggle speed challenge with shoulders locked in pairs and a cooperative relay around obstacles.
pe-06565:
1) Drop the ball from a 10-15 cm height on a half table and use backhand and forehand push shots to hit targets across the net.
 2) Use push shots to land table tennis balls into an egg carton to complete a bingo line.
 3) Maintain a 10-shot continuous push rally with a partner or complete a sequential push relay with 3-4 players.
 4) Compete in a two-racket match holding a paddle in each hand to reach 11 points first.
pe-06566:
1) Warm up with Ice Cream Cone Battle by balancing a basketball upside down on a cone.
 2) Lift the ball off the floor using only dribbling, complete 10 alternating dribbles, and travel to designated lines in set dribble counts (3, 6, 10).
 3) Dribble two balls simultaneously with a partner and play a dribble tag rock-paper-scissors game.
 4) Protect your own bounce while knocking away opponents' balls in individual and team dribble survival games.
pe-06567:
1) Form teams of 3 with red or blue stones, while other players assist by collecting stones outside.
 2) Scatter the target stones clustered in the center with a strong push to start.
 3) Take turns pushing the cue stone in the center to hit your team's stones.
 4) A point is scored when a propelled team stone enters a pocket marked by cones.
 5) Pushing a stone out of bounds yields the turn, and the team pocketing all 3 stones first wins the set (best of 3).
pe-06568:
1) Teams of 2 play a 2v2 doubles match using one shuttlecock per court.
 2) The game is played to 20 points, with a forbidden technique designated for every 5-point block.
 3) Using a restricted shot in that score bracket awards an immediate point to the opponent.
 4) Strategize using allowed shots, such as sending deep clears and finishing with pushes when smashes are banned.
 5) The first team to reach 20 points while adhering to all restrictions wins.
pe-06569:
1) Scatter cup sets across the area and divide the class into two equal teams.
 2) One team is designated as the Up-stacking team, and the other as the Down-stacking team.
 3) On signal, the Up-stack team builds 6-6 pyramids while the Down-stack team collapses them for 3 minutes.
 4) Cups must be stacked or unstacked into proper 6-6 shapes without throwing them.
 5) When 3 minutes expire, count the completed up-stacks and down-stacks to determine the winning team.
pe-06570:
1) Form 3-player teams with bibs and play a fast-paced 3v3 king-of-the-court format.
 2) The offense starts at the top of the key in a low triple threat stance holding the ball.
 3) The offense gets one scoring attempt; make it to score and rotate out, or miss and become defense.
 4) Successfully defending moves the team to the waiting line, while failing defense requires staying on defense.
 5) The first team to reach 5 points wins the match.
pe-06571:
1) Form 3-player teams, decide first server by rock-paper-scissors, and line up on opposite sides.
 2) Determine the serving order among the three teammates in advance.
 3) The starting team serves in order while the receiving team returns; a valid serve gains 1 point while an error loses 1 point.
 4) After the first team completes all serves, switch roles so the other team serves.
 5) The first team to reach 11 points without deuce wins the set, rotating order in the next set.
pe-06572:
1) Set cones at the four corners; a player dribbles around the opponent's cone to score.
 2) Draw three 2-meter circles; after at least 3 passes, successfully pass to a teammate with both feet inside a circle to score.
 3) One team uses one wide combined goal while the other attacks two separated goals; switch sides after a 5-minute half.
pe-06573:
1) Face each other slightly apart and practice tossing and catching two juggling balls.
 2) Stand side-by-side with arms around each other's shoulders and pass one ball back and forth 3 times per hand.
 3) Hold one ball each while shoulder-to-shoulder and exchange them simultaneously in an arc.
 4) One person holds two balls and the other holds one to complete full 3-ball partner juggling.
pe-06574:
1) Designate 1-2 taggers, and the remaining students become survivors.
 2) Taggers may only move using the specific step called out by the leader to catch survivors.
 3) Survivors must also flee using only the same specified step.
 4) Tagged survivors freeze in place and can be unfrozen when touched by another survivor.
 5) If all survivors are caught within the 3-minute limit, the tagger team wins.
pe-06575:
1) Face a square target area (such as a table tennis table) holding a badminton racket with a forehand grip.
 2) Bend your knees to maintain a low stance.
 3) Keep the racket face strictly vertical and hit the shuttlecock hard and straight forward.
 4) Successfully hit the target area at least 2 out of 5 times to complete the mission.
pe-06576:
1) Start with players positioned at home plate, first base, and second base.
 2) The player at home throws the ball to first base and runs to the open third base.
 3) The first base player throws to second base and runs to home, while the second base player throws to third base and runs to first base.
 4) The team that touches home plate the most times within the designated time wins.
pe-06577:
1) Divide players into teams of 5 to 6 to form offense and defense.
 2) The offense receives a pass from a defender and dribbles 10m toward the goal to shoot.
 3) The defense starts 5m behind and chases only the player they passed to.
 4) Scoring without a goalkeeper earns 1 point, while rule violations like double dribble forfeit the turn.
 5) Each team member attacks twice, and the team with the higher total score wins.
pe-06578:
1) Set up desks and one cup set on both sides across a 20m distance.
 2) Sprint to the opposite side on the start signal and begin cycle stacking.
 3) Complete stacking before a multiple of 3 is called after numbers 1 and 2, then sprint back when the multiple of 3 sounds.
 4) A player is eliminated if they fail to start within 1 second of the call or commit a stacking fault.
 5) Repeat the rounds until the last remaining player wins.
pe-06579:
1) Assign 3 to 4 players per court for variations like sitting badminton or 4v4 position matches.
 2) Waiting players line up outside and practice shuttlecock lifting inside hula hoops.
 3) Any player who accumulates 2 personal errors leaves the court and joins the back of the queue.
 4) The next waiting player at the front enters the court to continue the game.
pe-06580:
1) Make a 3x3 bingo grid using tape 10 to 15 meters away from the starting line.
 2) On the starting signal, the first runner of each team carries a team cone to the grid, places it in a chosen square, returns, and tags the next runner.
 3) Once all cones are placed, runners move existing cones to complete a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line first.
pe-06581:
1) Face your partner and take turns throwing and catching a beanbag from top to bottom using alternating hands.
 2) Practice cross-catch throws where the throwing hand matches the catching hand.
 3) Aim to succeed at least 6 consecutive times in both missions.
pe-06582:
1) The first runner crosses the incoming long rope to the opposite side as it rises.
 2) Pick up the ball, place it on the cone toward the team's side, and jump over the turning rope to return.
 3) Subsequent runners repeat in order, and the team that successfully moves the ball to the final cone first wins.
pe-06583:
1) Form pairs and face each other.
 2) The partner calls out the required number of touches (e.g., three times).
 3) The receiver touches the balloon exactly that many times using hands, calls out the number, and passes it back.
pe-06584:
1) Take a 10-minute theory class to understand the physical and mental benefits of walking.
 2) Move to the sports field and walk for 30 minutes while practicing the ten key posture points.
 3) Accumulate walking distance and receive individual posture feedback.
pe-06585:
1) Master four basic travel steps: chassé, shuffle, weave, and jazz box on beat.
 2) Pair up and mirror each other's steps while turning 90 degrees.
 3) Freely combine the steps to music, add arm movements, and return to the starting position.
pe-06586:
1) The offensive team lines up in the corner and the defensive team stands at the free throw line, each holding a basketball.
 2) On signal, the offensive runner dribbles around the half court while the defense shoots free throws.
 3) Points are scored based on how many runners complete the course before all defenders make their shots.
pe-06587:
1) Hang a mat or tarp across the net to block the opponent's view.
 2) In pairs, one defender stands in the court center while the attacker drops 10 shuttlecocks to various spots from the opposite side.
 3) The defender must read the flight, move with footwork, and successfully hit back at least 5 shots.
pe-06588:
1) Place multiple paper cups evenly along the edge of the table tennis table.
 2) Hit the table tennis ball with a paddle to knock down the cups on the opposite side.
 3) The team that knocks down the most cups in 1 minute wins.
pe-06589:
1) Determine offense and defense by rock-paper-scissors, placing the offensive team in the outfield and the defensive team in the infield.
 2) On the starting signal, the offensive team attacks by sliding 2 flying discs along the floor.
 3) Infielders jump to dodge the discs, getting eliminated if hit on the foot; when an infielder stops a disc with their foot, 1 eliminated teammate returns.
pe-06590:
1) Learn 10 basic jump moves, divide into teams, and move forward in groups of three in time with music.
 2) Accurately perform the jump movements indicated on the signs randomly raised by the opposing team.
 3) The team that completes the most correct jump moves without making a mistake wins.
pe-06591:
1) Divide participants into two or three teams and line up to decide the turn order.
 2) The first runner draws a card from the deck, performs the indicated jump (T jump, tuck jump, spread eagle jump, or free jump), or calls pass and tags the next runner.
 3) If successful, place the card beside and the next runner performs the accumulated jumps first before adding the newly drawn jump to build combos; the team with the most combos within time or the first to finish 4 combos wins.
pe-06592:
1) Form a team of 4 and set up three zones on the court: 3-6m (1 pt), 6-9m (2 pts), and 9-12m (4 pts).
 2) Toss the jokgu ball by hand and serve it using the inside of the foot into the target zones.
 3) Each player gets 2 attempts for a total of 8 attempts per team, successfully clearing the challenge if the team score exceeds 6 points.
pe-06593:
1) Place one table tennis table horizontally, connect another tabletop panel to the center to form a T-shape, and install the net.
 2) Three players face each other 2 against 1, and the two-player team coordinates their hitting order.
 3) Decide serve by rock-paper-scissors, start with the winner's serve, and the first team to reach 11 points without deuce wins.
pe-06594:
1) Two players face each other at the table, greet, and decide the first serve with rock-paper-scissors.
 2) The server stands on the backhand side and alternates shots between the opponent's forehand and backhand sides once each.
 3) The receiver must only return the ball to the server's backhand side; breaking the rule results in a loss of point, and the first to reach 11 points without deuce wins.
pe-06595:
1) Write self-introductions on A4 paper, collect them folded, and take turns randomly introducing each other.
 2) Form teams of 7 to 8 students and sit in a straight line on chairs.
 3) On signal, pass the ball backward from the front person overhead, sideways, or between legs.
 4) When the ball returns from the back to the front person, shoot into the portable hoop.
 5) Once a shot is made, team members shift forward by one seat to continue, and the team that returns to original spots first wins.
pe-06596:
1) Face your partner and perform cross side steps by moving left together, meeting in the middle, and moving right.
 2) Perform jumping jacks and in-place walking alternately to loosen leg muscles.
 3) Hold hands facing each other and lean back slightly to perform partner squats together.
 4) One person holds a crunch position while the partner lies down, holds the partner's ankles, and performs leg raises.
 5) One person performs a glute bridge while the partner grips their knees to perform dips simultaneously.
pe-06597:
1) Warm up by tossing and catching two balls with one hand.
 2) Each player holds two balls; play rock-paper-scissors and the winner tosses a ball to the other person, who catches it and juggles for three cycles to earn 1 point.
 3) Juggle three balls and toss one into a designated bucket, then place the remaining two balls in one by one to score within the time limit.
 4) Receive a tossed ball while holding two balls, juggle three balls, and toss one accurately back to the partner without dropping.
pe-06598:
1) Warm up with a circle jumping game and practice timed ball-handling challenges step by step.
 2) Perform partner ball-handling drills and a ball-handling mafia game to find the secret leader.
 3) Learn the pivot technique keeping one foot planted and play a 3-round 1-on-1 battle after rock-paper-scissors.
pe-06599:
1) Warm up with the Go-Back Jump game and complete individual agility and cone-touch reaction drills.
 2) Practice cut-and-catch routines and team running passes across end zones with minimal passes.
 3) Play a 5-on-5 modified ultimate game where players enter the end zone one by one in designated order.
pe-06600:
1) Clear the reaction drill by weaving hands around a bouncing ping pong ball on a desk or floor at least 10 times with a partner.
 2) Catch falling balls dropped by a partner, trap balls into a cup after designated bounces, and toss a ball off an inverted cup to catch it no-bounce.
 3) Stand in a team relay line and throw two ping pong balls each to land at least five into cups or cones.
pe-06601:
1) Form a circle with 5 to 6 students and hold hands tightly with neighboring teammates.
 2) Coordinate cues and lie back down together, then sit up simultaneously for 20 seconds.
 3) Complete at least 10 group sit-ups without breaking the shared rhythm.
pe-06602:
1) Students form a circle placing a cone in front and a table tennis racket 3 meters behind them.
 2) A 'tagger' wears a vest and closes eyes while a hidden leader is chosen to perform strokes and referee signals.
 3) The group mimics the leader secretly while the tagger gets up to 3 chances within 3 minutes to spot the leader.
 4) If found, all students do 10 side-steps, and the last to finish becomes the next tagger.
pe-06603:
1) Form a team of 3 players and set up a dartboard and throw line.
 2) Starting from 301 points, teammates take turns throwing 3 darts each to reduce the score.
 3) The team must reach exactly zero, and the final dart must hit a double segment to win.
 4) Scoring more points than remaining triggers a 'Bust', reverting the score to the previous round.
pe-06604:
1) Hold the corner of the scarf, throw it high into the air, and win by keeping it airborne the longest.
 2) Throw the scarf up, spin 360 or 720 degrees, and catch it before it hits the floor.
 3) Two players toss their scarves simultaneously and quickly swap positions to catch each other's scarf.
 4) Face forward in pairs while the front person tosses and the back person catches in a relay for 30 to 60 seconds.
pe-06605:
1) Stage 1: Hold a ball in each hand, toss and catch alternately with right and left hands, then toss and catch both simultaneously.
 2) Stage 2: Perform the "elephant trunk catch" by looping one arm under the other twice on each side, then toss and execute hand rubs before catching.
 3) Stage 3: Practice two-ball juggling using one hand.
 4) Stage 4: Retrieve the third ball from your pocket and perform standard three-ball juggling.
 5) Connect all four stages continuously in sequence to the rhythm of music.
pe-06606:
1) Hold one ball in each hand and tuck the third ball securely between your armpit and torso to start.
 2) Toss the balls into the air alternately, catching and circulating them to perform a three-ball cascade with large balls.
 3) In pairs, practice taking over the pattern when a partner tosses the third ball in to continue the cascade.
pe-06607:
1) Perform static stretches including lunge ankle press, kneeling hamstring stretch, hip opener, quad stretch, and groin stretch for 20-30 seconds per leg.
 2) Perform dynamic stretches including overhead lunge with trunk twists, elbow-to-floor trunk rotations, leg swings, hip rotations, and high-knee running in place.
pe-06608:
1) Divide into teams of three on a half-pitch with a goal and let the rock-paper-scissors winner start passing.
 2) The defending team cannot defend the first pass, but can intercept passes or steal the ball starting from the second pass.
 3) If the ball goes out of bounds, restart with a kick-in, and switch offense and defense once possession is completely stolen.
 4) The offensive team scores 1 point for every 5 consecutive successful passes, and the first team to reach 10 points wins.
pe-06609:
1) Two players take turns taking shots at the basketball hoop.
 2) In Two-Bounce Basketball, the partner shoots from the exact spot where the ball bounces twice off the rim.
 3) In No-Bounce Basketball, the partner catches the rebound before it hits the floor and immediately shoots from that spot.
 4) In Rally Point Basketball, players designate five post spots, advance to the next spot upon each basket made, and win by completing all five spots.
pe-06610:
1) Four or more students sit upright on chairs with arms free to move.
 2) The first student shouts 'Going to the Market' and performs an upper body or hand movement like clapping.
 3) The second student repeats the previous movement and adds a new upper body action.
 4) Subsequent students repeat all preceding movements in order and add their own to complete a round.
pe-06611:
1) Lie down, hug one bent knee to the chest, place it across the opposite knee, and pull the thigh inward.
 2) Lie face up with straight knees and kick one leg straight up toward the ceiling.
 3) Lie sideways, extend the bottom arm, slightly rotate the foot outward, and kick upward.
 4) Position hands and knees on the mat and kick one straight leg back toward the ceiling.
 5) Stand up and kick forward, sideways, and backward in three progressive height stages.
pe-06612:
1) Perform jumping lunges by switching front and back legs in the air into a 90-degree stance.
 2) Start in a low squat touching the floor and perform frog jumps extending limbs wide in the air.
 3) Jump vertically in place, lifting knees high to touch them with both hands.
 4) Perform single-leg ankle hops 4 times consecutively, then switch legs.
 5) Rest with deep breathing and repeat the entire sequence for a second set.
pe-06613:
1) Determine player order via rock-paper-scissors and mark a shooting spot 10 steps from the hoop.
 2) Each player takes turns shooting 3 times from the marked shooting location.
 3) Award 5 points for a basket, 2 points for hitting the rim, and 1 point for hitting the backboard.
 4) Choose new distances or angles with classmates and repeat for a total of 3 rounds.
 5) Tally all points across the three rounds to determine the winner.
pe-06614:
1) Warm up with a rock-paper-scissors jumping game and vertically hit a shuttlecock up to 3 meters 5 times in a row.
 2) Complete a 25-hit wall rally relay with a partner at a 60-degree angle and practice sudden grip tightening.
 3) Play an underhand target game aiming into 3 hula hoops and an overhead rally game catching shuttlecocks in stacking cups for 3 points.
pe-06615:
1) Warm up with joint stretches, then strengthen core muscles by holding a squat leg-grab for 3 seconds and a V-sit for 5 seconds.
 2) Stand facing a partner, play rock-paper-scissors, and progressively widen leg stance in a 2-player leg stretch challenge.
 3) Practice alignments for Warrior 2, Warrior 3, Child's Pose, and Corpse Pose, then attempt a 3-minute team relaxation time-attack mission.
pe-06616:
1) Stretch shoulders and complete a 1-minute 10-hit wall target throw and a 1-minute 10-rep stationary one-bounce spike drill.
 2) Perform a 10-hit wall spike relay with teammates and play a 5-shot goalkeeper shootout challenge using a mini goal.
 3) Learn arm-swing mechanics and topspin hitting, complete a 6-player rotation drill, and play a 10-point floor spike bounce match.
pe-06617:
1) Warm up with agility cone-tag drills and hit a ball with a paddle against a wall target at 2m at least 5 out of 10 times.
 2) Practice dropping balls into the kitchen, a 4-player 5-hit rally routine, a 20-hit quick ping-pong rally, and a line-touch dink drill.
 3) Learn proper form bending knees rather than the waist, and play an 11-point game reacting to the 'Dink-Pang' cue in the non-volley zone.
pe-06618:
1) Freely stick paper tape on the floor in various directions and shapes to create paths.
 2) Walk or run along the tape lines while exploring diverse body movements.
 3) Complete specific body expression movement missions designated along the route.
pe-06619:
1) Two students face each other keeping an arm's distance apart.
 2) The turner rotates the rope at a smooth, constant speed using the wrists.
 3) Both agree on a cue and jump simultaneously in sync.
 4) Complete the face-to-face jump rope challenge written on the mission card, then pass the turn to the next teammate upon success.
pe-06620:
1) Form a team of three and wait at the starting line.
 2) The first runner performs individual exercises: 15 jump squats, 10 in-and-outs, and 10 side jacks.
 3) Bear crawl 10 meters forward and throw two shuttlecocks into the basket target.
 4) Bear crawl back to the start and tag the next runner with a high five.
 5) The winning team is determined by the total number of shuttlecocks landed in the basket.
pe-06621:
1) Mark designated target boundaries on the wall and floor, and form singles (1 vs 1) or doubles (2 vs
 2) teams.
 2) Determine the first server via rock-paper-scissors, hit the ping pong ball against the wall target, and take turns returning it.
 3) Return the ball before it bounces twice on the floor (volley or single bounce) into the wall area to compete for 15 or 21 points.
pe-06622:
1) Pairs hold a stick and weave through 3 cones, turning back in reverse order
 2) Teams of four run from corner cones to high-five in the center for 3 continuous laps
 3) Teams adjust spacing by holding hands while passing a ball overhead and between legs in a relay
pe-06623:
1) Write your name using a finger in front of you, in the sky, on the floor, small, large, fast, and slowly.
 2) Write your name using various body parts such as shoulders, elbows, back, belly button, hips, heels, and toes.
 3) Create an original name dance using at least five body parts within 1 minute and 30 seconds.
 4) Perform the name dance to fast music, then to slow music, comparing how the rhythms feel.
pe-06624:
1) Stack stacking cups into a pyramid shape on top of a desk.
 2) Stand behind the throwing line at a set distance and throw a jump rope to knock down the cup pyramid.
 3) Each team throws jump ropes for a designated number of turns and counts the knocked-down cups.
 4) The team that knocks down the higher number of cups wins the game.
pe-06625:
1) Form 2-player teams and have every player throw their tee shot from the starting area.
 2) Team members identify and select the disc landed in the most favorable position.
 3) All team members advance to that spot and take their next throw from behind the marker.
 4) Repeat this process until holing out into the disc catcher; the team with the lowest score wins.
pe-06626:
1) Runner 1 throws the ball straight up and catches it securely with both hands 3 times, then tags off.
 2) Runner 2 tosses the ball up, claps three times before catching it 3 times, then tags off.
 3) Runner 3 tosses the ball, spins 360 degrees clockwise to catch once, and repeats counter-clockwise once.
 4) Runner 4 throws the ball to knock down a designated target; the team completing all tasks first wins.
pe-06627:
1) Set up a net or chairs in the center of a classroom-sized area to divide courts.
 2) Line up three players on each side facing each other across the net.
 3) The first player kicks the ball over the net and moves to the back of the line.
 4) The receiving player kicks it back over the net and goes to the back of their line, continuing the relay.
pe-06628:
1) Tape a virtual net line on the wall at arm's reach and mark a court with 5m sidelines and 6m endlines.
 2) One player stands behind the endline, calls 'serve', and hits the ball underhand above the virtual net line on the wall.
 3) The receiver allows one bounce off the wall and returns the ball toward the wall using underhand or overhand passes.
 4) A point is scored by the opponent if the ball lands out of bounds, is missed, or hits below the net line; played up to 11 points (best 2 out of 3).
pe-06629:
1) Sit comfortably to stretch the neck sideways with one hand, then reach overhead to stretch the torso and flanks.
 2) Move through lunge and prone positions to progressively stretch the hips, quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves.
 3) Lie down or sit tall to extend the upper body with arm reaches, chest openers, and back extensions.
pe-06630:
1) Clap palms, clap back of hands, bump fists up and down, bump fists, turn 360 degrees, and finish with a palm clap.
 2) Bump both fists twice, hit up and down, high-five with wrists, link arms, and swap places with a jump.
 3) Bump right and left arms twice, clap up and down, touch inside/outside of feet, and bump shoulders together.
 4) Line up facing each other and take turns performing unique created handshake dances in a relay.
pe-06631:
1) Form teams with one tagger and non-tagger players, ensuring everyone stays within the designated area.
 2) The tagger anticipates the flight path of the flying disc to intercept or touch it.
 3) If the tagger touches the flying disc in the air, the thrower becomes the tagger, and if it goes out of bounds, the thrower also becomes the tagger.
 4) If a player fails to catch a passed disc, the thrower and the receiver play rock-paper-scissors to determine the next tagger.
pe-06632:
1) Repeatedly raise and lower both heels to strengthen ankles and calves.
 2) Lift one leg backwards while raising both arms overhead to balance, alternating right and left.
 3) Raise a straightened leg sideways and lower it to strengthen hips and thighs.
 4) Perform lunges keeping the front knee bent at 90 degrees without letting it travel too far forward.
 5) Stand shoulder-width apart, keep the torso upright, push hips back, and squat down slowly.
pe-06633:
1) Divide into two teams with a net or obstacle set up in the middle.
 2) Catch the ball coming over the net with hands and toss it comfortably to a teammate.
 3) (Variation 1) Designate one student who struggles with Jokgu to pass using hands.
 4) (Variation
 2) Allow any player to touch the ball with hands once per rally without catching and throwing, like volleyball.
 5) (All-Hand Jokgu) All players may catch the ball with hands, but cannot move after catching and must kick from that spot.
pe-06634:
1) Learn core rules and umpire signals after warming up.
 2) Practice body gestures as the teacher calls out umpire signals.
 3) Form groups of four with one umpire and three runners/batters to role-play scenarios and make immediate calls.
 4) Earn points from peer evaluation and teacher feedback to clear the challenge with 6 or more points.
 5) Role-play scorekeeping, operate real games, and complete fairness worksheets.
pe-06635:
1) Warm up by pairing up to slide and catch stones left and right.
 2) Slide stones from challenging postures (walking, lying down, elephant trunk spins) to stop inside the center white circle.
 3) Play curling clay shooting by aiming and colliding stones into a moving target stone slid by a partner.
 4) Learn guard, freeze, and takeout tactics, then play a 4-end team floor curling match.
pe-06636:
1) Stretch wrists and ankles, then practice gentle service tapping at a 6m distance using a return shuttlecock.
 2) Circle around a hula hoop to music in groups of four, running to the service area to serve into the hoop when a number is called.
 3) Learn proper service grip by placing the thumb on the handle.
 4) Compete 3-on-3 in 'Pass the Service', clearing 10 shuttlecocks over the net within 30 seconds.
 5) Play 'Tunnel Service' targeting a hula hoop (1 pt) and box (2 pts) to reach 21 points first.
pe-06637:
1) Warm up with a crown game balancing a cone on the head while knocking off opponents' cones using side steps without hands.
 2) Complete timed 10-second side-step challenges along side lines, the 3-point line, and the paint area.
 3) Pair up to catch dropped balls within two bounces, grab cones based on indicator directions, and race to cones.
 4) Play 'Protect My Territory', flipping spot markers to match team colors within one minute.
 5) Play a 3-on-3 half-court game to 7 points where the first player to side-step to the top and grab the ball attacks.
pe-06638:
1) Perform a modified jumping jack by moving side to side while opening and closing your arms.
 2) Step sideways and twist your body and legs in opposite directions alternately.
 3) Pull both arms back while touching your heel to your buttock as you move laterally, followed by brisk forward-and-back walking with large arm swings, then rest for 30 seconds before repeating set 2.
pe-06639:
1) Two teams play offense and defense; the offense lands discs in the Dokdo zone while defenders knock them down, and the team with more discs remaining wins.
 2) Team members stationed in 3m x 3m zones link designated curve throws to sink the disc into the disc catcher first.
 3) Players take turns throwing from set distances, earning 1 point for each disc closer to the catcher, and the team with higher total points wins.
pe-06640:
1) Lightly run and rhythmically jump over the rotating jump rope 15 consecutive times.
 2) After completing 15 jumps, move to the shooting station, catch your breath, shoot, and score at least 2 points to succeed.
 3) Participate in comprehensive target sports matches such as darts, curling, and shooting for team competition.
pe-06641:
1) Hide a table tennis ball under cups placed upside down, then run in relays to find the hidden ball.
 2) Set up 6 cups in a row, stack 5 across them, and push 1 cup from the side to topple them like dominoes.
 3) Two players run parallel, repeating 3-3-3 stacking every 10m, and the one who catches up and lightly tags the opponent first wins.
pe-06642:
1) Set the ball 5 consecutive times without dropping a cone placed on top of your head.
 2) Set the ball, let it bounce once, and catch it in a large trash bag (or cone) 3 consecutive times.
 3) In teams of four, one player exchanges sets with the other three, and the final player shoots the ball into the basketball hoop; the first team to win 2 out of 3 rounds wins.
pe-06643:
1) Form two teams of 3 players, assigning one team to offense and the other to defense.
 2) Build target castles using Jumbo Stacks cups (or cones) in four directions (N, S, E, W).
 3) The attacking team uses passes and floorball shots to knock down the castles.
 4) Three defenders position themselves to block shots or clear the ball to run out the clock.
 5) Switch roles after 3 minutes; the team that knocks down more targets wins.
pe-06644:
1) Form groups based on fitness levels and assign them to suitable courses (flat vs. hilly).
 2) Plan the walking route, time, traffic hazard points, and recycling methods in advance.
 3) Run a running app and jog together in groups while collecting litter in designated areas.
 4) Stay cautious of street hazards and maintain communication with the teacher and group leaders.
 5) Sort the collected waste for recycling and log the running distance and reflections.
pe-06645:
1) Set up three fitness stations: stair climbing, shuttle jumps, and side steps.
 2) Pair up as performer and recorder, timing and counting reps using a tablet.
 3) Move immediately to the shooting line after completing high-intensity fitness drills.
 4) Fire the designated number of shots (10 rounds) at the electronic target from a standing stance.
 5) Combine the fitness station completion times and shooting scores for the team result.
pe-06646:
1) Stand in front of the webcam and launch the AI motion recognition program.
 2) Train the AI with the start and end postures of exercises like squats or push-ups.
 3) Train common incorrect postures (e.g., bending back) to set real-time error detection.
 4) Perform the exercises while checking the voice count given by the AI program.
 5) Correct faulty form in real time based on AI feedback during the circuit training.
pe-06647:
1) Form teams of 3 and wait in line behind the throwing line (2m distance).
 2) Each player takes turns throwing 3 darts toward the target board.
 3) Add the scored points from each throw to the team's cumulative total score.
 4) Continue taking turns across 8 rounds to build the highest team score.
 5) The team with the highest total score after 8 rounds wins the match.
pe-06648:
1) Form teams of four and line up at the starting line.
 2) On the start signal, the first runner moves through cones while continuously bouncing the Kin-Ball.
 3) Successfully turn around the cone marker and return within 10 seconds without dropping the ball to earn 10 points.
pe-06649:
1) Position teammates across the designated playing area.
 2) On the start signal, pass the volleyball continuously to each other using underhand passes.
 3) Work together to steer and drop as many volleyballs as possible into the mobile ball cart within 3 minutes.
pe-06650:
1) Divide into two teams, set the turn order, and arrange number spot markers from 0 to 9 on a basketball half court like a telephone keypad.
 2) When the opposing team designates a player from your team, call out that player's phone number digits in order.
 3) The opposing team moves to the corresponding numbered spot markers and attempts shots, ensuring every player shoots at least once.
 4) If a shot misses, the turn transfers to the other team, resuming from the missed spot.
 5) Teams score 3 points for completing all spots or 1 point for partial completions, and the team with the most points wins.
pe-06651:
1) Form pairs and decide the turn order by playing rock-paper-scissors.
 2) The pitcher throws the ball by hand so that it bounces once into the strike zone.
 3) The batter hits the ball and backsteps through third, second, and first bases.
 4) The batting team scores one point if the batter finishes running before the fielding team places the ball on the cone.
 5) The team with the highest score after 3 innings wins.
pe-06652:
1) Set up the target mat and start line, marking the hog line in front of the start line.
 2) Teams take turns sliding bearing stones across the wooden floor toward the target.
 3) Any stone failing to cross the hog line is removed from play.
 4) After all stones are delivered, score points for each stone located closer to the center than the opponent's closest stone.
 5) The team with the highest cumulative score across all ends wins.
pe-06653:
1) Place 8 cones along each long service line of a badminton court and 3 dodgeballs on the center line.
 2) Form teams of around 10 players, dividing into 3-4 attackers and 6-7 retrievers.
 3) On the signal, attackers retrieve center balls and throw from behind the service line to knock down opponent cones.
 4) Defenders block with balls or their bodies, while retrievers collect out-of-bounds balls and pass them to attackers.
 5) Play 2-minute sets; the team that wins 2 out of 3 sets wins the match.
pe-06654:
1) Leader and follower face each other and establish a closed position hold.
 2) Sway hips for 8 beats to the rhythm when the music starts.
 3) Maintain the dance frame and execute the Jive chassé steps to the count.
 4) The leader guides the direction and the follower responds smoothly to both sides.
 5) Switch partners every 20 seconds and dance freely around the floor.
pe-06655:
1) Form pairs and position each team on opposite sides of the net.
 2) When a serve is made, do not return it directly; let it bounce before starting play.
 3) Player A drops and lifts the ball, and Player B executes a stroke toward the other side.
 4) Cooperate with your teammate to return the ball over the net within 3 contacts.
 5) Hitting out or into the net results in conceding a point; play until 7 to 11 points.
pe-06656:
1) Place 5 mini hurdles in a row followed by a cone at the end.
 2) Run and clear the 5 mini hurdles with single-leg strides, touch the cone, and return to the start line.
 3) On the next attempt, clear the hurdles with two-foot jumps, touch the cone, and return.
 4) Clear them in a natural running rhythm; if the time difference between attempts is within 2 seconds, the mission is cleared.
pe-06657:
1) Mark 0m, 4m, and 5m points with cones along a 10m straight course and set the running order.
 2) The first runner holds a backpack in each hand and completes 5 backpack squats at the start line.
 3) Perform 6 backpack walking lunges up to the 4m mark, sprint around the 5m cone, and return to the start line.
 4) Tag the next runner with a high-five; the challenge is successful when all 5 members complete the course.
pe-06658:
1) Form a square arena with desks and have 4-8 players place their hands on the desks to start.
 2) The teacher drops the ball in the center, and play starts after it bounces 3 times.
 3) Players hit the ball with open hands below opponents' waists; hit players are eliminated.
 4) Touching the ball twice consecutively or hitting it out of bounds results in an out, and the last remaining player wins.
pe-06659:
1) Perform bicycle crunches by lying down, interlacing fingers behind head, and crossing elbow to knee.
 2) Hold a plank by placing elbows on the floor and keeping the body in a straight line.
 3) Do Russian twists by sitting, lifting feet slightly, and rotating torso side to side.
 4) Lie face down and lift arms and legs upward into a superman pose.
 5) Perform marching bridges by lifting hips and raising alternate legs, completing two sets.
pe-06660:
1) Learn abdominal and thoracic breathing while seated, followed by partner 2-person chair squats and flexibility challenges.
 2) Practice fundamental yoga postures step-by-step including mountain, tree, cat, cobra, camel, and pigeon poses.
 3) Play freeze tag where runners avoid the pinnie-holding tagger by calling 'Tree' and holding the tree pose before being tagged.
pe-06661:
1) Warm up with a no-bounce passing drill with one ball to practice predicting ball trajectories.
 2) Practice in a 2-on-1 formation where one player receives and returns two incoming balls continuously.
 3) Start the game by serving two balls simultaneously from both courts, and re-serve if the two balls collide in midair.
pe-06662:
1) Teams of 3 or more take turns kicking a bouncy ball.
 2) After hitting, runners grab a cone from the field and run to base.
 3) The runner is out if the ball reaches base first, and teams switch after 3 outs.
pe-06663:
1) Two turners face each other and alternate turning two long jump ropes inward.
 2) A jumper enters the ropes in one fluid motion right as the far rope strikes the floor and jumps continuously.
 3) The team with more participants successfully jumping within the given time limit wins.
pe-06664:
1) Ball on the Racket Relay: In teams of three, Runner 1 walks/runs, Runner 2 hops on one foot without switching feet, and Runner 3 jumps with both feet together while balancing a ping-pong ball on the racket around a 10m turning point.
 2) If the ball drops, the team restarts from Runner 1, and the team with the fastest completion time wins.
 3) Together Table Tennis Relay: Six players form a team with three lined up on each side of the table tennis table.
 4) Players take turns hitting the ball in sequence to keep the rally going as many times as possible within the time limit.
 5) As variations, try the Lifting on the Racket Relay by bouncing the ball while running, or add cups as obstacles on the table centerline.
pe-06665:
1) Jump back and forth over cones twice with both feet together at square 1.
 2) Move past the mat at square 2 to fire one shot at the tchoukball rebounder target and roll out to the right mat.
 3) Crawl under the low obstacle obstacle made of chairs and a bar at square 3.
 4) Shoot the auto-reverse target with the remaining 5 darts at square 4 to earn points and return to the starting line before the timer runs out.
pe-06666:
1) Both teams line up for inspection and greetings, then start the match with a jump ball.
 2) The attacking team throws the ball to hit opponents while adhering to pass rules, avoiding the face and head.
 3) Hit defenders move to the outfield, while catching the ball without a bounce counts as a save.
 4) Students take on roles as referees, line judges, scorekeepers, and coaches to manage the game with official signals and scorecards.
pe-06667:
1) Place 3 cones in the center of the circular court, and one runner enters to protect the cones.
 2) Fielders surround the circle and roll the ball, which the batter must kick within 3 attempts.
 3) Once the runner kicks the ball outside the circle, they run to tag and switch with the next waiting runner.
 4) If fielders pass the ball and knock down a cone before the switch, it is an out; if the switch succeeds first, the batting team scores.
pe-06668:
1) Select 4 to 8 smartphone emoticons and choreograph movements to an 8-count beat.
 2) Express the meanings and shapes of emoticons, such as directions and hand gestures, to the rhythm.
 3) Team up with two or more peers to combine choreographies, add formation changes, and perform to music.
pe-06669:
1) Form a team of 5 players and decide the order.
 2) A lead student lofts the ball high using a hand or paddle.
 3) Team members take turns smashing the ball consecutively into the target 5 times to succeed.
pe-06670:
1) Split into two teams of 4 with a cup set on each desk, placing 9 hoops in a 3x3 grid 10m ahead.
 2) Each runner completes the 1-10-1 stack, runs to place the cup into one hoop, and returns.
 3) Alternating runners continue until one team completes a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line to win.
pe-06671:
1) Sit on a mat, hug knees to the chest, round the spine, and practice rolling back and forward like a ball.
 2) When the whistle blows, the student currently rolling or preparing becomes the tagger.
 3) Both the tagger and runners hop on one foot only, trying to tag or evade while keeping core balance.
 4) In teams of four, lie with heads outward, lift the upper body and legs, and support a stability ball with toes in a pyramid hold.
pe-06672:
1) With a partner, navigate zigzag cones by rolling a tennis ball with racquets for 3 laps (Hockey Tennis).
 2) Bounce a ball between two racquets and impact it simultaneously at sweet spots while navigating back around cones (Clap Challenge).
 3) Hold a racquet in one hand and a mini hoop in the other, rallying the ball back and forth for 10 consecutive bounces.
 4) Play a 2-on-2 double touch rally game from the service lines, returning the ball within 3 touches (drop, set, attack) up to 11-15 points.
pe-06673:
1) Practice alone: throw and catch, bounce and catch, clap hands while throwing/bouncing, step back, and catch after a 360-degree spin.
 2) Two players face each other, throw and bounce catch, and move one step right and left to catch falling balls.
 3) Step one step back, bounce the ball, spin 360 degrees on the spot, and catch the falling ball synchronously.
pe-06674:
1) Draw a circle or square area about 1 meter in diameter on the floor.
 2) Start the rally with an underhand serve below the waist, bouncing the ball into the designated area toward the opponent.
 3) Players take turns hitting the ball into the designated area, conceding a point if they fail to bounce it into the area or fail to return it.
pe-06675:
1) Draw a target with a diameter of about 2–3 meters 10–15 meters ahead of the starting line.
 2) Each team takes 5 discs and players take turns sliding them across the floor toward the target.
 3) After all discs are slid, the team with the disc closest to the center of the target wins.
pe-06676:
1) Face a partner and cross hands in an X-shape with right palm down and left palm up.
 2) Untangle hands without letting go by raising arms and turning bodies.
 3) Progress by forming a circle with four or more players to untangle together.
pe-06677:
1) Warm up for 10 minutes with squats and hip hinge exercises.
 2) Perform main workouts like jump rope, squats, and burpees for 8 minutes repeatedly.
 3) Record the total completed repetitions in a logbook and compare with records from 3 months ago.
pe-06678:
1) Divide the class into teams or prepare inter-class competitions.
 2) Compete based on each group's lowest recorded score to encourage mutual support without leaving any student behind.
 3) Create running mission activities together with students and share results on a board in real time.
pe-06679:
1) Spin the hula hoop around your waist, neck, feet, or arms
 2) Run while spinning the hula hoop
 3) Jump over the hula hoop
 4) Roll the hula hoop and catch it
 5) Hold the hula hoop and balance on one leg to wrestle
pe-06680:
1) Bend your knees and move to the rhythm
 2) Step side to side to the beat
 3) Perform box steps and side steps
 4) Finish with deep breathing
pe-06681:
1) Three students in the first tier kneel down with extended shoulders.
 2) Two students in the second tier stand up holding the shoulders of the first tier.
 3) One student in the third tier climbs up holding the shoulders of the second tier.
 4) Perform the movement simultaneously to the count of "Se no, Ichi ni, San."
pe-06682:
1) 10 people gather and line up in a single file according to height and physical strength.
 2) The base members kneel on one knee and prepare to support each other by holding hands.
 3) The rider places their feet on the first row's shoulders and the remaining rows support the body.
 4) Raise the upper body together in sync with the signal.
pe-06683:
1) Horizontal balance: Stand on one leg, lift the other leg at least 90 degrees, and extend arms.
 2) Y-balance: Stand on one leg, hold the heel of the other leg, and lift it to form a Y-shape.
pe-06684:
1) Lie on your back on a mat, practice deep breathing, and reach overhead with your arms
 2) Cross legs to stretch the hamstrings, bend knees, and hold a bridge pose for 5 seconds
 3) Transition to hands and knees for cat-cow and hip rocks, then sit to stretch the neck and wrists
pe-06685:
1) Learn the three phases of jumping: takeoff, flight, and landing.
 2) Warm up with skipping and varied jumping styles inside the volleyball court.
 3) Rotate through four stations (jump rope, speed and agility ladders, steppers, etc.) practicing two-foot and one-foot takeoff missions.
 4) Leap over steppers and ladder squares to navigate the jungle obstacle course.
 5) Complete and hand in an exit slip listing or drawing the cues for jumping and landing.
pe-06686:
1) Hungry Hippos: Divide into teams at corner bases and dribble balls into your base one at a time for 5 minutes.
 2) Human Foosball: Goalies and defenders move only sideways along designated lines, while attackers hold pool noodles together to move as a unit and kick towards the goal.
 3) Place Kicking: Practice the approach, planting the non-dominant foot one foot from the ball, striking with a locked ankle, and following through.
 4) Assessment: Complete an exit slip labeling the kicking phases.
pe-06687:
1) In the center position, hike the ball between the legs upon the snap count from a chair or stance, then immediately stand up and block side-to-side for 5 reps.
 2) In the quarterback position, receive the snap, drop back, step with the opposite foot, and complete 5 forward passes to the receiver.
 3) In the wide receiver position, sprint forward on the snap count and catch low or high passes inside the end zone.
 4) Practice keeping both feet strictly inside the boundary line when making the catch while avoiding simulated defenders.
pe-06688:
1) Locate and step onto designated color spot markers on the gym floor.
 2) Follow verbal cues to place hands on specified colors or raise hands while maintaining balance.
 3) Walk to the center colored marker and return, then perform 10 seconds of continuous one-hand dribbling.
pe-06689:
1) Stand inside a hula hoop and kick the ball toward targets using the instep or laces instead of toes.
 2) Divide into four groups and take turns kicking a ball from a hula hoop to knock down three cans in football bowling.
 3) Practice drop kicking and punting by holding the ball straight out above the foot and dropping it into contact.
 4) Partner holds a football with one finger at a slight 37-degree angle while the kicker approaches to kick a field goal.
pe-06690:
1) A player with the ball can hold it for up to 3 seconds or take up to 3 steps while dribbling.
 2) Defenders cannot strip the ball from hands or push opponents; fouls result in yellow cards or a 2-minute suspension.
 3) If the ball goes out of the boundary line, possession turns over to the opposing team.
 4) Practice dynamic warm-ups and play small-sided games targeting 20 consecutive passes to create shot opportunities.
pe-06691:
1) Follow an interval workout format consisting of 30 seconds of jumping followed by 30 seconds of rest.
 2) Begin with a single-time jump, then progress to double-time jumps and running in place jumps.
 3) Challenge variations including lateral side-to-side jumps, 360-degree turning jumps, and backward jumps.
pe-06692:
1) Select one player as the shark and give pool noodles to the jellyfish.
 2) The shark can run, while the jellyfish can only tag players within their area using the noodles.
 3) The minnows cross the ocean area performing the specific locomotor skill designated by the teacher, such as galloping.
 4) The shark must tag players gently on the torso between the shoulders and waistline using two fingers.
pe-06693:
1) Flees stay inside the area marked by four cones.
 2) Chasers start on their stomachs inside the designated circle and call out the locomotor skill to use.
 3) As the chasers get to their feet to pursue, the flees must run outside the baseline to reach safety.
 4) Chasers must tag runners using only one finger without pushing them.
pe-06694:
1) Perform locomotive movements around flashcards and freeze on signal to complete exercises.
 2) Face a partner and practice ball control, inside-foot trapping, and alternating toe taps.
 3) Dribble to the half court line and make an inside-foot pass to your partner while following through.
 4) Navigate the obstacle course by circling the roundabout, steering around mats (parked cars), and controlling the ball through a narrow road made of jump ropes.
pe-06695:
1) Warm up around the gym performing prompted locomotor skills like galloping and one-foot hopping
 2) Practice one-foot balance inside individual hula hoops
 3) Perform two-footed and single-leg hopping drills through the agility ladder rungs
 4) Jog a lap around the perimeter of the gym when rotating to the next activity station
pe-06696:
1) Tap over the cones with feet as quickly as possible
 2) Dribble the ball with a hockey stick held in both hands across the gym floor
 3) Knock the cone over with the hockey stick and hide the ball underneath without using hands
 4) Dribble or pass balls through targets and sort beanbags into green and red baskets based on health categories
pe-06697:
1) Face the gym wall and set a goal of 30 seconds or 10-30 repetitions per skill.
 2) Practice various passing and dribbling skills against the wall including bounce passes and combo moves.
 3) Progress to challenging skills like overhead tosses, 360-degree turns, and between-the-leg passes.
 4) Utilize the wall space individually to practice both right and left hands evenly without a partner.
pe-06698:
1) Roll the dice and check the number shown (e.g., 6).
 2) Lie on your stomach and army crawl under the rope.
 3) Pick up the exact number of beanbags matching the dice roll and return.
 4) Stand at the throwing mark and toss the beanbags to knock down bowling pins or land them inside the hula hoop.
pe-06699:
1) Perform heel-to-toe (Argentina), ankle circles (Brazil), toe touches (Canada), tick-tock (Denmark), and magic wand (England) for 40s on and 20s off.
 2) Continue with open-space dribbling (France), drag-backs (Germany), knee taps (Hungary), drop-and-traps (Iceland), and juggling (Japan).
 3) Alternate equally between left and right feet for each skill and record completed reps.
 4) Transition into the World Cup game where students perform the skill of the called country and freeze the ball when 'USA' is called.
pe-06700:
1) Perform standing shoulder shrugs and overhead reaches for 30 to 60 seconds.
 2) Execute lateral raises, seal claps, scissor arms, wrist circles, and air boxing punches.
 3) Follow with lower body movements including step backs with knee drives, marching, side kicks, squats, and glute kickbacks.
pe-06701:
1) Crew members will be divided into four teams.
 2) The first round all team members will work together to capture Pokemon.
 3) The second round will be groups of two.
 4) After each round, teams will add up their own total based on Poke value.
pe-06702:
1) Place a doormat on the floor and stand in the designated space
 2) Keep feet together and perform continuous jumps forward, backward, and sideways
 3) Perform single-leg hops in and out of the mat and ice-skating balance movements
pe-06703:
1) Jog on the spot for 30 seconds.
 2) Continue with warm-up movements including jumping side to side and touchdowns.
 3) Perform jumping jacks, punches, side-to-side jumps, and high knee drives for 30 seconds each.
 4) Perform side leg lifts and fast feet quickly.
 5) Finish with planks and crab kicks.
pe-06704:
1) Place hands on waist and do neck stretches and shoulder rotations.
 2) Jog lightly on the spot changing directions every 20 seconds.
 3) Perform ski jumps, squat touchdowns, punches, and front kicks in order.
 4) Complete 35 invisible jump rope jumps and repeat the cycle if desired.
pe-06705:
1) Divide the class into small groups and assign each group to their own line of benches and mats.
 2) The teacher demonstrates each exercise first in slow motion and then at regular speed.
 3) Students practice the movement by completing one to three laps across their assigned stations.
 4) Once comfortable, students progress to level two variations or perform the movements synchronized to a musical beat.
pe-06706:
1) Divide roles so one student moves while the other supports with a stick or suspended ball
 2) The supporter adjusts difficulty and speed to match the mover's capability
 3) Transition to non-verbal body movement without tools and take turns alternating roles
pe-06707:
1) Choose the path for Mario by performing the designated pose.
 2) Earn points for correct answers and move to dodge obstacles.
 3) Freeze immediately in place when the freeze signal appears.
pe-06708:
1) Hold a fun stick in one hand and a picture card in the other.
 2) On the signal, place the fun stick between your legs and run.
 3) Run around the cone and return to the starting point.
pe-06710:
1) Team members get into a push-up position in a line
 2) The person at the back crawls to the front
 3) Once at the front, they grab the ball and move to the cone
 4) Once everyone has moved, the team sits down and holds the ball above their heads to finish
pe-06711:
1) Take 10 seconds to choose your favorite character among the three shown on screen.
 2) Do the exercise that pops up where that character was.
 3) Take a 15-second break at the halfway mark and continue through the remaining rounds.
pe-06712:
1) Set spot markers in a zigzag line and hop side to side balancing on toes.
 2) Perform four-step in-and-out footwork around a hoop on the ground.
 3) Balance on one foot and bend down slowly to touch a large ball on a cone with the nose.
 4) Practice lateral steps over hurdles and jumping in/out of a spinning hoop.
pe-06713:
1) Infinity Loops: Dribble around two cones set 1m apart in a figure-eight infinity loop using both feet without touching the cones.
 2) Direction Change: Trap the ball with the sole of the foot and drag it behind to turn, alternating feet.
 3) Gate Passing: Kick the ball through a 1m cone gate toward a wall using the inside of the foot, taking a step back after each successful pass.
 4) Side to Side Taps: Tap the ball left and right moving forwards and backwards between two cones 5m apart.
 5) Circle Weaving: Weave through a circle of cones using small touches with one foot, then reverse direction with the other foot or use sole rolls.
 6) Chipping into Goal: Kick the underside of the ball to chip it over a line of cones into the net.
 7) Zigzag Skill Dribble: Dribble along zigzag spot markers, trapping the ball on each spot to complete 5 step-overs or 5 toe-taps.
pe-06714:
1) Set cones wide apart and warm up for 30 seconds each with one-legged jumps, sumo lunges, and hamstring kicks.
 2) Exercise for 30 seconds with 15-second rests doing shuffle burpees, pogo jumps, A-skips, and monkey skips between cones.
 3) Move cones 1 meter apart to perform infinity loops, alternating cone touch balances, and side squat jumps.
 4) Conclude with hip lunges and low lunges, holding each stretch for 15 seconds per side.
pe-06715:
1) Warm up with pendulum swings, side lunges, and torso chops for 30 seconds each.
 2) Perform up-downs, northeast-southwest hops, scissor jacks, step-back lunges, skip shuffles, and running on the spot for 30 seconds each with 15 seconds of rest.
 3) Take a 2-minute rest after finishing the round and repeat the routine once more.
 4) Cool down by holding calf lunges, side lunge stretches, and triceps stretches for 15 seconds each.
pe-06716:
1) Flick the ball up into the air using a starting trick.
 2) Juggle using at least two different body parts such as feet and knees.
 3) Reach a total of at least 10 touches before losing control, allowing bounces between touches if needed.
pe-06717:
1) Hold a large ball with both hands and make circles 4-5 times in each direction with straight arms.
 2) Wrap the ball around the waist and pass it under high knees to warm up.
 3) Perform split jumps, up-downs, ball twists, ball push-ups, bunny jumps, one-arm ball rolls, and leg-to-hand passes for 30 seconds each with 15-second rests.
 4) Finish by stretching the triceps, quadriceps, and hips for 15 seconds per side.
pe-06718:
1) Place cones 10 meters apart and perform hamstring kicks across the space by hugging the knee and kicking out.
 2) Open and close the gates 10 times on each leg to warm up hip flexors and adductors.
 3) Complete 20 jump lunges and 20 seated knee turns touching the knee to the floor.
 4) Stretch the hamstrings, lower back, and glutes by holding each position for 10-15 seconds.
pe-06719:
1) Practice basic two-foot and single-foot jumps swinging arms and bending knees.
 2) Jump like frogs through a zigzag line of hoops on two feet.
 3) Perform pogo jumps as high as possible along spot markers.
 4) Jump over an increasingly wider river line.
 5) Jump forward and sideways over mini hurdles and leap to catch a large inflatable ball.
pe-06720:
1) Balance and bounce a tennis ball continuously on a bat or racket without letting it drop.
 2) Control and pass a ball against a wall moving left and right through cones.
 3) Fling a beanbag from the racket underhand and overhead into a hoop target 4-5 meters away.
pe-06721:
1) Hop in and out with feet together moving forward, right, back, and left in a north-east-south-west pattern.
 2) Place hands on hips, balance on one foot, and lift one leg as high and wide as possible.
 3) Get into a crab position keeping the butt off the ground and touch the foot with the opposite hand.
 4) Perform each exercise for one minute with a 15-second rest between exercises.
pe-06722:
1) Toss the ball, touch a tall cone, and dig the ball
 2) Toss the ball with backspin and place a flat hand under the bouncing ball for a pancake
 3) Set the ball continuously while sitting down and standing back up
 4) Practice quick wrist setting against a wall
 5) Throw the ball over the net, duck under the net, and catch or dig it
 6) Alternate digging and setting off a wall
 7) Keep the ball bouncing inside a hoop using one-armed forearm touches.
pe-06723:
1) Tap one or two balloons with hands or different body parts like head, shoulders, elbows, and knees to keep them off the floor
 2) Hit the balloon high and complete challenges such as spinning, touching the floor, or jump turning before catching it
 3) Practice sports fundamentals including basketball dribbling and shooting, soccer drop kicks, volleyball digs and sets, tennis swings, and noodle golf and fencing
pe-06724:
1) Each activity allows 10 attempts to earn points for every successful trick.
 2) Students challenge 13 individual soccer tricks such as scooping the ball up and balancing it on the foot for three seconds.
 3) Harder tricks award more points while easier tricks award fewer points to challenge personal and class scores.
pe-06725:
1) Hop along a zigzag line of spot markers from side to side alternating feet like an ice skater.
 2) Stand 4-5 meters from a wall behind a hoop and hit the ball with a racquet so it bounces off the wall and lands inside the hoop.
 3) Throw a tennis ball against a gym ball and catch it, or flick a soccer ball over mini hurdles using the top of the foot.
pe-06726:
1) Throw a tennis ball against a gym ball and catch it before it hits the ground.
 2) Toss a bean bag in the air, tap your knee with the same hand, and catch it with that same hand.
 3) Bounce two balls simultaneously with both hands and catch them, or cross hands to switch bounce directions.
 4) Hold a tennis ball directly above a basketball, release them together, and catch the popping tennis ball.
 5) Stand facing away from a wall, throw a large ball backwards overhead against the wall, and catch the rebound.
 6) Bounce a ball, touch or lift a tall cone with the same hand, and catch the ball in your hand or inside the cone.
 7) Stand 3-4 meters away behind a hoop, throw the ball overhead against the wall so it bounces into the hoop, and catch it.
pe-06727:
1) Each team receives a bingo board.
 2) Run to the other side to collect a bingo card and a coin.
 3) Perform the exercise shown on the card with your team.
 4) Once completed, mark the spot on the board and shout 'Bingo' when you complete a line horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
pe-06728:
1) Students choose a striking implement from the bucket.
 2) Partners bounce or drop the ball and strike it with the implement.
 3) Strike the ball towards various targets like nets, floor spots, and hoops.
 4) Use underhand strikes only and practice with different implements and balls.
pe-06729:
1) Stand facing a partner and practice throwing and catching the foam dek ring.
 2) Try different catches such as catching through the middle, foot catch, or rolling to your partner.
 3) Pass and move around the floor continuously.
 4) Perform fitness movements determined by rolling dice with your partner.
pe-06730:
1) Divide into two teams on opposite sides of a center dividing line (fence).
 2) When music starts, pick up balls (trash) from your court and throw them into the opposing team's court.
 3) Players may only hold one ball at a time and cannot kick balls.
 4) Stepping over the line sends the player to jail (bench) to sing the ABC song before returning, and the team with fewer balls when the music stops wins.
pe-06731:
1) Divide the area into four quadrants, place a batting tee and ball bucket in each corner, and assign teams.
 2) When music starts, the first batter places a ball on the tee and takes one swing toward another quadrant.
 3) After swinging, drop the bat safely, tag the team bucket, and rotate to the next runner.
 4) Once the bucket is empty, players may pick up balls from their own court to hit onto opponent courts.
 5) After about 2 minutes when the music stops, collect and count the balls; the team with the fewest balls in their area wins.
pe-06732:
1) Practice the locomotor movement shown on screen (walking, skipping, backwards skipping, sliding) to music while finding open space.
 2) When the music stops, move directly to the closest hula hoop.
 3) Perform the fitness exercise corresponding to your hoop's color (jumping jacks, sit-up punches, planks, burpees, line jumps, squats) for 20 to 30 seconds.
 4) If unable to do a specific exercise due to health reasons, pick a different colored challenge.
pe-06733:
1) The batting team lines up at the batting tee, hits the ball in order, drops the bat, tags the bucket, and returns to the back of the line.
 2) The fielding team spreads out across the field to catch or field balls and place them into the fielding bucket.
 3) The batting team scores points based on distance zones: past half-court cone (2 pts), past second cone (3 pts), rolling to the wall (4 pts), hitting the wall in the air (10 pts), or hitting the basketball backboard (20 pts).
 4) If a fielder catches a hit ball in the air, the batter scores zero points.
 5) After 3 minutes, the fielding team receives 2 points for each ball collected in their bucket, then teams switch roles.
pe-06734:
1) Form pairs, stand facing each other, and hold the frisbee with your thumb on top.
 2) Throw and catch the frisbee back and forth with your partner while music is playing.
 3) When the music stops, the partner holding the frisbee must walk to try and tag the other partner.
 4) If you tag your partner, drop the frisbee; the tagged partner picks it up to switch roles.
 5) When music resumes, immediately stop tagging and resume throwing and catching.
pe-06735:
1) Hold the parachute at belly height and shake it gently like boiling water.
 2) Add noodles and foam balls as vegetables onto the parachute while shaking together.
 3) Add the rubber chicken at the end and pretend to taste the soup.
 4) Shake the parachute up and down vigorously in dishwasher mode to bounce all ingredients off.
pe-06736:
1) The giant tags participants while guarding the bridge, and players wait for the signal.
 2) When the giant steps away, players cross the bridge made of balance mats from the start.
 3) When the giant sleeps, players cross over, retrieve balls (food) from the bucket, return to the safe house, and shut the door.
pe-06737:
1) Practice slow walking, vigorous fast walking, slow jogging with chest open, and fast running with wider strides.
 2) Perform horizontal bar activities including low hanging, high hanging, and leg-hook hanging.
 3) Practice bodyweight holds like lying leg raises, push-up holds, wall sits, stretching bends, and partner push/pull drills.
pe-06738:
1) Push classroom desks together to create wide pathways and obstacles.
 2) Select 2 zombies while the remaining students become citizens and hide in classroom corners.
 3) Zombies wear blindfolds and hold sponge sticks.
 4) Play eerie background music, turn off the classroom lights, and zombies begin roaming to tag citizens with their sticks.
 5) Citizens tagged by a zombie are eliminated and move to the front of the classroom.
 6) When time expires, count surviving citizens: if more than half are out, the zombies win; otherwise, citizens win.
pe-06739:
1) Warm up by stepping side-to-side to the upbeat music rhythm.
 2) Extend arms overhead and perform forward punch combinations along with steps.
 3) Transition into heel touches, knee lifts, and torso twists sequentially to the beat.
pe-06740:
1) Perform the Bullim motion by chanting 'Nakyangdongcheon-ihwajeong' and swinging the arms with bounce.
 2) Do the Gogaejabi head movement by dipping the chin to make circles left and right.
 3) Practice leg lifts by lifting one leg at a time to the rhythm with knee bends.
 4) Do the Hwangso-georeum bull-walk by tapping near the opposite knee with the lifted foot while bouncing.
 5) Perform Oesawi by twirling and casting the Hansam sleeve with one hand while lifting the leg.
 6) Perform Yangsawi by twirling and casting both hands overhead.
pe-06741:
1) Practice basic underhand and overhand pass postures using lower body bounce.
 2) Attempt to tap a plastic bag ball 10 consecutive times without letting it drop.
 3) Practice underhand receiving postures by shifting quickly side to side and absorbing the ball's force.
 4) Practice blocking mechanics 10 times by lifting heels instead of jumping with fingers angled downward.
 5) Practice the 3-step approach footwork for spiking.
pe-06742:
1) Sing the orange song while rotating hands, and the first player shapes a tiny imaginary orange and passes it.
 2) The receiver expresses the orange slightly larger than before and passes it to another player.
 3) Players use body language and expressive acting to depict the orange growing increasingly larger.
 4) A player receives a penalty if they fail to depict the growing weight/size or portray it smaller than the received size.
pe-06743:
1) Stand with feet apart, place one hand on the waist, and extend the other hand up and down 4 times each.
 2) Connect alternating arm reaches upward and forward 4 times each.
 3) Bend knees slightly and sway side to side twice as if playing guitar.
 4) Place hands by the mouth and step forward 4 paces calling out before returning.
 5) Step sideways with large overhead claps, then cross-extend arms and legs in place.
 6) Link hip waves and arm reaches from side to side and complete the full routine to the song.
pe-06744:
1) Serve by throwing the ball over the net from the 3m line.
 2) Receive the first ball either on a bounce or without a bounce.
 3) Catch the second ball, run toward the net, and throw it up to set.
 4) Spike the third ball; score 2 points if connected without a bounce, or 1 point if connected after a bounce.
pe-06745:
1) Students sit at desks and stand up one by one calling out consecutive numbers.
 2) If two students stand simultaneously or fail to call until the end, they perform squats.
 3) In the popcorn variation, students pop up right after the previous one sits back down.
pe-06746:
1) Set up 3 throwing lines using towels and cardboard cores.
 2) Throw a paper plate flying disc from each spot to knock down paper cups and balloons.
 3) Knock down all targets within 1 minute while performing 1 squat after each throw to beat the time.
pe-06747:
1) Follow the teacher's chant ("Papaya, Papaya") while swaying arms and body.
 2) After shouting "Ooh~", the teacher instantly transforms into a specific pose (banana, pineapple, hamburger, helicopter, etc.).
 3) Any student making the exact same pose as the teacher is eliminated and must sit down.
pe-06748:
1) Players play dodgebee while balancing candy on the back of their hands.
 2) If hit by the dodgebee or if the candy falls, the player is eliminated.
 3) Players aim to survive until the end without dropping the candy.
pe-06749:
1) The kicker kicks the ball and runs around the base loop to score.
 2) If the runner completes extra laps before the defense retrieves the ball, extra points are awarded.
 3) If the defense catches a fly ball or records an out, the defensive team also scores 1 point.
pe-06750:
1) Roll A4 paper and fold the tip to make two paper rockets.
 2) Perform one squat and launch both paper rockets upward.
 3) Catch both launched paper rockets at the same time to score 1 point.
 4) No points are awarded if only one or none is caught, and challenge your best score.
pe-06751:
1) Step 1: Hit a balloon upward 3 times consecutively using a handheld ball.
 2) Step 2: Hit the balloon, wrap the ball around the back/body once, and hit it again.
 3) Step 3: Pass the ball between the legs after each hit, and Step 4: Toss and catch the ball in the air between balloon hits.
pe-06752:
1) Sit on the floor and raise your legs to a 90-degree angle.
 2) Hold a roll of toilet paper and pass it side to side beneath the raised legs, touching the floor.
 3) Complete the designated number of repetitions within the set time without losing posture.
pe-06753:
1) Team members jog or walk together in a single-file line.
 2) The ball is passed from the front person progressively backwards to the last person.
 3) The last person receives the ball and sprints to the very front to become the new leader.
pe-06754:
1) Form a circle and look down at your own feet.
 2) On the count of 'one, two, three', look up and stare directly at another person.
