 3) If two players make mutual eye contact, both run to touch the classroom wall and sit down.
pe-06755:
1) Cross two ropes and make a simple overhand knot.
 2) Take the rope resting on top, place it over the other again, and tie once more to create a symmetrical knot.
 3) Pull the short end firmly to quickly release the knot when needed.
pe-06756:
1) The first player bounces a balloon using 3 different body parts such as head, shoulder, knee, or foot.
 2) The second player watches and replicates the exact sequence of body parts to bounce the balloon.
 3) As rounds progress, increase the challenge to 4 and 5 body parts sequentially.
pe-06757:
1) Spread the numbered cups from 1 to 12 across the desk or floor.
 2) On the start signal, stack the cups in numerical sequence from floor 1 to floor 12.
 3) After completing the 12th floor, dismantle the tower by taking cups down one by one from the top.
pe-06758:
1) Write down your birthday (month and day) on a whiteboard beforehand.
 2) Shoot a basketball toward the hoop from the spot marker.
 3) If the ball goes in, collect your birthday number.
 4) The player or team that completes their birthday numbers first wins.
pe-06759:
1) Place spot markers with designated point values on the floor.
 2) Throw disc cones from behind the starting line like flying discs.
 3) Score the points on the spot marker if the cone lands on and covers it.
 4) The team with the highest accumulated score after throwing all cones wins.
pe-06760:
1) Balance a saucer cone on the head as a crown and walk to avoid the tagged chaser.
 2) If the cone drops or a player steps out of bounds, kneel down on one knee.
 3) A teammate can revive the player by picking up the crown and placing it back on their head.
pe-06761:
1) On the start signal, pick up one piece of equipment (treasure) scattered on the floor.
 2) Hold the item overhead with both hands and run to the treasure island.
 3) Place it down and sprint back and forth until all treasures are moved.
pe-06762:
1) Three teams play; the attacking team calls a defending team's color and hits the Kin-Ball toward the tchoukball frame.
 2) The attacking team can make up to two passes before shooting at the goal.
 3) The called team concedes a point if they fail to catch the rebounding ball before it hits the floor.
pe-06763:
1) Players run out one by one from the starting line to stack cones facing alternately.
 2) Stack the cones up to 10 stories high to complete the tower and sprint back.
 3) If the tower collapses, rebuild it from where it fell before continuing.
pe-06764:
1) Both teams wear pinnies and secretly assign King or Queen cards to designated runners.
 2) The game starts with a center tap, and players advance toward the end zone by passing or running with the ball.
 3) Defenders stop attackers by pulling the ball carrier's flag or tagging them.
 4) Scoring a try by touching the ball down past the opposing end line earns 1 basic point.
 5) If the player holding the King card scores a try, the team earns bonus points.
pe-06765:
1) About 10 students stand at a safe distance and choose their own unique jump poses.
 2) On the teacher's count of 'One, Two, Three', all students leap into the air simultaneously.
 3) The teacher takes a photo to verify whether everyone's feet are completely off the ground.
 4) If anyone's foot is touching the ground, the attempt fails, and the group retries until all are airborne.
pe-06766:
1) Line up paper cups filled with water.
 2) Blow air from your mouth to make a table tennis ball skim across the cups.
 3) Upon reaching the final cup, perform 2 push-ups and return.
 4) The person who first completes 4 rounds wins.
pe-06767:
1) Cut the bottom of a paper cup and attach a cut balloon to create a cannon.
 2) Insert a table tennis ball and release the pulled balloon to launch.
 3) The facing partner catches the launched ball to earn 1 point.
pe-06768:
1) All students start at Level 1 (Mouse) and play rock-paper-scissors with peers of the same level while making animal sounds and gestures.
 2) Winners advance to the next level (Level 2 Cat, Level 3 Tiger, Level 4 Hunter), while losers drop down one level.
 3) Students who win at Level 4 become Level 5 Angels and rush to give the teacher a high five.
pe-06769:
1) Hook the ring with a fun stick and dribble zigzag through the cones.
 2) Turn around the cone and pass the ring toward the next waiting runner.
 3) The next runner controls the ring with their foot, hooks it with the stick, and starts.
pe-06770:
1) Place one or two stacking cups on top of an elongated inflated balloon.
 2) Gently shake the balloon so the cup slides forward from start to finish line.
 3) If the cup falls, replace it at the dropped distance mark and continue.
 4) In pairs, one student performs the challenge while the partner acts as judge.
pe-06771:
1) Stack two cups together and hold the bottom cup.
 2) Toss the bottom cup to flip it and catch, or toss the top cup vertically to catch it into the bottom cup.
 3) Practice repeatedly to improve hand-eye coordination.
pe-06772:
1) The batter punches the ball with a fist and runs to 1st and 3rd bases.
 2) If the defense catches the ball in the air, the batter is out immediately.
 3) On a ground ball, fielders throw the ball from outside the zone to knock down a center bowling pin.
 4) If the pin falls before the runner reaches the base, the runner is out.
pe-06773:
1) Place scooter boards on opposite sides of a parachute, and two riders sit on the boards.
 2) The remaining students hold the edges of the parachute all around.
 3) On the signal, students holding the parachute rotate slowly in a circle, gliding the scooter riders along the floor.
pe-06774:
1) Fasten a long rope securely to an ankle jump rope so it does not come loose.
 2) One player rotates the extended rope low around in the center.
 3) Multiple participants time the swing from the opposite side and jump in one by one.
 4) Anyone who trips on the rope alternates to turning the rope or performs an assigned exercise task.
pe-06775:
1) Follow teacher cues or screen poses from sitting or lying positions.
 2) When the whistle sounds, stand up as quickly as possible and freeze in attention stance.
 3) Score points if you stand up and finish the stance before the teacher does.
pe-06776:
1) Treat the beanbag as a fragile egg and carefully toss and catch it with a partner.
 2) Whenever both partners successfully toss and catch, both take one step backward.
 3) If either partner drops the beanbag, both take one step forward and resume throwing.
pe-06777:
1) Arrange 7 numbered spot markers on each side in an identical pattern facing each other.
 2) The leader performs a series of jumping steps on the markers to a 4-beat rhythm.
 3) The partner faces the leader like a mirror and imitates the exact 4-beat stepping sequence.
pe-06778:
1) All students move around the play area while balancing a mini cone (battery) on the back of their hand.
 2) The tagger chases players and tries to knock the battery off their hands.
 3) When a player's battery falls, they must freeze; another teammate can revive them by placing it back, and the class wins if enough survive the time limit.
pe-06779:
1) Each student picks a number card and scatters across the hall.
 2) On the signal, students call out their numbers to locate their matching partner.
 3) Once paired, they place cards down and complete assigned partner exercises (jumping jacks, foot rock-paper-scissors, hand-held turns).
pe-06780:
1) Flip the saucer cone with fingers to make it stand upright on the desk.
 2) Stand up and bounce the table tennis ball once to land it inside the upside-down saucer cone.
 3) Walk to the classroom wall and touch it each time a step is completed.
 4) Return to the start if touching or bumping into another student while moving.
 5) Finish within the top 8 out of 15 students to win.
pe-06781:
1) Place spot markers of green (1 pt), yellow (2 pts), and red (3 pts) on the floor.
 2) The batter hits the ball with a fist, steps on one of the colored markers, and returns home to score that marker's points.
 3) The fielding team gets the batter out by catching a fly ball directly or by throwing the ball to the catcher before the runner returns home.
pe-06782:
1) Scatter and shuffle numbered spot markers from 1 to 10 face-down on the floor.
 2) In teams of two, runner 1 dashes out to place dish cones on markers 1 through 10 in sequential order.
 3) Once cone 10 is placed, runner 2 sprints out to collect the cones in order starting from number 1, competing for faster time.
pe-06783:
1) The first runner sprints toward the turning point holding the ball.
 2) Turn around and run directly to the back of the team line.
 3) All team members spread their legs wide, and the runner rolls the ball through their legs to the front.
 4) The front player catches the ball and repeats the sequence until all four finish.
pe-06784:
1) Form pairs where one player holds a hula hoop and the other throws a soft flying disc.
 2) The hoop holder adjusts their position to make the thrown disc pass cleanly through the hoop.
 3) With each success, step back to increase the distance and aim for a hole-in-one.
pe-06785:
1) Place 5 table tennis balls inside a container and spin your wrist to keep them circling inside without dropping.
 2) Maintain the spin and move toward the destination container.
 3) The team that successfully transfers all 5 balls into the goal container first wins.
pe-06786:
1) Hold a stacking cup and a table tennis ball in each hand.
 2) Toss both table tennis balls upward at the same time and catch them with the opposite hand's cup.
 3) Score full points (100 or 200) for catching both, or partial points (50 or 100) for catching one.
pe-06787:
1) Place several beanbags inside a hula hoop to prepare.
 2) Grip one beanbag between both feet at a time and jump to move it outside the hoop.
 3) After taking all out, jump them back inside the hoop one by one using both feet and shout done.
pe-06788:
1) Form a group of four where two players hold hands to create a circle with their arms.
 2) The other two players use rackets to rally a fleece ball back and forth through the circle.
 3) After achieving the target number of hits, switch roles and try again.
pe-06789:
1) Two players stand facing each other and play rock-paper-scissors.
 2) Only the loser spreads their feet shoulder-width apart, and if they lose again, kneels on one knee.
 3) With consecutive losses, players transition to kneeling, mermaid sit, and extending legs until lying down completely to win.
pe-06790:
1) Line up 6 cups on the floor approximately 1 to 1.5 meters in front of the players.
 2) Sit on the floor and bounce a table tennis ball once so that it lands inside one of the cups.
 3) Collect and stack each cup the ball lands in, and the first player to collect all 6 cups wins.
pe-06791:
1) Each team secretly designates one Prince (or Princess) and informs only the referee.
 2) Play regular dodgeball and attempt to eliminate opposing players by throwing the ball.
 3) Regular players are eliminated when hit, but if the hidden Prince/Princess is hit, that entire team loses immediately.
pe-06792:
1) Place multiple beanbags at one end of the mat and a target box at the opposite end.
 2) Roll sideways with the body straight or perform forward rolls across the mat.
 3) Pick up a beanbag after rolling and transport it to the opposite target area.
pe-06793:
1) One thrower and two to three catchers line up facing the same forward direction.
 2) When the thrower flies the disc forward, the runners sprint ahead together.
 3) The runner who tracks the disc down and catches it first earns a point.
pe-06794:
1) Each student prepares 12 cups and faces the game leader.
 2) Everyone plays Rock-Paper-Scissors simultaneously against the leader.
 3) Winners stack 2 cups, ties stack 1 cup, and losers cannot stack any cups.
 4) If the cup tower collapses during stacking, restart from the very beginning.
 5) The first person to successfully stack all 12 cups wins the round.
pe-06795:
1) Cut a hole in a box lid for a ball to fit through and place an egg tray underneath.
 2) Place 10 table tennis balls inside the box lid.
 3) Tilt the box lid with both hands to drop the balls through the black hole.
 4) Any ball that bounces outside must be put back; the first to drop all 10 balls into the egg tray wins.
pe-06796:
1) Arrange 5 spot markers on the floor in the traditional pumpkin gonu diagram.
 2) Divide into two teams of 2 players who stand on the markers as human pieces.
 3) Teams take turns moving one player along the connected lines to an adjacent vacant marker.
 4) The team that completely blocks all valid paths of the opposing team wins.
pe-06797:
1) Form teams of three players each to play.
 2) Defend by lifting and supporting the ball before it drops to the floor.
 3) Cooperate with all three team members to serve and attack during gameplay.
pe-06798:
1) Serve the ball over the net into the opposing court.
 2) Pass and set the ball within the team before sending it back across the net.
 3) Pushing or throwing the ball instead of striking it results in a foul and awards one point to the opponents.
pe-06799:
1) Form groups of three, with the middle player holding a hula hoop as the Shark.
 2) The two outside players pass the ball using bounce or lob passes while avoiding the hoop.
 3) If the ball touches the hoop or passes through its opening, the thrower swaps roles with the Shark.
pe-06800:
1) Sit in a circle on the floor with each participant holding one beanbag.
 2) Practice the 5-step rhythm: 1) catch/hold,
 2) tap left knee,
 3) tap right knee,
 4) toss to the peer on the left,
 5) clap.
 3) Repeat the 5 rhythm movements in unison to music or chants, continuously passing beanbags around the circle.
pe-06801:
1) In groups of four, each student writes numbers 1 through 49 randomly on a sheet without empty spaces and turns it face down.
 2) Determine player turns by rock-paper-scissors and rotate papers so everyone holds another player's paper.
 3) When player 1 calls out a number, that player circles it while the other three quickly locate and cross it out.
 4) Until all three players say "Found it," the caller quickly marks X's on their own sheet to fill their squares.
 5) The first player to mark all squares on their sheet wins first place.
pe-06802:
1) After hitting the ball, the batter runs continuously without being called out, scoring 1 point at first base, 2 at second, 3 at third, and 4 at home.
 2) The fielding team catches the ball and passes it among teammates toward home plate.
 3) The batter continues scoring until the fielder at home catches the ball and shouts stop.
pe-06803:
1) Shuffle 12 numbered cups from 1 to 12 by swapping positions with a partner.
 2) Place hands on head and, at the start signal, locate cup number 1 first.
 3) Rapidly stack cups in numerical order from 1 to 12; the fastest to complete wins.
pe-06804:
1) Prepare 12 stacking cups by placing them in two stacks of 6.
 2) Stand up and hold the cups on both sides, then pull them outward.
 3) If the upper cup falls directly and nests into the lower cup, it is a success.
 4) Challenge yourself to set a record within a set time or target number of successes.
pe-06805:
1) Players occupy four squares numbered 1 through 4 while waiting players line up outside.
 2) The player in square 4 serves the ball using an overhead pass to start the rally.
 3) Players return the ball using underhand passes, and if a player faults, they leave the court and lower-ranked players promote forward.
pe-06806:
1) All students start at Level 1 sitting (or lying) on the floor.
 2) Play rock-paper-scissors against the teacher; only students who win advance to the next level.
 3) Progress through levels: Level 1 sitting, Level 2 kneeling, Level 3 sitting on chair, Level 4 standing on chair, Level 5 perching on desk (or raising hands).
 4) See who reaches and completes the final level first.
pe-06807:
1) Set up a makeshift basket made of a hanger and plastic bag on a door or wall.
 2) Perform 3 squats, then shoot a ping pong ball or sock ball into the basket.
 3) Score 10 points each time the ball goes into the basket.
pe-06808:
1) Two teams of 4 face each other across a desk net.
 2) All four teammates must touch the ball once each after one bounce.
 3) On the mandatory fourth touch, send the ball across the net to the opponent's court.
 4) Failing to achieve all touches before returning concedes 1 point, and the team does 1 squat together.
pe-06809:
1) Wear a cone inverted over the forearms where the volleyball makes contact.
 2) As the partner tosses a beanbag, step into the proper underarm bump pass stance.
 3) Step forward and catch the incoming beanbag directly inside the inverted cone, then switch roles.
pe-06810:
1) Set up team bases with dish cones and tape two rough paper sheets to each player's front and back.
 2) Each team secretly elects a king and fills water guns using 10 limited PET bottles per team.
 3) Shoot water guns to soak or detach enemy paper sheets; the team that eliminates the enemy king wins.
pe-06811:
1) Set up four goals in a rectangular court and place two balls inside each goal.
 2) Divide into two teams with team vests, take out balls from goals on signal, and dribble or pass.
 3) Score 1 point by putting a ball into an opponent goal, update the scoreboard, and the team with more points when time expires wins.
pe-06812:
1) Form groups of four, set the order, and place two hoops side by side in front of the starting line.
 2) The first player serves the shuttlecock into the far hoop and retrieves it.
 3) If successful, move the nearer hoop further back to increase the distance.
 4) The group that advances the farthest within the set time wins.
pe-06813:
1) Form two teams of 4 players each and begin play with a serve from 2.5 meters behind the net.
 2) Return the ball within 5 contacts using only the feet or head.
 3) Players may catch the ball by hand and bounce it once if difficult, but crossing the net requires a foot or head shot.
 4) Score 1 point if the ball bounces twice on the opponent's court or if they fail to return within 5 touches.
 5) The first team to win 3 sets of 15 points wins the match.
pe-06814:
1) Set up a batting tee and mark lines at 10m (infield) and another 10m beyond (outfield).
 2) Form teams of 4 players and establish a batting order.
 3) Hit the ball off the tee: 1 point for the infield zone and 2 points for the outfield zone.
 4) Each player hits 5 times before rotating, and the team with the highest combined score wins.
pe-06815:
1) A kicker kicks a ball from the kicking spot toward zones marked at 5-meter intervals (1 to 5 points) away from defenders.
 2) The team scores points corresponding to where the ball lands, earning 1 point even on ground balls.
 3) If a defender passes the kicked ball through a hula hoop, the kicker is called out and scores no points; the team with the higher score wins.
pe-06816:
1) The fielding team assesses the kicker's tendencies and places floor markers corresponding to their player count.
 2) Every fielder must stand with at least one foot on their designated marker before the kick.
 3) The kicker kicks the pitched ball and runs toward the bases.
 4) Catches in the air or force outs at bases result in an out; catching a grounder while touching a marker causes an immediate out.
 5) Grounders fielded without touching a marker follow standard kickball throw-and-force rules.
 6) All team members kick per inning, and the team with more runs after two innings wins.
pe-06817:
1) Walk the course in advance while plogging to become familiar with the route.
 2) Learn correct running posture, arm movement, and breathing techniques in class and practice inside the school.
 3) Head out the back gate in two lines and run the 1.1km course together.
 4) Return to school upon completing the course and perform cool-down stretches.
pe-06818:
1) Teams determine their running order at the starting line, while 3 target cones with 3 stacked rings (or school supplies) are set at the finish line.
 2) On signal, the first runner sprints to the cones and moves exactly one disc to another cone.
 3) The runner returns to tag the next teammate's hand at the starting line before the next runner departs.
 4) Follow Hanoi rules strictly: move only one disc per turn, and never place a larger disc onto a smaller one.
 5) The first team to transfer the entire tower to the far-right cone wins the race.
pe-06819:
1) Place five spot markers in a pentagon, form a team of three, and stand skipping one marker each.
 2) Player 1 runs to the next marker and passes the ball to Player 2, who catches it, runs to the next marker, and passes to Player 3.
 3) Count successful passes in 1 minute, or race between two teams to see who completes 5 laps first.
pe-06820:
1) Lay out red and blue flip boards evenly across the court and divide participants into two teams with balls.
 2) When the game begins, step on an opponent's board and bounce the ball on the floor 5 times.
 3) After successfully bouncing 5 times, stop the ball and flip the board to your team's color.
 4) The team with the most boards of their color when time expires wins.
pe-06821:
1) Separate basic movement skill cards (blue) and movement concept cards (green) face down.
 2) The teacher draws one blue card and one green card.
 3) The teacher announces and explains the two drawn cards to the students.
 4) Students follow and express the combined movement creatively according to their imagination without fixed answers.
pe-06822:
1) Place a table tennis ball into an egg carton slot.
 2) Flick or bounce the ball sequentially from one slot to the adjacent slot.
 3) Measure the time it takes to navigate the ball across all 30 slots.
 4) Advance by lining up multiple balls in a row and shifting them line by line.
pe-06823:
1) Place three paper cups along a tilted table like dominoes with the wide lip positioned higher.
 2) Tap the first cup so it rolls and knocks down subsequent cups into the target box.
 3) If a cup drops and fails, set it aside and run to the distant cup storage station.
 4) Bring replacement cups, perform two jumping jacks, set up the cups again, and repeat until successful.
pe-06824:
1) Kneel facing each other on the mat and grip the satba or waist belt.
 2) Raise the left knee, stand up together, and bend forward into the ready stance.
 3) On command, practice hand and leg skills such as knee tapping, inner-thigh pull, and outside leg hook.
pe-06825:
1) From the soccer goal on the field, walk with long strides to draw a line based on age-appropriate distance.
 2) Kick the ball from behind the line toward the soccer goal.
 3) The ball must hit the goalpost itself (top or sides) rather than entering the goal to count as a success.
pe-06826:
1) Insert fingers into the ball holes and lean forward into the ready stance.
 2) Gradually increase stride across four steps, raising the arm back on the third step.
 3) Slide the final foot and use arm momentum to roll the ball close to the floor.
pe-06827:
1) Divide each team into 2 attackers and 2 defenders by playing rock-paper-scissors.
 2) Give 20 gonggi stones in a basket to each group.
 3) Attackers take 1 gonggi stone from their basket and challenge defenders of other groups to rock-paper-scissors.
 4) If an attacker wins, they take 1 stone from the defender and put it into their own basket; if the defender wins, they take the attacker's stone.
 5) If attackers lose their stone, they must return to their group basket to pick up another one before challenging again.
 6) When time is up, count the gonggi stones in each basket and the team with the most stones wins.
pe-06828:
1) Pair up students and have each pair play soccer while holding hands.
 2) If holding hands is uncomfortable, partners can hold either end of a short baton or handkerchief.
 3) If partners let go of their hands during play, they must go to the sideline and count from 1 to 50 before returning.
pe-06829:
1) The kicker kicks the ball off a cone, circles their seated team twice, and touches the offensive base
 2) The fielder who catches the ball sits down and all fielders line up behind to pass the ball overhead to the back
 3) The last fielder runs to touch the defensive base; if touched before the runner, or if caught on the fly, the runner is out
pe-06830:
1) Three players play Rock-Paper-Scissors to assign roles: 1st place is the VIP, 2nd is the bodyguard, and 3rd is the stalker (tagger).
 2) The bodyguard and the stalker grip left hands like arm wrestling, while the VIP and bodyguard hold their remaining hands together.
 3) When the game begins, the bodyguard maneuvers to physically block the stalker from touching the VIP.
 4) The stalker attempts to maneuver around the bodyguard and tag the VIP within 10 seconds.
 5) Switch roles and continue the activity once the VIP is tagged or the time limit expires.
pe-06831:
1) Divide into three color teams (Yellow, Blue, Green) and two kickers kick two balls simultaneously.
 2) The kickers immediately run around their waiting team line and return to the start.
 3) Each fielding team retrieves the ball matching their vest color and passes it home.
 4) Points are awarded based on finish order: 1st gets 3 points, 2nd gets 2 points, 3rd gets 1 point.
pe-06832:
1) Place hula hoops on the opposite court and stand at the service line.
 2) Toss the ball slightly and hit the lower underside of the ball with a fist to perform an underhand serve.
 3) Score 2 points if the serve lands inside a hula hoop, and 1 point if it lands in the court outside the hoops.
 4) Each player attempts 3 serves, and the team with the highest combined total score wins.
pe-06833:
1) Form pairs and face each other about 10 meters apart.
 2) Practice 5 throwing techniques: backhand, forehand, hammer, chicken wing, and air bounce.
 3) Challenge to complete back-and-forth passes from technique 1 to 5 consecutively without dropping.
pe-06834:
1) Set up a 3x3 bingo board on the wall and divide into two teams.
 2) Take turns throwing a flying disc toward the board from 7 to 8 meters away.
 3) Mark hit squares, and the team that completes a line horizontally, vertically, or diagonally first wins.
pe-06835:
1) Two turners hold and swing a long jump rope.
 2) The jumper enters the swinging long rope while holding an individual jump rope.
 3) The jumper skips both the long rope and their own jump rope simultaneously.
pe-06836:
1) Complete individual technique challenges across 16 court spots to complete a line on the bingo card.
 2) In teams of 5 to 8, take shots for 1 minute using two balls while teammates box out and secure rebounds before the ball touches the floor.
 3) Play a scrimmage completing designated team tasks (screens, fast breaks, rebounds) on the bingo board to score points.
pe-06837:
1) Form a large circle using spot markers; one team stands inside and two teams sit around the outside.
 2) Outside players slide beanbags along the floor to hit the feet of inside players, who jump to dodge.
 3) Hit players run around the outer circle once to respawn, and roles switch after 2 minutes.
pe-06838:
1) Start on signal with the ball, move to the dribble zone, and perform five stationary dribbles quickly.
 2) Move to the pass zone, place the ball on the floor, spin three times with an elephant trunk pose around the ball, and attempt passes until successful.
 3) Pass through the zigzag dribble zone to the shooting zone and shoot until one basket is scored, either finishing the record or tagging the next runner.
pe-06839:
1) Perform push-ups on knees, exploding up with a light hand jump moving alternately left and right.
 2) Take an active walking break, then vigorously swing arms forward and back at high speed.
 3) Perform burpees by squatting hands down, extending legs to a push-up position, pulling knees back in, and jumping up quickly.
 4) Assume a kneeling push-up stance and rapidly shift both hands forward and backward to train upper body power.
pe-06840:
1) Perform standard push-ups keeping the body in a straight line and lowering the chest close to the floor.
 2) Lift hips high into a pike position and bend elbows to execute pike push-ups.
 3) Lean upper body slightly more forward and perform elbow-focused push-ups for core and upper body.
 4) Keep elbows on the ground and lift hips upward into a reverse-style plank to strengthen shoulders.
 5) Clench fists firmly and curl wrists inward repeatedly to strengthen forearm and wrist muscles.
pe-06841:
1) In Catch It Badminton, a player serves with bare hands, and the receiver catches it and throws it back outside the service line within 3 seconds.
 2) A point is lost if the shuttlecock hits the floor, with advanced variations allowing touches with any body part before grounding.
 3) In Court Cleaner Badminton, 9 shuttlecocks are set on each side, and players throw them across the net upon the start signal.
 4) Throwing with two hands, throwing multiple shuttles at once, or tossing under the net counts as a foul; fewer shuttles after 30 seconds wins.
pe-06842:
1) Two players face each other, place cones 15 steps behind each, and lie prone facing each other.
 2) Play rock-paper-scissors: the winner dashes to their cone, while the loser tries to tag their shoulder.
 3) For group play, 4 to 6 students form a circle and each choose a dice number.
 4) Roll the dice; the chosen player becomes the tagger for 30 seconds, and tagged players do 5 jumping jacks.
pe-06843:
1) Step on stairs using full foot contact while keeping chest and back straight.
 2) Compete 1-on-1 using varying tasks such as squats, two-step rapid climbs, or taking two steps at once.
 3) Play rock-paper-scissors to advance stairs (scissors 2 steps, rock 1 step, paper 5 steps) to reach the top first.
pe-06844:
1) Stand in front of a wall, toss the ball up, and spike it downward toward the floor.
 2) Practice catching or repeatedly spiking the ball as it rebounds off the wall.
 3) Form a single line where each player spikes off the floor to the wall, steps aside, and the next player spikes after one bounce.
pe-06845:
1) Learn basic pen strokes: wrist strike (A), pen head tap (B), and full pen flat strike (C).
 2) Combine the basic techniques to play 4-beat, 8-beat, and 16-beat rhythms on the desk.
 3) Learn hand-beat moves like palms down, crossed palms, clapping, and back of hand to perform together.
pe-06846:
1) Set up four adjacent square courts of about ten paces each; players 1 to 4 enter a square while players 5 and 6 wait outside.
 2) Player 1 bounces the volleyball once and hits it with hands to serve to player 3.
 3) Players let the incoming ball bounce once and hit it with one or two hands into another player's court.
 4) Catching the ball, letting it double bounce, hitting out of bounds, or touching with body parts other than hands causes elimination to the waiting queue.
 5) When someone makes a fault, the other three players each earn 1 point, and the first to reach 15 points wins.
pe-06847:
1) Prepare one flying disc per person and warm up with circular motion disc activities.
 2) Practice basic defensive stances through individual and partner scarecrow defense drills.
 3) Complete the six-player pass challenge and moving pass challenge consecutively.
 4) Line up facing each other in groups of three to practice Give & Go six-player relay and three-player square passing drills.
 5) Compete in 3v3 or 6v6 games using only pivots within 10 seconds to reach 15 cumulative passes first to win.
pe-06848:
1) Warm up with shoulder preparatory exercises and stretches to release upper body tension.
 2) Spread feet twice shoulder-width, lower the hips, and practice catching grounders by covering the ball with the bare hand.
 3) Judge the drop point of fly balls and practice catching overhead at a safe angle.
 4) Practice throwing a ball against a wall from 3 to 5 meters away at chest and upper levels, catching the rebound individually and in teams.
 5) Form groups of four to take turns catching rebounds and alternating throws against the wall to complete two relay cycles first to win.
pe-06849:
1) Warm up with a disc passing ring game where runners race against a passed disc around a circle.
 2) Practice cardinal pivot rotations on the left pivot foot and a random directional call reaction challenge.
 3) Execute a 5-step relay passing the disc exclusively via pivots into a bin, followed by a 4-player catching drill.
 4) Practice backhand and forehand pivot throws with deep lunges over a 10-meter distance in pairs and quads.
 5) Play Disc Hunter in groups of 4 with 2 attackers and 2 defenders, attempting end-zone passes over 5 rounds to score points.
pe-06850:
1) Practice tossing a team pinny high overhead in place and catching it with both hands.
 2) In pairs 3 meters apart, both toss pinnies overhead and sprint forward to catch each other's falling pinny.
 3) Each time successful, move the spot markers one step back to widen the distance and try with 3 students running clockwise.
pe-06851:
1) Throw-and-Catch Table Tennis is played 2 vs 2 without paddles, serving and catching by hand and throwing back within 3 seconds.
 2) Passing to teammates is forbidden, dropping the ball loses a point, and the game plays to 10 points.
 3) Catch-and-Drop Table Tennis is played 3 vs 3 facing each other 2 vs 1, hitting and receiving the ball with paddles.
 4) Teams play for 1 minute to put balls into their cup using paddles without touching them with hands, and the team with the most balls wins.
pe-06852:
1) Make a makeshift lifebuoy by securely tying a hula hoop and a long jump rope twice with a basic knot.
 2) Spread beanbags on the floor at a certain distance.
 3) Stand at the designated spot, throw the makeshift lifebuoy, and the team that rescues the most beanbags wins.
pe-06853:
1) Perform high-knee explosion drills on each side by driving the knee up and extending back.
 2) Practice shooting pumping motions repeatedly on the spot using knees and arm extension without a ball.
 3) Jump to grab simulated rebounds with one or both hands, then land and pivot.
 4) Practice left-right fake and jump moves, as well as step-back shooting motions.
 5) Follow footwork patterns for crossover, behind-the-back, and reverse dribbling.
pe-06854:
1) Two players face each other inside a 3m circle and hit a balloon once using body parts other than arms and hands to score inside the circle.
 2) Set up 3m courts across a net and play balloon jokgu by returning the balloon within two touches.
 3) Start with a header from 5m away and keep the balloon up to score into a mini goal first.
pe-06855:
1) Learn the up-rhythm by bending and straightening knees, and the down-rhythm by straightening then bending knees.
 2) Practice the kick step by lifting the knee and kicking forward as if kicking a door so the body pushes back.
 3) Complete the shuffle step (running man) by landing on the ball of the foot with straight legs and running arm motions.
 4) Learn and combine the T-step by shifting weight across heel and toe pivots to move sideways.
pe-06856:
1) Divide into runners and 2-4 taggers, each holding a disc like a pizza on one hand while walking, with taggers trying to knock down runners' discs.
 2) Throw the disc from the goal line to cross the center line in the air at least twice.
 3) Complete at least 6 running passes in pairs, run around cones, and place pinnies to form a line on a 3x3 bingo grid.
 4) Three players maintain spacing, passing only from a complete stop to complete a round trip without dropping the disc.
 5) In 7-on-7 Ultimate, every team member must touch the disc at least once for a score to count.
pe-06857:
1) Tap the right foot forward, bring the other foot together, step back while extending and retracting arms, then step aside and shake hips four times.
 2) Step to the side and return while flapping arms like wings, then step forward and backward with the right foot while swinging arms.
 3) Stand with feet apart, bump hips to the right eight times while punching forward, crossing, and opening arms.
 4) Step forward with the right foot and wipe sweat, return to position, and repeat all movements continuously to the music.
pe-06858:
1) Form teams of three, determine order, and assign roles of hitter, fielder, and first baseman.
 2) The hitter hits a tennis ball with a tennis racket, the fielder catches and throws to first base, and the first baseman catches it.
 3) Each successful catch scores one point, and the team with the most points within the time limit wins.
pe-06859:
1) Stand in a circle and roll a die twice.
 2) The first roll determines the movement and the second roll indicates the number of repetitions.
 3) The student who rolled demonstrates the action, and the others stretch by repeating it that many times.
pe-06860:
1) Divide the court into 3 to 6 identical zones using line tape and assign different point values to each zone.
 2) Play regular volleyball until one team reaches 15 points, which activates the zone scoring system for the trailing team.
 3) When the trailing team ties or takes the lead, the zone scoring system applies to both teams equally.
pe-06861:
1) Play on a half court and decide offense and defense through rock-paper-scissors or free throws.
 2) The defensive team bounces a basketball from a designated box near the endline.
 3) The offensive team predicts the ball path and rebounds the ball on its second bounce.
 4) The player who secures the rebound shoots toward the basket directly from that spot to score.
 5) The team that reaches the target score first or scores more points wins.
pe-06862:
1) Draw a large square divided by four crossing lanes and form two teams of four attackers and four defenders.
 2) Defenders occupy the crossroad lanes (one per lane) while all attackers start inside Room 1.
 3) Attackers visit Rooms 2, 3, and 4 without stepping into the defenders' lanes and exit to score 1 point.
 4) When skirting outside rooms, chant "Ho-Tteok-Jjin-Bbang" taking one step per syllable (four steps total).
 5) Defenders stay within their lanes and tag passing attackers to get them out during a 5-minute round.
pe-06863:
1) Conduct thorough warm-up exercises and learn how to properly put on a life jacket before entering the pool.
 2) Splash water over the body before entering to adapt to the cold water temperature.
 3) Enter the pool for warm-up movements, practicing rhythmic breathing and basic floating postures.
 4) Practice survival floating techniques such as the leaf float or using available floating objects to retain body heat.
pe-06864:
1) Team members assign specific body-contact roles to each person, such as hand, foot, and head.
 2) The serving team clearly and loudly calls out the required sequence (e.g., Hand-Head-Foot) as they serve the ball.
 3) The receiving team must listen carefully and contact the ball in that exact designated order for 3 hits before returning it.
 4) Failure to call out the order on serve, contacting out of sequence, touching twice consecutively, or missing 3 hits results in lost points.
pe-06865:
1) Form a circle and bounce or toss a basketball before sliding sideways to catch the adjacent peer's ball.
 2) Complete a 5-step solo challenge including tossing the ball high to clap 7 times and underhand tosses.
 3) Face a partner with two balls to exchange alternating passes and bounce balls together in mid-air.
 4) Play basketball volleyball where 5 teammates bounce a soft dodgeball into the air using their basketballs.
 5) Play pass tag where players cannot run with the ball and must tag opposing runners solely by passing to open teammates.
pe-06866:
1) Set bowling pins in the center circle and have students stand on spot markers with a soft ball each.
 2) Kick the ball with the inside of the foot like a push pass to knock down the bowling pins.
 3) If the ball rolls away, retrieve it, return to the marker, and record the team time taken to knock down all pins.
pe-06867:
1) Split the group into pairs and form an inner circle and an outer circle.
 2) The inner circle walks left and the outer circle walks right using fundamental movements.
 3) When the teacher calls Warriors, Kings, or Horses, find your partner and hold the designated statue pose.
 4) On the Scram call, the outer circle flees while inner circle partners chase and try to tag them within 10 seconds.
pe-06868:
1) Walk in various pathways including zigzag, spirals, backwards, and sideways while making eye contact and giving high-fives.
 2) Freeze on call, jump, and make your body form the first letter of your name upon landing.
 3) Gather tight and shake hands, then play drum/bongo motions in front and around you.
 4) Widen legs, look down, swing arms, and stomp around to the beat.
 5) Freeze and bounce to the beat while playing imaginary drums all around and with peers.
pe-06869:
1) Two players lie on the floor side by side facing opposite directions with their elbows and hips locked.
 2) Keep the inside hand placed firmly on your own chest to prevent arm injuries.
 3) On the referee's count, both players raise and lower their inside legs in cadence.
 4) On the final signal, interlock inside legs and push to flip the opponent over.
 5) The player who successfully pushes and flips the opponent wins the round.
pe-06870:
1) Roll a rolled-up sock ball down the body from head to toes 5 times each, and circle it around the torso 5 times in both directions.
 2) Balance the ball on a racket, tilt it for 10 laps each hand, and toss/cushion-catch the ball on the racket surface.
 3) Flip a quarter-filled water bottle a full 360 rotation to land upright 5 times on each hand.
 4) Drop the ball, kick it up with the foot to catch it with hands, progressing to tossing, kicking, and catching.
pe-06871:
1) Divide into two attackers and one defender; attackers pass the ball to get through the gate or reach the end zone.
 2) The defender scores by tagging the ball carrier, while attackers score if they reach the goal untagged.
 3) The supporting attacker without the ball constantly finds open space to receive passes safely.
pe-06872:
1) Two players face each other holding a plank position with drink bottles placed beneath them.
 2) While maintaining the plank, roll a ball with one hand to hit the opponent's drink bottle.
 3) The opponent blocks the ball with one hand and rolls it back toward the other bottle.
 4) Keep holding the plank position even while your partner goes to retrieve the ball.
pe-06873:
1) Hold a front support plank position balancing on hands at the top of a push-up.
 2) Toss a bouncy ball from one hand to the other while maintaining the plank.
 3) Catching it directly or after a bounce counts as one, and count total catches in 1 minute.
pe-06874:
1) Place a folded beach towel in front and start just behind it.
 2) Use an underarm throw to land the sock ball in the center of the towel.
 3) If successful, go and flip the towel forward once.
 4) Keep throwing and flipping the towel to race and see how far you can get.
pe-06875:
1) Place puzzle pieces with exercises (star jumps, push-ups, etc.) on one end and designate the other end as the puzzle-building area.
 2) Run from the start to the puzzle pieces and pick one up.
 3) Complete the designated exercise reps on the card, bring it back, and assemble the puzzle.
pe-06876:
1) Donkey Kick: From a push-up position, lift hips high, kick one foot back, and hold in a straight line.
 2) Table: Sit, place arms behind for support, push hips up to shoulder height, and look up at the ceiling.
 3) Bridge: Lie down, place hands beside head pointing towards toes, and lift body using triceps and shoulders into an arch.
 4) Front Support: Support body on hands and toes keeping a straight line from heels to shoulders.
 5) Back Support: Sit, reach arms back, lift hips into a straight line from heels to shoulders.
pe-06877:
1) Only perform the gymnastic pose if the caller says Simon Says.
 2) If the caller does not say Simon Says and you perform the pose, you are out.
 3) When a player gets out, swap roles and continue the game.
pe-06878:
1) Set up 12 numbered pins in a specific cluster.
 2) Throw the large throwing block to knock down the pins.
 3) If one pin is knocked down, score its face value; if multiple pins fall, score the number of fallen pins.
 4) Stand the fallen pins back up right where they landed.
 5) The first player to reach exactly 50 points wins, but exceeding 50 resets the score to 25.
pe-06879:
1) Keep your eyes on the ball and grip the bat or racket with your preferred hand on top.
 2) Stand side-on to the target and hold the bat behind your shoulder prior to the strike.
 3) Step towards the target with your opposite foot during the strike.
 4) Rotate your hips and shoulders, contact the ball in line with your front foot with straight arms, and follow through around your body.
pe-06880:
1) Place a water bottle (skittle) about one to two meters away from a wall.
 2) Place the ball next to the target and kick it against the wall.
 3) Try to have the rebounding ball knock over the water bottle target.
 4) If successful, move the ball one step further back from the wall and try again.
 5) Add challenge variations by placing an obstacle (such as a bin) in the way, or by changing the size of the target or ball.
pe-06881:
1) Arrange towels of different sizes on the floor layered like a dartboard
 2) Score 1 point for the bare ground, 2 points for the largest mat, 3 and 4 points for inner towels, and 5 points for the center bull's eye
 3) Throw a rolled-up pair of socks from a designated distance and count points based on where the sock lands first
pe-06882:
1) Hold up one hand and use the opposite finger to trace your fingers like mountains
 2) Breathe in deeply through your nose as you move up each finger
 3) Breathe out through your mouth as you move down the other side of each finger
pe-06883:
1) Stand at the tee area holding a golf ball made of crumpled paper.
 2) Throw or strike the ball along the course toward the pin while avoiding hazards such as bunkers and water.
 3) If the ball lands in a bunker, you must throw it over your head to complete the shot.
 4) The player who completes the hole in the fewest throws to achieve par or better wins.
pe-06884:
1) Step on poly spots with a beanbag on the head and hop on one foot to balance
 2) Perform weight transfers such as rolling on mats, side planks, stepper jumps, and bear crawls
 3) Balance noodles vertically or walk on them, and cooperate with a partner to transport a ball on two noodles
pe-06885:
1) Begin with the ball between your feet and perform 30 seconds of dynamic stretching.
 2) Two-Hand Pound: Dribble with both hands as fast as possible for 30 seconds with head up, counting total dribbles.
 3) Single-Hand Pound: Drop low to knee level and pound the ball with fingertips for 30 seconds on each hand, keeping the non-dribbling guard hand up.
 4) Crossovers: Progress through low, medium, and shoulder crossovers for 30 seconds each while keeping the head up and back straight.
 5) Around the World: Wrap the ball around the waist, head, and feet continuously, counting how many full rotations are completed in 30 seconds.
 6) Figure Eights: Roll or dribble the ball through and around both legs in a figure-eight pattern in both directions for 30 seconds.
pe-06886:
1) 'Racing Rackets': Practice footwork with 5 steps forward, 5 side shuffles right, 5 backpedal steps, and 5 shuffles back.
 2) 'Racket Switch': Stand 5 feet apart with a partner, release standing rackets on 'three', and sprint to catch the partner's racket before it hits the ground.
 3) 'Pancake Flips': Balance and flip a poly spot or ball on the racket's sweet spot to build wrist control.
 4) 'Hula Hoop Passing': Bounce and pass a tennis ball inside a hula hoop to sustain a volley rally with a partner, then move back.
pe-06887:
1) Partner one puts on the blindfold at the start spot
 2) The guide places both hands on the partner's shoulders to walk forward
 3) The guide removes hands to stop, keeps only the left hand to turn left, or keeps only the right hand to turn right through the obstacles
pe-06888:
1) Sit on the floor, roll down, and pull up using stomach muscles as if pulling a pretend rope.
 2) Lie flat on the back, lift the head to wave at friends, and shake each leg in the air.
 3) Gallop counterclockwise while swinging a pretend lasso, then switch directions.
 4) Perform arm circles and sliding, then hold a push-up position to do arm circles and shoulder touches.
pe-06889:
1) Perform forward and backward jumps with claps and swivel steps in rhythm to the cues and music.
 2) Bend backward to pass underneath a rope held by two people.
 3) Lower the rope step by step to increase the challenge.
pe-06890:
1) Divide into teams and wear belts to identify team members.
 2) A player who receives the ball cannot pass it right back to the person who passed it.
 3) Pass the ball to other teammates and complete five consecutive passes to score a point.
pe-06891:
1) Students sit quietly in groups of six in a circle with one beach ball per group.
 2) The game begins with an underhand toss to start the rally.
 3) Players use a bump if the ball is below shoulders, and a set if it is above shoulders.
 4) The same person cannot hit the ball twice in a row, keeping the ball floating without hitting the floor.
pe-06892:
1) Students pair up, retrieve an orange soccer ball, and face each other.
 2) One partner rolls the ball and the other performs a sole trap using the bottom of the foot, then rolls it back.
 3) Next, practice side trapping using the inside of the foot while absorbing the impact so the ball does not ricochet.
 4) Transition to inside-of-the-foot short passing, trapping with either the sole or inside before passing back.
 5) Increase the distance and practice long passes using the shoelace part of the foot with toes pointed down, followed by a trap.
pe-06893:
1) Divide students into two teams, Crows and Cranes, facing each other in the center.
 2) When the teacher calls the name of one bird team, that team runs to their nest (the black line) while the other team chases them to the line to tag them.
 3) If the runner reaches their nest without being tagged, they score 1 point, and if the chaser tags them before the line, the chaser scores 1 point.
 4) As a math variation, assign one team as Evens and the other as Odds, and when the teacher calls out addition, subtraction, or multiplication problems (such as 5+5, 5+4, 15-5, or 6×6), the team matching the answer runs to their line while the other team chases.
pe-06894:
1) Place obstacles lengthwise through the gym and mark a line for throwers.
 2) Divide students into runners, throwers, and retrievers.
 3) Runners must touch every obstacle as they race toward the opposite wall, starting once the previous runner touches the first obstacle.
 4) Throwers stay behind the line and attempt to hit runners with dodgeballs, while retrievers feed balls to throwers.
 5) Runners earn one point if they touch the opposite wall without being hit, then return along the back wall, whereas getting hit requires rejoining the line immediately.
 6) After 4 minutes, tally the points and switch roles between runners and throwers.
pe-06895:
1) Each team builds two spaceships near the back of their side using hoops.
 2) All players start at the end line and run to grab dodgeballs on the go signal.
 3) Players throw dodgeballs from their own half to knock down opposing spaceships, with only one guard allowed per spaceship.
pe-06896:
1) Players form a large square or circle with one or two people in the middle as 'it'.
 2) Outside players pass a ball around without it being intercepted or deflected by the person in the middle.
 3) The ball must be passed at or below the head height of the person in the middle.
 4) The person in the middle can intercept the pass or run up and tag whoever is holding the ball.
 5) If a pass is intercepted, deflected, or a player is tagged while holding the ball, they switch places with the middle player.
pe-06897:
1) Divide players into 2 or 3 teams and have each team form a single file line
 2) The first runner balances a beanbag on a designated body part and moves as quickly as possible to the far end and back
 3) If the beanbag drops or is grabbed with hands, the runner must stop and reset it before continuing; the first team whose members all complete the run and sit down wins
pe-06898:
1) Stand on a flat surface and focus eyes on a fixed object in the distance.
 2) Tighten abdominal core muscles to keep the body upright and steady.
 3) Keep arms straight without excessive swinging to aid balance.
 4) Start by holding onto a wall and lifting one foot at a time.
 5) Progress by letting go of the wall, spreading arms outward, and practicing on both legs equally.
pe-06899:
1) Line all children up along one side of the playing area.
 2) Give each child a specific pizza topping name.
 3) When the leader calls out their topping, race to the opposite side to grab a beanbag and deliver it to the chef, or all run when 'deluxe' is called.
pe-06900:
1) Keep your head and body upright and straight with eyes looking forward.
 2) Land on the balls of your feet and lift knees high as if climbing low stairs.
 3) Bend elbows at 90 degrees and pump arms by the sides without crossing in front.
 4) Ensure feet land directly under the body quietly and lightly without slapping the ground.
pe-06901:
1) Construct a stomp board by securing a PVC pipe and foam noodle to plywood using duct tape.
 2) Place a beanbag on the end marked with tape (X mark).
 3) Stomp the opposite colored end of the board with your foot to launch and catch the beanbag.
pe-06902:
1) Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and keep eyes looking forward.
 2) Bend hips, knees, and ankles while bringing arms straight back behind the body.
 3) Forcefully straighten legs, swing arms forward to jump up, and land softly on both feet simultaneously.
pe-06903:
1) Focus your eyes forward on the target area where you are going to leap.
 2) Stand on one leg and ground that foot firmly into the floor to hold balance.
 3) Bend the knee and leap forward to land on the other foot.
 4) Hold your balance on the landing foot and practice leaping back and forth or in multiple directions.
 5) If struggling with balance, hold onto a wall to assist with balance while practicing the leap.
pe-06904:
1) Step forward with the lead leg and hop.
 2) Move arms on the sides in opposition to the legs.
 3) Land softly on the balls of the feet.
 4) Keep eyes focused forward to see where you are going.
pe-06905:
1) Split the group into two even teams lining up on opposite sides of the playing area.
 2) Assign numbers starting with 1 to each team member and place 1 yoga ball in the middle of the playing area.
 3) When the leader yells out a number, the players with that number from each side run to the middle to pick up the yoga ball and bring it back to their team line.
 4) The player without the ball tries to tag the ball carrier before they cross their team line; bringing the ball back safely scores 1 point, and making a tag before the line scores 1 point for the tagger's team.
pe-06906:
1) Perform varied footwork and jumping jacks by crossing arms and legs in alternating patterns
 2) Hop onto colored spots with the designated foot to train balance and coordination
 3) Keep one or two balloons afloat using hands or body parts while adding spins and rotations
pe-06907:
1) Single-Leg Stand: Shift weight to one side, lift the other leg, and hold a steady posture for up to 30 seconds before switching legs.
 2) Flying Bird: Stand feet together, focus on a spot 4-5 feet ahead, lift one leg back, and hinge forward with arms extended to balance.
 3) One-Leg Touch: Stand on one foot, gradually bend forward to touch the floor, stand back up, and repeat on the other side.
 4) ABC Balance: Stand on one leg and use the opposite foot in the air to trace alphabet letters or numbers with large motions.
 5) Line Walk: Walk along a straight line heel-to-toe with arms outstretched, pausing for one second as the back leg lifts before stepping forward.
 6) Color Jump: Start on a center spot, jump toward a colored target, hold your balance for 3 seconds upon landing, and jump back to center.
pe-06908:
1) Divide the area into two equal halves with cones and place bean bags
 2) Kick or flick bean bags to the opponent's side continuously for 60 seconds
 3) The player with more bean bags on their side at the end loses the round, playing 3 rounds in total
pe-06909:
1) One player kicks a hula hoop toward a cone to knock it down while the defender kicks another hoop to block it
 2) In the second variation the defender stands in front of the cone and jumps inside the rolling hoop to stop it
 3) In the third variation both players protect their own cone and kick hoops to knock down the opponent's cone
pe-06910:
1) Roll up socks into ball shapes.
 2) 'Target Retrieval': Scatter sock balls, then collect them one by one into the target area as fast as possible (or hop on one leg for dynamic balance).
 3) 'Mat Jump Transfer': Pick up a sock ball and jump across to transfer all socks from one mat to another.
 4) 'Into the Box': Hold a sock ball between your feet, jump, and drop it into the box.
pe-06911:
1) Mark a small inner circle with cones and a larger outer circle with markers.
 2) Defending team guards the cones in the center, and attacking team spreads around the outer circle.
 3) On the command 'go', attackers enter the circle to touch the cones and must exit before being tagged.
 4) Safely touching a cone and exiting earns 1 point; being tagged inside voids the attempt, and roles switch after 2-3 minutes.
pe-06912:
1) Divide students into four lines, selecting one tagger and one runner.
 2) On the go command, the tagger chases the runner; the runner escapes by standing in front of any line and clapping.
 3) Once the runner joins the front, the last player of that line instantly becomes the new runner.
 4) If tagged, roles reverse; runners must escape within 10 to 20 seconds.
pe-06913:
1) Place flat cones equal to the number of teams in the center, and teams of two or more arrange in a circle 1-2m apart.
 2) On the command 'go', the last player of each team runs around the circle in the same direction back to their team.
 3) The player crawls between teammates' legs to the center to capture a flat cone.
 4) Reduce cones each round, and the team with the most cones wins.
pe-06914:
1) Toss the thin plastic up and shake the table tennis racket to generate air and keep it floating
 2) The player who keeps it in the air longest without directly hitting it wins
 3) Play variations by blowing air from the mouth or pushing it toward a chair
pe-06915:
1) Players toss the hanky back and forth and catch it on their foot or knee
 2) Once caught, players must toss it back without bringing the foot down to the floor
 3) Dropping the hanky results in losing a point, playing for 3 sets of 5 to 10 points
pe-06916:
1) Push right up onto your toes before takeoff and lift your legs straight into the air.
 2) Keep your legs straight all the way up and all the way down.
 3) For the straddle headstand, take off and land maintaining the straddle shape.
pe-06917:
1) Perform a cartwheel travelling in a long line.
 2) Connect immediately into a handstand forward roll without putting the foot down twice.
 3) Follow with another forward roll, a half twist jump, and a backward roll before finishing with a present.
pe-06918:
1) Practice gymnastics skills on the floor first before taking them to the beam.
 2) Step onto the beam and hop forward lifting your knee above hip height with a strong base leg.
 3) Turn around and practice hopping backwards while keeping the knee lifted as high as possible.
 4) Practice the same hops and leaps on the other leg.
 5) Imagine a big puddle in the middle of the beam, split your legs wide in the air to leap across without getting wet, and hold the finish landing.
pe-06919:
1) Practice a cartwheel starting facing forward and finishing facing backward with a quarter turn.
 2) Practice a cartwheel starting facing forward and finishing facing forward with a quarter turn at the end.
 3) Perform a one-handed cartwheel with the free hand on the hip or side, kicking legs fast so the hand stays on the floor briefly.
pe-06920:
1) Begin with an arabesque and roll smoothly into a dish shape.
 2) Transition straight from the dish into an L-sit position.
 3) Lift hips into a back support, hold for three seconds, then lift one leg and hold for three seconds.
 4) Roll over into a front support and bring the leg round straight into the splits, holding for three seconds.
 5) Place hands and feet straight into a bridge shape, then finish with a kick over or rolling in a ball.
pe-06921:
1) Mount the balance beam by squatting onto it.
 2) Walk forward into a front support, transition to a side support with hand on hip, and hold the shape tightly for 3 seconds.
 3) Jump into a crouch and stand up tall to execute an artistic pose.
 4) Walk to the end of the beam and perform a pivot turn with chin up.
 5) Run to the end of the beam and dismount with a stretched jump, landing with feet together.
pe-06922:
1) Lay out six conditioning skill cards on the floor next to the dice numbered 1 through 6.
 2) Roll the dice to determine which number appears on top.
 3) Identify the corresponding gymnastics skill card and perform the designated reps for that exercise.
 4) Once the reps are completed, roll the dice again to continue with the next gymnastics exercise.
pe-06923:
1) Sit on the floor in a wide straddle position with legs straight and toes pointed.
 2) Place one shoulder directly onto the floor rather than falling straight backward.
 3) Roll across the back so the tummy faces up toward the ceiling.
 4) Keep legs straight, hold tightly onto them, and sit upright facing the opposite direction.
 5) For a paired variation, sit back-to-back and roll in opposite directions around each other.
pe-06924:
1) Sit forwards with legs outstretched straight and toes pointed, keeping back straight and arms behind ears for long sit.
 2) Spread legs wide for a straddle shape, keeping toes pointed, back straight, and arms up by ears.
pe-06925:
1) Practice split leaps across two lines by taking off from one foot and landing on the other.
 2) Perform cat leaps by lifting one knee at a time up to the chest with pointed toes.
 3) Practice the stag leap shape on the floor with straight legs, then execute the leap in the air.
pe-06926:
1) Get into a bridge shape with straight legs and arms, feet firmly on the floor.
 2) Kick both legs over one after the other.
 3) Finish in a lunge shape and stand tall.
 4) For a walkover, drop your head back, look for the beam, and place your feet on it.
pe-06927:
1) Stand in a ready position at the end or side of the balance beam.
 2) Lift both arms high above your shoulders and perform a high stretch jump.
 3) Keep your legs straight in the air and land smartly with both feet flat on the beam.
pe-06928:
1) Start on the end of the beam, jump high into the air, and perform a stretch jump with a turn to face the other direction.
 2) Keep both arms stretched straight up above the head rather than bringing them out to the side.
 3) Practice jumping by starting facing forwards to finish facing backwards, and starting facing backwards to finish facing forwards.
 4) For the cartwheel dismount, start on the beam with a long reach, placing hands on the beam and landing feet onto the floor.
 5) Step deeply into the lunge, stretch legs with pointed toes, and hold the lunge upon landing to finish.
pe-06929:
1) Copy one of the demonstrated gymnastics artistic poses or create your own variation with personal flair.
 2) Lift your head and chin high and maintain a full stretch from your fingers to your toes while minding finger, wrist, head, and elbow positions.
 3) Hold the challenging artistic pose steadily for 3 seconds.
pe-06930:
1) Walk along the beam with good form until reaching the middle.
 2) [Pivot Turn] Lower arms, stay up on tiptoes, pivot on both feet until feet align straight, then raise arms and walk backwards.
 3) [Spin] Walk to the center, bring back foot down, lift knee up high onto tiptoe, and cross arms up across the body to spin.
 4) Once turned around facing the opposite direction, continue travelling backwards along the beam.
pe-06931:
1) Before moving onto the beam, put a line down on the floor and practice forward rolling straight along the line.
 2) On the beam, stretch up tall and squat down with one foot flat on the beam and the other foot up on its toe.
 3) Reach forwards and tuck your head nice and close into your body to perform the forward roll.
 4) Come up into a controlled squat landing position to finish.
pe-06932:
1) Start on the back with knees tucked into the chest in a tucked dish shape.
 2) Tighten tummy muscles to ensure no daylight appears under the back while bringing legs out one at a time.
 3) Lie face down and lift straight arms and legs off the floor to hold an arch shape with the head in line with the arms.
pe-06933:
1) Three players on each team enter the court and play simultaneously with two shuttlecocks
 2) Both teams serve at the same time from behind the back service line
 3) A team scores a point when both shuttlecocks land simultaneously on the opponent's side
 4) As long as one shuttlecock is in play, players can retrieve the grounded shuttlecock and serve again
pe-06934:
1) Pairs rally back and forth on a half badminton court to maintain the longest rally (Build 1).
 2) Divide each side into three zones (back 3 pts, middle 1 pt, front 2 pts) and play short games to 5 points (Build 2).
 3) Place 6 poly spots per court; scoring on a spot earns 3 points and removes the spot, and the first to 11 points wins (Build 3).
pe-06935:
1) Set up castle structures with pins, cones, and hoops in each end zone, and place mats on each side to serve as slingshot mounts.
 2) In Build 1, pairs play as slingshots and loaders where loaders retrieve balls and slingshots launch them at the opponent's castle using a powerful sit-up.
 3) In Build 2, half the team becomes blockers defending castles while their battery partners hold wall squats outside the court.
 4) In Build 3, lasers collect up to two balls and throw from a hoop mount while their power units do jumping jacks outside.
pe-06936:
1) Four teams start at their designated goals placed in each of the four corners.
 2) Players called by number enter the middle to contest the ball and shoot into any of the other three teams' goals.
 3) When scored upon, bench players place a ring on their cone, closing the goal once it reaches three rings, and the last surviving team wins.
pe-06937:
1) Spread spots out in the center as tee boxes and place matching colored hula hoops around the perimeter as holes.
 2) The first player tees off from the spot using a lollipop paddle or hockey stick toward the matching hoop.
 3) If the ball stays inside the hoop, count it as one point; otherwise partners alternate shots until the ball stays in the hoop.
 4) The next partner selects a different colored tee box and hole to continue the challenge.
pe-06938:
1) Two teams lie flat on their backs on mats separated by a center line
 2) Players keep their backs and bottoms on the mats and kick the cageball with their feet
 3) If a team kicks the ball over the opposing team, they earn a point
 4) Players can use their hands to block the ball from going over them to prevent the opponent from scoring
pe-06939:
1) Prepare a paper rocket (or short pool noodle) and view the demonstrated challenge on screen for 15 seconds.
 2) Bet on yourself whether you can complete the movement and catch the rocket 5 or less times or 6 or more times in 1 minute.
 3) Complete the designated 30-second fitness exercise based on your chosen bet.
 4) On 'Go', perform the rocket challenge for 1 minute and count your successful catches to see if your bet was correct.
 5) Progress through challenge variations including basic launch & catch, two claps & catch, floor tap & catch, jumping launch, kneel-to-stand catch, foot launch, and behind-the-back spin catch.
pe-06940:
1) Start the game with a serve over the net on a court.
 2) Instead of volleying with hits, players catch the ball and throw it back over the net.
 3) Points are scored when the ball lands on the opponent's floor or an error occurs; the scoring team retains the serve and rotates upon winning the serve back.
pe-06941:
1) Divide roles within the group into a bowler and a pin fixer.
 2) The bowler stands on the spot marker, bends, and rolls the ball toward the pins.
 3) The pin fixer resets fallen pins and returns the ball.
 4) Teammates switch roles and take turns.
pe-06942:
1) Dribble using both feet with little taps, keeping the ball under control and close
 2) Trap the ball at a floor dot
 3) Make an inside-of-the-foot pass to the wall, then dribble to find a different dot after the rebound
pe-06943:
1) Dog catchers hold pool noodle pieces while the rest of the players act as puppies running around
 2) Puppies who are tagged must return to their cages (designated mat area)
 3) When all puppies are tagged, choose new dog catchers for the next round
pe-06944:
1) Divide students into blue and red teams
 2) Blue team runners go one at a time dribbling a basketball zigzag through blue cones and sit at the end to cheer
 3) Meanwhile red team players take turns shooting from the free-throw line scoring 1 point for backboard, 2 for rim, and 3 for a basket
 4) Shooters retrieve the ball and return to the back of the line while points are accumulated until all runners finish.
pe-06945:
1) The running team lines up in a safe zone, and the first runner carries an item like a tennis racket or cricket bat.
 2) The runner scores a point for their team by running down to the opposite safe zone and returning.
 3) Throwers positioned in pairs along the sidelines attempt to hit the runner with dodgeballs.
 4) The runner can deflect balls with the item, but if hit, they freeze and pass the item to the next runner.
pe-06946:
1) Set up one volleyball net and use one volleyball per game.
 2) Two teams stand in the six different court positions on each side.
 3) One team serves and players rally following regular volleyball rules.
 4) Every single hit and pass during the rally counts as one accumulated point.
 5) Once the rally ends, the team that won the rally earns all the points accumulated during that rally.
 6) The winning team of the rally serves next, continuing play in the same manner.
 7) The first team to reach 100 points wins the game.
pe-06947:
1) Pair up with one partner at the starting line and the other ahead in the field.
 2) On go, throw and catch the frisbee, then the thrower runs ahead of the catcher to receive the next pass.
 3) Alternate throws down to the end line and back to win, restarting from the last checkpoint if dropped.
pe-06948:
1) Divide students into teams of 4 or 5, set up as many nets as there are teams, and line teams up at pylons or benches.
 2) Teammates take turns grabbing a puck or ball and shooting on an opposing team's goalie.
 3) If a player scores, the puck stays in the net and the player returns to the bench for the next teammate to go.
 4) If a player misses, they must retrieve the puck wherever it ended up and bring it back to the next person in line to try again.
 5) The first team to score all 10 (or
 5) of their pucks wins, and teams switch goalies every round.
pe-06949:
1) Set up hula hoops on each side of the net in groups of three (2 sets), two (2 sets), and one (1 set) to represent battleships.
 2) On the go signal, players serve the volleyball over the net into the opposing team's area.
 3) If a served ball lands inside an opposing hoop, that hoop is removed as a hit, and the first team to sink all opposing battleships wins.
pe-06950:
1) Set up safe zones at both ends of the gym and divide the class into a running team with hockey sticks in one safe zone and a throwing team with dodgeballs along the side boundaries.
 2) Place pucks or balls in the far safe zone, and on the start signal, runners run across to the far safe zone while dodging balls thrown from the sides.
 3) Runners who reach the far zone pick up one puck and stick-handle it all the way back to their starting safe zone without getting hit.
 4) Any runner hit by a dodgeball sits down for the rest of the round, and once all runners are out, count the pucks safely returned before switching roles.
pe-06951:
1) Place four sets of wickets in a diamond shape with one batter at each wicket and one bowler in the middle.
 2) The bowler bowls the ball to any of the four batters.
 3) Once a batter hits the ball, all four batters run simultaneously clockwise to the next wicket.
 4) Batters score one point each time they successfully switch wickets without getting out.
 5) A batter is out if the ball is caught in the air, if the fielding team hits the wicket with the ball while runners are between wickets, or if the bowl hits the wicket directly.
pe-06952:
1) Fielders form an umbrella shape 15 to 20 feet away from the thrower
 2) The thrower takes turns throwing or hitting the ball to each player
 3) The fielder must properly field the ball (catching or fielding a ground ball) and throw it back, losing a life if unsuccessful
 4) After each round, the fielders back up to increase difficulty until one player remains
pe-06953:
1) Set up pylons on one side for team lines and place benches across to create the pond area.
 2) Distribute targets such as hula hoops, bins, mats, and basketball nets inside the pond.
 3) The first player from each line steps up to the bench and hits or serves the birdie underhand into the pond.
 4) Collect the designated number of fish (bean bags) based on the target hit, retrieve the birdie, and return to pass to the next teammate.
pe-06954:
1) Partners stick-handle in opposite directions around the gym boundaries.
 2) When music stops or the whistle blows, continue all the way around without cutting across to meet your partner.
 3) Meet up and sit down together, and the last pair to do so completes an exercise or is eliminated.
pe-06955:
1) Divide into three teams with designated starting corners, giving each team two dodgeballs of their own color.
 2) On start, play elimination dodgeball by throwing balls to hit opponents or catching opponent throws.
 3) Players can only pick up and throw dodgeballs matching their team's color.
 4) A player holding the ball may take a maximum of 3 steps and hold it for only 3 seconds before passing or throwing.
 5) Players hit by a ball or whose throw is caught are eliminated, and the last remaining team wins.
pe-06956:
1) Designate a wall space and have players start an individual free-for-all game with 3 to 5 lives each.
 2) The starting player spikes the ball downward so that it bounces once on the floor before hitting the wall.
 3) The next player must return the ball by spiking it down against the wall in the same manner, losing a life upon any fault until the last remaining player wins.
pe-06957:
1) A team of 7-8 players sets up with one batter, one bowler, and the rest as fielders.
 2) The bowler delivers the ball 5 times to the batter to practice aimed hitting.
 3) If fielders catch or cleanly field the ball, the team earns a point, and that fielder sits out the rest of that batter's turn to let others field.
pe-06958:
1) Pairs move to their designated areas equipped with Chinese jump ropes.
 2) Progress through routines by raising the rope from Level 1 (ankles), Level 2 (shins/calves), Level 3 (knees), to Level 4 (thighs).
 3) Support partners to reach higher levels and create original routines at advanced levels.
pe-06959:
1) Practice the 40-yard dash by running in place as fast as you can following the coach.
 2) Train hand-eye coordination by catching footballs thrown toward the screen.
 3) Practice dodging left or right and executing spin moves to avoid tackles.
 4) Practice jumping over defenders and using stiff-arm movements to fend them off.
 5) Advance through 5 game levels combining these skills to score touchdowns and perform celebration dances.
pe-06960:
1) Put weight into a school backpack using books, toys, or shoes, taking items out if too heavy
 2) Put the backpack on and warm up with jogging in place
 3) Follow the guided routine including lunge jumps, tricep extensions, jogging happy hands, bicep curls, backpack thrusters, bass drum hits, balance squats, and trunk twists
pe-06961:
1) Teams line up in relay style, each with a bucket filled with throwing items (rubber turkeys, bean bags, balls).
 2) The first person steps up to the line and throws the turkey over the parachute wall using an overhand throw.
 3) Go around the wall to check the target: 1 point if it lands in any hula hoop, or 2 points if it lands in their team's color hoop.
 4) Retrieve the item, return it to the next runner in line, and track team points on the scorecard using a paper clip.
pe-06962:
1) Guess which of the three items the pot of gold is hidden behind.
 2) Look at the exercise displayed directly above your selected item.
 3) Perform the designated fitness movement while the timer counts down.
 4) Check the reveal at the end of the round to see where the gold pot was hidden.
 5) Continue to select items and perform different exercises in each new round.
pe-06963:
1) Divide the area into three sections: Bronze, Silver, and Gold.
 2) Each student carries 12 Speed Stacks cups and raises a hand to find a partner to compete in the Bronze area.
 3) Winners advance step by step to Silver and then Gold.
 4) Winning at the Gold level earns one silicone bracelet, and the player jogs back to Bronze to restart.
 5) Players who lose stay in their current section and find a new partner to compete.
pe-06964:
1) Rest for 10 seconds and listen to the next joke question.
 2) Perform the surprise exercise for 20 seconds.
 3) Listen to the answer to the joke after 10 seconds and keep exercising until the next question.
pe-06965:
1) Quickly count the number of leprechauns displayed on the screen within 5 seconds.
 2) Match the counted number to the corresponding on-screen exercise and perform it for 20 seconds.
 3) Check the revealed correct number when the exercise finishes and continue to the next round.
pe-06966:
1) Pick your favorite jump rope skill from each slide (doing the first option every time is fine).
 2) Jump rope for 30 seconds following the timer.
 3) Rest or dance for 10 seconds to get ready for the next round.
pe-06967:
1) A dance move or exercise pops up on screen during the rest period
 2) If you want to do that move, accept the 'deal' and perform that exercise for 30 seconds when the timer starts
 3) If you do not want to do that move, choose 'no deal' and perform the surprise movement that appears for the 30-second interval
pe-06968:
1) Choose the best exercise for yourself from four choices on the screen
 2) Perform the selected movement for 20 seconds
 3) Rest or dance for 10 seconds until the next exercise appears
pe-06969:
1) Extend legs straight together in front and place arms behind on a bench or chair
 2) Bend arms to dip your bottom below the bench or chair
 3) Straighten arms and push back up
pe-06970:
1) Banana Hold: Lie flat on a mat with arms and legs straight, lift them into a banana shape, hold for two seconds, and return down.
